Brush drawing in brown wash measuring 277 by 196 mm, held by the British Museum, the sheet belongs to the body of studies Zurbarán made for the austere Carthusian and Mercedarian friars who populate his Seville altarpieces.

title: Job mocked by his Wife
description: Job sits naked on his dunghill while his wife berates him by the light of a single candle. La Tour treats the Old Testament confrontation as an intimate two-figure nocturne, the flame between them mapping every fold of skin and cloth.

provenance.collection: Musée départemental d'Art ancien et contemporain
provenance.location: Musée départemental d'Art ancien et contemporain

title: Massacre of the Innocents
dateCreated: Entre 1625-1626 (selon Jacques Thuillier) et 1628-1629 (selon Anthony Blunt)
description: Compressed to its essential cruelty, the painting isolates a single soldier pinning a mother and child as Herod's slaughter unfolds. Poussin condenses the biblical episode into a sculptural triangle of figures, prefiguring later modern responses to depictions of state violence.

title: Portrait of Marchese Ambrogio Spinola
description: The Genoese-born Habsburg general Ambrogio Spinola, victor at Breda, appears in burnished black armor with a crisp lace collar and the red sash of command. Rubens, who knew the marquess personally during the Twelve Years' Truce, distills authority into a steady, weary gaze.
credit: Národní galerie v Praze - online collection

title: Smiling Girl
description: A young woman grins broadly at the viewer while holding up a small framed picture of a couple in flagrante. Signed oil on canvas of 82 by 64 cm in the Saint Louis Art Museum, the painting belongs to the genre of Utrecht Caravaggesque half-figures in which Honthorst turned tavern wit into salon entertainment.

title: The lapidation of Saint Stephen
description: Saul looks on from horseback as a knot of attackers raise stones above the kneeling deacon, who turns his face toward a beam of heavenly light. Signed and dated 1625, the canvas is Rembrandt's earliest documented painting, completed at nineteen in Leiden and now held by the Musée des Beaux-Arts de Lyon.
credit: Œuvre appartenant au musée des Beaux-Arts de Lyon Consulter cette image photographiée par Gilles Alonso spécialiste de la photo en gigapixel en très haute définition (+1 milliard de pixels)

title: The Matchmaker or The Procuress
description: A candle-lit brothel scene in which an old procuress brokers a young woman to a leering client. Honthorst, nicknamed Gherardo delle Notti in Rome, transplanted Caravaggio's tenebrism north; here a hidden flame carves the faces from the dark in glowing reds and ochres.

title: The Merry Student
description: A young man slumped at a table, drink in hand, his lute and books pushed aside in a candlelit interior. Catalogued as number 391 in the Bavarian State Painting Collections, the panel belongs to Honthorst's series of moralising tavern scenes in which Utrecht Caravaggism is bent toward the theme of squandered learning.

title: The Musicians' Brawl
description: Itinerant street musicians come to blows over a hurdy-gurdy, one wielding a knife as a companion squeezes a lemon to feign a wound. La Tour stages the brawl in cool daylight, his earlier Caravaggesque manner before he fully turned to candlelit nocturnes.

title: River landscape with Pan and Syrinx
description: A collaborative mythological landscape in which Rubens painted the figures of Pan pursuing the nymph Syrinx while Jan Brueghel the Younger supplied the dense reed bed and wooded river setting. Such partnerships between Antwerp masters were a hallmark of Flemish Baroque cabinet painting.

title: The Artist in his Studio
description: A small early panel showing a painter, dwarfed by an enormous panel on his easel, contemplating his work from across a bare studio. The image foregrounds thought rather than craft, framing painting as a fundamentally mental activity.

title: The Hermit and the Sleeping Angelica
description: An aged hermit, drawn from Ariosto's Orlando Furioso, gazes lasciviously upon the sleeping Angelica in a moonlit forest. Rubens contrasts ascetic gauntness with luminous female flesh, transforming the chivalric romance into a Baroque meditation on temptation.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"r/rubens/61other/05hermit"

title: Anton Giulio Brignole-Sale on horseback
description: The Genoese patron rides forward beneath a heavy classical arch, a swaggering equestrian formula van Dyck adapted from Rubens and Titian. Now in the Palazzo Rosso, the canvas anchors the painter's six-year Italian sojourn.

title: Christ on the Cross
description: A life-size crucified Christ emerges from impenetrable darkness, the body modelled with sculptural tenebrism that fooled at least one early viewer into thinking the work a polychrome carving. Painted for Seville's Dominican monastery of San Pablo, it announced Zurbarán's austere devotional manner.
credit: Art Institute of Chicago; Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"z/zurbaran/1/christ_x"

title: Adam and Eve
description: Rubens's homage to Titian, copied during his stay in Madrid where he studied the royal collection. The serpent-child reaches down to Eve as Adam grasps her arm; Rubens warms the Venetian palette and softens the contours toward his own fleshier ideal.

title: Pythagoras advocating vegetarianism
description: Rubens depicts the Greek philosopher gesturing toward a heap of fruit and grain as he urges his listeners to abstain from meat. The composition draws on Ovid's Metamorphoses, with abundant still-life passages painted in collaboration with Frans Snyders.

title: Rembrandt van Rijn - Zelfportret
description: An early Leiden self-portrait in which the young Rembrandt's face is half-lost in shadow beneath a tousled crown of hair. He scratches into the wet paint with the butt of the brush to suggest stray locks, an experimental touch typical of these years.

title: Samson and Delilah
description: Delilah leans forward in shock as Philistine soldiers seize the shorn Samson from her lap, the moment of betrayal pitched between sensuality and violence. Van Dyck reworks Rubens's earlier composition with cooler colour and a more refined, elongated drawing.

title: Sansón matando al león
description: Samson grapples a roaring lion to the ground and tears its jaws apart, the biblical strongman rendered with anatomical force and twisting torso. Rubens reworked the subject several times, transposing the heroic male nude of antique sculpture into a violent Old Testament exemplum.

title: Self-portrait
description: The young painter turns from his easel, eyes shadowed beneath a tangle of frizzy hair, face half-lost in raking light. An oil on panel of about 22 by 19 cm in the Rijksmuseum, the picture experiments with highlights scratched into wet paint, a technique Rembrandt was developing in the Leiden workshop he shared with Jan Lievens.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"r/rembrand/27self/03sp1628"

title: The Triumph of Bacchus
description: A pale, half-nude Bacchus crowns a kneeling soldier with vine leaves while a circle of weather-beaten Spanish drinkers grins out at the viewer. Painted in Madrid before Velázquez's first trip to Italy, the canvas pulls classical mythology down to tavern level with a sober, almost documentary realism.

title: Concert of Birds
description: An owl serves as conductor while a riot of songbirds reads from a sheet of music, a witty allegorical conceit Snyders treated repeatedly. The tightly observed plumage of finches, parrots and birds of prey reflects his standing as Antwerp's premier animal specialist.

title: Esther before Ahasuerus
description: The biblical queen swoons before the Persian king as she pleads for her people, a subject Gentileschi treats with operatic gesture and sumptuous fabrics. Painted during her Neapolitan years, it shows her assimilation of Caravaggesque drama into a more courtly, decorative key.
credit: Metropolitan Museum of Art, online collection (The Met object ID 436453)

title: Isabella von Bourbon
description: A state portrait of Isabella of Bourbon, queen consort of Spain, in stiff black court dress and pearls. Rubens softens the rigid Habsburg formula with subtle modelling of the face and a discreet warmth in the flesh tones.

title: Minerva protects Pax from Mars
description: Painted in London for Charles I as a diplomatic gift, the allegory shows Minerva pushing back the war-god Mars while Pax nurses Plutus and children gather around the fruits of peace. The picture distilled Rubens's hopes for an Anglo-Spanish accord into a sumptuous tableau of bodies and abundance.

title: Portrait of Maria Louis de Tassis
description: A standing portrait of the Antwerp heiress in a starched lace ruff and black silk gown set with jewels, her hand resting on an ostrich-feather fan. Van Dyck's Genoese-influenced full-length format and silvery handling of fabric established the elegant template he would soon export to the Stuart court.

title: Portrait of Thomas Howard
description: A state portrait of Thomas Howard, 14th Earl of Arundel, the great English collector of antiquities, painted during Rubens's diplomatic stay in London. The sitter is shown armoured and commanding, in the rich blacks and gleaming highlights of mature Flemish Baroque portraiture.

title: Self-Portrait with Gorget
description: Bust-length self-portrait of the painter facing right, wearing a gleaming steel gorget over a white collar and gazing back at the viewer. Long catalogued as a Rembrandt, the panel in the Germanisches Nationalmuseum, Nuremberg, was reassigned by the Rembrandt Research Project to a Leiden studio assistant copying a lost prototype of about 1629.

title: Amor Asleep
description: Cupid lies sprawled in slumber, bow and quiver set aside, his pearly flesh modelled in the warm glazes Rubens favoured for putti and infants. The motif of disarmed love invites the viewer to contemplate desire's vulnerability when stilled.

title: Andromeda
description: The princess of Ethiopia stands chained to the rock, arms drawn back behind her head, awaiting the sea monster while Perseus is absent from the field. Painted on panel about 1630 and held by the Mauritshuis in The Hague, the canvas treats the Ovidian myth as an intimate nude study rather than a heroic action.
credit: Geheugen van Nederland : Home : Info : Pic

title: Avondlandschap met boerenkar
description: A peasant cart laden with felled timber rumbles down a rutted track as the day's last light catches clouds and treetops. The naturalistic Flemish countryside and warm low sun place this among the personal landscapes Rubens painted for his own pleasure.

title: Bust of an old man with a fur cap
description: An early tronie, or character study, of a bearded old man in a fur cap, painted in Leiden. Rembrandt explores the fall of light across creased skin and the shaggy textures of the cap as exercises in expressive description.

title: Cats Fighting in a Larder
description: A pantry overturned by brawling cats among hanging game, fish and copper vessels, a kitchen-piece genre popularized by Frans Snyders and continued by his brother-in-law de Vos. The hissing animals serve as a moralized emblem of greed and chaos disrupting domestic order.

title: Drawing of mules by Claude Lorrain
description: Three mules stand and graze in a campagna pasture, one shown full length in profile, the others lightly sketched behind. A brush drawing in brown wash over graphite of 143 by 257 mm in the British Museum, the sheet documents the patient livestock studies Claude made on his walks out of Rome, later transposed into the foregrounds of his idyllic ports and harbours.

title: Jeremiah Lamenting the Destruction of Jerusalem
description: The aged prophet leans on a sumptuous gold vessel, head in hand, while the city of Jerusalem smokes in the dim distance behind him. Signed and dated 1630, the panel in the Rijksmuseum is among Rembrandt's earliest narrative pictures to wed Caravaggesque chiaroscuro to a deeply introspective biblical subject.

title: Martyrdom of Saint Apollonia
description: The martyrdom of Saint Apollonia, whose teeth are being torn out while her pyre is prepared in the foreground. The print follows a composition by Jacob Jordaens and was engraved by the Antwerp printmaker Marinus Robyn van der Goes for the seventeenth-century devotional market.

title: Martyrdom of Saints John and Paul
description: A Bolognese Baroque altarpiece depicting the martyrdom of the Roman brothers John and Paul, beheaded under Julian the Apostate. Guercino orchestrates the figures along a steep diagonal, his characteristically warm tenebrism modelling flesh against deep shadow with the loose, painterly touch of his mature Roman period.

title: Portrait of a man
description: A bust-length likeness of an unidentified gentleman in dark dress with a starched white collar. The directness of the gaze and the economical handling of the flesh suggest a private commission painted in the artist's mature Antwerp studio.

title: Saint Luke as a painter
description: Saint Luke, traditionally credited with painting the Virgin's likeness, leans on a palette and gazes up at the crucified Christ, conflating the evangelist with the artist's own self-portrait. The sober brown ground and clipped lighting are characteristic of Zurbarán's monastic Sevillian commissions.

title: Self portrait in a cap
description: An early self-portrait etching from Rembrandt's Leiden years, the young artist studies his own face under a soft cap, probing expression and shadow. Such prints functioned as exercises in physiognomy and as advertisements of his graphic virtuosity.

title: Selfportrait
description: A tiny self-image of the painter in dark cloak and beret, head turned three-quarters into a pool of light. Measuring just 15.5 by 12.2 cm on copper and held by the Nationalmuseum, Stockholm, the panel is among Rembrandt's smallest self-portraits, made for the same collectors' cabinets that prized his etched heads of the same year.

title: The Assumption of the Virgin
description: Mary is borne aloft on a tumbling cloud of putti, her arms outflung, while astonished apostles look up from her empty tomb. Painted in Rome around 1630, the canvas belongs to Poussin's early Italian years when he was absorbing Titian's colour and Roman Baroque altarpiece composition before settling into his sterner classicism.

title: The Fortune Teller
description: A naive young man has his palm read by an old gypsy while her accomplices pick his purse and cut his medal chain. La Tour stages the swindle in cool daylight rather than candlelight, exploiting fixed sidelong glances to spell out the deception.

title: The Garden of Love
description: Elegant couples flirt and recline in a balustraded garden while putti scatter roses overhead. Painted soon after Rubens's marriage to Helena Fourment, the scene celebrates conjugal pleasure in his late, pearly Flemish manner and now hangs in the Prado.
credit: Transferred from de.wikipedia to Commons by Outisnn . Original uploader was Nocturne at de.wikipedia . Later version(s) were uploaded by Louis le Grand at de.wikipedia .

title: The Holy Family under the Apple Tree
description: Reverse panel of the Ildefonso Altar painted for Albert and Isabella of the Spanish Netherlands, in which the Holy Family rests in a luminous garden beneath a fruiting apple tree. Rubens links Eve's tree of knowledge to Christ's redemption through the warm Flemish flesh, billowing draperies, and pearly sky that defined his late Baroque manner.

title: The Three Graces
description: The mythological trio stand intertwined in a wooded glade, their pearly flesh set against deep green foliage. Rubens models the women on his second wife Helena Fourment, celebrating an unidealised, sensuous standard of female beauty.

title: Man with viola da gamba
description: A bearded musician in a slashed doublet bows a viola da gamba, his hand stilled on the fingerboard as if pausing between phrases. Signed and dated 1631, the canvas hangs in the Lviv National Art Gallery and continues the half-length musician type Honthorst had popularised after returning from Rome in 1620.

title: The institution of the Eucharist during the Last Supper
description: Christ raises the bread at the centre of the long table while the apostles react in agitation; Judas turns toward the viewer with averted eyes. The picture concentrates on the moment of institution rather than the announcement of betrayal, in line with Counter-Reformation Eucharistic devotion.

title: Diana on the stag hunt
description: The huntress goddess in red, drawing back her bow as hounds drive a stag through dense woodland. The picture belongs to Rubens's late series of aristocratic chase subjects, where landscape, animals and figure painting were typically distributed among studio specialists.

title: Hercules as Heroic Virtue Overcoming Discord
description: An allegorical Hercules, club raised, tramples a writhing female personification of Discord underfoot. The image was conceived as a ceiling design celebrating princely virtue triumphing over civil strife.

title: Landscape with a Rainbow
description: A panoramic Flemish countryside after a storm, peasants and cattle moving among glistening fields beneath a translucent rainbow. Painted on his country estate at Het Steen, it shows Rubens turning to landscape in his late years with broad atmospheric breadth.

title: Portrait of Aeltje Petersdr Uylenburgh
description: An elderly woman in a starched ruff and embroidered cap, the lined face turned slightly toward the light. Signed and dated 1632, this portrait of Aeltje Pietersdr. Uylenburgh, cousin of Rembrandt's future wife Saskia, hangs in the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, and dates from the painter's first Amsterdam year in the workshop of Hendrick Uylenburgh.

title: The abduction of Europa
description: Europa is borne away across the water on the back of Jupiter disguised as a white bull, while her companions react in alarm on the shore. The dark, wooded riverbank and tiny carriage on the bridge give the Ovidian subject the weight of a Dutch landscape.

title: The Anatomy Lesson of Dr Nicolaes Tulp
description: A group portrait of the Amsterdam Surgeons' Guild gathered around the dissected forearm of an executed criminal. Tulp's demonstration of the flexor tendons and the differentiated reactions of his colleagues turn a guild commission into a study of attention.

title: Christ in the Storm on the Sea of Galilee
description: The disciples struggle with sail and rigging on a heaving boat as Christ is roused to calm the sea. Rembrandt's only known seascape, it was stolen from the Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum in 1990 and remains missing.

title: Portrait of Saskia van Uylenburgh
description: A portrait of the artist's wife shortly after their marriage, dressed in fanciful pastoral costume with a feathered hat. Rembrandt's warm light glances across pearls, embroidery, and her unguarded expression.

title: Venetia
description: Venetia, Lady Digby is shown the morning after her sudden death, propped against a pillow with a single rose shedding its petals. Commissioned by her grieving husband Sir Kenelm, the picture is a rare seventeenth-century memorial portrait painted from the corpse.

title: Cook at a Kitchen Table with Dead Game
description: A market cook arranges deer, swans and waterfowl across a generous table while a cat and dog skirmish below, staging abundance as theatre. The display piece, scaled for a Flemish patrician dining room, is typical of Snyders's collaboration with Rubens's circle.

title: Descent from the Cross
description: Christ's slack body is lowered from the cross onto a white shroud while torchlight picks out Joseph of Arimathea, the weeping Virgin and a clamouring crowd below. Signed and dated 1634, the canvas in the State Hermitage, Saint Petersburg, is the second of Rembrandt's full-scale Passion pictures commissioned by Stadholder Frederick Henry of Orange.
credit: www.artchive.com : Home : Info : Pic; arthermitage.org; The Hermitage, St. Petersburg

title: Flora
description: Saskia van Uylenburgh in the guise of the goddess Flora, an enormous garland of tulips and irises crowning her head, a flowered staff in her hand. Signed and dated 1634, the canvas at the Hermitage in Saint Petersburg was painted in the year of Rembrandt's marriage, recasting his young wife in Venetian pastoral fancy dress.

title: Hércules lucha con la hidra de Lerna
description: Hercules grapples with the many-headed Hydra of Lerna, his muscular body twisting against the dark serpentine coils. The canvas belongs to a series of ten Labours of Hercules painted for the Hall of Realms in the Buen Retiro Palace, where Zurbarán's stark tenebrism set the hero against an almost theatrical void.

title: Nicolas Poussin - L'Enlèvement des Sabines
description: Roman soldiers seize Sabine women in a violent twist of bodies, framed by classicizing architecture. Poussin choreographs the abduction as a sculptural relief of opposing diagonals, applying his rigorous study of antique gesture to the legendary founding episode of Rome.

title: Portrait of Haesje Jacobsdr. van Cleyburg
description: A widow of seventy-three sits in profile in a black gown and starched ruff, prayer book closed on her lap, the face carved by quiet light. Signed and dated 1634, the panel in the Rijksmuseum is the pendant to a portrait of Dirck Pesser and belongs to the run of Amsterdam burgher commissions that established Rembrandt as the city's leading portraitist.

title: The Battle of Nördlingen
description: A Rubens-school battlepiece commemorating the Cardinal-Infante Ferdinand's decisive victory over the Swedes in the Thirty Years' War. The cavalry mêlée in the foreground gives way to drifting smoke and a panoramic plain, in the manner Rubens established for Habsburg state imagery.

title: A Landscape with Cows and Duck Hunters
description: A pastoral panorama unfolds along a wooded riverbank, with cattle watered in the foreground and duck hunters moving through the reeds beyond. Painted in the artist's final years at his country estate Het Steen, the work belongs to a group of expansive landscapes notable for their loose handling and golden, atmospheric light.
credit: Objekt in der Onlinesammlung der Staatlichen Museen zu Berlin: 865663 Fotograf: Christoph Schmidt

title: Atalanta and Hippomenes
description: Hippomenes sprints past Atalanta as she stoops for the golden apple of Aphrodite, the wager that costs the huntress her freedom. The Prado canvas is a workshop version after Rubens's design, retaining the diagonal sweep of bodies and the fluttering drapery typical of his Ovidian commissions for Philip IV.

title: Bathsheba at Her Toilet
description: Bathsheba sits at her bath while a black page delivers David's letter, the Old Testament narrative reframed as an excuse for sumptuous flesh, drapery, and still life. The painting now hangs in the Gemäldegalerie Alte Meister, Dresden.

title: Belshazzar's Feast
description: The Babylonian king recoils as a glowing Hebrew inscription, MENE MENE TEKEL UPHARSIN, appears on the wall during his blasphemous feast. Rembrandt stages the moment with theatrical lighting, overturned vessels, and a sumptuous gold-embroidered cloak.

title: Charles I
description: The Stuart king is presented in three-quarter length with elegant hauteur, a pose Van Dyck refined repeatedly to fix the image of Caroline kingship. The painter's silvered palette, fluid drapery, and aristocratic poise shaped English portraiture for a century.

title: Francisco de Zurbarán 006
description: A bound lamb lies on a grey ledge against a dark ground, an Agnus Dei meditation on Christ's sacrifice rendered with extraordinary fleecy detail. The picture, in the Prado, distils Zurbarán's ascetic Sevillian piety into one of the most economical still lifes of the Spanish Baroque.

title: Market Scene on a Quay - Frans Snyders and Workshop
description: A teeming Antwerp quayside laden with game, fish, fruit and live animals, painted on a near three-metre canvas typical of Snyders's grand market series. The Flemish Baroque specialist often collaborated with Rubens on such still-life pageants, and his workshop reproduced the format for aristocratic dining halls.

title: Nativity of St. John the Baptist
description: An interior crowded with attendants tends to the newborn John the Baptist while Elizabeth rests nearby. Gentileschi treats the sacred subject as a domestic event, modelling figures in the warm tenebrist light typical of her Neapolitan period.

title: Rape of Ganymede
description: Rembrandt reimagines the classical myth as a startled, urinating infant snatched skyward by Jupiter's eagle. The unsettling realism breaks sharply with the idealized Italian tradition of the subject.
credit: Cropped from File:Rembrandt - The Abduction of Ganymede - Google Art Project.jpg , originally from Google Art Project.

title: Saint Teresa of Avila's vision of the dove
description: The Carmelite reformer kneels in ecstasy as the Holy Spirit descends in the form of a dove, an episode central to her Vida and to Counter-Reformation devotional propaganda. Rubens renders the moment as a swift, fluid oil sketch built around upward-spiralling drapery and light.

title: Still Life with Fruit
description: The Antwerp specialist piles a Baroque larder with grapes, peaches, dead hare and game birds, animated by a thieving monkey, a wary cat and a darting squirrel. Snyders, Rubens's regular still-life collaborator, treats abundance as theatre, a moralising display of plenty under threat.
credit: Hohenbuchau Collection, on permanent loan to Liechtenstein, The Princely Collections, Vienna

title: The Birth of Venus
description: Venus rises from the sea attended by tritons, nereids and putti in a Baroque treatment of the Anadyomene theme. Poussin organizes the marine cortege into a frieze-like rhythm, marrying Ovidian mythology with the cool classical structure he distilled from antique relief sculpture.

title: The Brazen Serpent
description: Moses raises the bronze serpent on a pole as Israelites writhe with snakebites below, looking up to be healed (Numbers 21). Rubens packs the foreground with anatomical contortions, a Counter-Reformation allegory of salvation through faith in the Crucified.

title: The lamentation over the dead Christ
description: painting ( http://vocab. getty. edu/aat/300177435 ), Anthony van Dyck( https://viaf.
credit: Royal Museum of Fine Arts Antwerp

provenance.collection: Royal Museum of Fine Arts Antwerp
provenance.location: Royal Museum of Fine Arts Antwerp

title: The rape of Europa
description: Quellinus, a close collaborator of Rubens in Antwerp, retells Ovid's myth of Jupiter abducting the Phoenician princess in the guise of a white bull. The composition pairs Flemish Baroque drama with the polished classicism Quellinus absorbed during his Roman training.

title: The Repentant Magdalen
description: The Magdalen sits before a mirror that reflects only a candle and skull, her jewels discarded at her feet. La Tour pares the vanitas iconography to its essentials and lets the single flame model her face and hands with mathematical calm.

title: The Sacrifice of Isaac
description: An angel grasps Abraham's wrist at the instant the knife slips from his hand, while Isaac lies bound and bare-throated beneath him on the altar. Signed and dated 1635, the canvas in the Hermitage was painted for an Amsterdam patron and seizes the most violent split second of the binding, with the blade caught mid-fall.

title: The Surrender of Breda
description: Justin of Nassau hands the keys of the Dutch city to the Genoese general Ambrogio Spinola, who lays a conciliatory hand on the defeated commander's shoulder. The forest of upright Spanish pikes that gives the painting its nickname, Las Lanzas, organises the right half of the composition, painted for the Hall of Realms in the Buen Retiro.

title: A View of Het Steen in the Early Morning
description: Rubens's own country estate near Mechelen lies under a low, golden dawn, with a hunter, hay wagon and far-flung fields stretching to the horizon. The expansive panorama, painted for personal pleasure, helped redirect Northern landscape toward atmospheric naturalism.

title: Adoration of the Magi
description: A Neapolitan-period altarpiece in which the Magi crowd around the Virgin and Child by torchlight. Gentileschi pushes the figures close to the picture plane and stages the gift-giving in heavy raking light, drawing on the Caravaggism she had carried south from Rome.

title: Diana and two nymphs surprised by satyrs while bathing
description: Diana and her companions recoil from leering satyrs at a forest pool in a late mythological invention treating chastity disturbed. Rubens entrusted much of the landscape and animal staffage to specialist collaborators, while reserving the warm, dimpled female nudes for himself.

title: Landscape with a Rainbow
englishTitle: Landscape with Cattle and a Rainbow (Wallace Collection)
description: A broad Flemish countryside opens out under a sky cleared by a passing storm, a rainbow arching over fields, milkmaids and grazing cattle. Often paired with the View of Het Steen, it expresses Rubens's late identification with the land around his country house.
credit: https://wallacelive.wallacecollection.org:443/eMP/eMuseumPlus?service=ExternalInterface&module=collection&objectId=64938&viewType=detailView Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"r/rubens/5landsca/16landsc"

title: Landscape with a Tower
description: A small panel showing a fortified tower set on a wooded rise, approached by a slender bridge under the warm light of a lowering sun. The intimate scale and rapid, fluid brushwork are characteristic of the late landscape sketches Rubens made around his estate at Elewijt.
credit: Objekt in der Onlinesammlung der Staatlichen Museen zu Berlin: 867302 Fotograf: Jörg P. Anders

title: Landscape with Cows
description: Cattle wade through reedy lowland water beneath a wide Flemish sky, the herd dispersed across pasture and ditch. Rubens turned to such polder views in the late 1630s after retiring to his country estate at Het Steen.

title: Mercury and Argus
description: Mercury, sent by Jupiter, lulls the hundred-eyed guardian Argus to sleep with his pipes before drawing his sword. The Ovidian story is staged in a wooded landscape with the white heifer Io tethered to one side.

title: Orpheus and the animals
description: Orpheus charms a menagerie of beasts and birds with his lyre, the Ovidian subject becoming a pretext for Snyders's encyclopaedic display of fur, feather and scale. The composition crowds exotic species into a forested clearing in the Flemish Baroque manner.

title: Saturn
description: The aged god Saturn devours one of his infant sons, biting into the flesh as the child writhes in his grip beneath the cold light of his eponymous planet. Painted for Philip IV's Torre de la Parada, Rubens fuses Ovidian myth with unflinching late-Baroque violence.

title: Silenus
description: The drunken satyr Silenus, tutor of Bacchus, lurches forward supported by his bacchic retinue, his bloated torso pinkly luminous against shadow. Rubens revisits the antique theme with characteristic relish for unidealized flesh and the comic gravity of intoxication.

title: Susanna
description: Rembrandt's small panel catches Susanna at the moment she steps from her robe, glancing back with sudden alarm as the elders emerge from the dark garden. The pearly nude and deep umber surroundings show the painter testing a Lastman-derived biblical mode in the year of Danaë.

title: The Blinding of Samson
description: A violent rendering of Judges 16, with Philistine soldiers pinning Samson while a blade is driven into his eye and Delilah flees with the shorn hair. Rembrandt extracts maximal drama from a sudden shaft of daylight cutting into the cave-like darkness.

title: The creation of the milky way
description: The infant Hercules, set to Juno's breast by Jupiter, draws milk so forcefully that the spilled stream becomes the Milky Way. Painted for Philip IV's Torre de la Parada, the canvas turns an Ovidian etiology into a swirl of cosmic drapery and divine flesh.

title: The Feast of Venus
description: Worshippers garland a statue of Venus while putti, nymphs and satyrs dance in pagan revelry. Inspired by Titian's Worship of Venus and a passage in Philostratus, the late composition assembles Rubens's lifelong vocabulary of mythic celebration.

title: The Massacre of the Innocents - Peter Paul Rubens
englishTitle: The Massacre of the Innocents (Alte Pinakothek, c. 1638)
description: The Massacre of the Innocents - Peter Paul Rubens

title: The Rape of Europe
description: The Phoenician princess clings to the white bull-Jupiter as he wades into the sea bound for Crete, while companions wave helplessly from shore. Painted as a copy after Titian for Philip IV, the canvas pays homage to Venetian color while asserting Rubens's own touch.

title: The Sacrament of Ordination
description: Christ hands the keys of the Church to a kneeling Peter, with the apostles ranged in a measured Roman setting. From Poussin's second series of the Seven Sacraments, the painting translates the institutional moment into the artist's mature, archaeologically informed classicism.

title: A Polish Nobleman
description: A bearded man in furred coat and a tall fur cap, a heavy gold chain across his chest, turning to meet the viewer's eye. Signed and dated 1637, the panel in the National Gallery of Art, Washington, belongs to Rembrandt's series of tronies of sitters in exotic and Eastern European costume rather than to commissioned portraiture.
credit: National Gallery of Art, Washington, D. C., online collection

title: An Elephant
description: A black chalk study of a tame Asian elephant, the wrinkled hide built up with smudged and stumped strokes, trunk curled toward the ground. Signed and dated 1637, the sheet in the Albertina, Vienna, was drawn from Hansken, the celebrated travelling elephant who visited Amsterdam and reappears in Rembrandt's etching The Fall of Man.

title: The abduction of the Sabines
description: Roman soldiers seize the Sabine women at Romulus's signal in a frieze of taut, sculptural figures arrayed before classical architecture. Poussin choreographs the violence with archaeological detail and disciplined gesture, exemplifying the rational French classicism he forged in Rome.

title: The Consequences of War
description: An allegory painted for the Medici and addressed to the disasters of the Thirty Years' War. Mars, dragged forward by a Fury, tramples the arts and a despairing Europe, while Venus tries vainly to restrain him — Rubens's late, politically engaged history painting at its most charged.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"r/rubens/30allego/06allego"

title: As the Old Sing
description: A multi-generational Flemish family bellows around a table while a child blows a pipe, illustrating the proverb inscribed at the top: as the old sing, so the young pipe. Jordaens returned to the boisterous moralised feast many times, this version inscribed Ut genus est genius.

provenance.collection: Department of Paintings of the Louvre

title: Bacchus
description: The young wine god lolls on a bank with a crown of vines, grapes spilling from his hand as putti steady the cup. An undated panel by the Utrecht Mannerist Wtewael, who specialised in small cabinet pictures on copper and oak in which mythological nudes are turned with sinuous elegance against deep landscape vistas.

title: Bull subdued by dogs
description: A bull-baiting scene of the kind de Vos perfected in Rubens's Antwerp circle, with mastiffs lunging at a tethered bull's flanks. The diagonal tangle of muscle, horn and fang demonstrates the Flemish taste for animal combats as showcases of anatomical drama and tonal bravura.

title: Het Pelsken
description: An intimate, near-life-size portrait of Rubens's second wife Helena Fourment, draped only in a fur cloak. The picture's frank sensuality and tender naturalism mark it as a private image, kept in the artist's own household.

title: Landscape with the Good Samaritan
description: An imaginary landscape staging Christ's parable beneath a thunder-bruised sky. Rembrandt favoured these dramatic 'heroic landscapes' in the late 1630s, dwarfing the small figures of the Samaritan and the wounded traveller within ruined towers, stormlight and tonal contrasts that recall Hercules Seghers.

title: Landscape with the Tower of Castle "Steen
description: A panoramic view of the country estate Rubens purchased in 1635, with its turreted manor set among golden Brabant fields. The artist treats native landscape with vigorous brushwork and a low, glowing horizon, anticipating later Romantic vistas.

title: Self-Portrait as the Allegory of Painting
description: Gentileschi merges self-portrait and emblem, depicting herself as the personification of Painting from Ripa's Iconologia: brush raised, gold chain bearing a mask, sleeves pushed back over a working arm. The conceit could only be staged by a woman, since the allegory was female.

title: Selfportrait
description: The painter, near sixty, presents himself in broad-brimmed hat, sword, and gloves — courtier and diplomat as much as artist. The dignified late self-portrait, withholding palette and brushes, asserts his ennoblement and standing among Europe's rulers.

title: The Crucifixion of Saint Peter
description: The apostle is shown crucified upside down at his own request, his contorted, foreshortened body filling a tall altarpiece format. Commissioned for St Peter's Church in Cologne, the work was among the artist's last major altarpieces, completed shortly before his death and dispatched to the parish where his father had once lived.

title: The Judgment of Paris
englishTitle: The Judgement of Paris (late version, c. 1638)
description: Paris awards the golden apple to Venus while Juno and Minerva recoil in defeat, their nudes arranged in a graceful triad against an Arcadian landscape. Rubens revisited this mythological subject several times; the late Prado version is among his most assured.

title: The Raising of the Cross
englishTitle: The Raising of the Cross (modello after the Antwerp triptych, 1638)
description: Straining executioners heave the cross bearing Christ skyward in a violent diagonal of muscular labor. A late reprise of his Antwerp altarpiece, this version concentrates the drama into a tighter, more urgent gathering of bodies and tackle.

title: Virgin with Child and saints
description: Painted as the altarpiece for Rubens's own funerary chapel in St Jacob's Church, Antwerp, the panel surrounds the Virgin and Child with saints in whose features the artist included self-portrait and family likenesses. It is among his last works, executed in the warm, fluid manner of his final Antwerp years.

title: Diana and nymphs attacked by satyrs
description: Diana and her companions, returning from the hunt with hounds and game, are accosted by lecherous satyrs at the edge of a wood. The collision of nude bodies, fur and dead quarry typifies Rubens's late mythological mode.

title: Hercules and the Nemean Lion
description: Hercules grapples the invulnerable Nemean lion in a knot of straining limbs, the hero's first labor reduced to its essential close-quarters violence. The Apsley House version follows a Rubens prototype that translates antique sculptural sources, especially the Belvedere Torso, into Baroque flesh and sinew.

title: Hercules Strangling the Nemean Lion
description: Hercules wraps the invulnerable lion in a strangling embrace, the hero's bunched muscles answered by the beast's twisting flank. The motif derives from antique sarcophagi Rubens had studied in Italy.

title: Naked old man
description: An academic figure study of an aged male model, drawn from life with the meaty corporeality typical of the Antwerp Baroque. Jordaens repeatedly used such studies as a stockpile for the satyrs, river gods, and apostles populating his crowded canvases.

provenance.collection: Department of Prints and Drawings of the Louvre

title: Self-Portrait Leaning on a Stone Sill
description: The painter at thirty-three, in velvet cap and rich furred robe, leans his folded arm on a stone sill that runs across the picture. Signed and dated 1640, the canvas in the National Gallery, London, quotes the pose of Titian's so-called Portrait of Ariosto and Raphael's Castiglione, both then in Amsterdam collections Rembrandt had recently studied.

title: A Female Saint and Martyr
description: A half-length saint, traditionally identified as Catherine of Alexandria by the spiked wheel of her martyrdom. Gentileschi favoured strong-willed female protagonists set against deep shadow, building flesh in luminous Caravaggesque chiaroscuro across a career that spanned Rome, Florence, and Naples.

title: Four Studies of a Head of a Moor
description: Four oil sketches of the same Black sitter, observed from different angles and in varied light, made as working material for finished compositions including the Adoration of the Magi. The studies are notable for their direct, dignified attention to an individual model.

provenance.collection: Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium

title: Portrait of Mary Ruthven
description: A tender likeness of the painter's Scottish wife, posed with a quiet half-smile against a neutral ground. Van Dyck reserves his usual aristocratic finery for a domestic intimacy, the silvery silks softened by his late, more thinly brushed manner.

title: Prometheus Bound
description: Chained to the Caucasus, Prometheus writhes as the eagle of Zeus rends his liver — a punishment renewed each day. Jordaens treats the Titan with brawny, ruddy realism, working in the Rubensian Antwerp idiom of muscular flesh and dramatic chiaroscuro.

title: Rachel de Ruvigny
description: Rachel de Ruvigny, Countess of Southampton, is shown as Fortune perched on a globe, a moralised allegory of worldly mutability much favoured in Caroline court portraiture. Cool blue satins and a still, ovular face are vintage van Dyck.

title: The Dream of Saint Joseph
description: An angel appears to the sleeping Joseph in a candlelit interior, the standard Lorraine nocturne formula put to a religious end. The shielded flame, smooth modelling and quiet psychology are characteristic of La Tour's mature devotional pictures.

title: The Feast of the Bean King
description: A boisterous Twelfth Night feast in which whoever finds the bean in the cake reigns as king while companions roar 'The king drinks!' Jordaens returned to the proverbial subject several times, packing the table with three generations and the wet-eyed comedy of overindulgence.

title: Woman with a Mirror
description: A half-length nude turns toward a mirror held by a maid, her pearly flesh rendered in the warm, fluid manner of Rubens's late period. The composition belongs to a Venetian-derived tradition of the toilette of Venus, transformed here by Flemish opulence.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"r/rubens/30allego/08allego"

title: Scholar at his Writing Table
description: A bearded scholar in fur-trimmed gown stands at a high lectern, quill poised over an open ledger, attention turned to the page. Signed and dated 1641, the canvas in the Royal Castle, Warsaw, is the pendant to A Girl in a Picture Frame and forms one of the few Rembrandt pairs to survive together since their commission.

title: The Girl in a Picture Frame
description: A young woman leans out of a painted frame, her hands resting on the illusory ledge in a sly play on the picture's own boundary. The trompe l'oeil device reflects Rembrandt's interest in animating the threshold between image and viewer.

title: The Windmill
description: An etching of a stoutly built post mill rising above the bastion of an old town wall. Rembrandt's careful drypoint touches give the brickwork, thatch, and surrounding figures a grainy luminosity prized by collectors of his prints.

title: Famille de paysans dans un intérieur
artist: Attributed to Louis Le Nain / Antoine Le Nain
description: A peasant family pauses around a sparse table in a dim cottage interior, each face turned outwards with quiet directness. The Le Nain brothers' rare empathetic treatment of rural poverty, painted in a sober earthen palette, anticipates the realism of Courbet two centuries later.

provenance.collection: Department of Paintings of the Louvre

title: Self-Portrait in a Flat Cap
description: The painter at thirty-six gazes outward in a black flat cap and dark coat with embroidered gold trim, the face lit from the upper left against a neutral ground. RCIN 404120 in the Royal Collection at Windsor, the panel entered the British royal collection under George IV and is among the most sober of Rembrandt's mid-career self-portraits.

title: The Night Watch
description: Captain Frans Banning Cocq in black with red sash steps forward giving the order to march, Lieutenant Willem van Ruytenburch in pale yellow strides beside him, and the company tumbles into motion behind. Signed and dated 1642, the canvas of 363 by 437 cm in the Rijksmuseum is the largest of the Amsterdam civic-guard group portraits.

title: The three trees Alternative title
description: Three trees crown a low rise above a flat Dutch polder, with a thunderstorm rolling in from the left and tiny figures fishing and sketching at the margins. Rembrandt's largest landscape etching combines drypoint and engraving to model an unusually dramatic sky.

title: Daedalus and Icarus
description: Daedalus binds the wax wings to the shoulders of the eager young Icarus, his own face shadowed with foreknowledge of the flight to come. Painted about 1645 and now in the State Hermitage, Saint Petersburg, the canvas is an early work by Le Brun, completed before the long Roman study under Poussin that shaped his mature classicism.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"/l/le_brun/daedalus"

title: Judith and her maid Abra with the Head of Holofernes
description: In the aftermath of the killing, Judith pauses with sword raised while Abra wraps the severed head in a sack. A late Naples-period work, it returns to Gentileschi's signature subject in a quieter, more nocturnal register, lit by a single candle that gilds the drapery.

title: The Mill
description: A windmill stands silhouetted against a turbulent, luminous sky on a high earthen rampart above a quiet river. Long read as a brooding emblem of Dutch identity, the painting fuses topographical record with charged atmosphere.

title: The Rape of Lucretia
description: The Roman matron Lucretia turns the dagger on herself rather than live with dishonour, a subject Gentileschi returned to repeatedly. The compressed half-length composition and raking light typify her late Naples manner, where female protagonists confront violence with stoic resolve.

title: Le Souffleur à la pipe
description: A pipe-smoker leans into his glowing taper, the small flame illuminating cheek, hand and clay bowl against deep shadow. La Tour reduces the genre subject to a meditative still life in light, the kind of intimate nocturne that defines his late Lunéville workshop.

title: Winter Landscape
description: A rare winter landscape in oil, with skaters, a horse-drawn sledge, and low farm buildings beneath a wide pale sky. The thinly brushed surface and silvery palette stand apart from the artist's more familiar dark interiors.

title: Portret van Willem II
description: William II, Prince of Orange, stands in full armour with a commander's baton beside his English wife Mary Stuart on a balcony, both shown full-length. Painted in 1647 for the Stadholder's court, the double portrait belongs to the Rijksmuseum (SK-A-871) and helped fix Honthorst's reputation as the dynasty's preferred image-maker.

title: Susanna and the Elders
description: The chaste Susanna shrinks as the two elders intrude upon her bath, drawn from the Book of Daniel. Rembrandt focuses on her vulnerability and the elders' menace, modeling flesh and drapery with a soft, glowing chiaroscuro.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"r/rembran/painting/biblic1/suzanna"

title: The Sacrifice of Polyxena
description: Polyxena is led to the altar to appease the ghost of Achilles while her mother Hecuba reaches to restrain her and the soldier Neoptolemus lifts his sword. Le Brun painted the subject from Ovid's Metamorphoses in 1647, before his career as premier peintre to Louis XIV.

title: Allegory of Painting
description: A female personification of Painting holds her palette and brushes amid putti and the attributes of the art, set on a low dais. Painted by Boucher in 1765, the year he was appointed Premier Peintre du Roi, the canvas is held by the Smithsonian's National Gallery of Art in Washington.

title: Christ Preaching
description: Christ stands at the centre with the sick crowded to his right and parents pressing children toward him on the left, the dark archway opening onto Lazarus the leper. Known as the Hundred Guilder Print for the unprecedented price it fetched in Rembrandt's lifetime, the etching combines drypoint and engraving to compress several episodes from Matthew 19 into one nocturnal scene.

title: Portrait of Innocent X
description: A famously unflinching state portrait of the pope, whose shrewd, suspicious gaze emerges from a cascade of crimson and white. Velázquez orchestrates a near-monochrome of vermilions and rose tones, using fluid brushwork to render lace, silk and satin with startling immediacy.

title: Susanna and the Elders
englishTitle: Susanna and the Elders (later autograph version)
description: A late treatment of the Book of Daniel episode, with the bathing Susanna recoiling from the two judges who threaten to denounce her. Gentileschi returned to the subject across her career, here in a more restrained, tenebrist key than her early Pommersfelden version.

title: Equestrian portrait of Louis XIV of France
artist: Charles Le Brun / Adam Frans van der Meulen
description: Louis XIV charges forward on a rearing horse in full armour and a flowing red sash, a smoking battlefield receding behind him. The composition was a collaboration between Le Brun, who designed the king and figures, and the Flemish battle painter Van der Meulen, who supplied the landscape and military staffage for the royal commission.

title: Frederik Hendrik
description: Frederick Henry of Orange-Nassau, three years dead at the time of painting, stands at knee-length in burnished armour beside a column. The picture is a posthumous workshop replica from the Honthorst atelier, designed to hang as a pendant to the portrait of his widow Amalia van Solms in the Stadholder's gallery at the Rijksmuseum.

title: Greyhound Catching a Young Wild Boar
description: A lean greyhound seizes a piglet boar in mid-flight across a wooded clearing, captured with the anatomical precision Snyders brought to Rubens's hunt commissions. Slashing brushwork in the foliage and a smoky sky heighten the violent Baroque drama.

title: Juan de Pareja
description: A portrait of Velázquez's enslaved assistant, an artist of Moorish descent whom the painter would soon free. Painted in Rome as a demonstration piece, it stunned contemporaries with its dignified presence, controlled silvery palette, and the assured economy of its brushwork.

title: Landscape with a Calm
description: A serene Italianate landscape with shepherds, livestock and a distant fortified town beneath still water and clear sky. Poussin's late landscapes treat nature as a measured, almost stoic order, with each motif placed for compositional balance rather than picturesque incident.

title: Les reines de Perse aux pieds d'Alexandre dit aussi la tente de Darius
description: The mother, wife and daughters of the defeated Darius prostrate themselves before Alexander and Hephaestion in the Persian camp after Issus. Painted between 1660 and 1661 and shown to Louis XIV at Fontainebleau, the canvas won Le Brun his role as premier peintre and ushered in his cycle of Alexander histories for the Crown.

title: Lying Lioness
description: A lioness rests in profile against a darkened landscape, her tawny coat brushed with the loose, confident strokes Snyders reserved for living animals. The study likely served as a model for the great Antwerp hunt pieces produced with Rubens's workshop.

title: Man in a Ruff
description: A bust-length portrait of a bearded gentleman in the stiff white ruff fashionable in early seventeenth-century Antwerp. The Colchester picture is an after-Rubens version, its frontal pose and economical handling typical of workshop replicas produced for civic and merchant patrons.

title: Narcissus
description: The Antwerp Baroque painter, a pupil of Cornelis de Vos and a follower of Rubens, takes up the Ovidian theme of the youth fixed by his own reflection. The half-length composition turns on a strong oblique light that picks out flesh and stream against deep shadow.
credit: Details of painting at the Prado Museum site Narciso at the Prado

title: Portrait of Amalia van Solms
description: Amalia van Solms, widow of Frederick Henry, stands at knee-length beside a balustrade and column, an olive branch of peace in her right hand. Painted in 1650 as the pendant to her husband's posthumous portrait, the canvas commemorates the Treaty of Münster that ended the Eighty Years' War.

title: San Jerónimo leyendo
description: The Church Father is depicted half-length in a rocky grotto, bare-chested and absorbed in his book, a crucifix steadying his left hand. Murillo treats the penitent scholar with restrained naturalism, the warm Sevillian light modelling weathered skin and beard against a deep brown ground.

title: Self portrait
description: A late self-portrait of the Antwerp master, looking directly out at the viewer with the broad, fleshy modelling he applied to all his sitters. The panel is in the Bavarian State Painting Collections in Munich.

title: The Adoration of the Shepherds
description: Shepherds press forward to venerate the naked Christ Child held by the Virgin, a lamb bound at the foreground as a foreshadowing of sacrifice. The earthy palette and tender, everyday types reflect Murillo's early debt to Ribera and the Spanish naturalist tradition before his manner softened in later years.

title: The boar hunt
description: Hounds tear at a cornered boar in a churning Baroque mêlée, the kind of large hunting piece Snyders supplied with workshop assistance for aristocratic galleries. Sweeping diagonals, splayed limbs and a bruised sky echo the dynamic compositions he had honed beside Rubens.

provenance.collection: Art Gallery of New South Wales
provenance.location: Art Gallery of New South Wales

title: The Holy Family with a Bird
description: Joseph stoops to play with the infant Jesus and a small bird while Mary pauses at her spinning, the goldfinch a traditional emblem of the Passion to come. The domestic warmth and soft chiaroscuro are typical of Murillo's Sevillian devotional pictures, which translated sacred subjects into the rhythms of family life.

title: The Man with the Golden Helmet
description: A bearded soldier in shadow tilts his head down, the entire light of the picture pooled on the embossed gold helmet that gives the work its name. Long catalogued as a Rembrandt at the Gemäldegalerie in Berlin, the painting was reattributed in 1986 to a member of his close circle, though the impasto handling of the gilt remains exceptional.

title: The Shell
description: A rare still life from Rembrandt's etched oeuvre, depicting a single cone shell (Conus marmoreus) rendered with delicate cross-hatching and drypoint burr. The print attests to the Dutch fascination with exotic naturalia gathered through global trade.

title: The Triumph of Bacchus
description: A Flemish baroque procession of Bacchus and Ariadne, with putti, satyrs, and tipsy revellers wreathed in vine. De Vos, best known for his crisp portraits of Antwerp burghers, here works closer to Rubens's mythological idiom, ordering the throng with broad, ruddy modelling.

title: Triumphant Cupid among Emplems of Art and War
artist: Thomas Willeboirts Bosschaert / Paul de Vos
description: Cupid sits in triumph atop instruments of art, science and war, a Baroque allegory of love's universal sway. Willeboirts Bosschaert painted the figures and de Vos the still-life trophies, reflecting the seventeenth-century Antwerp practice of collaborative specialization.

title: Two young seals on the shore
description: Two young harbor seals lie on a stretch of Flemish shoreline, painted with the close observation of fur, hide, and salt-damp sand for which the de Vos workshop was prized. The Antwerp painter built his career on Baroque animal subjects, often supplying livestock and game for collaborators including Rubens.

provenance.collection: Musée des Beaux-Arts et d'Archéologie de Besançon
provenance.location: Musée des Beaux-Arts et d'Archéologie de Besançon

title: Stormy Landscape with Pyramus and Thisbe
description: Storm clouds boil over a vast Italianate landscape as the Ovidian lovers meet their tragedy beside a reflective lake. Poussin uses meteorological drama to magnify human catastrophe, with sheet lightning, fleeing horses and bowed trees orchestrated into a single classical machine.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"p/poussin/4/38landsc"

title: The Kitchen Maid
description: A young woman leans on a stone windowsill, her arms folded, gazing out at the viewer in warm reds, browns and ochres. Signed and dated 1651, the half-length is now in the Nationalmuseum in Stockholm and is thought to depict a member of Rembrandt's own household rather than a hired model.

title: Large Self Portrait
description: Rembrandt presents himself at forty-six in a dark cloak and skullcap, hands folded in front of him, gazing out with composed gravity. Painted in 1652 and now in the Kunsthistorisches Museum in Vienna, the canvas marks the moment his Amsterdam fortunes had begun to turn but before bankruptcy forced the inventory of 1656.

title: Margaretha Maria de Roodere
description: Margaretha Maria de Roodere stands at her easel painting a portrait while her parents look on from either side, framing her practice within the family. Honthorst signed and dated the picture in 1652, recording his sitter as one of the few documented women painters working in Utrecht in the mid-seventeenth century.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"h/honthors/2/13rooder"

title: Mercury and Argus
description: An engraving after Jordaens showing Mercury raising his sword above the slumbering hundred-eyed giant Argus, with Io transformed into a cow at the left. The print belongs to the wide diffusion of Jordaens' mythologies through reproductive engraving, here cataloged in Hollstein as Dutch 7.

title: Psyche receives the cup of immortality on the Olympus
description: On Olympus, Psyche is offered the cup of immortality that will allow her marriage to Cupid, attended by an assembly of gods. Jordaens stages the Apuleian fable with his characteristic warm palette and tightly clustered, bench-front composition.

title: Triumph of Frederick Henry
description: An allegorical celebration of the Dutch stadtholder Frederick Henry, painted for the Oranjezaal at Huis ten Bosch. Jordaens orchestrates a swirling Baroque cavalcade of personifications, captives, and trophies in the Rubensian Antwerp manner, glorifying the prince's military and political triumphs.

title: Aristotle with a Bust of Homer
description: The philosopher Aristotle, in black robes and a gold chain bearing a portrait of Alexander, lays his hand on a marble bust of Homer. Commissioned in 1653 by the Sicilian collector Don Antonio Ruffo for 500 florins, the canvas was the first painting of a series the patron assembled around the philosopher and now hangs at the Metropolitan Museum.

title: A View of Delft after the Explosion of 1654
description: A topographical record of the gunpowder explosion that levelled a quarter of Delft on 12 October 1654, killing van der Poel's own daughter. The artist made the catastrophe his recurring subject, painting smouldering rubble, broken roofs and bewildered survivors with documentary specificity.
credit: Transfered from nl.wikipedia; -; National Gallery, London - online catalogue

title: Bathsheba with David's letter
description: Bathsheba sits naked after her bath, holding the letter from King David that summons her to him, her old servant drying her feet at the side. Signed and dated 1654, the canvas in the Louvre uses the body of Rembrandt's companion Hendrickje Stoffels for the biblical heroine caught between duty and complicity.

title: Christ in the House of Martha and Mary
description: Vermeer's largest known painting and a rare history piece, made early in his career before he turned to domestic interiors. Christ gestures toward the seated, attentive Mary while Martha presents a basket of bread; the broad handling and warm reds anticipate the artist's mature poise.

title: A Woman bathing in a Stream
description: A woman in a thin white shift lifts the hem above her knees as she wades into a dark stream, rich brocade and red garments piled on the bank. Painted on a small oak panel in 1655 and signed in the lower right, the picture in the National Gallery is rendered in startlingly free, loaded brushwork that anticipates Rembrandt's late style.

title: Christ presented to the people: the oblong plate
description: An etching, in its later state, of Pilate presenting the bound Christ to a crowd that demands his crucifixion. Rembrandt scraped away the foreground onlookers and replaced them with shadowed arches, intensifying the confrontation between judge and viewer.

title: Pallas Athena
description: A figure in gleaming helmet and gorget, traditionally identified as the goddess of wisdom and war. Rembrandt models the armour with thick, gilded impasto against deep shadow, a hallmark of his late chiaroscuro.

title: The Polish Rider
description: A young horseman in Eastern European costume rides through a twilit landscape on a pale mount, bow and sabre at his side, a fortified hill rising behind him. Acquired by Henry Clay Frick in 1910 from the Polish Dzialynski family, the canvas remains one of Rembrandt's most debated late works, its identity oscillating between portrait, allegory and historical type.

title: Jacob Blessing Ephraim and Manasseh
description: Aged Jacob, propped on his deathbed, crosses his arms to lay his right hand on the younger Ephraim while Joseph tries to redirect it, his wife Asenath watching at the side. Signed and dated 1656, the canvas in Schloss Wilhelmshöhe at Kassel reframes the Genesis scene as a tender domestic gathering rather than a formal blessing.

title: Portrait of Hendrickje Stoffels
description: Hendrickje Stoffels, Rembrandt's common-law wife after Saskia's death, appears at half-length in dark warm browns, a fur-trimmed garment opening at the neck. Painted around 1656, the year of his bankruptcy, the picture in the Gemäldegalerie at Berlin is one of several intimate portraits Rembrandt made of the woman who managed the household with his son Titus.

title: The anatomy lesson of Dr. Joan Deijman
description: A foreshortened cadaver lies on the dissection table while Dr Joan Deijman, his hands shown above, performs an autopsy on the brain. Painted in 1656 for the Amsterdam Surgeons' Guild as a sequel to the Tulp anatomy of 1632, most of the canvas was destroyed by fire in 1723; only the central fragment survives in the Amsterdam Museum.

title: The Maids of Honour
description: The Spanish court group portrait centred on the Infanta Margarita, her maids and dwarves, with Velázquez himself at the easel and the king and queen reflected in a distant mirror. The picture is a sustained meditation on vision, painted for Philip IV and now the cornerstone of the Prado.
credit: The Prado in Google Earth: Home - 7 th level of zoom, JPEG compression quality: Photoshop 8.

title: Girl Reading a Letter at an Open Window
description: An early interior in which a young woman reads at a leaded casement, her face echoed in the panes. Recent restoration at the Gemäldegalerie in Dresden uncovered a painted Cupid on the back wall that had been overpainted after Vermeer's death, sharpening the picture's amorous subtext.

title: Self-portrait
description: A self-portrait from the artist's later years, in which he sits frontally with a mahlstick and palette implied by his pose. Broad, loaded brushwork records a lined face that meets the viewer with sober self-knowledge.

title: The Wine Glass
description: A genteel courtship scene in which a man waits attentively while a young woman drains a roemer of wine. The stained-glass roundel at the upper window depicts Temperance with bridle and square, an emblem ironically warning against the very excess being staged below.

title: View of Houses in Delft
description: A modest stretch of Delft brickwork, with figures absorbed in domestic chores in a doorway and an alley. One of only two surviving cityscapes by Vermeer, the picture distills the painter's quiet attention to weathered surface, mortar, and clouded northern light.

title: Figure Studies
description: Drawing; Drawings

title: Self-portrait
description: A late self-portrait in which the painter sits with hands folded, dressed in a heavy gold-trimmed robe and dark cap. The frank, unflattering record of his own ageing has come to define how subsequent centuries imagine the artist.

title: Rembrandt’s Son Titus in a Monk’s Habit
description: Rembrandt's son Titus, then about nineteen, is shown in the brown habit and rope girdle of a Franciscan friar, his face emerging from the cowl in golden light. Painted in 1660 and now at the Rijksmuseum, the picture casts the young man as a saint, probably Francis of Assisi, in the genre of the tronie rather than as an actual portrait of religious vocation.

title: Self-portrait
description: Rembrandt at fifty-four faces the viewer in a dark cap and brown jerkin, the face built up in thick, scraped layers of paint. Signed and dated 1660 and now in the Louvre, the canvas was painted the year he left his bankrupt house on the Jodenbreestraat for a smaller dwelling on the Rozengracht.

title: The Chancelor Séguier
description: Chancellor Pierre Séguier rides under a parasol carried by six pages, his ceremonial red robes spreading across the canvas in a Venetian procession of horses and finery. Painted between 1660 and 1661 and now in the Louvre, the picture was Le Brun's homage to the patron who had funded his Italian studies and secured his appointment as premier peintre.

title: The Milkmaid
description: A sturdy kitchen maid pours a thin stream of milk into an earthenware bowl, the room hushed by daylight from a leaded window. Vermeer's pointillé highlights flicker on bread crusts and copper, and the lapis-derived blue of her apron exemplifies his costly pigment habits.
credit: Google Arts & Culture — AHrw. Z3. Av6. Zhjg 9. AHrw. Z3. Av6. Zhjg

title: View of Delft
dateCreated: between circa 1660 and circa 1661 Baroque (late 16 th century –1750s )
description: A panorama of the artist's home city seen across the Schie, rendered with the peculiar optical fidelity for which he is celebrated. Pinpoint dabs of impasto on the boats and roofs, possibly studied via a camera obscura, mimic the glint of refracted morning light.

title: St. Bartholomew
description: The apostle holds the knife of his martyrdom and turns aside in pensive reflection. Painted late in Rembrandt's career, the figure is built from rough, palpable strokes that give the saint the weathered weight of a real man.

title: The Conspiracy of the Batavians under Claudius Civilis
description: The surviving central fragment of Rembrandt's largest history painting, commissioned for Amsterdam's new Town Hall. Civilis raises a sword in a one-eyed oath-taking with his Batavian rebels — a coarsely lit, almost barbaric image that the city soon rejected.

title: The evangelist Matthew and the angel
description: The evangelist pauses over his manuscript as an angel leans in to whisper at his ear. Rembrandt models both faces with a quiet warmth, treating divine inspiration as an intimate exchange.

title: The Lute Player
description: A young man tunes his lute in a quiet Rotterdam interior, a music sheet open before him. Sorgh, a pupil of Teniers and Buytewech, specialised in such genteel domestic genre scenes, building tone with a warm brown ground beneath crisp local colour.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"s/sorgh/luteplay"

title: Gerard Honthorst - gulden cabinet
description: Engraved portrait of Gerard van Honthorst published in 1662 in Cornelis de Bie's Het Gulden Cabinet der edel vry schilder const, the Antwerp directory of painters. Pieter de Jode II cut the plate after a Honthorst self-portrait, with the print issued by Joannes Meyssens for an entry that placed the Utrecht master among the leading Northern painters of his century.
credit: Het gulden cabinet vande edel vry schilder const , online facsimile version in Google books, p.165

title: Alexander Entering Babylon
description: Alexander the Great rides into Babylon in a triumphal chariot drawn by white elephants, the city's defeated populace strewing the path with gold and burning incense before him. Painted between 1664 and 1665 as part of the Alexander cycle for Louis XIV, the canvas hangs in the Louvre and inspired Le Brun's tapestry designs at the Gobelins manufactory.

title: A Lady Writing
description: A young woman in a yellow ermine-trimmed jacket pauses at her writing table, lifting her gaze toward the viewer, an ink pot and pearl jewellery at her hand. Painted around 1665 and now in the National Gallery of Art in Washington, the small panel is one of Vermeer's most intimate evocations of the moment of address from writer to absent reader.

title: Girl with a Pearl Earring
description: A tronie rather than a portrait: an anonymous young woman turns over her shoulder, lips parted, against a deep glazed-black ground. Vermeer reserves his most expensive pigments, ultramarine and lead-tin yellow, for the turban, and renders the famous teardrop earring with two soft dabs of lead white. In the Mauritshuis, The Hague.

title: Portrait of a couple as figures from the Old Testament
description: Long known as The Jewish Bride, the painting shows a couple in tender embrace, often identified with Old Testament pairs such as Isaac and Rebecca. Built up with thickly trowelled pigment, the gold sleeve and ruby skirt are among Rembrandt's most celebrated passages of paint.

title: Rest on the Flight into Egypt
description: The Holy Family pauses on its journey into Egypt, Mary cradling the sleeping Christ Child while Joseph watches over them and the donkey grazes nearby. Now in the Hermitage, the picture exemplifies Murillo's mature estilo vaporoso, in which figures emerge from a hazy, golden atmosphere with notably softened contours.

title: Lucretia
description: Lucretia stands in a white shift stained with blood, a dagger in one hand and a bell pull in the other, her eyes lowered in the moment after the self-inflicted wound. Signed and dated 1666, the canvas at the Minneapolis Institute of Art was the second and more restrained of Rembrandt's two paintings of the Roman heroine.
credit: Minneapolis Institute of Arts, online collection

title: The Art of Painting
dateCreated: circa from 1666 until 1668 Baroque (late 16 th century –1750s )
description: An allegory of painting in which an artist seen from behind sets brush to a portrait of Clio, the muse of history, identified by her trumpet and laurel. Vermeer kept the canvas in his Delft studio until his death, and the heavy map of the Seventeen Provinces above the model carries political weight.

title: Charles Le Brun La Colère
description: Sheet from the Méthode pour apprendre à dessiner les passions, showing the face of Anger with brows drawn together, nostrils flared and teeth bared. Le Brun's 1668 lecture at the Académie Royale built a Cartesian taxonomy of emotion for painters, and the engraved sheets circulated in artist pattern books well into the nineteenth century.

title: The Astronomer
description: A scholar in a long robe leans over a celestial globe, his hand brushing its surface as if to set the cosmos turning. Painted as a pendant to The Geographer, the picture reflects Delft's culture of empirical inquiry, its still light and book-strewn study tuned to quiet concentration.

provenance.collection: Department of Paintings of the Louvre

title: The Geographer
description: The companion piece to The Astronomer, showing a scholar with dividers paused over a chart, a terrestrial globe behind him. Vermeer drapes the figure in an exotic Japonse rok, framing seventeenth-century Dutch knowledge-making as a contemplative, light-filled pursuit.

title: The Return of the Prodigal Son
description: The ragged son kneels before his aged father, who lays trembling hands on the bowed shoulders while elder figures watch from the shadowed background. Painted in Rembrandt's final years around 1668, the canvas now hangs in the Hermitage, its thick impasto and warm umber light marking the late style of his last decade in Amsterdam.

title: The lacemaker
description: The smallest of Vermeer's surviving paintings, focusing tightly on a young woman bent over her bobbins and pins. Threads of red and white spill from a cushion in molten blurs that anticipate optical photography, while her concentrated face is rendered with the artist's signature stillness.

provenance.collection: Department of Paintings of the Louvre

title: Santa Rosa de Lima
description: The first canonised saint of the Americas kneels in the white and black habit of a Dominican tertiary, gazing on the Christ Child seated on a cushion above her workbasket. Murillo presents the Limeña mystic with the gentle sweetness and silvery half-light that defined his late religious painting.

title: Woman Writing a Letter
description: A seated lady drafts a letter at a draped table while her standing maid waits, glancing toward a sunlit window. Vermeer constructs the interior with his characteristic geometry of floor tiles, parallel walls, and a hanging picture, weaving the small domestic event into a quietly orchestrated study of light and waiting.
credit: Derived from National Gallery of Ireland

title: Alexander and Porus
description: The wounded Indian king Porus is brought before Alexander the Great after the Battle of the Hydaspes, his tall figure refusing prostration. Le Brun painted the scene in 1673 as part of his cycle on the conquests of Alexander, commissioned by Louis XIV to flatter the Sun King by historical parallel.

title: Still Life with Servant
artist: Paul de Vos / Possibly Cornelis de Vos
description: A monumental Flemish pronk still life heaped with fruit, game and silver, attended by a servant figure likely contributed by a collaborating figure painter. The composition exemplifies the Antwerp specialty of combining a Snyders-school animal painter with a portraitist for sumptuous decorative ensembles.

title: Capture of the city and citadel of Gand in six days
description: Louis XIV reviews the rapid surrender of Ghent in March 1678, his cavalry drawn up before the captured citadel during the Franco-Dutch War. Le Brun designed the composition between 1681 and 1684 as one of the painted panegyrics intended for the Galerie des Glaces programme at Versailles.

title: Portrait of Charles Le Brun
description: The First Painter to the King sits at his easel with palette and brushes, gesturing toward a canvas of his own equestrian compositions. Largilliere painted the homage between 1683 and 1686, late in Le Brun's life, recording the man who had directed the Academie royale and the Gobelins manufactory under Colbert.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"l/largilli/le_brun"

title: Democritus
description: The laughing philosopher of Abdera turns from his open book, a bony skull and globe at his elbow indicating his meditations on human folly. Coypel painted the bust-length allegory in 1692, treating the Greek thinker in the Caravaggesque half-light then fashionable for half-figures of antique sages.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"/c/coypel/antoine/democrit"

title: La famille Laffite
description: A group portrait of the Laffite family by the leading court painter of Louis XIV. Rigaud's studio specialised in elaborate full-length likenesses of French nobility, with rich drapery, polished flesh tones and carefully posed sitters that established the visual vocabulary of Bourbon state portraiture.

provenance.collection: Department of Paintings of the Louvre

title: Susannah accused of adultery
description: Susannah stands draped before the council of Israel while the two elders point in false accusation, the young Daniel rising to interrogate them. Coypel painted the Book of Daniel episode between 1695 and 1696, the smooth modelling and theatrical gesture already pointing toward the early Rococo.

title: Albinus skeleton w less muscles
description: A plate from Bernhard Siegfried Albinus's Tabulae sceleti et musculorum corporis humani (Leiden, 1747), engraved by Jan Wandelaar. The skeleton is set in a poetic landscape with a rhinoceros, marrying anatomical exactitude to Enlightenment-era pictorial staging.
credit: Historical Medical Books at the Claude Moore Health Sciences Library, University of Virginia

title: Albinus skeleton w muscles
description: Another plate from Albinus's Tabulae sceleti et musculorum, in which Wandelaar layers the superficial muscles over the skeleton in a posed standing figure. The series was prized for its proportional accuracy, achieved with grids and double-perspective drafting unusual for medical illustration of the period.
credit: Historical Medical Books at the Claude Moore Health Sciences Library, University of Virginia

title: Anatomy
englishTitle: Skeleton, back view, with left arm extended (Scotin after Albinus, 1747)
description: Anatomy Iconographic Collections Keywords: Bernhard Siegfried Albinus; G. Scotin; Bernhard Siegfried 1697-1770. Albinus

title: Anatomy
englishTitle: Standing skeleton, side view, with left arm extended (Ravenet after Albinus, 1747)
description: Anatomy Iconographic Collections Keywords: Bernhard Siegfried Albinus; Simon Frangois Ravenet; Bernhard Siegfried 1697-1770. Albinus

title: Anatomy
englishTitle: Écorché figure, front view, with rhinoceros in the background (Grignion after Albinus, 1747)
description: Anatomy Iconographic Collections Keywords: Bernhard Siegfried Albinus; Charles Grignion; Bernhard Siegfried 1697-1770. Albinus

title: Self Portrait in a Turban
description: Rigaud, the great portraitist of Louis XIV's court, presents himself in an exotic turban, a studio prop conveying artistic vanity and learned cosmopolitanism. The lustrous fabrics and confident chiaroscuro foreshadow the polished grandeur he would soon bring to royal portraiture.

title: Diana and Her Dog
