description: The huntress goddess pauses at rest, half-draped, with her hound pressed against her side and quiver beside her. Ricci handles the mythological subject with the airy palette and rococo grace that bridge late Venetian Baroque and the eighteenth century.

title: Susannah and the Elders
description: The chaste Susanna twists away from two leering elders who corner her at her bath, the apocryphal subject a favorite vehicle for the female nude. Chiari, a pupil of Carlo Maratta, paints in a late-Roman Baroque idiom of cool flesh tones and theatrical gesture.
credit: Walters Art Museum : Home page Info about artwork

title: Portrait of Louis XIV
description: The Sun King at sixty-three, draped in ermine and blue velvet fleurs-de-lis, his bewigged head turned over a leg cocked in a courtly dance pose. Rigaud's state portrait set the template for European royal imagery, multiplied across embassies and palaces in countless studio replicas.

title: Kaigetsudo Ando - Standing Portrait of a Courtesan
description: A Yoshiwara courtesan stands alone in a richly patterned kimono, hip cocked in the languid S-curve that became the workshop's hallmark. As founder of the Kaigetsudō school, Ando concentrated entirely on monumental beauties, painted in fluid ink with broad swathes of color and gold on paper.

title: Matteo Ripa001 - Morning Glow on the Western Ridge
englishTitle: Morning Glow on the Western Ridge, from Thirty-six Views of the Imperial Summer Resort at Chengde
description: A copperplate view of the Kangxi Emperor's summer retreat at Chengde, with mist breaking over the western ridge in fine engraved hatching. Ripa, a Neapolitan missionary at the Qing court, produced the imperial album that introduced Western intaglio printing techniques to China.
credit: Scan from "New Visions at the Ch'ing Court"

title: Portrait of Herman Petersen
description: The Swedish merchant Herman Petersen sits in a dark coat against a neutral ground, the soft pastel medium giving his face a powdery bloom. Lundberg trained in Paris under Boucher and the pastellist Rosalba Carriera before returning to Stockholm to become the most sought-after portraitist at the court of Adolf Frederick.

title: KIYONOBU-Yamanaka-Ichikawa-1714
description: Two kabuki actors square off in a confrontational pose typical of aragoto bravura roles. Kiyonobu, founder of the Torii line of theatre artists, defined the early ukiyo-e print with bold contour lines and the hand-applied tan-e orange-red pigment characteristic of pre-polychrome woodblock work.

title: Self portrait of Antoine Coypel
description: Coypel turns toward the viewer in a powdered wig and dark coat, the painter aged into the senior office of First Painter to the King. The self-portrait dates to 1715, the year before his death, when he had been directing the Academie royale and the royal painting collections under Louis XIV.

title: KorinsScreen
description: A pair of folding screens depicting the rocky pine-clad islets of Matsushima Bay, with stylised waves curling in gold-leaf and malachite green. Kōrin, leading master of the Rinpa school, treats the famed scenic site as flat decorative pattern rather than topographic record.
credit: Ogata Kōrin's Waves at Matsushima, public domain from the Smithsonian Museum of Asian Art

title: Man Resting in the Lap of a Woman
description: A reclining man sleeps with his head pillowed against a woman's lap, her hand still resting on his temple. Coypel painted the small intimate scene around 1716, near the end of his life, the loose handling and pastoral mood already prefiguring the fetes galantes of Watteau.

title: Venus and Satyr
description: A reclining Venus, attended by putti, is approached by a leering satyr in a confection of soft pinks, blues, and silver greys. Ricci's eroticized mythology helped translate the Venetian tradition of Veronese into a lighter rococo idiom.

title: Pilgrimage to Cythera
description: Lovers prepare to leave the island of Venus in golden afternoon light, a melancholic departure rather than the arrival the title might suggest. Watteau's reception piece for the Académie royale invented the genre of the fête galante, with feathery brushwork drawn from his study of Rubens.
credit: Retouched from File:L'Embarquement pour Cythere, by Antoine Watteau, from C2RMF.jpg , originally C2RMF: Galerie de tableaux en très haute définition : image page

provenance.collection: Department of Paintings of the Louvre

title: Nymphe de fontaine
description: A reclining nymph leans on her urn beside a flowing stream in a wooded glade. The drawing's soft contours and pastoral setting prefigure the Arcadian fete galante imagery for which Watteau would soon become known.
credit: reproarte.com; Sotheby's New York, 26 January 2012, lot 63

title: Portrait of Charles de Geer
description: Pastel portrait of the Swedish industrialist and entomologist Friherre Charles de Geer, shown in coat and powdered wig against a neutral ground. Lundberg, court painter in Stockholm after a long apprenticeship in Paris under Boucher and La Tour, built his reputation on exactly these intimate pastel likenesses of Sweden's eighteenth-century aristocracy.

title: Portrait of Marie Anne de Bourbon
description: Marie Anne de Bourbon-Conde sits in court dress, her powdered coiffure dressed with pearls and a small lace fontange. Lundberg made the 1720 pastel after a painted prototype by Jean-Baptiste Santerre, the Parisian portraitist whose flattering formulae he carried back into Swedish court fashion.

title: Portrait of Cardinal Guillaume Dubois
description: Dubois, tutor to the future Louis XV and chief minister under the Regent, sits enveloped in a voluminous wrap of scarlet silk topped by a short fur cape. Rigaud channels the swagger of Louis XIV-era state portraiture into a study of ecclesiastical and political power, the textiles handled with the sumptuous fluency that made him the Bourbon court's favoured face-maker.

title: Le Peintre dans son atelier
description: The painter sits in shirtsleeves at his easel, brush poised over a canvas, with prints and plaster casts arranged in the cluttered studio behind. Boucher painted the small genre piece between 1730 and 1735, in the years immediately after his return from Rome, where he had studied at the French Academy.

title: La Continence de Scipion
description: The Roman general Scipio refuses the captive Iberian princess offered as spoils of war, gesturing for her return to her betrothed Allucius. Pittoni painted the moral exemplum in 1733, one of many Venetian treatments of the Livy episode in the pale, sweetened palette he favoured.

title: Farinelli
description: The castrato Carlo Broschi, known as Farinelli, stands in court dress with the music for one of his operatic arias in hand. Nazari painted the portrait in 1734, during Farinelli's London seasons at the Opera of the Nobility, and the canvas now hangs in the Royal College of Music.

title: Venus asks Vulcan for Weapons for his Son Aeneas
description: Venus leans toward Vulcan in his forge to plead for arms for her son Aeneas, the Cyclopes labouring at the anvil behind. Submitted as the painter's morceau de réception to the Académie Royale in 1734, the picture is a polished demonstration of the decorative Rococo mythology Natoire would soon deploy at Versailles.

title: The Triumph of Bacchus; oil on canvas
description: An exuberant Rococo procession of the wine god, attended by satyrs, maenads and tumbling putti amid garlands and overturned vessels. Natoire animates the mythological subject with feathery brushwork and pearled flesh tones characteristic of the French eighteenth century court taste.

title: Nishikawa Sukenobu
description: Sixteenth page of the Ehon Asakayama by Japanese artist Sukenobu
credit: Hillier, J : The Art of the Japanese Book London : Sotheby's Publications, 1987, pp. 158–173.

title: Louis XV
description: Louis XV is shown in armour beneath the blue sash of the Order of the Holy Spirit, his wig tightly curled in the high court fashion of the late 1730s. Lundberg drew the king in pastel around 1740, the portrait once attributed to Louis-Michel van Loo before research reassigned it to the Swedish pastellist working in Paris.

title: Pinacoteca Querini Stampalia - Angelo Maria Querini - Bartolomeo Nazari
englishTitle: Portrait of Cardinal Angelo Maria Querini
description: Cardinal Angelo Maria Querini in red moiré watered silk, holding a book in his Paduan study. Bartolomeo Nazari painted the Venetian-born cardinal and bibliophile around 1740; the portrait hangs in the Pinacoteca Querini Stampalia in Venice, founded on the family library Querini helped enlarge.

title: The Rebuke of Adam and Eve
description: Adam and Eve are driven from Eden by an admonishing angel in this Rococo treatment of Genesis. Natoire softens the moralizing subject with flowing draperies, pastel colour and graceful attitudes drawn from his work as director of the French Academy in Rome.

title: The Triumph of Venus
description: Venus Anadyomene

title: Portrait of François Boucher
dateCreated: Reception piece for the Académie royale de peinture presented on January 28, 1741.
description: Boucher turns from his easel with palette in hand, the painter at the height of his Parisian career. Lundberg presented the pastel as his reception piece to the Academie royale de peinture on 28 January 1741, the work that secured his admission as an academician.

title: La Foire chinoise
description: Figures in fanciful Eastern dress mingle at a market under bamboo awnings, monkeys and exotic birds scattered through the stalls. Boucher designed the canvas around 1742 as part of his chinoiserie cycle for the Beauvais tapestry manufactory, where the cartoons supplied a long-running suite of woven panels.

title: La Pêche chinoise
description: Anglers in pagoda hats cast their lines from a delicate wooden bridge while attendants prepare baskets on the bank. Boucher painted the piece around 1742 as another panel of the Beauvais chinoiserie cycle, his fantasy China assembled from imported porcelains and traveller's prints rather than direct observation.

title: Leda and the Swan
description: Leda reclines on a riverbank as the swan presses against her thigh, a companion nymph half-turning behind her. Boucher painted the 1742 mythology in a pale, sugared palette and the canvas now hangs at the Los Angeles County Museum of Art.

title: Clayton Jones
description: The Welsh sitter Clayton Jones is shown half-length in a brown coat, with the soft rural foliage of a parkland background just visible behind. Gainsborough painted the portrait between 1744 and 1745, during his early London years before he moved his practice to Ipswich.

title: en
description: A wooded Suffolk lane opens onto pasture with grazing cattle and a distant church tower under heavy English cloud. Gainsborough painted the canvas between 1746 and 1750, during the early years he spent at Sudbury where the flat East Anglian countryside shaped his lifelong landscape vocabulary.

title: A skeleton
description: Iconographic Collections

title: Cornard Wood
description: An early woodland scene from Gainsborough's Suffolk years, made before he turned full-time to portrait commissions in Bath and London. Drawing on Dutch landscape models, particularly Ruisdael, he threads a sandy track through scrubby oaks under a broken English sky.

title: Mr. and Mrs. Andrews
dateCreated: between 1748 and 1750 Romanticism (second half of 18 th century –first half of 19 th century )
description: A double portrait of a young Suffolk landowner and his bride seated at the edge of their estate, the rolling cornfields and oak deliberately presented as part of their identity. The crisp early style fuses French rococo elegance with topographical precision unusual in English portraiture.

title: Orchids
description: A literati-style study of orchids in ink on paper, drawn with the calligraphic spontaneity that defined Ike no Taiga's Nanga painting. The plant's sparse leaves and blossoms are set down in a few rapid strokes, a Confucian emblem of refined virtue rendered with Edo-period painterly freedom.

title: Portrait of Alexandrine Le Normant d'Étiolles
description: The young Alexandrine Le Normant d'Etiolles holds a goldfinch on a tethered thread, daughter of Madame de Pompadour by an earlier marriage. The picture, attributed to Boucher and dated 1749, was painted during the years when the painter served as Pompadour's favourite portraitist and decorator.

title: Blind-Man’s Buff
description: A blindfolded girl gropes through tall grass after her companion in an overgrown garden of luxuriant trees and tumbled stonework. Painted by Fragonard as a teenage pupil in Boucher's atelier, the canvas pairs with The See-Saw (Thyssen-Bornemisza) as a courtship pendant for Baron Saint-Julien.

title: Death of Sophonisba
description: The Carthaginian noblewoman receives the cup of poison sent by Masinissa, surrounded by attendants as she chooses suicide over Scipio's Roman triumph. Pittoni, a founding member of the Venetian Academy in 1750, treats the Livy episode with the pale flesh and silver-grey palette typical of his late Rococo manner.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"/p/pittoni/sophonis"

title: Harunobu 2 Pers
description: A pair of figures in the slender, doll-like proportions Harunobu favoured, set within a softly muted interior. He was the pioneer of full-colour nishiki-e printing in 1760s Edo, shifting ukiyo-e away from hand-tinted limited palettes toward layered woodblock impressions.

title: Landscape with Stream and Weir
description: A wooded riverbank with a low weir, painted in Gainsborough's Suffolk period after his return from London to Sudbury and Ipswich. The canvas, now at the Yale Center for British Art, was acquired by the dealer Panton Betew and engraved in 1764, after which it was cut down on the left to its present near-square shape.

title: Old man in an eastern attire
description: A bearded sitter in a fur-trimmed coat and oriental headdress, painted in the half-length tronie format the Venetians adopted from Rembrandt and his Dutch followers. Bartolomeo Nazari worked mainly as a portraitist in Venice, where wealthy Grand Tourists prized such picturesque character studies as ornaments for the gallery wall.

title: Portrait of Juliana Dorotea Henck
description: A Swedish sitter in powdered hair and pink-trimmed gown, around the time of her 1750 marriage to the mill owner Vilhelm Schröder. Lundberg trained for two decades in Paris under Boucher's circle before returning to Stockholm as court portraitist, importing the French pastel manner that made him the leading Rococo portraitist in Sweden.

title: Sketch for a Portrait of Madame de Pompadour
description: An oil sketch of the king's official mistress standing before a mirror, holding her hat. Boucher worked up the small panel as a study for one of the full-length state portraits he produced for Madame de Pompadour, his principal patron for nearly two decades. The sketch entered the Rothschild collection and is now at Waddesdon Manor.

title: The See-Saw
description: Two young lovers play on a plank-and-log seesaw beneath a sweeping willow, the girl's skirts flaring with the motion. Painted around 1750-52 as the pendant to Blind Man's Buff (Toledo Museum of Art), the canvas was commissioned by Baron Saint-Julien while Fragonard was still in Boucher's studio and now hangs in the Museo Thyssen-Bornemisza in Madrid.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"f/fragonar/father/1/021swing"

title: Woman Admiring Plum Blossoms at Night
description: A young woman holds a paper lantern up to a flowering plum branch in the snow, the colour-printed surface tuned to soft greys and blacks. Harunobu was the first ukiyo-e artist to exploit the full nishiki-e palette, and the quiet nocturne is a showcase for it.

title: The Bridge
description: A pastoral with figures crossing a wooden bridge over a stream, the trees and ruined masonry arranged in the manner Boucher adapted from Claude Lorrain. The 1751 canvas keeps the Rococo formula of small shepherd figures lodged in a luxuriant decorative landscape, a type Boucher repeated throughout the 1750s for the Parisian and court market.

title: The Toilet of Venus
description: Venus is attended by three putti among rich silks, pearls, and roses, in a panel originally set into the carved boiseries of Madame de Pompadour's Château de Bellevue. Boucher referred back to her 1750 stage role in Pierre Laujon's ballet La Toilette de Vénus, and the Vanderbilts bequeathed the panel to the Metropolitan Museum in 1920.
credit: Metropolitan Museum of Art, online collection (accession number 20.155.9)

title: Venus Consoling Love
description: Venus reclines beside a stream while Cupid, his bow set aside, leans into her arms for comfort. Signed and dated 1751 and painted for Madame de Pompadour, possibly for her apartment at Versailles or her Château de Bellevue, the canvas now hangs in the National Gallery of Art in Washington.
credit: National Gallery of Art, Washington, D. C., online collection

title: Jeroboam Offering Sacrifice for the Idol
description: The Israelite king kneels before a golden idol as the prophet's curse withers his arm and overturns the altar, the figures pitched in violent Baroque diagonals. Fragonard, only twenty and trained outside the Académie, won the Prix de Rome with this picture on 26 August 1752; it remained with the Académie until the Revolution and now belongs to the Académie des Beaux-Arts.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"f/fragonar/father/1/01jerobo"

title: John Plampin
description: The young squire of Chadacre Hall sits on a grassy bank with his legs splayed and his dog beside him, the tower of All Saints, Lawshall just visible beyond the trees. Painted around 1752 during Gainsborough's Ipswich period and now National Gallery NG5984, the small canvas treats English landscape and portraiture as a single intimate field.

title: John and Ann Gravenor
description: The Ipswich apothecary John Gravenor sits with his second wife Ann and their daughters Elizabeth and Ann at the edge of a cornfield, the daughters holding freshly picked flowers. Probably commissioned in 1754 to mark Gravenor's entry into local politics, the square canvas is now in the Paul Mellon Collection at the Yale Center for British Art.

title: Mars
description: Vulcan looms at the forge while Venus reclines with Mars and two cupids gather around a heap of armour, after Ovid's tale of the lovers exposed in the smith god's net. Signed and dated 1754, the canvas is among the earliest surviving paintings by Copley, then about sixteen and working out a European mythological vocabulary from prints in colonial Boston.

title: The Grape Gatherer
description: A young woman cradles a bunch of grapes in her gathered skirt while squeezing juice over a baby at her feet. Painted around 1754-55, the canvas belongs to a set of four pastoral seasons at the Detroit Institute of Arts that Fragonard produced as overdoor or wall-panel decoration for an interior scheme.

title: Aurora Triumphing over Night
description: Aurora rides above the clouds scattering rose petals onto the sleeping figure of Night, lit by an upward-raking perspective. Painted around 1755-56 as an overdoor for a Parisian townhouse, the horizontal canvas was acquired by the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston at Sotheby's New York in January 2013.

title: Landscape with a Watermill
description: Travellers and washerwomen pause beside a thatched mill with a turning wheel, in a landscape of leafy trees and a circular ruin recalling the Temple of Vesta at Tivoli. Boucher signed and dated the canvas 1755 and set the imaginary scene in the rolling country near Beauvais; the picture is now National Gallery NG6374.

title: The Skating Minister
description: A Church of Scotland minister glides across a frozen Edinburgh loch in elegant profile, arms folded against the chill. The silhouetted black figure on pale ice and misty hills became an emblem of the Scottish Enlightenment and a touchstone of Scottish national painting.
credit: National Gallery of Scotland, Edinburgh, online collection

title: Portrait of Madame de Pompadour
description: Madame de Pompadour reclines on a green silk sofa in an embroidered floral gown, surrounded by books, sheet music, a quill, and her spaniel Inès. Signed and dated 1756 and now in the Alte Pinakothek in Munich, the full-length state portrait shows Louis XV's official mistress as the educated patron of Diderot, Voltaire and the philosophes.

title: A Man Called Mr. Wood
description: A slim, elegantly dressed man identified as Mr Wood, said to have been a dancing master, stands in a quiet Suffolk landscape. The portrait dates from around 1757, near the end of Gainsborough's Ipswich years before he left for Bath in 1759, and is now in the Paul Mellon Collection at the Yale Center for British Art.

title: Vulcan Presenting Venus with Arms for Aeneas
description: The muscular smith god offers Venus the armour he has forged for her son Aeneas, after the eighth book of the Aeneid. Boucher produced the 1757 canvas, now in the Louvre and over three metres square, as the cartoon for one of four tapestries on the Loves of the Gods commissioned for Louis XV alongside designs by Vanloo, Pierre and Vien.

title: Mary and Elizabeth Royall
description: The teenage daughters of the Medford merchant Isaac Royall Jr. sit together with a small spaniel and a hummingbird tethered to a string. Painted around 1758 when Copley was twenty, the canvas is believed to be his first double portrait; the Loyalist Royalls fled to England in 1776, leaving it behind, and the Museum of Fine Arts acquired it in 1925.

title: Portrait of Ann Fairchild Bowler
description: Ann Fairchild Bowler, wife of the Newport merchant and politician Metcalf Bowler, sits in a blue silk gown with a fold of drapery behind her. The 1758 canvas is one of a pair of pendant portraits Copley painted of the Bowlers during his early Boston practice and now belongs to the Colby College Museum of Art in Waterville, Maine.
credit: The Colby College Museum of Art <br(>2. The Colby College Museum of Art

title: Self-portrait
description: A self-portrait painted around 1758-59, just as Gainsborough left Ipswich for the spa town of Bath. The small canvas, now NPG 4446 in the National Portrait Gallery, almost certainly hung in his studio as an advertisement of his skill; behind the loose, fluent brushwork the trees of a Suffolk landscape can still be made out.

title: Jupiter in the Guise of Diana
description: Jupiter, disguised as the chaste Diana, leans toward the nymph Callisto with the seducer's eagle hidden above a pink satin curtain. Signed and dated 1759 and acquired by the Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art in Kansas City through the William Rockhill Nelson Trust, the small canvas concentrates the late Rococo into a tight palette of pinks, greens and blues.
credit: The Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art, Kansas City, Missouri

title: Epes Sargent
description: The Gloucester merchant and shipowner leans nonchalantly against a marble pedestal, his weathered hand resting flat on the stone. Copley, only about twenty-two when he signed the canvas around 1760, borrowed the pedestal from European print sources because carved monuments were rare in the American colonies; the portrait now hangs in the National Gallery of Art in Washington.

title: Portrait of Ann Ford
description: Ann Ford sits in a fashionable Bath drawing room with her English guitar across her lap and a viola da gamba propped beside her chair. Painted in 1760 shortly after Gainsborough settled in Bath, the portrait celebrates Ford as a professional musician, a calling unusual for a woman of her class and one her father had tried to suppress.

title: The Painter's Daughters with a Cat
description: Margaret and Mary Gainsborough, the painter's daughters, lean into one another while a cat curls into Margaret's arm, the picture left unfinished with the animal sketched only in outline. One of around a dozen portraits Gainsborough painted of the girls across their childhood, it now hangs in the National Gallery, London.

title: Two faces expressing veneration and rapture. Etching
description: Two heads tilted upward in devotional rapture, the eyes rolled and lips parted in expressions codified by Charles Le Brun's lectures on the passions. The etching, made around 1760 after Le Brun, belongs to the long afterlife of his physiognomic system in academic drawing manuals, and is held by the Wellcome Collection.

title: A woman with a rose
description: A young woman holds a single rose at her bodice, the figure built up in soft black chalk with the costume left as quick contour. Catalogued by the British Museum as entry 749307, the drawing dates from Gainsborough's Bath years, when he sketched women's portraits at speed in chalks before working them up in oil.

title: Dreaming Shepherdess
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"b/boucher/2/shepdrea"

title: Hilly Landscape with Figures Approaching a Bridge
description: A wooded river landscape in the Dutch-influenced manner of Gainsborough's middle years, with travellers descending toward a rustic bridge. Feathered foliage and a silvery palette establish the gentle, picturesque mood that defined his Bath-period landscapes.

title: Mary Little
description: Mary Little, later Lady Carr, stands in a pale grey-blue gown with lace cuffs, set against a screen of foliage in the Bath manner. Painted around 1763, the portrait belongs to Gainsborough's mature Bath period and now hangs at Yale Center for British Art, gift of Paul Mellon.

title: Mrs. Benjamin Pickman
description: Mary Toppan, newly married to the Salem merchant Benjamin Pickman, sits in a satin gown with a string of pearls at her throat, painted in 1763 when she was nineteen. The canvas is at the Yale University Art Gallery, accession 1966.79.3, and is one of Copley's earliest essays in the polished colonial manner he would carry to London.

title: Mrs. Daniel Sargent
description: Mary Turner Sargent leans on a pedestal beside a fountain, water cupped in her hand, in a Boston society portrait of 1763. The conceit of the basin and the pose derive from English mezzotints after Reynolds, sources Copley studied avidly in colonial Massachusetts before his move to London.

title: Mary Hopkinson
description: Mary Hopkinson holds a sheet of music against a dark ground, painted by West in 1764 shortly after he settled in London. The sitter was the sister of Francis Hopkinson, signer of the Declaration of Independence, and the picture entered the Smithsonian American Art Museum in 1926.

title: Portrait of Mary
description: Mary, Countess Howe, walks through a wooded landscape in a pink silk gown lifted to show a quilted petticoat, a black ribbon at her throat. Painted in 1764 at Bath and now at Kenwood House, the portrait is among Gainsborough's most admired full-lengths, the gown rendered in feathery strokes that animate the silk.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"g/gainsbor/04m_howe"

title: A Boy with a Flying Squirrel
description: Henry Pelham, Copley's half-brother, sits at a polished mahogany table with a flying squirrel tethered by a gold chain, a glass of water beside him. Shipped to London for the 1766 Society of Artists exhibition, the picture earned Copley election to the Society and Joshua Reynolds's qualified praise.

title: Allegory of Painting
credit: This file was derived from: Allegory of Painting sc493.jpg :

title: Gathering Bamboo Shoots
description: "Gathering Bamboo Shoots". Colored woodblock print

title: Harunobu Kanzan et Jittoku
description: A mitate of the Chinese Chan eccentrics Hanshan and Shide, Jittoku identifiable by his ever-present broom. Harunobu reimagines the Buddhist pair in the contemporary dress of Edo youths, the kind of layered classical-vernacular play that defined his refined nishiki-e output.

title: Hatred or Jealousy
description: A grimacing head with knotted brow and bared teeth illustrates Hatred or Jealousy, plate from Heads Representing the Various Passions of the Soul published by Robert Sayer in 1765. The series engraves Le Brun's 1668 Paris lecture diagrams, turning the French academy's physiognomic codes into a drawing manual for English students.

title: John Hancock
description: John Hancock sits at a writing table in a blue coat with his ledger open before him, the merchant and future signer of the Declaration of Independence painted at twenty-eight. Copley made the portrait in 1765 for the Hancock family in Boston, and it now hangs in the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.

title: Karl Friedrich Abel
description: The composer Carl Friedrich Abel sits with his viola da gamba and a sheet of manuscript, a virtuoso of the instrument and Gainsborough's close friend. Abel and Johann Christian Bach ran the Bach-Abel concert series in London from 1765, and the painter, himself an amateur gambist, owned several Abel autograph scores.

title: Mrs. George Watson
description: Elizabeth Oliver Watson, wife of the Boston merchant George Watson, sits in a russet silk gown holding a sprig of flowers. The 1765 portrait pairs with Copley's likeness of her husband and entered the Smithsonian American Art Museum as a gift from the family.

title: Mrs. Theodore Atkinson Jr.
description: Frances Deering Wentworth, painted at twenty in oil on canvas, holds a flying squirrel by a chain in a gesture borrowed from Copley's Pelham portrait of the same year. Married first to Theodore Atkinson Jr. and later to Governor John Wentworth, she sat to Copley in 1765 in Boston.

title: Portrait of Nathaniel Hurd
description: The Boston silversmith and engraver Nathaniel Hurd leans on two folios, one labelled with the heraldic engraver's reference works that supplied his trade. Painted around 1765 and now in the Cleveland Museum of Art, the portrait shows Hurd in working dress, a rare colonial likeness of a craftsman rather than a merchant.

title: Terrour or Fright
description: A head with eyes flung wide and mouth open in a scream, codifying Terrour or Fright in the system of facial passions. Engraved for Robert Sayer's 1765 English edition after Charles Le Brun's Paris academy lectures, the plate is held by the Metropolitan Museum of Art.

title: The High Priest Coresus Sacrificing Himself to Save Callirhoe
description: The high priest Coresus plunges a dagger into his own breast before the altar to save the maiden Callirhoe from the sacrifice Bacchus had demanded, the temple filled with collapsing onlookers. Fragonard's morceau d'agrément for admission to the Académie Royale in 1765, the canvas was bought immediately by Louis XV and hangs in the Louvre.

title: Virgin and Child with the Young Saint John the Baptist and Angels
description: Madonna and Child

title: Pylades and Orestes Brought as Victims before Iphigenia
Commodore the Hon. Augustus Hervey
description: Augustus Hervey, third Earl of Bristol, stands in commodore's undress uniform with a coil of rope at his hand and his ship riding at anchor offshore. Painted by Gainsborough in 1767 for Hervey's seat at Ickworth, the portrait is now in the National Trust collection.

title: Judge Martin Howard
description: Judge Martin Howard sits in a brown coat with a sheaf of legal papers at his hand, painted in oil on canvas at 125.7 by 101 cm. The 1767 portrait is held by the Museo Thyssen-Bornemisza in Madrid, an unusual European home for a Copley colonial likeness.

title: Road from Market
description: A rural landscape in which figures with laden horses return along a sunken track at the close of day. Gainsborough constructs the scene from imagined, idealised motifs, building a poetic vision of English country life in the Bath-period pastoral mode.

title: The Happy Accidents of the Swing
description: A young woman in a pink silk gown swings forward through a garden bower, kicking off one slipper as a hidden suitor peers up from the bushes below. Commissioned by the Baron de Saint-Julien for his château, Fragonard's canvas became the defining image of Rococo libertinage.

title: The Secret Message
description: A young woman in a satin gown leans on a stone parapet to read a folded billet, her companion looking on in the garden shade. Oil on canvas, 60 by 50.5 cm, signed and dated lower right FBoucher / 1767, now in the Herzog Anton Ulrich-Museum at Braunschweig.

title: Young lady with a Bird and dog
description: A girl in a blue silk dress holds a length of ribbon tied to a small bird while a spaniel rests at her side. Painted in Boston before Copley's departure for Europe, the portrait entered the Toledo Museum of Art and shows his close-observed treatment of fabric, fur, and feather.

title: Agrippina Landing at Brundisium with the Ashes of Germanicu
description: The widow Agrippina disembarks at the Italian port of Brundisium carrying the urn that holds her husband Germanicus's ashes, flanked by mourners and her children. Commissioned by Archbishop Robert Hay Drummond after a passage in Tacitus, the picture launched West's Neoclassical history practice in London and now hangs at Yale.

title: An Experiment on a Bird in an Air Pump
description: A candle-lit demonstration of a vacuum pump, with a cockatoo gasping in its glass globe as a mixed audience reacts in awe, fascination, and dread. Wright transposes religious chiaroscuro onto the new theatre of Enlightenment science.

title: Cleombrotus Ordered into Banishment by Leonidas II
description: Leonidas II points his son-in-law Cleombrotus toward exile while the younger man's wife pleads at his feet with their children. West drew the episode from Plutarch's Life of Agis, treating Spartan civic duty in the friezelike arrangement that marked his Neoclassical history pictures of the late 1760s.

title: Portrait of Paul Revere
description: The Boston silversmith sits in his shirtsleeves at a polished workbench, holding a teapot he is about to finish, engraving tools laid out before him. Copley shows Revere as an artisan rather than a gentleman, an unusually direct conception for a colonial portrait, now in the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.

title: Figure de fantaisie autrefois désignée à tort comme Denis Diderot
description: A man in a feathered cap and ruff turns sharply toward the viewer, brush rapidly defining the lace and the dark eyes. Long catalogued at the Louvre as Diderot, the picture is now classed among Fragonard's figures de fantaisie, painted in roughly an hour each as virtuoso essays in costume portraiture.
credit: Louvre: Denis Diderot , vue sans cadre

title: Fragonard Woman w Dog 1769 MMA
description: A young woman in a loose pink wrap holds up a small lapdog to kiss its muzzle, the bedclothes tumbling around her. The canvas, now at the Metropolitan Museum of Art, belongs to Fragonard's series of intimate boudoir pictures of the late 1760s, painted with a feathery, rapid touch.

title: François-Henri d'Harcourt
description: The future Duc d'Harcourt, governor to the Dauphin, leans on an open book in a brocaded jacket, his attention caught mid-thought. Oil on canvas, the portrait belongs to Fragonard's group of figures de fantaisie of about 1769, in which sitters appear in fanciful Spanish or Renaissance costume.

title: Inspiration
description: A young man in seventeenth-century costume looks upward from his writing desk, quill in hand, as if catching a passing thought. One of Fragonard's figures de fantaisie, the canvas was likely painted at speed in about an hour, an exercise in bravura brushwork over careful underdrawing.

title: Isaac Royall
description: The Massachusetts merchant and slaveholder Isaac Royall sits in a damask-upholstered armchair in a green coat, the gilt frame and column behind him signalling rank. Now in the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, the canvas belongs to Copley's Cambridge sittings of the late 1760s, before he left for Europe in 1774.

title: Self-portrait
description: Copley shows himself at thirty-one in a soft cap and open collar, brush poised, eyes meeting the viewer's. Painted in Boston five years before he left North America for good, the small canvas records the painter's pre-European style, built on dense local colour and forensic observation.

title: The Departure of Regulus
description: The Roman consul Marcus Atilius Regulus tears himself from his wife and children to return to certain torture in Carthage, having kept his oath to the enemy. The first picture George III commissioned from West, RCIN 405416, established the painter's role as history painter to the King and now hangs in the Royal Collection.

title: the two sisters
description: Two young girls in white muslin dresses lean close together over a basket of flowers, the older steadying the younger on a cushioned bench. The canvas, sometimes called Les Deux Soeurs, belongs to Fragonard's series of intimate domestic groups painted in the late 1760s.

title: A woman whose face expresses sadness. Etching in the crayon
description: A young woman bows her head into her shawl, mouth set and eyes downcast in unconcealed grief. Etching in the crayon manner by W. Hebert, around 1770, the print belongs to the Wellcome Collection's holdings of physiognomic studies that imitated red-chalk drawing through stippled etched dots.

title: A Young Girl Reading
description: A young woman in lemon-yellow silk sits in profile, absorbed in a small book held close to her face, her elbow propped on a velvet cushion. Oil on canvas at the National Gallery of Art in Washington, the picture is among the most settled and finished of Fragonard's late-1760s portraits of figures lost in thought.

title: Benjamin West
description: The American history painter Benjamin West appears half-length in a powdered wig and brown coat, a sheet of drawing paper at hand. Painted in London by James Smith around 1770, the portrait records West at the moment he was establishing his Pall Mall studio as a training ground for visiting American artists.

title: Colonel John Bullock
description: Colonel John Bullock of Faulkbourne Hall stands at three-quarter length in scarlet uniform, his hand resting on a sword hilt. Gainsborough painted the militia officer in the early 1770s, during the Bath years when his commissions from county gentry and military sitters were at their height.

title: Girl with Dog
description: A girl in tumbled sheets lifts a small dog onto her lap, both turned toward the viewer in a flush of laughter. Painted around 1770, the canvas belongs to Fragonard's intimate group of boudoir scenes, finished with rapid, broken brushwork over a thin pinkish ground.

title: Portrait of Dr. William Hunter's Spaniels
description: Two white-and-brown spotted spaniels stretch beneath a Newport Chippendale mahogany tea table, the larger asleep facing left and the smaller looking out at the viewer. Painted by the young Gilbert Stuart in Newport around 1770, the canvas is among the earliest surviving works by the future portraitist of George Washington.

title: The Blue Boy
description: A young man in a slashed blue satin suit of the Van Dyck period stands in a parkland landscape, plumed hat in hand. Painted around 1770 and shown at the Royal Academy in 1770, Gainsborough's portrait of the ironmonger's son Jonathan Buttall now hangs at the Huntington Library in San Marino.
credit: britsattheirbest.com; The Huntington Library, Art Collections

title: The Death of General Wolfe
description: British General James Wolfe lies dying among his officers on the Plains of Abraham after the 1759 capture of Quebec, a Mohawk scout watching at his side. West broke history-painting decorum by showing his subjects in contemporary uniform rather than classical dress, and the canvas at the National Gallery of Canada was widely copied in engraving.

title: The Love Letter
description: A young woman at a writing table looks up from a sealed letter, a sprig of flowers tucked among the ribbons of her dress, a small dog beside her. Oil on canvas of about 1770, now at the Metropolitan Museum of Art, the picture is among Fragonard's most polished essays in the gallant tabletop scene.

title: The Oath of Hannibal
description: The young Hannibal kneels at an altar before his father Hamilcar Barca, swearing the lifelong oath of enmity against Rome. Painted as a pendant to The Departure of Regulus for George III, RCIN 405417 in the Royal Collection, the picture pairs Carthaginian and Roman exemplars of stoic resolve.

title: Daniel Crommelin Verplanck
description: The nine-year-old Daniel Crommelin Verplanck of New York sits under a tree in a tan coat, a tame squirrel on a chain in his lap. Now at the Metropolitan Museum of Art, the canvas was painted at the Verplanck family seat on lower Wall Street in 1771, during Copley's late colonial period.

title: Ezekiel Goldthwait
description: The Boston merchant and town clerk Ezekiel Goldthwait sits in a wing chair with a ledger on the table beside him, his hand resting on the open page. Oil on canvas of 1771, paired with Copley's portrait of his wife Elizabeth at the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, accession 41.85.

title: JohnMontresorByCopley
description: Captain John Montresor, the British military engineer who surveyed Quebec and Detroit, sits in three-quarter view in his red officer's coat. Copley painted the portrait in oil on canvas around 1771, during his Boston practice before he left for London on the eve of the Revolution. The Detroit Institute of Arts holds the canvas.
credit: From the Detroit Institute of Arts ( http://www.dia.org/ ). URL at time of upload: http://www.dia.org/the_collection/overview/viewobject.asp?objectid=41296

title: Jupiter and Antiope
description: Jupiter, disguised as a satyr, leans over the sleeping nymph Antiope while a putto pulls back the drapery. David painted the canvas in 1771 as a student in Paris, before winning the Prix de Rome; it survives in the collection at Sens. The mythological eroticism still belongs to the late Rococo idiom David would soon repudiate for severe Neoclassicism.

title: Mrs Humphrey Devereux
description: Mrs Humphrey Devereux, the artist's mother-in-law, sits in a satin gown with a lace cap, her hand resting on the carved arm of a chair. Copley painted the half-length portrait in oil on canvas in 1771 and shipped it from Boston to her in Halifax. It now hangs at the Auckland Art Gallery Toi o Tamaki.

title: Portrait of a Lady
description: A young woman in a blue silk gown poses with one hand at her bodice, the other holding a length of pearls. Copley painted the half-length portrait in oil on canvas in 1771, near the end of his Boston decade in which he documented the merchant class of pre-Revolutionary New England.

title: Portrait of Mrs. Thomas Gage
description: Margaret Kemble Gage, American wife of the British general Thomas Gage, reclines in Turkish-style robes against a brocade cushion. Copley painted the portrait in 1771 at the Gage estate in New Jersey; she was reputedly the source who tipped off Joseph Warren about the march on Lexington. It hangs at the Timken Museum of Art in San Diego.
credit: from http://www.mcah.columbia.edu/dbcourses/vrc/large/copley_gage_mrs_thomas.jpg Uploaded to english Wikipedia by en:User:Flying Jazz on 9 May 2005.

title: Sir Joseph Banks
description: Joseph Banks, just back from Cook's first Pacific voyage, stands in a long Maori cloak of dogskin with a taiaha at his feet and a tattooed mere on the table. West painted the portrait between 1771 and 1772 in London, presenting Banks as the gentleman naturalist of the Endeavour. The picture belongs to the Usher Gallery in Lincoln.

title: The Alchemist Discovering Phosphorus or The Alchemist in Search of the Philosophers Stone
description: An aged alchemist kneels before a glowing flask as phosphorus ignites in his laboratory, alluding to Hennig Brand's 1669 discovery. Wright stages the scene with the theatrical single-source illumination that defined his Enlightenment subjects, balancing scientific wonder against gothic shadow.

title: The Progress of Love: The Meeting
description: A young man scrambles over a garden balustrade with a letter as his lover, alarmed, leaps to her feet beneath a statue of Venus. Painted between 1771 and 1773, the canvas is the first of four panels in Fragonard's Progress of Love cycle, commissioned by Madame du Barry for her pavilion at Louveciennes. The Frick Collection in New York holds the suite.

title: Apollo and Diana Attacking the Children of Niobe
description: Apollo and Diana shoot down the children of Niobe from a cloud while their mother shields the youngest beneath her cloak. David painted the canvas in 1772 as his second unsuccessful entry for the Prix de Rome; the rejection prompted a suicide attempt before he finally won the prize in 1774. It now hangs at the Dallas Museum of Art.

title: Elizabeth and Mary Linley
description: Elizabeth and Mary Linley, daughters of the Bath composer Thomas Linley, sit close together in a wooded glade, the elder holding a sheet of music. Gainsborough painted the double portrait around 1772 and retouched it in 1785, after Elizabeth's elopement with Sheridan. It belongs to the Dulwich Picture Gallery in London.

title: Erasistratus the Physician Discovers the Love of Antiochus for Stratonice
description: The court physician Erasistratus takes the pulse of the lovesick prince Antiochus as his stepmother Stratonice enters the chamber, revealing the cause of his illness. West painted the Hellenistic anecdote, drawn from Plutarch, in 1772. The canvas is in the Birmingham Museum of Art.

title: Portrait of Samuel Adams
description: Samuel Adams stands at a table with the Massachusetts charter under one hand and points to the petition demanding the removal of British troops after the Boston Massacre. Copley painted the portrait around 1772 on commission from John Hancock, who hung it in his Beacon Hill house. The Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, holds it now.

title: The Death of Chevalier Bayard
description: The French knight Bayard, mortally wounded by an arquebus shot during the retreat from the Sesia in 1524, leans against a tree to receive the rites as his enemy the Constable de Bourbon kneels beside him. West painted the canvas in 1772 for George III; it remains in the Royal Collection.

title: Mademoiselle Guimard as Terpsichore
description: The Opera dancer Marie-Madeleine Guimard poses as Terpsichore, muse of dance, in classical drapery beside a lyre. David began the portrait around 1773 for Guimard's hôtel particulier on the Chaussée d'Antin but abandoned the commission after a quarrel with the sitter, who reportedly turned the figure's features into those of a Fury before Fragonard was brought in to complete the related decorative scheme. The unfinished canvas is an early glimpse of the neoclassical idiom David would soon define.

title: Portrait of Mr. and Mrs. Thomas Mifflin
description: Thomas Mifflin, the Pennsylvania merchant and future first governor of the state, sits beside his wife Sarah Morris, who works at a small loom of fringed silk. Copley painted the double portrait in 1773, just before sailing for Europe, as a tribute to the non-importation movement that the Mifflins championed. The Philadelphia Museum of Art holds it.

title: The Artist's Brother
description: An early portrait by the teenage Vigée Le Brun shows her younger brother Étienne in elegant attire, his open expression rendered with the precocious assurance that would soon win her royal commissions. The handling already displays the porcelain finish and Rococo grace of her mature manner.

title: The muscles of the human body
description: The muscles of the human body, fourth layer, seen from the front. Colour mezzotint by A. E.

title: The Wife of Arminius brought captive to Germanicus
description: Thusnelda, wife of the Cheruscan chief Arminius, stands captive with her son before the Roman general Germanicus after the campaigns of 15 AD. West painted the Tacitean episode in 1773 for George III as part of the Windsor history series, in oil on canvas. It remains in the Royal Collection.

title: Adolf Ludvig Gustav Albert Couschi
description: Adolf Ludvig Gustav Albert Couschi, a courtier of African descent brought to Sweden as a child and ennobled as Badin by Queen Lovisa Ulrika, sits in a powdered wig and embroidered coat. Lundberg drew the portrait in pastel in 1775; it belongs to the Nationalmuseum in Stockholm under inventory NMGrh 1455.

title: Benjamin Waterhouse
description: Benjamin Waterhouse, the Newport physician who later introduced smallpox vaccination to America, sits in a buttoned waistcoat with his hand at his lapel. Stuart painted the portrait in 1775, before either sitter or painter had left for medical and artistic training in London. The Redwood Library and Athenaeum in Newport holds it.
credit: Redwood Library and Athenaeum, Newport, Rhode Island, Bequest of Louisa Lee Waterhouse (Mrs. Benjamin Waterhouse) of Cambridge, Massachusetts. Digitized at National Gallery of Art

title: Blindman's Buff
description: A blindfolded girl, arms outstretched, gropes for her companions in a sunlit park beneath flowering trees. Fragonard painted the game of colin-maillard between 1775 and 1780 as a pendant to The Swing variant called See-Saw. The Toledo Museum of Art holds the canvas.

title: Chaumiére Italienne
description: An Italian peasant cottage with a thatched roof crouches beneath a stand of windswept trees, two figures at the threshold. Fragonard etched the small landscape in 1775 from sketches made during his second Italian journey with the abbe de Saint-Non. An impression is held at the Ghent University Library.

title: Daniel Interpreting to Belshazzar the Writing on the Wall - 485-2018 - Saint Louis Art Museum
englishTitle: Daniel Interpreting to Belshazzar the Writing on the Wall
description: Daniel points to the burning letters MENE TEKEL UPHARSIN on the wall of Belshazzar's banquet hall as the Babylonian king recoils among his cowering courtiers. West painted the canvas in 1775, drawing on the Book of Daniel for one of his early biblical histories. The Saint Louis Art Museum acquired it in 2018.

title: De Kloveniersdoelen aan de Amstel-De Kloveniersburgwal op de hoek van de Amstel met de toren "Swijgh Utrecht
description: View of the Kloveniersdoelen on the Amstel, with the militia guildhall and the Swijgh Utrecht tower rising at the corner of the Kloveniersburgwal. Painted in 1775, the cityscape records a stretch of Amsterdam that the Dutch capital would substantially rebuild in the nineteenth century.

title: Isaac's servant tying the bracelet on Rebecca's arm
description: Abraham's servant Eliezer fastens the gold bracelet on Rebecca's wrist at the well, marking her as the chosen bride for Isaac. West painted the Genesis episode in 1775 in oil on canvas. The composition belongs to a series of Old Testament subjects he produced for English patrons in the 1770s.

title: Mr. and Mrs. Ralph Izard
description: The South Carolina planter Ralph Izard and his wife Alice DeLancey sit at a marble table in a Roman interior, a Greek vase between them and the Colosseum visible through the window. Copley painted the double portrait in 1775 during the couple's grand tour in Rome, his first European commission. The Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, holds it.

title: Portrait of Colonel Guy Johnson and Karonghyontye
description: Colonel Guy Johnson, British superintendent of Indian affairs for the northern colonies, stands in a green ranger's coat beside the Mohawk diplomat Karonghyontye, with Niagara Falls in the distance. West painted the double portrait around 1775 in London during Johnson's visit to lobby for Iroquois alliance. The National Gallery of Art in Washington holds the canvas.
credit: Photographed by me at the NGA, 18 August 2005

title: The Honourable Mrs Graham
description: Mary Cathcart, the seventeen-year-old Honourable Mrs Graham, stands in a feathered hat and dress of pink silk and lace, one hand resting on a stone pedestal. Gainsborough exhibited the full-length at the Royal Academy in 1777, two years after painting it; her widower hid the canvas after her early death and it entered the Scottish National Gallery in 1859.

title: The Visit to the Nursery
description: A young mother and a visitor lean over a wicker cradle as a nurse holds an older child by the hand, the scene set in a sun-streaked country room. Fragonard painted the canvas around 1775, in the genre vein of domestic sentiment that Greuze had popularized. The National Gallery of Art in Washington holds it under accession 32685.

title: William Curtis 1775
description: Oil portrait of the English botanist William Curtis, demonstrator of plants at the Chelsea Physic Garden from 1771 and later author of Flora Londinensis. The picture, held in the RHS Lindley Collections, captures Curtis during the years before he launched The Botanical Magazine in 1787.

title: Benjamin West
description: Self-portrait of the Pennsylvania-born history painter Benjamin West, then in his late thirties and established in London as historical painter to George III. The National Gallery of Art version, oil on canvas at 75.8 by 63 cm, is an 18th-century copy after a slightly earlier West original.

title: Gunseondo
description: From Gunseondo, Kim Hong-do's screen of Daoist Immortals painted in 1776 for the newly enthroned King Jeongjo. Designated National Treasure 139, the work shows the Sennin as full-figured, robust heroes, departing from Kim's linear style and securing his reputation as the leading court painter of the Joseon dynasty.

title: Helen Brought to Paris
description: Venus and Cupid lead Helen of Troy toward the kneeling Paris in West's neoclassical history painting, oil on canvas at roughly 143 by 198 cm, now at the Smithsonian American Art Museum. West, painter to George III, made the work in 1776 while balancing royal patronage against his American birth on the eve of revolution.

title: Kim Hong-do
description: Painted view of Kyujanggak, the royal library founded in 1776 on the grounds of Changdeokgung by King Jeongjo. Kim Hong-do, the king's designated painter, produced this colour-on-paper record at the moment the institution was established, documenting one of Jeongjo's major cultural undertakings.

title: Portrait of Johann Christian Bach
description: Portrait of the composer Johann Christian Bach, youngest son of J. S. Bach and known in his adopted country as the 'English Bach'. Gainsborough painted this likeness in 1776 at the sitter's request for the gallery of musicians in Bologna assembled by Padre Giovanni Battista Martini, with the composer holding a sheet of music in a green velvet coat.

title: Richard St George Mansergh-St George
description: Richard St George Mansergh-St George stands in the red uniform of the 4th Regiment of Foot, hat in hand, with a ship at anchor in the distance. Gainsborough painted the full-length on commission in 1776 just before St George shipped for North America, where he was wounded at Germantown in October 1777.

title: The Copley Family
description: Group portrait of the artist with his wife Susanna, their four children, and his Loyalist father-in-law Richard Clarke, painted in London after Copley fled the Revolution in 1775. Exhibited at the Royal Academy in 1777, the canvas announced Copley's arrival in British society and is now at the National Gallery of Art, Washington.

title: The Fountaine Family' by John Singleton Copley
description: Conversation piece showing the Norfolk landowner Brigg Price Fountaine with his wife Mary and children Andrew and Elizabeth, a spaniel at their feet, set in the drawing room of Narford Hall. Painted in 1776 at the start of Copley's English career, the picture adapts the manner of Johann Zoffany and entered Tate Britain through Arts Council England's Cultural Gift Scheme.

title: George IV
description: Double portrait of the future George IV in state robes alongside his younger brother Prince Frederick, later Duke of York, painted in 1777 for George III. West executed the canvas (RCIN 403399, Royal Collection) while serving as historical painter to the king, a post he had held since 1772.

title: John singleton copley
description: Bust-length study of a Black sitter, possibly a London dockworker, made by Copley in 1777-78 as he prepared Watson and the Shark. The Detroit Institute of Arts holds the canvas, oil at 41.3 by 53.3 cm, which presents its subject as an individual at a moment when such treatment was rare in British painting.

title: Portrait of Anne
description: Anne Stanhope, wife of the 5th Earl of Chesterfield, sits in a blue and white satin gown with her left arm resting on a plinth, dense foliage behind her and her family's lands opening to the right. Gainsborough painted the 221 by 156 cm canvas in 1777-78, his loose, sweeping brushwork registering sky, drapery, and leaves with equal speed. It is now at the J. Paul Getty Museum.

title: Two Officers and a Groom in a Landscape
description: Two mounted officers and their groom pause in a wooded landscape, painted by West in 1777 at the height of the American Revolution. The 101.6 by 127 cm canvas is held by the Princeton University Art Museum, made during years when West, born in Pennsylvania, neither endorsed nor condemned the war in his land of birth.

title: Académie d´homme
description: Académie of a recumbent male nude, posed as the dead Hector with one arm hanging limp. David painted the study in 1778 during his Prix de Rome years at the French Academy in Rome, and it never left his studio, eventually entering the Musée Fabre in Montpellier where it remains.

title: Joseph Vernet
description: A bust-length portrait of the marine painter Joseph Vernet, posed in a powdered wig and dark coat against a neutral ground. Vigée Le Brun renders the older painter with the soft modeling and warm flesh tones that defined her late-Ancien Régime studio practice, treating him as a colleague rather than a patron.

provenance.collection: Department of Paintings of the Louvre

title: Portrait of Margaret Gainsborough
description: Half-length portrait of the artist's wife Margaret, née Burr, the illegitimate daughter of the 3rd Duke of Beaufort. Gainsborough painted the canvas around 1778, perhaps to mark her 50th birthday, contrasting carefully observed features with rapid zigzags of paint for the black shawl. It is held by the Samuel Courtauld Trust at the Courtauld Gallery, London.

title: Portrait of Mrs. Grace Dalrymple Elliott
description: Full-length portrait of the courtesan Grace Dalrymple Elliott, known as 'Dally the Tall', in a yellow Van Dyck-style gown with a towering 1770s coiffure. Commissioned by her lover the Earl of Cholmondeley and shown at the Royal Academy in 1778, the canvas measures 234.3 by 153.7 cm and is now at the Metropolitan Museum of Art.

title: The Artist Moved by the Grandeur of Antique Fragments
description: Fuseli's draughtsman slumps against a colossal antique foot and hand, overwhelmed by the ruins of classical achievement. Drawn in red chalk and sepia wash during his Roman years, the sheet captures the Sublime sense of inadequacy before antiquity that shaped Anglo-Continental Romanticism.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"f/fuseli/02antiqu"

title: The Battle of La Hogue
description: Admiral George Rooke stands sword aloft in a boat amid the wreckage of the French fleet during the 1692 engagement off La Hogue, with the Soleil Royal running aground in the distance. West began this version in 1778, then his pupil John Trumbull completed it in 1785 and West retouched it in 1806, now at the National Gallery of Art.

title: The Death of Chatham
description: Modello showing William Pitt the Elder collapsing in the House of Lords on 7 April 1778 after speaking against surrendering the American colonies. West, painter to George III, prepared this 71.4 by 92.1 cm oil at the Yale Center for British Art but abandoned the larger project, leaving the subject to his protégé Copley.

title: The Collapse of the Earl of Chatham in the House of Lords
description: William Pitt collapses among fifty-five identifiable peers beneath tapestries of the Spanish Armada's defeat, the moment of his fall in the House of Lords on 7 April 1778. Copley worked on the ten-foot canvas for two years and in 1781 installed it in a pavilion as a paying one-work show; it is now at Tate.

title: Danwon-Bbalrae.teo
description: Women beating laundry at a stream while a passing scholar peers over a rock, from Kim Hong-do's Danwon pungsokdo cheop. The sheet, ink and light colour on paper at 27 by 22.7 cm, is held by the National Museum of Korea and belongs to the album of genre scenes that established his reputation as the great chronicler of everyday Joseon life.

title: Danwon-Mudong
description: Dancing boy with musicians playing flute, drum, and zither, a scene from the Danwon pungsokdo cheop. Kim Hong-do worked in ink and light colour on paper at 27 by 22.7 cm, with the album of genre studies now held by the National Museum of Korea and considered a benchmark of late 18th-century Joseon painting.

title: Danwon-Nongali
description: Farmers driving an ox-drawn plough through a paddy field, from the Danwon pungsokdo cheop. Kim Hong-do painted the leaf in ink and light colour on paper at 27 by 22.7 cm, part of the album of agricultural and artisanal scenes held by the National Museum of Korea as a record of common life under King Jeongjo.

title: Danwon-Ssireum
description: Two wrestlers locked in a ssireum hold while spectators ring the contest, divided into upper and lower groups around the action. From the Danwon pungsokdo cheop in the National Museum of Korea, the sheet is ink and light colour on paper at 27 by 22.7 cm and counts as the most reproduced image of Joseon genre painting.

title: Hugh Montgomerie
description: Hugh Montgomerie, future 12th Earl of Eglinton, stands in the scarlet uniform of the 77th Regiment of Foot against a wooded landscape suggesting the American frontier. Copley painted the full-length portrait in London in 1780 after Montgomerie's service in the French and Indian War, now held by the Los Angeles County Museum of Art.

title: Kim Hong-do
description: Officials and attendants gather around low banquet tables inside the Pyongyang governor's hall, with dancers and musicians arranged on the floor below. The painting is the first scroll in Kim Hong-do's three-part series documenting an official feast, executed in the documentary genre painting style of late Joseon court commissions.

title: Kiyonaga bathhouse women-2
description: Half of a celebrated diptych depicting women in a public bathhouse, an unusually informal subject from the Tenmei era. Kiyonaga, head of the Torii school, sets his tall, calm figures in the careful spatial recession that reformed bijinga for the next generation.

title: Madame Lebrun
description: A young Frenchwoman in a powdered chignon and pale gauze gown sits half-length against an indistinct landscape. Gainsborough painted the sitter, identified as Madame Lebrun, in London in 1780 with the feathery brushwork and limited palette he favoured in his late portraiture.

title: Patroclus
description: The dead body of Patroclus lies stretched on a draped cloth, head fallen back, the muscular nude treated as an academic exercise in heroic anatomy. David painted the study in Rome in 1780 during his French Academy pensionnat, drawing on Homer and on the antique sculpture he was copying for his return submission.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"d/david_j/1/107david"

title: Peace bringing back Prosperity
description: An allegorical pair: Peace, in classical drapery, gently leads forward Abundance, who carries a sheaf of wheat and a cornucopia. The painting was Vigée Le Brun's reception piece for the Académie Royale, accepted in 1783, and shows her combining Neoclassical subject matter with the warm flesh tones and silken finish of her portrait practice.

provenance.collection: Académie royale de peinture et de sculpture

title: Songhamaenghodo
description: A tiger crouches beneath a gnarled pine, eyes round and tail curled along its flank in the convention of Joseon tutelary beasts. Kim Hong-do painted Songhamaenghodo in colour on silk, the picture combining the apotropaic tiger with the longevity emblem of the pine in a single auspicious composition.

title: The Garroted Man
description: An etching of a condemned prisoner slumped in the iron collar of the garrote, crucifix in hand. Goya pares the scene to a single lit body against deep aquatint shadow, prefiguring the political grimness of the Disasters of War.

title: The muscles of the hand
description: An anatomical engraving combining a flayed hand after Bernhard Siegfried Albinus with a foot after De Courcelles, the muscles, tendons and bones laid bare for study. Engraved by Robert Bénard for the late eighteenth-century editions of the Encyclopédie, the plate typifies the Enlightenment project of consolidating earlier anatomical illustration into a single compendium.

title: Woman in Blue
description: A woman in a powdered coiffure and pale blue silk gown turns three-quarters toward the viewer, the cool palette set against a neutral ground. Gainsborough painted the sitter, sometimes identified as the Duchess of Beaufort, in the loose, late style associated with his Schomberg House years; the canvas now hangs in the Hermitage.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"g/gainsbor/07lady_b"

title: Portret konny Stanisława Kostki Potockiego
description: The Polish nobleman Stanisław Kostka Potocki salutes from a rearing dappled horse, dressed in a buff coat and cocked hat against an Italian landscape. David painted the portrait in Rome in 1781 during Potocki's grand tour, applying Van Dyck's equestrian formula to a sitter who would later commission the picture's installation at Wilanów.

title: Madame du Barry
description: Marie-Jeanne Bécu, the former royal mistress of Louis XV, is shown in a relaxed garden setting with loose curls and a simple white gown. The image belongs to a series of informal portraits painted at Louveciennes, exchanging court formality for the pastoral neoclassical mode then fashionable in Paris.
credit: The Corcoran Gallery of Art, Washington, D.C. [1]

title: Portrait of Henry Laurens
description: The South Carolina statesman Henry Laurens sits at a writing table in a dark coat, a quill and papers at hand. Copley painted Laurens in London in 1782 shortly after his release from the Tower of London, where he had been held for two years as a captured American envoy.

title: Self Portrait in a Straw Hat
description: The artist holds palette and brushes beneath a wide plumed straw hat, smiling outward in a pose adapted from Rubens's Chapeau de Paille. Vigée Le Brun cast herself as both fashionable subject and confident professional, a self-promotional image she repeated.

title: The Skater
description: William Grant of Congalton glides on the frozen Serpentine in a black coat and hat, arms folded, with skating figures and Westminster trees behind. Stuart's 1782 portrait, exhibited at the Royal Academy, established his London reputation and is now in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
credit: originally uploaded to en.wikipedia by Csberger ( talk · contribs ) on 7 July 2005, 18:58 under the file name GSskater.jpg . ( +/− )

title: The Tribute Money
description: Copley, John Singleton; The Tribute Money; Royal Academy of Arts; http://www. artuk. org/artworks/the-tribute-money-148695

title: Yolande-Martine-Gabrielle de Polastron
description: A portrait of Marie Antoinette's intimate favourite, shown in a soft straw hat and informal muslin dress holding a sheet of music. Vigée Le Brun's pearly flesh tones and feathery brushwork epitomise the late ancien régime ideal of natural elegance.

title: Admiral Rodney at the Battle of the Saintes
description: A swagger portrait of Admiral Lord Rodney, victor over the French at the 1782 Battle of the Saintes, the captured ensign of the Ville de Paris draped behind him. Gainsborough's feathery brushwork and silvery palette soften the formal demands of state portraiture.

title: American Commissioners of the Preliminary Peace Agreement with Great Britain
description: John Jay, John Adams, Benjamin Franklin, Henry Laurens and William Temple Franklin sit together around a table in West's unfinished oil sketch for the planned Treaty of Paris group portrait. The British commissioners refused to sit, and West abandoned the canvas; the fragment is held at the Winterthur Museum in Delaware.

title: Coastal Landscape with a Shepherd and His Flock
description: A late landscape in which a shepherd and flock cross a windswept shore beneath gathering clouds. Gainsborough loosens the topography into soft, tonal silhouettes, prefiguring the atmospheric coastal scenes that would influence British Romantic painters.

title: Frances Browne
description: Frances Browne, later Mrs John Douglas, stands full-length in a white satin gown with a wide black sash, leaning against a stone plinth in a wooded park. Gainsborough painted the portrait in 1783 to 1784 for the sitter's family; it now hangs at Waddesdon Manor, the National Trust Rothschild house in Buckinghamshire.

title: John Adams
description: John Adams stands in a brown coat beside a globe and a draped table, one hand resting on a sword hilt, the other holding diplomatic papers. Copley painted Adams in London in 1783 as the Massachusetts minister was negotiating the peace that recognised American independence; the canvas is in the Harvard Art Museums.

title: Marie-Antoinette with the Rose
description: The queen in a simple white muslin gaulle holding a single rose, a deliberately informal court image the painter produced for the Salon. Public outrage at the chemise dress forced the picture's withdrawal and replacement with a more conventionally regal version.

title: Romantic Landscape with Sheep at a Spring
description: A flock of sheep clusters around a stone spring in a wooded valley, with a herdsman half-glimpsed beneath the dense trees. Gainsborough painted the rural fantasy in 1783 from clay and broccoli models arranged on his studio table, and presented it to the Royal Academy as his diploma work on his election.

title: The Angora Cat
description: A young woman in a white dress cradles a fluffy Angora cat against her shoulder, the animal staring back at the viewer. Painted between 1783 and 1785 in collaboration with Marguerite Gerard, who had entered Fragonard's household as a pupil and sister-in-law, the panel hangs in the Wallraf-Richartz Museum in Cologne (inv. WRM 3652).

title: The Death of Major Peirson
description: British soldiers rally over the body of Major Francis Peirson after the French assault on Jersey in January 1781, the Union flag advancing through the smoke of the market square at St Helier. Copley's 1783 history painting, commissioned by the print publisher John Boydell, hangs in Tate Britain.

title: The Defeat of the Floating Batteries at Gibraltar
description: Spanish and French floating batteries burn at anchor under the guns of Gibraltar on the night of 13 September 1782, the rock looming behind the rescued sailors in the foreground. Copley spent eight years on the vast canvas, commissioned by the Corporation of the City of London, which still hangs in the Guildhall.

title: The Mall in St. James's Park
description: Fashionable Londoners promenade in pairs and small groups under the avenue of trees in St James's Park, their pale dresses catching the filtered light. Gainsborough modelled the figures from a doll dressed in different gowns; the canvas of 1783 is held by the Frick Collection in New York.

title: Dr Richard Price
description: The dissenting minister and political philosopher Richard Price sits in his study reading a 1784 letter from Benjamin Franklin, a longstanding correspondent. West painted Price in 1784, the year the National Library of Wales journal records the sittings; the portrait now belongs to the National Museum of Wales.

title: Oath of the Horatii
description: Three brothers extend their arms to swear an oath on the swords their father holds aloft, while their womenfolk collapse in grief at the right. David painted the canvas in Rome in 1784 to 1785 for Louis XVI, and its severe Doric setting and frieze-like composition became the manifesto of Neoclassical history painting; it hangs in the Louvre.

title: Portrait of Charles-Alexandre de Calonne
description: The Controller-General of Finances under Louis XVI shown at his desk, gesturing to a state document. The portrait, lavishly painted in silks and gilt, became notorious as evidence at court of the painter's alleged closeness to her Versailles sitters.

title: Portrait of Marie Gabrielle de Gramont
description: The young duchesse sits in a relaxed pose, an open book in her lap and her powdered hair tumbling in fashionable disarray. Vigée Le Brun, official portraitist to Marie-Antoinette, favoured this informality of dress as a calculated marker of natural sensibility.

title: Sir Joshua Reynolds
description: Sir Joshua Reynolds, first president of the Royal Academy, sits in a brown coat with his wig powdered, glancing alertly at the viewer. Stuart painted his master in 1784 during the years he spent in Reynolds's London circle; the portrait is held by the National Gallery of Art in Washington.

title: Dovedale by Moonlight
description: A silvered view of the Derbyshire valley of Dovedale under a full moon, its limestone crags and quiet river rendered in a cool, near-monochrome palette. Wright pursued nocturnes throughout his career, applying the dramatic chiaroscuro he developed for candlelit interiors to the open landscape.

title: Horror
description: Plate showing a head wrenched back in horror, eyes wide and hair lifted, from Charles Le Brun's catalogue of the passions. The red-brown stipple engraving was issued by Bowles around 1785 as part of his English edition of Le Brun's lecture on expression, a treatise that codified facial expression for academic painters for over a century.

title: John Philip Kemble
description: The tragedian John Philip Kemble appears bust-length in a dark coat and white cravat, the face modelled with the sober directness Stuart used for his stage portraits. Painted in 1785 around the time of Kemble's London debut as Hamlet, the canvas is NPG 49 in the National Portrait Gallery, London.

title: Mrs Siddons
description: The actress Sarah Siddons sits in profile against a red curtain, wearing a striped silk dress and a wide black plumed hat. Gainsborough painted his rival to Reynolds's celebrated Tragic Muse in 1785, complaining of the difficulty of her nose; the canvas hangs in the National Gallery, London.

title: Plate from Le Brun
description: An engraved head demonstrates one of the expressions catalogued by Charles Le Brun in his 1668 lecture on the passions of the soul, drawn in red and brown ink. The plate comes from Carington Bowles's English edition published in London around 1785; the impression belongs to the Wellcome Collection.

title: Portrait of Benjamin West
description: The history painter Benjamin West sits in his London studio, brush and palette set aside, the face turned in three-quarter view. Stuart painted his teacher and patron around 1783 to 1785 during his apprentice years on Newman Street, paying back the older painter who had taken him in when he arrived from Newport.

title: Portrait of Georgiana
description: Georgiana Cavendish, Duchess of Devonshire, stands beside a stone urn in a white silk dress and a wide tilted black hat trimmed with feathers. Gainsborough painted the Whig hostess between 1785 and 1787; the canvas was stolen from Agnew's gallery in 1876, recovered in Chicago in 1901, and is now at Chatsworth.
credit: Original uploader was Pendragon09 at en.wikipedia Later version(s) were uploaded by Paul Barlow at en.wikipedia .

title: Portrait of Joseph Brant
description: The Mohawk leader Thayendanegea, known to the British as Joseph Brant, appears bust-length in a fur-edged blue coat, silver gorget, and feathered headdress. Stuart painted Brant in London in 1785 during the Mohawk leader's diplomatic mission to negotiate land grants for Loyalist Iroquois resettled in Upper Canada after the American war.

title: Portrait of Mrs. Richard Brinsley Sheridan
dateCreated: between 1785 and 1787 Romanticism (second half of 18 th century –first half of 19 th century )
description: A full-length portrait of the singer and society beauty Elizabeth Linley, wife of the playwright Sheridan, posed against a windswept landscape. Gainsborough merges sitter and setting through fluttering drapery and feathery foliage in his late, freely brushed manner.
credit: National Gallery of Art pen Access Images Project. Link: https://www.nga.gov/content/ngaweb/Collection/art-object-page.99.html

title: Scorn" from Le Brun
description: Head turned aside with brow raised and lip curled to illustrate the passion of scorn, drawn from Charles Le Brun's lecture on expression. Issued by Bowles around 1785 in red-brown ink as part of his English Passions of the Soul, the print belongs to the long afterlife of Le Brun's 1668 lecture to the French Academy.

title: Simple bodily pain
description: Head contracted around tightened brow and grimacing mouth to illustrate simple bodily pain, after Charles Le Brun. The red-brown stipple engraving was issued by Bowles around 1785 in his English Passions of the Soul, one of many reprints that carried Le Brun's expression studies into eighteenth-century drawing manuals.

title: Alexander III of Scotland Rescued from the Fury of a Stag by the Intrepidity of Colin Fitzgerald
description: Colin Fitzgerald spears a charging stag as the young King Alexander III recoils on his horse, the hunt party scattering in the Highland glen. Commissioned in 1786 by Francis Humberston Mackenzie to assert his clan's descent from Fitzgerald, West treats the medieval Scottish episode with the heroic compositional logic he had established in The Death of General Wolfe.

title: Portrait of Madame Molé-Reymond
description: The actress of the Comédie-Italienne turns toward the viewer in a fur-trimmed coat and broad black hat, a muff held loosely at her side. Vigée Le Brun catches the sitter mid-movement with a fresh, animated brushwork that announces the informal, theatrical portraiture of the late ancien régime.

provenance.collection: Department of Paintings of the Louvre

title: George Augustus Eliott
description: The defender of Gibraltar stands in scarlet uniform on the ramparts, the Rock's batteries smoking behind him during the Great Siege. Copley painted the portrait in 1787 as a study for his vast Siege of Gibraltar canvas, now in the National Portrait Gallery, London.

title: Sarah Siddons
description: The tragedienne Sarah Siddons sits in a powder-blue dress, her gaze direct, her hair upswept under a soft cap. Stuart painted the portrait in 1787 during his London years, when Siddons was the leading Shakespearean actress at Drury Lane; it now hangs at the National Portrait Gallery as NPG 50.

title: The Death of Socrates
description: Socrates sits upright on his prison bed, one hand reaching for the cup of hemlock, the other raised in mid-discourse as his grieving disciples surround him.
