David painted the canvas in 1787 for Charles-Michel Trudaine de la Sabliere, exhibiting it at the Salon as a Neoclassical exemplum of stoic civic virtue; it now hangs at the Metropolitan Museum of Art.

title: The Institution of the Order of the Garter
description: Edward III invests the founding knights of the Order of the Garter in 1348, the Black Prince kneeling at the centre of a crowded hall hung with banners. West painted the picture for George III's Audience Chamber at Windsor as part of a chivalric history cycle; it remains in the Royal Collection as RCIN 407521.

title: The Marquise de Pezay
description: A double portrait set out of doors, the Marquise de Pezay seated beside the Marquise de Rougé, whose two young sons press in beside her. Painted on the eve of the Revolution, the canvas blends the natural settings and tender maternal grouping that Vigée Le Brun had refined in her portraits of Marie Antoinette and her circle.
credit: www.ne.jp; National Gallery of Art, Washington, DC

title: The Marsham Children
description: The four Marsham children of Stratton Strawless play in a wooded landscape, the eldest girl gathering nuts while her brother reaches up to a sapling. Gainsborough painted the group portrait in 1787, the year before his death, combining the conversation-piece tradition with the feathery foliage and silvery palette of his late manner.

title: Edward III Crossing The Somme
description: Edward III leads his army across the tidal ford at Blanchetaque in August 1346, mounted knights pressing forward as French defenders contest the far bank. Part of the Windsor history cycle commissioned by George III, West's canvas was painted in 1788 and is catalogued in the Royal Collection as RCIN 404566.

title: Edward III with the Black Prince after the Battle of Crécy
description: Edward III embraces his sixteen-year-old son the Black Prince on the field of Crecy in August 1346, French dead heaped at their feet. The 1788 canvas belongs to West's eight-picture chivalric cycle for the Audience Chamber at Windsor Castle, where it remains as RCIN 407523.

title: Élisabeth-Louise Vigée-Le Brun - Hubert Robert
description: The painter of picturesque ruins, Hubert Robert, is shown half-length in painter's smock, palette in hand, his unruly hair and quick-eyed glance conveying improvisatory energy. Vigée Le Brun's portrait of her colleague is a touchstone of late Ancien Régime artistic friendship, executed shortly before the Revolution dispersed both sitter and painter.

title: King Lear
description: Lear rages bareheaded on the heath as the Fool and disguised Edgar shelter against a wind-torn hovel, the storm tearing across a black sky. Painted in 1788 for John Boydell's Shakespeare Gallery, West's canvas illustrates Act III, scene 4; it now belongs to the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.

title: Paris and Helen
description: Paris reclines half-naked with a lyre while a draped Helen leans against him in a Greek interior, a marble caryatid framing the alcove. Commissioned by the comte d'Artois in 1788, David's canvas is now in the Louvre and exhibits the archaeological exactness he drew from his Roman sketchbooks.

title: Portrait of Monsieur de Lavoisier and his Wife
description: The chemist Antoine Lavoisier looks up from a manuscript while his wife Marie-Anne leans on his shoulder, their pneumatic apparatus arrayed on a red-draped table. David completed the double portrait in 1788, the year Lavoisier published the Traite elementaire de chimie; it entered the Metropolitan Museum of Art in 1977 as accession 1977.10.
credit: Metropolitan Museum of Art : entry 436106 (accession number: 1977.10)

title: Portrait of Muhammad Dervish Khan
description: Tipu Sultan's ambassador to the court of Louis XVI stands full-length in robes of patterned silk, hand resting on a sabre. Painted in Paris in 1788 on the eve of revolution, the work remained in the artist's possession for fifty years as a record of her cosmopolitan clientele.

title: Thomas Gage John Singleton Copley
description: General Thomas Gage stands in the scarlet coat of a British commander, his right hand resting on a cane, an encampment visible behind him. Copley's three-quarter-length canvas measures 127 by 101 cm and is inscribed at the lower right with Gage's name and death date of 1788; it belongs to the Paul Mellon Collection at the Yale Center for British Art.
credit: Yale Center for British Art, Paul Mellon Collection

title: A Moonlight with a Lighthouse
description: A Tyrrhenian lighthouse silhouetted against a cool, full moon over the Italian coast, recalled from Wright's 1773-75 sojourn near Naples. The painting exemplifies his fascination with competing light sources, here moonlight alone setting the spectral palette.

title: Elisabeth Louise Vigée-Lebrun
description: The painter is shown embracing her young daughter Julie in a Neoclassical interior, both wearing simple white chemise dresses. The intimate, sentimental staging was calculated to project natural maternal feeling for a Salon audience on the eve of revolution.

provenance.collection: Department of Paintings of the Louvre

title: Portrait of John FitzGibbon
description: John FitzGibbon, the future 1st Earl of Clare, sits in a wig and dark coat with the loose neckcloth of an Irish barrister. Stuart painted the portrait in 1789, during the years FitzGibbon was prosecuting cases that would lead to his appointment as Lord Chancellor of Ireland in the following year.

title: The Burghers of Calais
description: Six leading citizens of Calais, ropes around their necks and city keys in hand, kneel before Edward III as Queen Philippa pleads for their lives. West's 1789 canvas illustrates the chronicle by Froissart of the surrender of 1347 and forms part of the Windsor history cycle for George III, catalogued in the Royal Collection.

title: The Lictors Bring to Brutus the Bodies of His Sons
description: The Roman consul Brutus sits in shadow as lictors return the bodies of his sons, executed for treason on his order. David exhibited the picture at the Salon weeks after the storming of the Bastille, and Revolutionary audiences read its civic stoicism as immediate political instruction.

provenance.collection: Department of Paintings of the Louvre

title: The Washington Family
description: George Washington, Martha, and her two grandchildren stand around a draped table on the Mount Vernon terrace, a map of the new federal city of Washington spread before them. Savage worked on the group portrait between 1789 and 1796 and engraved a popular print after it; the canvas is now at the National Gallery of Art.

title: A View of the Archbishop's Palace
description: Submitted to the Royal Academy in April 1790, the month Turner turned fifteen, this was his exhibition debut. The watercolour shows a topographical precision learned from Thomas Malton, the architecture set at sharp angles to flaunt the teenager's grasp of perspective.

title: Anne-Marie-Louise Thélusson
description: Anne-Marie-Louise Thelusson, Comtesse de Sorcy, sits in a white empire-line gown with a pink shawl, her dark curls falling against an unornamented grey wall. David painted the Geneva banker's daughter in 1790, the austere setting and unbroken contour typifying his Revolution-era female portraits; the picture is now in the Neue Pinakothek, Munich.
credit: http://www.wga.hu/frames-e.html?/html/d/david_j/2/210david.html Original uploader was Gogafax at en.wikipedia ; transfer was stated to be made by User:kirtap .

title: Countess Ekaterina Vassilievna Skavronskaia
description: The Russian countess reclines in a white empire-line gown trimmed with gauze, painted during Vigée Le Brun's emigration years among the European aristocracy. The picture's smooth porcelain finish and pearly tonality typify her courtly manner adapted to Saint Petersburg taste.

title: Fisherman's Cottage
description: A modest coastal cottage on the Kentish cliffs, rendered in the picturesque idiom Turner absorbed from Thomas Girtin and the watercolour tradition. The sheet dates from his teenage years working up topographical views for the print market.

title: Maria Luisa di Borbone
description: The Neapolitan princess, later Holy Roman Empress as wife of Francis II, painted during Vigée Le Brun's Italian sojourn after fleeing the French Revolution. The portraitist's flattering palette and soft, naturalistic informality made her a favourite of Europe's exiled royalty.

title: Portrait of Emma
description: Emma Hart, later Lady Hamilton, sits in three-quarter view with cascading dark hair and an open shawl, her gaze turned outward. The portrait reflects Vigée Le Brun's Italian period and her interest in the antique 'attitudes' for which Hamilton was already celebrated in Naples.

title: Portrait of Princess Maria Christina
description: A Bourbon princess of the Two Sicilies depicted with the soft, flushed informality Vigée Le Brun favoured for royal sitters. Painted during the artist's long European exile after fleeing Revolutionary France, the portrait carries her trademark blend of neoclassical poise and rococo warmth.

title: Self-portrait
description: Painted in Florence for the Uffizi's gallery of artists' self-portraits during her revolutionary exile, Vigée Le Brun shows herself at the easel sketching Marie Antoinette. The picture asserts both her professional standing as portraitist to the queen and her loyalty in the face of political upheaval.
credit: Art Renewal Center old image: from [1]

title: Titania and Bottom
description: The fairy queen, drugged by Oberon's love-juice, fawns over the ass-headed weaver from A Midsummer Night's Dream. Fuseli, a key contributor to Boydell's Shakespeare Gallery, exaggerates limbs and eyes into a mannerist dream-language drawn from Michelangelo and his own night terrors.

title: Le Serment du Jeu de paume
description: Deputies of the Third Estate raise their right hands and swear not to disperse until France has a constitution, packed into the Versailles tennis court on 20 June 1789. David's monumental project of 1791, recording the event from sketches and portrait studies, survives only as a large pen-and-ink drawing now at the Musee Carnavalet.

title: Portrait of Hyacinthe-Gabrielle Roland
description: The young Irish actress and future Marchioness Wellesley sits with a drift of sash and ribboned hair against a wooded ground. Vigée Le Brun's London exile period produced a string of such portraits in her airy, neoclassical mode of softened drapery and glowing skin.

provenance.collection: Fine Arts Museums of San Francisco

title: Life Study of Lady Hamilton as the Cumaean Sybil
description: Emma Hamilton turns in the studio with a turbaned head and parted lips, posed as the prophetic Sibyl of Cumae. Vigée Le Brun carried the resulting composition through her exile from Naples to Vienna and Russia as a calling card of her Italian period.

title: The Rising Squall
description: An early oil view from the cliffs above the Avon Gorge as a sudden storm sweeps in over the Hot Wells spa. The seventeen-year-old Turner already orchestrates wind, rain and shifting light into a unified atmospheric event.
credit: Sotheby's, London, 2 July 2025, L25033, lot 28 ( 2000 × 1609 pixel / 1,40 MB ) — with frame

title: Catherine Brass Yates
description: Catherine Brass Yates sews with white thread, her head turned in a half-glance, a black cap framing her grey curls. Stuart painted the New York merchant's wife in 1793 just after his return from Dublin; the canvas is now in the Andrew W. Mellon Collection at the National Gallery of Art.

title: Clare Hall and King’s College Chapel
description: An early topographical watercolour from Turner's Cambridge tour, viewing Clare Hall and the soaring Perpendicular pinnacles of King's College Chapel across the Cam. Drawn at eighteen, the sheet shows the precise architectural draftsmanship that earned him admission to the Royal Academy schools.

title: Horatio Gates
description: The Continental Army general Horatio Gates stands in his blue and buff Revolutionary uniform, the laurel of his Saratoga victory implied in the laurel-coloured drape. Stuart painted the portrait between 1793 and 1794 in New York; it is now in the collection of the Metropolitan Museum of Art.
credit: Downloaded from The Athenaeum original is at the Metropolitan Museum of Art.

title: King Lear and Cordelia
description: The mad Lear, crowned in wildflowers, is reunited with the kneeling Cordelia at the French camp in Act IV, scene 7 of Shakespeare's tragedy. West painted the canvas in 1793 for John Boydell's Shakespeare Gallery; it now belongs to the Folger Shakespeare Library.
credit: Folger Shakespeare Library Digital Image Collection http://luna.folger.edu/luna/servlet/s/0847d6

title: Portrait of La comtesse Siemontkowsky Bystry
description: A society portrait from Vigée Le Brun's twelve-year exile after fleeing revolutionary Paris, when she travelled the courts of Italy, Vienna, and Saint Petersburg. Soft pastel-key flesh tones, a feathered hat, and a deliberately informal pose carry forward the Marie-Antoinette idiom that made her career.

title: Princess Karoline von Liechtenstein
description: The young princess is presented as Iris, draped in classicizing white muslin against a stormy sky, a length of rainbow gauze trailing from her shoulder. Vigée Le Brun painted her in Vienna during the émigré years that followed the artist's flight from revolutionary France.

title: The Death of Marat
description: The murdered Jacobin Jean-Paul Marat slumps in his medicinal bathtub, the bloodied knife on the floor and Charlotte Corday's letter still in his hand. David finished the canvas in October 1793, three months after the assassination, presenting it to the National Convention as a martyr's icon; it is now in the Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium, Brussels.

title: Courtyard with Lunatics or Yard with Madmen
description: A small tin-plate painting from Goya's recovery after the illness that left him deaf, drawing on a violent scene he claimed to have witnessed in Zaragoza. Naked inmates wrestle under a barred opening while a warden flogs them, the cell's harsh chiaroscuro foreshadowing the Black Paintings.
credit: The Meadows Museum's Permanent Collection , accessed 2010-03-20.

title: Ebisu
description: An ukiyo-e print issued during Sharaku's brief, intense ten-month career, depicting a kabuki actor in the role of the smiling fisherman-deity Ebisu. The mica-grounded portrait style condenses a stage character into bold contour and exaggerated expression.
credit: Yamaguchi, Keizaburō (1994). Sharaku no Zenbō 写楽の全貌 (in Japanese). Tōkyō Shoseki. ISBN 978-4-487-79075-3 .

title: Gentlemen Fishing
description: Two anglers in tricornes cast lines into a willow-shaded river, their dog watching from the bank under a pale English sky. West painted the modest cabinet picture in 1794 during his Hammersmith years, a rare departure from the grand-manner history subjects that occupied his Royal Academy practice.

title: PeterGansevoortByStuart
description: Peter Gansevoort, the defender of Fort Stanwix in 1777, wears the dark blue coat and gold epaulettes of a Continental general. Stuart painted the portrait in 1794, around the time Gansevoort was commissioned brigadier general of the New York militia; the canvas is now at the Munson-Williams-Proctor Arts Institute in Utica.
credit: Downloaded from the The Athenaeum Original is in the Munson-Williams-Proctor Institute of Art

title: Portrait of John Jay
description: John Jay sits in the black robes of the first Chief Justice of the United States, a closed book under his hand. Stuart began the portrait in London in 1794 while Jay was negotiating the treaty that bears his name, completing the canvas after his return; it is now in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.

title: Self-portrait
description: David paints himself at the easel in shirtsleeves and a loose dark coat, palette in one hand, brush poised in the other. He executed the self-portrait in 1794 while imprisoned in the Luxembourg Palace after the fall of Robespierre; the canvas is now in the Louvre.

title: The Angler
description: A solitary angler beside a wooded stream, painted in Turner's youthful picturesque manner. The watercolour reflects his early apprenticeship copying after Richard Wilson and the British landscape engravers.

title: William Bayard
description: The New York merchant William Bayard sits in three-quarter view, his dark coat and white stock set against a neutral ground. Stuart painted the portrait in 1794 during his New York period, before settling in Philadelphia to begin the presidential portraits that would define his career.

title: Harvesting at Windsor by Benjamin West
description: Reapers cut and bind sheaves in the fields below Windsor Castle, whose towers rise on the wooded ridge beyond. West painted the harvest scene in 1795 while serving as Surveyor of the King's Pictures, part of a series of rural subjects for George III recording the royal estate at work.

title: Musidora and Her Two Companions
description: Three nude bathers from Thomson's poem The Seasons stand at a woodland pool while Damon watches unseen from the foliage. West first painted the subject in 1795 and retouched the canvas in 1806, working in the polished neoclassical idiom expected of the President of the Royal Academy.

title: Portrait of George Washington
description: Washington faces the viewer in a black coat with white stock, his powdered hair brushed back from a high forehead. The 1795 canvas at the Metropolitan Museum (accession 07.160) belongs to the so-called Vaughan type, the first of three Washington portrait formats Stuart developed from life sittings.
credit: Metropolitan Museum of Art, online collection (accession number 07.160)

title: Portrait of Pierre Sériziat
description: Pierre Sériziat, the painter's brother-in-law, sits on a grassy bank in riding dress with crop and gloves, a yellow straw hat held in one hand. David painted the portrait in 1795 after his release from prison, where his Jacobin politics had landed him following the fall of Robespierre.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"d/david_j/3/308david"

title: Takashima Ohisa Using Two Mirrors to Observe Her Coiffure: Night of the Asakusa Marketing Festival
description: Ohisa, a celebrated Edo teahouse beauty, inspects the back of her coiffure with paired mirrors during the Asakusa autumn festival. Utamaro's precise hairlines and luminous mica-dusted ground typify his bust-portrait okubi-e of fashionable contemporary women.

title: The Nude Maja
dateCreated: 1800 / between 1795 and 1800 Romanticism (second half of 18 th century –first half of 19 th century )
description: A reclining nude meets the viewer's gaze without mythological alibi, the first life-size unidealized female nude in Spanish painting. Commissioned by prime minister Manuel Godoy for a private cabinet, the picture later drew the Inquisition's attention to Goya himself.
credit: The Nude Maja . On-line gallery . Museo del Prado (2012). Archived from the original on 2010-01-03 . Retrieved on 2013-04-07 .

title: Woodcutters in Windsor Park
description: Labourers fell and trim oaks in a clearing of Windsor Great Park, the felled trunks arranged in diagonals across the foreground. West painted the scene in 1795 as part of the royal commission documenting estate work, pairing rural labour with the picturesque conventions of late eighteenth-century landscape.

title: Alexandra and Elena Pavlovna of Russia
description: A double portrait of Grand Duchesses Alexandra and Elena Pavlovna, daughters of Paul I, painted soon after Vigée Le Brun's arrival at the Russian court in exile from revolutionary France. Soft pastel-like flesh and silvery silks display the courtly grace that made her Marie Antoinette's preferred portraitist.

title: Countess Anna Ivanovna Tolstaya
description: Painted during Vigée Le Brun's émigré years in Saint Petersburg, the Russian countess wears a soft white gown and a velvet wrap. The artist's Russian sitters helped sustain her career through the Revolution and account for many of her finest late portraits.

title: Fishermen at Sea
description: Turner's first oil exhibited at the Royal Academy, depicting a fishing boat tossed beneath a cold moon off the Needles, Isle of Wight. The contrast of silver lunar light and orange lantern glow announces a lifelong preoccupation with luminous opposition.
credit: Google Arts & Culture — UwG73jK8wqshlw Tate Images ( http://www.tate-images.com/results.asp?image=T01585&wwwflag=3&imagepos=2 )

title: George Washington
description: Washington stands in dark civilian dress beside a draped table, his right hand resting on a document. Savage based the National Gallery's circa 1796 portrait on his own life studies of the president, made during sittings in New York in 1789-90 that also fed his print The Washington Family.

title: George Washington
description: Washington stands full-length in a black velvet suit, his right hand extended over a table covered with bound volumes and a quill, an upholstered chair and crimson drapery behind. Stuart painted the Lansdowne portrait in April 1796 for William Petty, Marquess of Lansdowne, the British statesman who had supported American independence.

title: George Washington
description: The unfinished bust of Washington against a brown ground shows the sixty-four-year-old president from the chest up, his hair powdered and his mouth set over the new wooden dentures. Stuart began the Athenaeum portrait on 12 April 1796 and kept the original at his easel as the master from which he produced more than seventy replicas.

title: Kim Hong-do
description: An album leaf from the Eight Views of Hwaseong, showing the new walled city of Suwon laid out among hills and pavilions. Kim Hong-do, court painter to King Jeongjo, documented the royal fortress completed in 1796 in the ink-and-light-colour idiom of late Joseon dynasty topographic painting.

title: Martha Washington
description: Martha Washington, in a white cap and shawl, faces left in a half-length pose left unfinished against a brown ground. Stuart painted the canvas as a pendant to his Athenaeum portrait of the president in 1796, both works retained by the artist as templates and now jointly held by the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, and the National Portrait Gallery.

title: Newport Castle
description: The ruined keep of Newport Castle rises above the muddy banks of the river Usk, with figures and a small craft below. Turner painted the Welsh watercolour around 1796, the year of his first oil exhibition at the Royal Academy, drawing on sketches made during his 1795 South Wales tour.

title: George Washington
description: Washington appears in a half-length variation of the Athenaeum head, his black coat picked out against a brown background. Stuart painted this 1797 version for William Constable of New York, one of dozens of replicas in which the artist adapted his unfinished 1796 prime to standing commissions.

title: Hairdresser
description: From the Twelve Types of Women's Handicraft series, an elegant ukiyo-e study of a kamiyui dressing a client's elaborate coiffure. Utamaro's signature bijinga close-up, pale ground and supple linework foreground the intimate gestures of female labour in the pleasure quarters.

title: Portrait of Princess Anna Alexandrovna Galitzin
description: A Hermitage portrait of the Georgian-born Princess Galitzin, painted during Vigée Le Brun's long Russian exile after the Revolution. Pale silks and a soft sfumato face exemplify the flattering ancien-régime manner she carried across European courts.

title: Buttermere Lake
description: A rainbow arcs over Buttermere following a Lake District shower, the slate fells doubled in the still water below. Turner exhibited the picture at the Royal Academy aged twenty-three, after a Cumberland sketching tour. It is one of his earliest essays in the sublime mountain weather effects that would define him.

title: Shipping by a Breakwater
description: Merchant vessels ride the chop beside a stone breakwater in a dockside scene from Turner's early career, when he was building a reputation as a marine painter. The handling still leans on the Dutch seventeenth-century tradition of van de Velde.

title: Harlech Castle
description: Harlech Castle, from Tygwyn Ferry, Summer's Evening Twilig

title: John Constable by Ramsay Richard Reinagle
description: The young John Constable, then twenty-three, faces the viewer in dark coat and stock, his curling hair brushed forward. Reinagle painted the portrait in 1799, the year both men entered the Royal Academy Schools, and it now hangs in the National Portrait Gallery in London.

title: Julie as Flora
description: The painter's daughter Julie posed as the Roman flower goddess, garlanded and seen against a soft pastoral ground. The mythological costume portrait belongs to the artist's exile years following the Revolution, when she worked across the European courts.

provenance.collection: Museum of Fine Arts, St. Petersburg, Florida, USA
provenance.location: Museum of Fine Arts, St. Petersburg, Florida, USA

title: Maria Hamilton Beckford
description: Maria Hamilton Beckford, wife of the Fonthill builder William Beckford, sits in a high-waisted white gown holding a closed book. West painted the National Gallery portrait in 1799, the same year his patron's gothic abbey at Fonthill was beginning its first stages under James Wyatt.

title: Portrait de madame de Verninac by David Louvre RF1942-16 n2
description: Henriette de Verninac, sister of Eugène Delacroix, sits half-length in an Empire dress of white muslin against an olive ground, a yellow shawl draped across her lap. Jacques-Louis David painted the portrait in 1799, exhibiting it at the Salon of that year; the Louvre acquired it in 1942 (RF 1942-16).

title: The Intervention of the Sabine Women
description: Hersilia throws herself between the Roman king Romulus and her Sabine father Tatius, infants crawling at her feet as the two armies pause on the field. David painted the canvas in 1799 during and after his post-Thermidor imprisonment, intending the subject of reconciliation as a plea for an end to French factional bloodshed.

provenance.collection: Department of Paintings of the Louvre

title: The Surrender of the Dutch Admiral de Winter to Admiral Duncan at the Battle of Camperdown
description: Admiral Duncan receives the sword of the defeated Vice-Admiral de Winter on the quarterdeck of HMS Venerable after the British victory off Camperdown on 11 October 1797. Copley finished the canvas in 1799 for the City of London, now in the National Galleries of Scotland (NG 2661).

title: John Adams
description: John Adams, in a black coat and powdered hair, faces the viewer in a half-length pose against a plain ground. Stuart began the portrait around 1800, when Adams was the sitting second president, and finished it about 1815 for the former president's son John Quincy.
credit: National Gallery of Art, Washington, D. C., online collection

title: Kim Hong-do
description: A drunken Buddhist monk lies sprawled beneath a gnarled pine, a wine cup tipped beside him as a young attendant looks on. Kim Hong-do, the leading court painter of the late Joseon era, worked the subject in ink and light colour on paper around 1800, mixing genre humour with the literati ideal of the inebriated sage.

title: Napoleon Crossing the Alps
description: Bonaparte in an orange cloak reins in a rearing piebald horse on the slopes of the Great St Bernard Pass, the names of Hannibal and Karolus Magnus carved into the rock at his feet. David painted the Malmaison version in 1800, the first of five autograph variants commissioned by Charles IV of Spain after the Marengo campaign.

title: Oedipus and the Sphinx
description: Oedipus pauses on a rocky ledge to answer the riddle of the Sphinx, his polished nude profile set against deep shadow. Painted in Rome as part of Ingres's Prix de Rome obligations, it distils his Neoclassical doctrine of pure contour and idealised anatomy.

title: Portrait of Colonel Fitch and his Sisters
description: Colonel William Fitch stands in scarlet army uniform beside his charger, flanked by his sisters Sarah in neoclassical white and Ann in dark mourning. Copley painted the family group between 1800 and 1801 in London, where the American expatriate had settled and the Fitch siblings had gathered in widowhood.
credit: National Gallery of Art; National Gallery of Art, Washington, D. C., online collection

title: Portrait of George Spencer
description: George Spencer, 2nd Earl Spencer, faces the viewer in the dark coat and white stock of an Admiralty official, his hair powdered above a high collar. Copley painted the portrait around 1800, while Spencer served as First Lord of the Admiralty under William Pitt, overseeing the Royal Navy through Camperdown and the Nile.

title: Portrait of Madame Récamier
description: Juliette Récamier reclines barefoot on a Grecian couch in a high-waisted white chemise, her dark hair loosely bound, an antique lamp at her feet. David left the canvas unfinished in 1800 after disputes with the sitter and her decorator Percier, the unpainted ground and severe Pompeian furniture making it a manifesto of the new Empire taste.

title: Snow Scene
description: Kunisada, the prolific Utagawa-school designer, sets a kabuki-style figure against falling snow on the banks of an Edo river. The plush patterned kimono and densely speckled white sky show his command of beauty prints and the expanded palette of nineteenth-century woodblock printing.
credit: Online Collection of Brooklyn Museum ; Photo: Brooklyn Museum, X632.2_IMLS_PS3.jpg

title: Academic study of a male torso
description: A youthful académie made in Jacques-Louis David's studio, drawn from a posed model with painstaking anatomical observation. Such exercises were the bedrock of Ingres's Neoclassical training and prefigure the sculptural torsos in his later history paintings.

title: Kim Hong-do
description: A long horizontal handscroll in ink and colour on silk, Samgongbulhwando contrasts the freedom of nature with the burdens of office through scenes of recluses and scholars in mountain retreats. Kim Hong-do painted the scroll in 1801, measuring 133.7 by 418.4 cm and now held by the Leeum Samsung Museum of Art in Seoul.

title: Milkmaids in St. James's Park
description: Milkmaids sell pails of fresh milk to passers-by in the open ground of St James's Park, the towers of Westminster Abbey rising in the haze beyond. West painted the London genre scene in 1801, now at the Yale Center for British Art, joining royal pastoral subjects with a documentary view of city trade.

title: Study of a Male Nude
description: An academic male nude executed during Ingres's training under David, when he was competing for the Prix de Rome. The figure's smooth modelling and elongated proportions already announce the linear classicism that would define his career.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"i/ingres/00ingres"

title: Arethusa' by Benjamin West
description: The nymph Arethusa bathing in a stream, drawn from Book V of Ovid's Metamorphoses, the viewer positioned where the river god Alpheus first catches sight of her. Painted in 1802 and shown that year at the Royal Academy in London while West was its president, the canvas now hangs at the High Museum of Art in Atlanta.

title: Fishermen Upon a Lee-Shore in Squally Weather
description: Fishermen struggle to bring a sailing vessel ashore as breaking surf and squall lines press against a steep coast. An early Royal Academy exhibit, the canvas sets Turner's lifelong concern with mariners' jeopardy in a darker, more Dutch-inflected idiom.

title: Grenoble Seen from the River Drac with Mont Blanc in the Distance
description: Grenoble lies between the Drac and the distant snowfields of Mont Blanc, drawn during Turner's first Continental tour after the Peace of Amiens reopened France. The 1802 Alpine campaign permanently reshaped his sense of geological scale. The picture's stretched horizontal format prefigures his later panoramic mountain views.

title: Ships bearing up for Anchorage
description: A squally Channel scene of merchantmen turning into the wind, indebted to the Dutch tradition of Willem van de Velde. Commissioned by the third Earl of Egremont, the canvas still hangs at Petworth House where Turner often painted.

title: The Tenth Plague of Egypt
description: Storm and divine wrath sweep over a darkened Egyptian city as the firstborn die. An early bid for the prestige of Old Master history painting, the picture leans openly on Poussin's biblical compositions.

title: Tummel Bridge
description: A Highland packhorse bridge over the Tummel, recorded on Turner's 1801 Scottish tour that supplied subjects for engraved series and Walter Scott illustrations. The watercolour balances rugged geology against an open, weather-shifting sky.

title: Bonneville
description: An Alpine view from Turner's first Continental tour following the Peace of Amiens, recording the town of Bonneville against the Mont Blanc range. The classical compositional structure recalls Claude Lorrain, whom Turner studied closely as a young Royal Academician.

title: Calais Pier
description: Embarking passengers and fishwives crowd the French pier as a squall builds beyond the harbour mouth. Turner had himself crossed to Calais in rough weather in 1802, and he exhibited this large canvas to challenge the marine paintings of his French contemporaries.

title: The Pass of Saint Gotthard
description: A vertiginous Alpine gorge above the St Gotthard road, recorded on Turner's first Continental tour after the Peace of Amiens reopened Europe. The watercolour fed a series of Swiss subjects in which scale itself becomes the drama.

title: Boats Carrying Out Anchors to the Dutch Men of War
Dolley Madison
description: Dolley Madison, then wife of the Secretary of State, faces the viewer in a low-cut white Empire-waisted gown, a string of pearls at her throat and dark curls framing her face. Stuart painted the portrait in 1804 in Washington, four years before her husband became president and she emerged as the capital's leading hostess.

title: Jérôme Bonaparte by Gilbert Stuart 1804
description: Napoleon's youngest brother sits for an American portraitist while honeymooning in Baltimore with his first wife, Elizabeth Patterson. Stuart painted the 19-year-old Jérôme on canvas at 28 1/4 inches, the loose brushwork of the unfinished collar typical of his late Boston manner.

title: Newton
description: Blake's monoprint shows the natural philosopher hunched naked on a sea-floor rock, drawing geometric figures with a compass. The image reads as a critique of pure reason: Newton, absorbed in measurement, becomes blind to the imaginative cosmos beyond his diagram.

title: Portrait of Anna Payne Cutts
description: Dolley Madison's younger sister Anna Payne Cutts, wife of Massachusetts congressman Richard Cutts, sits in a soft white gown against a neutral ground. Stuart painted her in Washington shortly after her marriage, working in the bust-length format he reserved for society wives of the early Republic.

title: Ancient city at the foot of a mountain
description: An imagined Greek polis spreads along a rocky promontory, temples and stoa stacked up the slope toward a fortified acropolis. Schinkel painted the canvas in Berlin around 1806, years before his architectural career began, channelling his early training as a stage and panorama painter into archaeological reverie.

title: Coronation of Emperor Napoleon I and Coronation of the Empress Josephine in Notre-Dame de Paris
description: Joséphine kneels before Napoleon at Notre-Dame as he prepares to set the crown on her head, with Pope Pius VII seated behind him. David's nearly ten-metre canvas, painted between 1805 and 1807 and now in the Louvre, recasts a self-coronation as an act of dynastic ritual, with the dethroned king's mother inserted into the gallery despite her absence from the event.

title: Fall of the Rhine at Schaffhausen
description: The thundering Rheinfall in Switzerland, its spray rising into a churning sky encountered on Turner's first Continental tour after the Peace of Amiens. The painting marks his early engagement with the Alpine sublime that would shape his Romantic vocabulary.

title: Kim Hong-do
description: An autumn night landscape illustrating Ouyang Xiu's prose poem on the sound of autumn, the Chuseongbu, with wind-bent trees, distant mountains, and the Song poet's calligraphy occupying the upper half of the silk. Kim Hongdo painted it in 1805, late in his career as Joseon Korea's leading court painter, fusing Chinese literary subject with his characteristic ink-wash atmosphere.

title: Philipp Otto Runge
description: A close study of a hound's head in chalk and lead, the breed's soft fur and alert eye observed with quiet precision. The drawing belongs to Runge's wider effort to ground his Romantic symbolism in patient natural observation.

title: Portrait of Pope Pius VII
description: Pope Pius VII sits in white papal vestments and red cape, his hand resting on the arm of an ornate chair, painted in Paris in 1805 as the pontiff lingered in the city after Napoleon's coronation. David made the portrait now in the Louvre during one of the sittings the pope reluctantly granted on the emperor's order.

title: Sunset on the River
description: An English river caught at the end of the day, with rushes and a low bank silhouetted against burning sky. The work belongs to the loose Thames oil sketches Turner made from his boat around Walton and Windsor.

title: The Deluge
description: An early biblical disaster scene depicting the universal flood, with massed bodies struggling against rising water beneath churning storm clouds. Turner builds the composition from a baroque diagonal of light, a precedent for his later sublime catastrophes.

title: The Hülsenbeck Children
dateCreated: between 1805 and 1806 Romanticism (second half of 18 th century –first half of 19 th century )
description: Three young siblings of the Hülsenbeck family stand and crouch in a Hamburg garden, the toddler clutching a sunflower leaf almost as large as himself. Runge invests the children with hieratic gravity, treating childhood as a metaphysical state.

title: The Shipwreck
description: Survivors clinging to lifeboats amid mountainous green seas, the doomed vessel rolling beyond. Engraved by Charles Turner, this was the first of the artist's canvases reproduced as a mezzotint, spreading his fame as a painter of catastrophe.
credit: Google Arts & Culture — LwFch0SXuzBAIw Tate Images ( http://www.tate-images.com/results.asp?image=N00476&wwwflag=3&imagepos=1 )

title: Willows beside a Stream
description: A screen of willows leans over still water in an unforced piece of Thames-side observation. It belongs to the group of small oil sketches Turner kept in his studio rather than exhibiting.

title: Windsor Castle from the Thames
description: The royal castle rides above the river on its chalk bluff, painted from Turner's boat on one of his summer Thames campaigns. Sky and water are set down in long, wet sweeps that leave the paint visibly mobile.

title: Linlithgow Palace
description: The ruined Stewart royal palace above its loch in West Lothian, drawn from Turner's Scottish sketching tours undertaken for engraved topographical series. Soft watercolour washes blend the masonry into the surrounding landscape.

title: Newark Abbey
description: The Augustinian ruin on the Wey in Surrey, its broken walls reflected in still water. Turner mined such Gothic remains for the picturesque subjects favoured by Romantic patrons and the engraving trade.

title: Peter on the sea
description: Christ stretches out his hand to a sinking Peter on the Sea of Galilee, the figures reduced to clear, near-archaic outlines. Runge's interpretation of the Gospel episode reflects his ambition to fuse landscape, religion, and Romantic symbolism.

title: Robert Fulton
description: Steamboat engineer Robert Fulton, then thirty, leans against a draped table while sitting for his teacher Benjamin West in London, the year before the Clermont's first run up the Hudson. The 36 by 28 inch oil on canvas, gifted by Stephen C. Clark to the Fenimore Art Museum, dates from Fulton's final European stay as artist and inventor.
credit: Benjamin West, American, 1738-1820. Robert Fulton, 1806, London, England. Oil on canvas, 36 1/4 × 28 1/4 in. (92.08 × 71.76 cm). Fenimore Art Museum, Cooperstown, N.Y., gift of Stephen C. Clark, N0218.1961. Photograph by Richard Walker.

title: Shipping at the Mouth of the Thames
description: Working vessels labouring in the Thames estuary chop, sails braced against a low, weather-laden sky. The painting belongs to Turner's productive run of estuary subjects answering his rivalry with the marine tradition of van de Velde.
credit: Google Arts & Culture — qgGcWeWQCxwJMQ Tate Images ( http://www.tate-images.com/results.asp?image=N02702&wwwflag=3&imagepos=1 )

title: The Death of Nelson
description: Vice-Admiral Nelson collapses on the quarterdeck of HMS Victory at Trafalgar, surrounded by officers and ratings in a tightly compressed crowd. West composed the 1806 canvas, now at the Walker Art Gallery in Liverpool, in deliberate echo of his own Death of General Wolfe, applying his epic modern-history formula to a second imperial martyr.

title: The Victory Returning from Trafalgar
description: Nelson's flagship shown in three rotated views entering Sheerness with the admiral's body aboard, after Turner sketched her at anchor. The triple study reflects his marine fascination and the national mourning that followed Trafalgar.

title: Walton bridges
description: Cattle wade in the Thames below the timber arches of Walton Bridges, drawn from Turner's sketching campaigns along the river. The picture marks his transition from topographical watercolour into open-air oil painting.

title: Washington at Dorchester Heights
description: George Washington in Continental uniform stands beside his horse on the Boston-area hill where his artillery emplacement forced the British evacuation in March 1776. Stuart painted the full-length composition in 1806 for the Boston town fathers; it now hangs at the Museum of Fine Arts and remains the city's official Washington portrait.
credit: Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, online database

title: Weir and Cattle
description: Cattle wade in the slow water below a country weir in one of Turner's pastoral Thames-valley sketches. The thin oil handling and silvery palette recall his admiration for Cuyp.

title: Cassiobury Park: Reaping
description: Harvesters work an open field on the Earl of Essex's estate at Cassiobury in Hertfordshire. The painting was a private commission produced alongside a series of watercolours of the park. It shows Turner extending his Claudean pastoral mode to a contemporary English country-house setting.

title: Cliveden on Thames
description: A Thames-side prospect of the wooded Cliveden cliffs in Buckinghamshire, the river curling beneath in pale silver. Turner repeatedly returned to the Thames as a quintessentially English subject, here softening topography into atmospheric haze.
credit: Google Arts & Culture — AAF7MnUg-TIdUQ Tate Images ( http://www.tate-images.com/results.asp?image=N01180&wwwflag=3&imagepos=1 )

title: Cross in the Mountains
description: A wayside crucifix stands atop a fir-clad alpine peak, gilded by rays of an unseen setting sun. Originally an altarpiece for the Tetschen chapel, the work provoked the so-called Ramdohr controversy by daring to treat pure landscape as a vehicle of religious revelation.

title: Newark Abbey on the River Wey
description: The ruined Augustinian priory of Newark stands above the still waters of the Wey, framed by trees and scattered cattle. Turner adopts the picturesque vocabulary of the topographical watercolorists, softened by an early painterly attention to reflected light.

title: The Battle of Trafalgar
description: A close-quarters view of Nelson's flagship Victory at Trafalgar, taken from the mizen-shrouds rather than the more conventional broadside vantage. Turner had boarded Victory on her return to the Medway and used the sketches he made there to anchor the smoke-wreathed scene.

title: The Junction of the Thames and the Medway
description: An estuary scene with merchantmen and a small boat tossed in choppy water where the two rivers meet. Turner builds the squally light from layered glazes, showing his early debt to Dutch marine painters.

title: The Thames near Windsor
description: A quiet reach of the upper Thames painted from the boat Turner had fitted out as a floating studio. The fluid handling belongs to the Thames oil sketches in which he loosened his manner before the public ever saw it.

title: Tree Tops and Sky
description: Most of the panel is given over to evening sky, with foliage massed at the lower edge and Guildford Castle barely indicated. The composition foreshadows Turner's later willingness to let weather dominate topography.

title: Vue du lac de Challes et du Mont Blanc
description: A Savoyard panorama of Lake Challes with Mont Blanc rising in the distance, unusual within the painter's output for being a pure landscape rather than a portrait. The view records her travels through the Alps during her long emigration from revolutionary France.
credit: Minneapolis Institute of Art, online collection

title: Cupid and Psyche
description: The winged god Cupid lifts his sleeping mortal bride Psyche into an embrace against a dim chamber, after the Apuleius tale. West painted the 1808 canvas, now at Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art, during his presidency of the Royal Academy, the heroic nudes typical of his late mythological commissions for London collectors.
credit: Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art

title: La Grande baigneuse
description: Painted in Rome as one of Ingres's required envois to the Académie, the canvas presents a seated nude from behind, head wrapped in a striped turban. The smooth contour of the back, lifted to the surface as pure drawing, became a touchstone for the artist's later Turkish bath subjects.

provenance.collection: Department of Paintings of the Louvre

title: Mrs. James Swan
description: Hepzibah Clarke Swan, wife of the speculator James Swan, sits in a high-waisted dress with a sheer wrap around her shoulders. Stuart painted her in Boston in 1808; the portrait, accession 27.539 at the Museum of Fine Arts, joined the museum from the sitter's descendants over a century later.

title: Purfleet and the Essex Shore as seen from Long Reach
description: Sailing barges and Thames hoys ride the broad estuary off the chalk cliffs of Purfleet, the low Essex shore stretching beyond. The watercolor belongs to Turner's early topographical phase, when accurate maritime detail was still the foundation of his atmospheric effects.

title: Sheerness as seen from the Nore
description: Naval shipping anchored at the Nore sandbank off the Kent dockyard, with rigging and bunting catching wet wind. Turner exhibited the canvas at his own gallery, courting comparison with Dutch marine masters in scale and atmosphere.

title: The Colossus
dateCreated: after 1808 Romanticism (second half of 18 th century –first half of 19 th century )
description: A naked giant rises behind a mountain ridge as a panicked crowd and herds flee across the plain below. Long attributed to Goya and tied to the Peninsular War, the picture stages collective terror with the bituminous darkness of his late, troubled imagination.

title: The Confluence of the Thames and Medway
description: Estuary shipping gathers where Thames and Medway meet, painted in the tradition of seventeenth-century Dutch sea pieces. Heavy cloud and a low horizon underline Turner's command of English coastal weather.

title: The painter and writer Friedrich August von Klinkowström
description: A portrait of the painter and writer Friedrich August von Klinkowström, Runge's close friend and a fellow figure in early German Romantic circles. The sitter is shown with a Nazarene-like clarity of contour and a steady, contemplative gaze.

title: The Siege of Cozel
description: A panoramic battle scene of the 1807 siege of Cosel in Silesia, Bavarian troops repulsing a Prussian sortie across an open foreground while the fortress smokes in the distance. Kobell, court painter in Munich, here works in the large-format Schlachtenbild tradition, organising hundreds of small figures within a clear, brightly lit landscape.

title: Fishing upon the Blythe-Sand
description: Estuarine fishermen at low water on the Thames, the horizon line dropped to expose a vast, muted sky. The subdued grey-and-cream palette reflects Turner's study of seventeenth-century Dutch marine painters such as van de Velde.
credit: Google Arts & Culture — MQG2rOTbb5MaqQ Tate Images ( http://www.tate-images.com/results.asp?image=N00496&wwwflag=3&imagepos=1 )

title: London from Greenwich Park
description: A panoramic survey of the capital seen from the hill at Greenwich, with the Queen's House and Wren's Royal Hospital below and St Paul's hazed in coal-smoke distance. The painting belongs to a series celebrating the Thames as the artery of empire.
credit: Google Arts & Culture — IAHskvl8KuvdYw Tate Images ( http://www.tate-images.com/results.asp?image=N00483&wwwflag=3&imagepos=1 )

title: Mrs. Harrison Gray Otis
description: Sally Foster Otis, wife of the Federalist senator and mayor of Boston, sits in a white empire-line gown with a red shawl draped at her elbow. Stuart painted her in Boston in 1809, the canvas now held by the Reynolda House Museum of American Art in Winston-Salem.
credit: The Reynolda House Museum of American Art

title: Omnia Vincit Amor Alternative title
description: Cupid wrestles a heavy lion to the ground in a wooded clearing, illustrating Virgil's tag that love conquers all. West signed the canvas in 1809 and it entered the Metropolitan Museum of Art in 1895 as accession 95.22.1, one of his late London allegories aimed at the British print market.
credit: Metropolitan Museum of Art, online collection (accession number 95.22.1)

title: Philipp Otto Runge
description: A preparatory drawing in chalk and pencil for the unfinished Great Morning, mapping out the central goddess-figure rising amid lilies and infant spirits. The sheet shows Runge's diagrammatic approach to his cosmological Times of Day cycle.

title: The Abbey in the Oakwood
description: A procession of monks bears a coffin into the snow-rimed ruin of a Gothic abbey, the gnarled oaks around them silhouetted against a pale winter dusk. Friedrich exhibited the canvas in Berlin alongside Mönch am Meer as a Romantic meditation on death and resurrection.

title: The Garreteer’s Petition
description: A poet implores his muse in a cramped attic, an unusually literary genre subject for Turner. Exhibited at the Royal Academy with verses of his own composition, it shows him courting the hierarchy of history painting.

title: The Great Morning
description: A detail from the unfinished Great Morning, showing the radiant central figure Runge devised as the embodiment of dawn within his Times of Day cycle. The hard-edged drawing and saturated colour reveal the artist's mystical, almost emblematic Romanticism.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"r/runge/2morning"

title: The Trout Stream
description: An angler casts beside a wooded English river in a pastoral key drawn from Claude Lorrain. Painted in Turner's early Thames-and-Wales manner, the composition balances feathery foliage against a glassy reach of water.

title: Thomson's Aeolian Harp
description: A pastoral elegy for the poet James Thomson, with classical figures grouped on a hillside above the Thames at Richmond. Turner pairs the picture with verses of his own, blending Claudean idyll and literary tribute.

title: Abigail Smith Adams
description: The former First Lady, in her late sixties, sits in a black gown with a white lace cap and ruff, painted at her Quincy farm during Stuart's visits between 1810 and 1815. The unfinished canvas at the National Gallery of Art in Washington was begun as a pendant to the matching seated portrait of John Adams.
credit: National Gallery of Art, Washington, D. C., online collection

title: Grande Odalisque
dateCreated: 1810 Romanticism (second half of 18 th century –first half of 19 th century )
description: A reclining concubine turns her head over a famously elongated back -- Ingres lengthened her spine by several vertebrae in pursuit of an ideal sinuous line. Commissioned by Caroline Murat for the Naples court, the picture was scandalised at the 1819 Salon for its anatomical liberties.

title: Petworth House from the Lake: Dewy Morning
description: A view across the Earl of Egremont's lake, painted under the patronage that gave Turner the run of Petworth. Cool morning haze dissolves park, water and sky into the unified atmosphere typical of his Sussex landscapes.

title: Philipp Otto Runge
description: A black and white chalk drawing of the young Sophia Sieveking laid out in death, her features composed against a pale pillow. Runge made the sheet shortly before his own early death, lending its mortuary stillness an autobiographical weight.

title: Prado - Los Desastres de la Guerra - No. 04 - Las mugeres dan valor
englishTitle: The Disasters of War, Plate 4: Las mugeres dan valor
description: Plate 4 of the Disasters of War, captioned 'The women give courage'. Goya shows female combatants resisting French troops during the Peninsular War, the etching and aquatint biting through the page in his characteristically stark contrasts of black and gnawed white.

title: Prado - Los Desastres de la Guerra - No. 46 - Esto es malo
englishTitle: The Disasters of War, Plate 46: Esto es malo
description: Plate 46 of the Disasters of War, 'This is bad'. A friar is set upon amid scattered bodies, the scene drawn with the cramped, shallow space and bitten line that give the series its grim moral force. The plates were withheld until decades after Goya's death.

title: Shipwreck of the Minotaur
description: A naval transport founders amid towering green-grey waves, lifeboats overloaded with survivors swept up the swells. Turner makes the wreck of HMS Minotaur an early demonstration of his lifelong subject of nature's indifferent force at sea.

title: The Fish Market at Hastings Beach
description: Sussex fisherfolk hauling their catch onto the shingle, with luggers and chalk cliffs receding behind. Turner repeatedly painted Hastings during the Napoleonic years when its beach was both a working port and a fashionable resort.

title: (Venice) Aristotele by Francesco Hayez in gallerie Accademia Venice
description: A sober half-length study of the ancient philosopher, draped and meditative, painted by Hayez as a young artist in Venice. The work is an early example of the polished historicism that would later make him the leading painter of Risorgimento-era Italy, and it remains in the Gallerie dell'Accademia in the city where he trained.

title: Colonel Alastair Ranaldson Macdonell of Glengarry
description: The Highland chieftain stands armed in full Glengarry tartan against a heroic landscape, every weapon and badge of clan pride on display. Raeburn's broad, direct brushwork supplies the swagger that Macdonell himself cultivated as a self-styled embodiment of clan tradition.

title: John Eardley Wilmot
description: Lawyer John Eardley Wilmot sits at a writing desk, a quill in hand and an allegorical group of dispossessed American Loyalists behind him on the wall. West painted the 1812 canvas as a homage to Wilmot, who had chaired the British commission that compensated refugees from the Revolution, the picture-within-a-picture summarising the sitter's public service.

title: Major-General Henry Dearborn
description: Henry Dearborn, the Jefferson-era Secretary of War newly returned to active command at the outbreak of the War of 1812, sits in dark blue uniform with gold epaulets. Stuart painted him in 1812; the canvas entered the Art Institute of Chicago as accession 1913.793.

title: Teignmouth Harbour
description: Vessels lie at anchor under the red Devon cliffs of the Teign estuary, a coast Turner sketched repeatedly on his West Country tours. The watercolour links to his preparatory work for the Southern Coast engravings.

title: The Charging Chasseur
dateCreated: 1812 Romanticism (second half of 18 th century –first half of 19 th century )
description: A mounted officer of Napoleon's Imperial Guard wheels his rearing chestnut horse against a smoke-streaked sky. Géricault's Salon debut at twenty-one announced a new Romantic energy in French painting, with Rubensian colour and a kinetic diagonal that broke decisively from Davidian decorum.

title: Gothic Cathedral by the Water
description: A vast Gothic cathedral towers over a riverside town at sunset, its silhouette dwarfing the mortal traffic on the quay. The motif of the imagined medieval Dom appealed to Romantic painters as both architectural dream and patriotic emblem after the Napoleonic Wars.

title: Morning
description: Dawn light spreads across a placid river valley as a small boat puts out from the shore. Although the file references Schinkel, the work belongs to the meditative landscape mode of early-nineteenth-century German Romanticism, where the simple act of daybreak carries the weight of spiritual allegory.

title: (Barcelona) Apullia in Search of Appullus 1814 - William Turner - Tate Britain
description: An early classical landscape by J. M. W. Turner, exhibited at the British Institution and pointedly modelled on Claude Lorrain to challenge the older master's reputation. Sunlit foliage, distant temples and a literary Ovidian subject mark Turner's ambition to inherit the grand European pastoral tradition.

title: El Tres de Mayo
description: A Spanish patriot in a luminous white shirt flings out his arms before the firing squad of Napoleonic troops on Príncipe Pío hill. Commissioned after the French withdrawal, Goya treats martyrdom with the brutal lighting and crude paint of modern history painting.
credit: This file was derived from: El Tres de Mayo, by Francisco de Goya, from Prado in Google Earth.jpg :

title: Hokusai Manga 01
description: A page from the first volume of the Hokusai Manga, the artist's sprawling printed sketchbooks that catalogue figures, animals, landscapes, and curiosities. Issued from 1814, the volumes circulated widely as drawing manuals and later became a key conduit of Japanese form into European art.
credit: Michener, James A. (1958) Hokusai Sketchbooks: Selections from the Manga , Rutland, Vermont & Tokyo: Charles E. Tuttle Company

title: The Second of May 1808 or The Charge of the Mamelukes
description: Madrileños with knives drag Mamluk cavalrymen of the imperial guard from their rearing horses in the Puerta del Sol. Companion to The Third of May, Goya's painting reconstructs the chaos of the popular uprising against Napoleon's occupation in tumbling diagonals.

title: Gothic Church on a Rock by the Sea
description: A spired Gothic cathedral rises atop a cliff above the sea, more vision than topography. The motif - architecture as sacred outcropping - belongs to the shared Romantic imagination of Schinkel and Friedrich, where the medieval church stands in for a yearned-for unity of faith, nation and landscape.

title: Henry Rice
description: Boston merchant Henry Rice sits in a dark coat and high white collar against a misted sky, the loose brushwork of the unfinished cravat typical of Stuart's late style. The picture, painted around 1815, entered the Metropolitan Museum's collection and reflects Stuart's final decade as the preferred portraitist of the New England mercantile class.

title: Hokusai Manga 02
description: Another page from the Hokusai Manga, the encyclopedic woodblock sketch compendium that eventually ran to fifteen volumes. The loose, observational lines were intended as study material for students, though they read today as a portrait of Edo's everyday visual world.
credit: Michener, James A. (1958) Hokusai Sketchbooks: Selections from the Manga , Rutland, Vermont & Tokyo: Charles E. Tuttle Company

title: Painting for a stage design for Mozart's opera Magic Flute
englishTitle: Stage Set for The Magic Flute: The Hall of Stars (Queen of the Night)
description: The Queen of the Night appears on a crescent moon before a vast vaulted hall of stars, set design for Mozart's Die Zauberflöte. Schinkel produced the gouache around 1815 for the Berlin Hofoper premiere; the original sheet is held by the Staatliche Museen zu Berlin and remains one of the most reproduced opera designs of the 19th century.

title: The Eruption of the Soufrière Mountains in the Island of St Vincent
description: A Caribbean volcano detonates against the night, fountains of incandescent ash silhouetting palms and figures along the shore. Worked from eyewitness reports of the 1812 eruption, the picture exemplifies the early nineteenth-century taste for geological catastrophe.

title: Benjamin Franklin Drawing Electricity from the Sky
description: Benjamin Franklin sits on a cloud, surrounded by putti operating the kite-and-key apparatus of his 1752 lightning experiment, while a thunderhead breaks overhead. West painted the apotheosis around 1816 in London, knowingly framing his late countryman as a deified Promethean figure in the manner of Rubens or Reni.

title: Constable osmington bay
description: Osmington Bay on the Dorset coast spreads under a sky of broken cumulus, the cliffs running off toward Weymouth. Constable painted the small oil on his 1816 honeymoon at the village of Osmington, where the rector John Fisher had married him to Maria Bicknell that October.

title: Flatford Mill
description: A view from a footbridge on the Stour, with a barge being unhitched in the foreground beneath open Suffolk sky. Painted largely en plein air on Constable's family land, the picture exemplifies the truth-to-nature creed that underpinned his six large 'Stour' canvases.

title: Maria Bicknell
description: An intimate portrait of the painter's fiancée, completed shortly before their long-resisted marriage. Constable, primarily a landscapist, treats her face with a reserved tenderness, the muted palette and soft modelling reflecting the private nature of the commission.

title: Portrait of French politician and soldier Étienne Maurice Gérard
description: General Étienne Maurice Gérard, a Napoleonic comte d'Empire then in exile in Brussels, sits in dark civilian dress with the cordon of the Légion d'honneur visible at his collar. David painted the portrait in 1816, sharing exile with his sitter after the Hundred Days, the canvas now at the Metropolitan Museum of Art.

title: Portrait of the Comte de Turenne
description: Henri-Amédée-Mercure de Turenne, Napoleon's chamberlain and grand marshal, sits in his green uniform of master of the imperial hunt, his eyes turned aside. David painted him in Brussels in 1816, working steadily through the small group of fellow exiles and Bonapartist officers who joined him in the city.

title: Portrait of the Comtesse Vilain XIIII and her Daughter Louise
description: Sophie-Louise-Zoé de Feltz, Comtesse Vilain XIIII, sits in a Brussels garden in white empire dress with her five-year-old daughter Louise leaning at her knee. David painted the double portrait in 1816 during his Belgian exile; it remains one of the most tender of his late commissions and is now held by the National Gallery in London.

title: The Temple of Jupiter Panellenius Restored
description: A reconstructed view of the Doric temple on Aegina, imagined intact above the Aegean, painted from sketches supplied by an architect-traveller as Turner himself never visited Greece. The canvas answered the British vogue for Hellenic antiquity stoked by the Elgin Marbles.

title: The Wheat Field
description: Reapers and gleaners work a Suffolk wheat field under a high summer sky, painted on Constable's home ground near East Bergholt in 1816. The canvas, now at the National Gallery of Art in Washington with accession 2007.8.27, dates from the months around his marriage and prefigures the six-foot landscapes he began the following year.

title: Wivenhoe Park
description: A panoramic estate view commissioned by Major-General Francis Slater-Rebow, balancing fishermen, swans, a grazing herd, and the distant house. Constable expanded the canvas at the patron's request to include a lawn and outbuildings, evidence of his pragmatic handling of the country-house genre.

title: Cupid and Psyche
description: Cupid sits on the edge of the bed where Psyche still sleeps, smirking as he reaches for his quiver. David inverts the usual idealized adolescent, painting the god as an ungainly teenager registering sexual conquest, a deliberate provocation produced during his Brussels exile and now at the Cleveland Museum of Art.

title: Portrait of Emmanuel Joseph Sieyès
description: The abbé Sieyès, theorist of the Third Estate and architect of the Brumaire coup that brought Napoleon to power, sits in dark coat against a plain ground. David painted the portrait in Brussels, where both artist and sitter were exiled after the Bourbon Restoration of 1815.
credit: via commons image Image:Emmanuels.jpg Crop of a portrait by Jacques-Louis David (English) / Jacques-Louis David (spanish)

title: Portrait of Louis David
description: Jacques-Louis David, painted in Brussels exile by his Belgian pupil François-Joseph Navez. Navez had followed David to Belgium in 1817 and produced this respectful study of the elderly master, who continued teaching from his Rue Léopold studio until his death in 1825.

title: Raby Castle
description: A house portrait commissioned by the third Earl of Darlington, set in his County Durham deer park with a hunt in the foreground. Turner devotes the upper canvas to a churning, dramatic sky, signalling his shift from topography to Romantic landscape.
credit: Walters Art Museum : Home page Info about artwork

title: The hiker above the sea of fog
description: Seen from behind on a rocky outcrop, the wanderer surveys a swirling fog that swallows the peaks below. Friedrich's signature Rückenfigur device invites the viewer into the figure's vantage, making the landscape an interior as much as a topography of the Elbe Sandstone Mountains.
credit: The photographic reproduction was done by Cybershot800i . ( Diff )

title: Chelsea Pensioners Reading the Waterloo Dispatch
description: Veterans cluster outside a Chelsea pub as a despatch announcing the victory at Waterloo is read aloud. Commissioned by the Duke of Wellington, Wilkie filled the genre tableau with regimental specificity, prompting crowd-control rails when it was shown at the Royal Academy in 1822.

title: Dort or Dordrecht: The Dort Packet-Boat from Rotterdam Becalmed
description: A glassy Dutch harbour bathed in golden morning light, paying open homage to Aelbert Cuyp, whose paintings Turner studied on his 1817 Low Countries tour. The becalmed packet boat anchors a luminous sky that occupies more than half the canvas.

title: Gate in the Rocks
description: A natural rock arch frames a distant view, conceived as the Nordic pendant to a sunlit Italian landscape. The pairing stages a Romantic dialogue between the sublime German wilderness and the classical south, a polarity that runs through the era's painting and through Schinkel's own architectural imagination.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"/s/schinkel/gaterock"

title: John Trumbull
description: The history painter John Trumbull, in dark coat with white stock, faces the viewer in three-quarter profile. Stuart painted his fellow American while Trumbull was working in Washington on the four Revolutionary War scenes commissioned for the Capitol Rotunda; the canvas is at the Yale University Art Gallery.

title: Shah 'Alam
description: The Mughal emperor Shah Alam II hands a scroll to Robert Clive on a raised platform, transferring the diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa to the East India Company. West reconstructed the 1765 Treaty of Allahabad fifty years after the event, recasting a profit-making contract as a regal ceremonial scene for the Company's London directors.

title: The Farewell of Telemachus and Eucharis
description: Telemachus, son of Odysseus, takes leave of the nymph Eucharis on Calypso's island, drawn from Fénelon's didactic novel. David painted the canvas in Brussels for Count Nikolai Demidov; it is now at the Getty Museum and shows the late, softened style of his exile years.

title: The Field of Waterloo
description: Night falls on the battlefield as women search the heaped dead by torchlight, three years after the engagement. Turner had walked the ground himself; the picture quotes Byron's Childe Harold and refuses any patriotic triumph.

title: The Penny Wedding
description: A crowded Scottish wedding feast unfolds in a low-beamed interior, fiddler at the front and dancers, drinkers, and gossips crammed across the canvas. Wilkie's careful Dutch-inspired genre painting helped popularize sentimental rural Scottishness for a Regency audience.

title: Ingres
description: A study sheet from Ingres's mature years preserved at La Piscine museum in Roubaix, related to his Angelica compositions. The drawing shows his disciplined pencil contour and obsessive return to the same Orlando Furioso motif over decades.

title: Self-Portrait
description: The American-born president of the Royal Academy faces the viewer in old age, palette in hand. West succeeded Joshua Reynolds as RA president in 1792 and held the post until his death in 1820, the year after this late self-portrait was painted.

title: The Anger of Achilles
description: Achilles draws his sword on Agamemnon as Iphigenia stands veiled for sacrifice, the four figures pressed into a shallow neoclassical frieze. David completed the picture in Brussels in 1819 and exhibited it the following year; it now hangs at the Kimbell Art Museum in Fort Worth.

title: The Violinist Niccolò Paganini
description: A pencil portrait of the virtuoso violinist captured during Ingres's years in Rome. The drawing distils Paganini to crisp contour and minimal shading, exemplifying the precise linear style for which Ingres's portrait sketches of musicians and patrons remain prized.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"i/ingres/08ingres"

title: The White Horse
description: The first of Constable's six-foot Stour valley canvases, showing a workhorse ferried across the river on a flat-bottomed barge. Constable elevates everyday East Anglian labor to grand-manner scale, with broken impasto highlights and a damp, atmospheric sky.

title: Castle by the River
description: A fortified castle commands the bend of a broad river under a luminous, theatrical sky. The composition treats architecture scenographically, the way Schinkel did in his stage designs for Berlin, while the contemplative figures and burnished light belong to the wider Romantic landscape current.

title: Cattle Market before a Large City on a Lake
description: Drovers, riders and townspeople negotiate over cattle on a rise overlooking a Bavarian lake, with a distant city silhouetted under bright clear air. Kobell's crisp draftsmanship and high-keyed Alpine light typify his Biedermeier landscapes.

title: Elizabeth Greenleaf Parsons
description: Elizabeth Greenleaf Parsons in lace cap and dark dress, painted in watercolor on ivory. Goodridge was the leading miniaturist of Federal-era Boston, trained partly by Gilbert Stuart; the portrait belongs to the Harvard Art Museums.

title: Francis Osborne
dateCreated: Unknown date, but author died in 1820
description: Francis Osborne, 5th Duke of Leeds, in a star-spangled court coat, painted by Benjamin West in the final years of the artist's London career. Osborne served briefly as Foreign Secretary under Pitt the Younger; the portrait was given to the National Portrait Gallery, London in 1888.

title: Hampstead Heath by John Constable watercolour
description: View looking across the undulating ground of Hampstead Heath, where Constable lived for stretches of his later life. The British Museum sheet, watercolour at 124 by 206 mm, belongs to the artist's sustained engagement with the Heath as a working subject for cloud and weather studies.

title: Harwich: The Low Lighthouse and Beacon Hill
description: A breezy view of the Essex coast, with the squat Low Lighthouse anchoring a beach where small figures gather under a luminous, cloud-stacked sky. Constable's skies are scientifically observed, drawing on his sustained study of meteorology in oil sketches.

title: Saturn Devouring His Son
dateCreated: between 1820 and 1823 Romanticism (second half of 18 th century –first half of 19 th century )
description: From the Black Paintings Goya applied directly to the walls of his Quinta del Sordo, the titan Cronus tears into one of his children, eyes blazing in a void. The savage handling, sooty palette, and private setting belong to the bleak, late vocabulary now reassembled in the Prado.

title: Susanna and the elders
description: A Neoclassical treatment of the biblical episode in which the chaste Susanna, bathing in her garden, is spied upon by two elders concealed in foliage. The smooth handling of the nude and theatrical contrast of light and shadow reflect the Flemish painter's training in the academic tradition of David.

title: The Spring
description: A standing nude pours water from an urn at her shoulder, an allegory of a freshwater spring. Ingres began the picture in Florence around 1820 and worked at it intermittently for decades; its porcelain-smooth contours epitomise his late Neoclassical ideal of feminine form.

title: Waterloo Bridge
description: Waterloo Bridge seen from the Whitehall stairs, its arches stretching across the Thames under a banked grey sky. Constable worked on the Waterloo subject for nearly two decades, building from this study toward the large 1832 picture commemorating the bridge's opening on the seventh anniversary of the battle.

title: James Madison
description: James Madison in old age, in dark coat against neutral ground, painted years after his presidency ended. Stuart had first taken Madison's likeness in 1804; this late repetition, now at the National Gallery of Art, descends from that earlier sitting.

title: Ritratto della famiglia Begas
description: Carl Joseph Begas, his wife Wilhelmine and their young son grouped together in a domestic interior. The German Nazarene painter had recently returned from Rome under the patronage of Friedrich Wilhelm III when he made this family portrait in 1821.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"b/begas/carl/family"

title: The Hay Wain
description: A wooden hay cart fords the millpond at Flatford on the Stour, with Willy Lott's cottage to the left and a slow bank of cumulus overhead. Exhibited at the Royal Academy in 1821, the six-foot canvas was shown at the 1824 Paris Salon, where it won a gold medal and influenced Delacroix and the young Barbizon painters.

title: The Sisters Zénaïde and Charlotte Bonaparte
description: Joseph Bonaparte's daughters Zénaïde and Charlotte sit together reading a letter from their exiled father, who had fled to New Jersey after Waterloo. David painted the double portrait in Brussels in 1821; it is now at the Getty Museum.

title: Thomas Jefferson
description: Thomas Jefferson in old age, painted by Stuart from earlier sittings taken in 1805 during Jefferson's second presidency. Stuart kept the original Edgehill portrait in his Boston studio for years, working up replicas like this one for collectors and family members.

title: Dante and Virgil in Hell
description: Dante and Virgil cross the Stygian marsh in Phlegyas's skiff as the damned claw at the gunwale, drawn from the eighth canto of the Inferno. Delacroix's Salon debut in 1822, the picture was bought by the state and now hangs in the Louvre; the dripping water beads on the nude bodies pay direct homage to Rubens.
credit: Transferred from en.wikipedia ; transferred to Commons by User:NuclearWarfare using CommonsHelper . (Original text : WebMuseum, Paris: Delacroix, EugÃ¨ne )

title: Moonrise over the Sea
description: Two women and a man on a rocky shore watch sailing ships approach beneath a rising moon, the sky banded violet and gold. Friedrich repeated the moonlit-sea motif throughout his career as a Rückenfigur meditation on faith, return, and the threshold between visible and unseen.

title: Solitary Tree
description: A weathered oak rises at the centre of a Bohemian valley at dawn, its dead crown set against luminous distant mountains. Friedrich uses the broken tree as a quiet emblem of endurance, paired with the morning panorama as one half of a meditation on the cycle of day and life.

title: View on the Stour near Dedham
description: Barges and bargemen on the Stour at Dedham, with Dedham church tower distant under broken cloud. The third of Constable's six-foot Stour canvases, exhibited at the Royal Academy in 1822 and now at the Huntington in San Marino.

title: Bishop Jean-Louis Anne Magdelaine Lefebvre de Cheverus
description: Jean-Louis Lefebvre de Cheverus, French émigré priest and first Catholic bishop of Boston, in episcopal robes with a small crucifix at his breast. Stuart painted the portrait in 1823, shortly before Cheverus returned to France to take up the see of Montauban; the canvas belongs to the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.

title: First Sketch for ‘The Battle of Trafalgar’
description: A loose oil sketch toward the large Trafalgar canvas commissioned by George IV for St James's Palace. Turner stitched together multiple moments of the engagement onto a single mast-cluttered composition. The freedom of brushwork here, intended only as a working study, anticipates his later, looser exhibited manner.

title: Italian morning
description: A young woman bathes her face at a stone fountain in dappled morning light. Bryullov painted the canvas in Rome in 1823 as part of his pensioner programme for the Society for the Encouragement of the Arts, who sent it to Tsar Alexander I; it remains one of his earliest Italian successes.

title: Romeo and Juliet’s last kiss
description: Romeo, foot already on the balcony, embraces Juliet in an exchange of literary tenderness laced with foreboding. Hayez, the leading Italian Romantic painter and a quiet Risorgimento sympathiser, modelled the composition on theatrical tableaux to charge it with patriotic feeling.

title: Salisbury Cathedral from the Bishop's Grounds
description: The cathedral's spire rises through the screen of trees on a property owned by the painter's friend Bishop Fisher, who commissioned the picture. Constable renders the verdant grounds with characteristic flecks of white impasto — his 'snow' that animated foliage and water alike.

title: Branch Hill Pond
description: A pond on Hampstead Heath under a banked sky, with riders on the sandy track at the rim. Constable rented a house in Hampstead from 1819 to give his consumptive wife Maria cleaner air, and the heath supplied him with the open-sky subjects he returned to throughout the 1820s.

title: Death of Camilla by F. Bruni
