description: Tiny whaling boats encircle a leviathan in choppy waters off Kyushu, their oarsmen dwarfed by the dark mass beneath. From Hokusai's Oceans of Wisdom series, the woodblock print pairs documentary subject with sweeping rhythmic line.

title: Bathsheba
description: Bathsheba at her bath, attended by a black servant beside a fountain in a walled garden. Bryullov worked on the large canvas for three years without finishing it, and the painting now hangs in the Tretyakov Gallery in Moscow, the surface marked by a tear traditionally attributed to a boot the frustrated artist hurled at it.

title: Childe Harold's Pilgrimage
description: Inspired by Byron's Mediterranean poem, Turner builds a luminous Italian campagna of crumbling arches, distant hills, and a glowing sky. The picture is part of the artist's long late dialogue with Claude Lorrain, dissolving classical landscape architecture into atmosphere.
credit: abcgallery.com; Sotheby’s (not for sale, only as a reference image)

title: Highland Hospitality
description: An early Scottish genre piece from before Lewis's Mediterranean and Egyptian years, showing crofters welcoming visitors at a Highland hearth. The picture belongs to a brief vogue for Walter Scott-inflected tartan subjects shared with Landseer. Lewis already shows his appetite for textured plaids, deer carcasses and rough stone interiors.

title: Horsewoman
description: Giovannina Pacini reins in a black horse while her younger sister Amazilia watches wide-eyed from the steps of a villa, both wards of Countess Yulia Samoilova. Commissioned by Samoilova in Milan and exhibited at the Brera Academy in 1832, the picture earned Bryullov comparisons to Rubens and Van Dyck before it passed to Pavel Tretyakov in 1893.

title: Kunisada futamigaura
description: Sunrise breaks over the Wedded Rocks at Futami-ga-ura on the Ise coast, their sacred shimenawa rope linking the husband and wife stones. Utagawa Kunisada was the dominant Utagawa-school designer of the late Edo period and treated the pilgrimage site many times over his long career.

title: Portrait of Monsieur Bertin
description: The newspaper editor of the Journal des Débats sits forward, hands planted on his thighs, in a pose that became a touchstone for nineteenth-century bourgeois portraiture. Ingres's polished surface and tightly drawn contours register every wrinkle of Bertin's waistcoat without disturbing the granite stillness of the sitter.

provenance.collection: Department of Paintings of the Louvre

title: Utagawa Kunisada I
description: Dawn breaks over the linked Wedded Rocks at Futami-ga-ura on the Ise coast, their sacred shimenawa rope strung between them. Kunisada renders the famous pilgrimage site in soft graded blues typical of early-1830s ukiyo-e landscape.

title: Antwerp Van Goyen Looking Out for a Subject
description: An imagined homage in which the Dutch master Jan van Goyen sketches from a small boat in Antwerp harbor, surrounded by shipping under broken cloud. Turner pays tribute to the seventeenth-century landscape tradition while asserting his own atmospheric handling of sky and water.

title: Bridge of Sighs
description: Turner's Venetian capriccio assembles the Doge's Palace, the Bridge of Sighs and the Punta della Dogana along a sun-bleached lagoon. Architecture dissolves into luminous haze, foregrounding the Romantic interest in atmospheric light over topographic precision.

title: Chôshi in Shimôsa Province
description: Chōshi in Shimōsa Province, from Hokusai's Oceans of Wisdom series, shows fishermen working their nets beneath a heaving wall of water. The aggressive curl and sprayed crest reprise, in horizontal format, the breaking-wave motif Hokusai had perfected a few years earlier in the Great Wave.

title: Hayez
description: Lot's daughters ply their father with wine in the cave above the ruined Sodom, in Hayez's reading of the Genesis episode. The Milanese Romantic stages the scene like an opera, posing the figures within a sharply lit grotto and modelling flesh with the Neoclassical polish inherited from his teacher Canova.

title: Hiroshige-53-Stations-Hoeido-01-Nihonbashi-BM-03
description: A daimyō procession sets out across Edo's Nihonbashi bridge at dawn, opening Hiroshige's Tokaido Road series for the publisher Hōeidō. The print establishes the journey's ceremonial scale before the road's weather and incident take over.

title: Hiroshige-53-Stations-Hoeido-14-Hara-MFA-01
englishTitle: Hara Station: Mount Fuji in the Morning
description: Travellers cross the open plain at Hara station while Mount Fuji rises in pink-tinged morning light, breaking the sheet's upper border. The Hōeidō Tokaido is among the most successful print series of the Edo period, sold in tens of thousands of impressions.
credit: Database of the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston

title: Hiroshige-53-Stations-Hoeido-16-Kanbara-MFA-02
description: Three muffled figures trudge through deep night snow at Kanbara, the white sky bokashi-graded into a heavy grey. Long counted among Hiroshige's finest landscape prints, the design treats silence and stillness as subject in their own right.
credit: Database of the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston

title: Hiroshige-53-Stations-Hoeido-34-Futagawa-MFA-02
description: Travellers approach a thatched teahouse on the windswept Sarugababa heath outside Futagawa station. Hiroshige builds the scene from broad fields of muted ochre and pine green typical of the Hōeidō Tōkaidō's middle stretch.
credit: Database of the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston

title: Hiroshige-53-Stations-Hoeido-35-Yoshida-MFA-02
description: Workmen scaffold the Toyokawa River bridge at Yoshida station while Yoshida castle rises beyond. Hiroshige uses the diagonal of the bridgework as a vehicle for his characteristic recession into atmospheric distance.
credit: Database of the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston

title: Hiroshige-53-Stations-Hoeido-36-Goyu-MFA-01
description: Serving women aggressively haul reluctant travellers into an inn at Goyu, a stock comic episode of the Tōkaidō. The print is one of several in the series in which Hiroshige slips genre observation into what is nominally a landscape.
credit: Database of the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston

title: Hiroshige-53-Stations-Hoeido-37-Akasaka-MFA-01
englishTitle: Akasaka Station: Inn with Serving Maids
description: An Akasaka inn courtyard is shown in cross-section: maids preparing to receive guests on one side, bathing travellers on the other, separated by a clipped sago palm. The bird's-eye plan demonstrates the architectural curiosity Hiroshige brought to genre interiors.
credit: Database of the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston

title: Hiroshige-53-Stations-Hoeido-40-Chiryu-MET-New-York-01
description: Station Chiryū from the Tōkaidō series, depicting the early-summer horse fair on a grassy plain where merchants and tethered animals scatter under wide skies. Hiroshige uses subtle bokashi gradations along the horizon to evoke seasonal atmosphere; the Hoeidō publisher seal marks this as part of his career-making 1833 edition.
credit: Database of the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York

title: Hiroshige-53-Stations-Hoeido-44-Yokkaichi-MFA-01
description: Station Yokkaichi shows a lone traveler bracing against the wind beside the Mie River, a hat tumbling away across the reeds. The sweeping diagonals and muted blues are characteristic of Hiroshige's Hoeidō Tōkaidō, a series that fixed the iconography of journey and weather in Edo print culture.
credit: Database of the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston

title: Hiroshige-53-Stations-Hoeido-53-Kusatsu-MFA-01
englishTitle: Kusatsu Station: Famous Teahouse at the Post Stop
description: The penultimate station of the Tōkaidō, Kusatsu was famed for its meibutsu tateba teahouse where porters rested with fast palanquins. Hiroshige captures the bustle of arriving travelers under banners, his linework crisp and his palette anchored by the deep indigo blues of the early Hoeidō printing.
credit: Database of the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston

title: Hiroshige11 hakone
englishTitle: Hakone Station: View of the Lake
description: Hakone, the most mountainous station of the Tōkaidō, rises in jagged, faceted peaks shaded in flat planes of color. A small daimyō procession threads through the pass beside Lake Ashi, a composition Hiroshige used to dramatize the human scale against terrain.
credit: The fifty-stree stages of Tokaido (one of 53 prints, +2 for start and terminus)

title: Hiroshige19 ejiri
englishTitle: Ejiri Station: Distant View of Miho
description: Ejiri, set on Suruga Bay near the Miho pine grove, looks across a calm inlet dotted with sailing boats. Hiroshige flattens the distance into bands of graded color, a hallmark of his ukiyo-e landscape mode that influenced later Western printmakers.
credit: The fifty-stree stages of Tokaido (one of 53 prints, +2 for start and terminus)

title: Hiroshige20 fuchu
description: Travelers ford the Abe River at Fuchu, carried piggyback or on platforms by the station's licensed porters. The rhythmic figures across the shallow water exemplify Hiroshige's interest in the practical theater of travel along the Tōkaidō road.
credit: The fifty-stree stages of Tokaido (one of 53 prints, +2 for start and terminus)

title: Hiroshige22 okabe
description: The Okabe station turns inland through the gorge of Utsu Pass, where a stony stream cuts between steep wooded slopes. Hiroshige's compressed verticals and overlapping rocks give the print a closed, intimate atmosphere unusual for the series.
credit: The fifty-stree stages of Tokaido (one of 53 prints, +2 for start and terminus)

title: Hiroshige25 kanaya
englishTitle: Kanaya Station: The Distant Bank of the Ōi River
description: Kanaya sits on the western bank of the Ōi River, reached only by porters who carried travelers across its broad flats. Hiroshige looks down on the receding scene from a high vantage, ordering the mountains and water into clean horizontal registers.
credit: The fifty-stree stages of Tokaido (one of 53 prints, +2 for start and terminus)

title: Hiroshige28 fukuroi
description: At Fukuroi, travelers rest at a tea stand pitched beneath a leafy tree, a kettle steaming on the open fire. The genre vignette is set against a low, level landscape, demonstrating Hiroshige's gift for everyday observation within the Tōkaidō format.
credit: The fifty-stree stages of Tokaido (one of 53 prints, +2 for start and terminus)

title: Hiroshige30 hamamatsu
description: Hamamatsu features a great solitary pine on a windswept field, with figures gathered around a small fire at its base. The motif distills Hiroshige's recurring concern with weather and season, the bare branches and grey sky reading as winter on the road.
credit: The fifty-stree stages of Tokaido (one of 53 prints, +2 for start and terminus)

title: Hiroshige38 fujikawa
englishTitle: Fujikawa Station: Scene at Post Outskirts
description: Fujikawa shows a daimyō procession entering the station under banners, met by villagers prostrated in formal greeting. The print documents the parade etiquette of sankin-kōtai, the alternate-attendance system that drove Tōkaidō traffic in the Edo period.
credit: The fifty-stree stages of Tokaido (one of 53 prints, +2 for start and terminus)

title: Hiroshige39 okazaki
description: The Yahagi Bridge at Okazaki, said to be the longest on the Tōkaidō, stretches across the river in a single shallow arc. Hiroshige aligns the procession crossing it with the distant castle, framing infrastructure and authority in one elegant span.
credit: The fifty-stree stages of Tokaido (one of 53 prints, +2 for start and terminus)

title: Hiroshige45 ishiyakushi
description: Ishiyakushi takes its name from the Buddhist temple visible among trees behind the village fields. Hiroshige's quiet rural composition, with farmers at work and a stand of pines, exemplifies the lyrical pastoral mode he interleaved with the busier station scenes.
credit: The fifty-stree stages of Tokaido (one of 53 prints, +2 for start and terminus)

title: Hiroshige47 kameyama
englishTitle: Kameyama Station: Clear Weather after Snow
description: Kameyama Castle rises above a snow-blanketed slope as a daimyō procession climbs toward the gate. The print is among the most admired snowscapes of the Hoeidō Tōkaidō, its diagonal trail and white expanse drawn with Hiroshige's restrained graphic economy.
credit: The fifty-stree stages of Tokaido (one of 53 prints, +2 for start and terminus)

title: Hiroshige49 sakanoshita
description: Sakanoshita lies at the foot of the steep Suzuka pass, here dominated by the cliff known as Fudesute-yama, the 'brush-throwing mountain'. Travelers pause at a teahouse to contemplate the rock face, a scene that joins landscape and legend in Hiroshige's understated manner.
credit: The fifty-stree stages of Tokaido (one of 53 prints, +2 for start and terminus)

title: Hiroshige50 tsuchiyama
description: Tsuchiyama is shown in heavy spring rain, a daimyō procession crossing a swollen stream beneath dripping trees. The slanting rain lines and saturated greens make this one of the most atmospheric prints in the Tōkaidō series.
credit: The fifty-stree stages of Tokaido (one of 53 prints, +2 for start and terminus)

title: Nichiren bezweert de golven bij Kakuda tijdens zijn verbanning naar Sado
description: The Buddhist reformer Nichiren stands in a pitching boat off Kakuda, calming the waves with the Lotus Sutra during his exile to Sado. Kuniyoshi's woodblock print sets red robes against churning blue surf in the dramatic warrior-print idiom of late Edo Utagawa school design.

title: Rōben Waterfall at Ōyama in Sagami Province
description: Pilgrims bathe in the falls at Ōyama, where Rōben is said to have purified himself before founding the mountain's temple. From A Tour of the Waterfalls of the Provinces, Hokusai abstracts cascading water into ribbons of stylised line, treating each fall as a graphic emblem of place.

title: The Amida Falls in the Far Reaches of the Kisokaidō Road
description: From the celebrated series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, this woodblock print depicts the towering Amida Falls cascading from a circular pool said to resemble the head of the Buddha Amida. Hokusai pairs sweeping calligraphic line with flat planes of indigo and ochre, dwarfing tiny travellers beside the rushing water.

title: The Titan's Goblet
description: A colossal vegetation-encrusted goblet rises from a wooded plain, classical ruins crowning its rim and tiny boats sailing on its glassy water. Painted in 1833 and rejected by Cole's patron Luman Reed, the canvas now at the Metropolitan Museum of Art has been read variously as the Norse world-tree Yggdrasil and a Greek mythological cup.
credit: Own scan, source: Norbert Wolf, Ingo F. Walther (publ.), Romantik, Taschen, Hong Kong, Köln, London, Los Angeles, Madrid, Paris, Tokyo, 2007, ISBN 978-3-8228-5307-8 , p. 75

title: Caroline von Holnstein from Fronberg
description: Countess Caroline von Holnstein, a Munich society figure, painted for Ludwig I's Schönheitengalerie. Stieler frames her in dark drapery and pearls, the smooth modeling and steady gaze typical of the court's gallery of beauties.

title: Frauen von Algier
description: Three women in loose, jewelled garments sit on cushions in a tiled Algerian harem while a Black servant draws back a curtain to leave them. Painted from sketches Delacroix made during three days in Algiers in 1832, the canvas caused a sensation at the 1834 Salon and was bought immediately by King Louis-Philippe.

title: Hiroshige Full moon over a mountain landscape
englishTitle: Autumn Moon at Ishiyama Temple, from Eight Views of Ōmi
description: The Autumn Moon at Ishiyama Temple, from Eight Views of Ōmi, shows the bright disc rising over Lake Biwa behind the temple's wooded bluff. Hiroshige draws on the classical meisho tradition, pairing a literary scenic theme with his characteristic graded blue skies.

title: Hiroshige Heavy rain on a pine tree 2
englishTitle: Night Rain at Karasaki, from Eight Views of Ōmi
description: Night Rain at Karasaki, from Eight Views of Ōmi, isolates the great pine of Karasaki shrine as wind and rain lash its dark canopy. The near-monochrome palette and dense parallel lines give the print the hush of a literary classical theme treated in late ukiyo-e.

title: Hiroshige View of a long bridge across a lake
englishTitle: Evening Glow at Seta, from the series Eight Views of Ōmi
description: Evening Glow at Seta, from Eight Views of Ōmi, depicts the Karahashi bridge stretching across the southern reaches of Lake Biwa under a flushed sky. Hiroshige uses bokashi gradations to model dusk, a printing technique that gives the series its meditative tonal character.

title: Life stages
description: Five figures on a Baltic shore correspond to five sailing vessels at varying distances — an allegory of the ages of human life rendered in Friedrich's late, hushed palette. The painting was made near the artist's birthplace of Greifswald and is now in Leipzig's Museum der bildenden Künste.

title: Panorama of Berlin
description: One panel from Gaertner's six-part angular panorama of Berlin, taken from the roof of Schinkel's Friedrichswerdersche Kirche in the summer of 1834. The architectural painter worked daily in a wooden booth atop the church, recording the new buildings of the Schinkel circle for King Friedrich Wilhelm III.

title: Panorama of Berlin. View to the South
description: The southern segment of the 1834 Berlin panorama, recording rooftops, courtyards and chimneys spread out below the lantern of the Friedrichswerder church. Gaertner's six-part view was purchased by Friedrich Wilhelm III and a replica was later carried to Russia for Tsarina Alexandra Feodorovna.

title: Panorama von Berlin
description: Another panel from the 1834 panorama, with the dome of the Französischer Dom and the colonnade of Schinkel's Schauspielhaus at Gendarmenmarkt rising above pitched tile roofs. Gaertner painted his six-part survey on the roof of the Friedrichswerdersche Kirche almost every day of that summer.

title: Peaceable Kingdom
description: A lion lies beside a lamb, a leopard with a kid, and a child rests his hand on the leopard's neck, while in the left background William Penn signs his 1681 treaty with the Lenape on the Delaware. Hicks, a Quaker minister and sign painter, made roughly a hundred versions of the Isaiah 11 prophecy as an emblem of Pennsylvania's promise.
credit: National Gallery of Art, Washington, D. C., online collection

title: The Burning of the Houses of Lords and Commons
description: Westminster's old Palace blazes against the night sky on 16 October 1834, watched by a crowd massed on the Thames. Turner sketched the fire from a hired boat and produced two oil versions, of which this is the Philadelphia canvas. The conflagration let him paint exactly the kind of incandescent yellow-and-red sky he had been pursuing for decades.

title: The Burning of the Houses of Parliament
description: An eyewitness response to the conflagration that destroyed the medieval Palace of Westminster, watched by crowds along the Thames. Turner sketched the blaze from a hired boat and translated it into pyrotechnic yellows and reds against the cool Westminster Bridge.

title: 1849), Kirifuri waterval bij de Kurokami berg
description: The Kirifuri ("falling mist") cascade on Mount Kurokami breaks into four white tendrils against dark cliffs, with tiny travellers gazing up from below. Hokusai's Waterfalls series treats Japan's sacred falls as near-abstract patterns, the water carved as flat decorative line rather than naturalistic spray.

title: A colored version of the Big wave from 100 views of the Fuji
description: A reworked echo of the famous Kanagawa wave, drawn from the later One Hundred Views of Mount Fuji. Hokusai mirrors the composition, removes the fishing boats, and turns the spume into a flock of birds — a meditation on transformation rendered in his late, more graphic woodblock manner.

title: Head of a Person Asleep
description: A small, intimate study of a figure asleep, head sunk against bedding, kept in Turner's studio and bequeathed to the nation. The looseness of touch is closer to the colour-beginnings of his late watercolours than to anything he exhibited. It belongs to a private corpus of figurative sketches now in the Tate's Turner Bequest.

title: Keelmen Heaving in Coals by Moonlight
description: Tyneside coal-heavers loading colliers under a full moon at Shields, painted as a pendant to a Venetian scene to contrast industrial north and southern lagoon. The torchlit smoke and silvered water typify Turner's late nocturnes.

title: Line Fishing
description: Fishing boats work the swell off Hastings under a turbulent sky, the figures and rigging set against pale sea-light. Turner treats the everyday coastal labor with the atmospheric breadth of his mature marine paintings.

title: Ono Waterfall on the Kisokaidō
description: Travellers and packhorses pause on the Kisokaidō highway beside the Ono falls, dwarfed by a smooth blue sheet of water. From the Tour of the Waterfalls, the print pairs Hokusai's stylised, almost geometric treatment of cascades with the everyday traffic of one of Edo Japan's great post roads.

title: Stonehenge
description: A late watercolour showing the prehistoric stones beneath a roiling sky split by a double rainbow. Constable, working in his final years, treats the monument as a meditation on time and weather, the broken trilithons set against the moving drama of the English heavens.

title: The Bright Stone of Honour
description: The Rhine fortress of Ehrenbreitstein rises in golden haze above the confluence with the Moselle, paired with the riverside tomb of the French general Marceau. Turner illustrates a passage from Byron's Childe Harold, fusing topography with literary elegy.

title: The Grand Canal - Venice
description: A view down the Grand Canal toward the domes of Santa Maria della Salute, gondolas dispersed across luminous water. Turner dissolves the architecture of Venice into pale light and reflected color, characteristic of his late Romantic vedute.

title: The Yoshitsune Horse-Washing Falls at Yoshino
description: Yoshitsune's retainers wash their horses beneath the Yoshino falls, the cascade splitting into braided ribbons of pale paper. The plate from the Waterfalls series fuses warrior legend with landscape, characteristic of how Hokusai layered narrative into his late topographical print sets.

title: Fortune-teller Svetlana
description: A young woman in a kokoshnik and sarafan sits with her back to the viewer, peering into a candlelit mirror to catch sight of her future husband. Bryullov painted Svetlana in Moscow while staying with Antony Pogorelsky, transcribing the heroine of Vasily Zhukovsky's 1812 ballad in his only canvas on a Russian folk subject; it hangs in the Nizhny Novgorod State Art Museum.

title: Rome
description: A panoramic view of the Eternal City bathed in golden Mediterranean haze, with the Tiber winding past domes and ruins toward distant hills. Turner exhibited this canvas after his Italian travels, dissolving topographical detail into atmospheric light worthy of Claude Lorrain.
credit: dailymail.co.uk the second upload thehistoryblog.com the third upload thehistoryblog.com

title: The Consummation of Empire from The Course of the Empire
description: The third canvas in The Course of Empire shows a fictive classical city at its zenith, with porticoes, rotundas, statuary and a triumphal procession crossing a marble bridge above the harbour. Cole painted the five-part allegory for his patron Luman Reed's Greenwich Street picture gallery between 1833 and 1836; Reed died in June 1836 without seeing the series completed.

title: View from Mount Holyoke
description: Storm clouds break over a shattered foreground of cliffs and lightning-struck pines while, below the precipice, the Connecticut River loops in a brilliant U around the cultivated farms of Northampton. Cole interrupted The Course of Empire to paint the canvas for the 1836 National Academy exhibition; it sold to Charles N. Talbot for 500 dollars and is now at the Metropolitan Museum.

title: (Barcelona) Story of Apollo and Daphne 1837 - William Turner - Tate Britain
description: A late mythological landscape by Turner, the Ovidian chase staged across a golden Italianate valley bathed in the swirling light he had brought back from his Roman travels. Figures dwindle beside vast trees and rivers, drama dissolved into atmosphere in the manner of his ageing Claude homages.

title: Ancient Rome; Agrippina Landing with the Ashes of Germanicus
Arundel Mill and Castle
description: A water mill on the River Arun in the foreground, with Arundel Castle's keep rising through trees on the slope beyond. Constable spent the entire day of 31 March 1837 putting the last touches on the canvas and died unexpectedly that night; his friend C. R. Leslie sent it to the Royal Academy summer exhibition the following year as his final work.

title: Eugene delacroix
description: A self-portrait from the artist's late thirties, the painter facing the viewer with steady, somewhat melancholy eyes and a black coat that dissolves into shadow. Delacroix here adopts the sober, unidealised register of seventeenth-century Dutch self-portraiture rather than Romantic flourish.

title: Fishing Boats with Hucksters Bargaining for Fish
Karl Friedrich Schinkel Allegorie auf Beuth
description: An allegorical tribute to the Prussian industrial reformer Peter Beuth, shown astride Pegasus as he soars over a panorama of human civilisation and progress. The composition fuses Romantic landscape with Enlightenment allegory, celebrating Beuth's role in the modernisation of the Prussian state.

title: London National Gallery Turner Hero and Leander
englishTitle: The Parting of Hero and Leander
description: Turner sets the doomed lovers of Hero and Leander against an apocalyptic Aegean dawn, the sea churning as Leander drowns swimming the Hellespont. Exhibited at the Royal Academy in 1837, the canvas was bought from Turner's bequest by the National Gallery and exemplifies the late Romantic intensity of his mythological seascapes.

title: Look to the Large Cascade and Large Petergof Palace
description: The Grand Cascade tumbles down its sixty-four gilded fountains toward the Marine Canal at Peterhof, with the long facade of the Great Palace stretched along the upper terrace. Aivazovsky painted the view in 1837 as a graduating student of the Imperial Academy of Arts in Saint Petersburg; it is now in the State Museum-Reserve at Peterhof.

title: Sea coast at night. Near the beacon
description: A small bonfire glows on a rocky shore beside a lighthouse, with figures gathered at the water's edge and moonlight cutting across the swell beyond. Aivazovsky painted the seascape in 1837, the year he graduated from the Imperial Academy with a gold medal and was named official painter to the Russian Navy; it hangs in the Aivazovsky Gallery in Feodosia.

title: Christophe Colomb et son fils à La Rábida
description: Columbus arrives at the Franciscan monastery of La Rabida with his young son Diego, footsore after the failure of his Portuguese petitions. Painted in 1838 and now at the National Gallery of Art in Washington, the canvas inaugurated Delacroix's pair of Columbus subjects, the second showing the explorer's later reception at the Spanish court.

title: Flora Tristan 1838
description: Portrait of the French socialist and feminist writer Flora Tristan, author of Peregrinations of a Pariah. Published as a lithograph by Aubert in 1838 and reproduced in Le Charivari no. 53 on 22 February 1839, the print circulated her likeness during the years of her workers' organising tours through France.

title: Frédéric Chopin
description: Chopin in three-quarter view, lips parted, eyes lifted, his head silhouetted against a brown ground. Delacroix painted the composer in 1838 as part of a double portrait with George Sand sewing beside the piano; the unfinished canvas was cut in two after the artist's death and the Chopin fragment entered the Louvre.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"d/delacroi/3/313delac"

title: Hiroshige
description: Two mandarin ducks float together among reeds, the drake's plumage rendered in patterned blocks of vermilion, ochre, and indigo. Paired oshidori were a long-standing kachō-e symbol of marital devotion; Hiroshige treats the subject with the calligraphic economy of his late bird-and-flower work.

title: Médée
description: Medea clutches her two sons to her chest in a rocky grotto, the dagger raised as she prepares to kill them in revenge against Jason. Painted between 1836 and 1838 and shown at the Salon, the canvas was bought by the State and sent to the Palais des Beaux-Arts in Lille, where it has hung since 1839.

title: Schinkel2
description: Schinkel's elevation of the terrace at Orianda, a country retreat for Tsarina Alexandra Feodorovna planned on a cliff above the Black Sea in the Crimea. The architect's 1838 design fused a caryatid portico with hanging gardens and museum rooms; the cost was prohibitive and the palace was never built, surviving only in lithographs.
credit: Staatliche Schlösser und Gärten, Berlin, Postkarte, selbst gescannt

title: The death of Ophelia
description: Ophelia clings to a willow branch as it splits above the brook, her white shift catching on the bark while her wreath of flowers drifts away. Delacroix's first version of the subject, drawn from Gertrude's speech in Act IV of Hamlet, was painted in 1838 and is now in the Neue Pinakothek in Munich.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"/d/delacroi/3/315delad"; Bayerische Staatsgemäldesammlungen

title: The Last Meeting between Jacopo Foscari and his Family Before Being Sent into Exile
description: The painting was commissioned in 1838 by Emperor Ferdinand I , who had arrived in Milan for his coronation as king of Lombardy and Veneto , and it was destined for the Belvedere Gallery in Vienna. On its completion in 1840 the work was valued at the extremely high price of five thousand florins by the Commissione Permanente di Pittura dell’Accademia di Brera , which thus recognized its exceptional quality.

title: Wilhelmine Sulzer
description: A young woman gazes outward in a richly trimmed dress and lace collar. Painted for Ludwig I's Schonheitengalerie in Munich, the portrait shows Stieler's polished court manner: porcelain skin, unblemished surface, and discreet idealisation.

title: A View of the Mountain Pass Called the Notch of the White Mountains
description: A horseman crosses the V of Crawford Notch in the New Hampshire White Mountains, dwarfed by twisted pines and the bleached skeletons of trees torn from the slope. Cole painted the gorge in 1839, drawing on memories of the 1826 avalanche that wiped out the Willey family and their farmhands; it hangs in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.

title: General Sir David Baird Discovering the Body of Sultan Tippoo Sahib
description: A vast late history painting commemorating the British general's discovery of Tipu Sultan's body after the storming of Seringapatam in 1799. Wilkie staged the torch-lit scene with theatrical chiaroscuro, working in the grand manner he adopted following his travels in Spain.

title: Ivan Krylov
description: Ivan Andreyevich Krylov in old age, his coat lapel folded over to hide most of his decorations so only the silver edge of an order shows. Bryullov began the portrait of the fabulist in 1839 and left it unfinished, although the head and shoulders read as complete; the canvas hangs in the Tretyakov Gallery.

title: Panorama vom Kreml in Moskau
description: The Ivan the Great bell tower rising above the cathedrals and crenellated walls of the Moscow Kremlin, seen across the slate roofs of Kitay-gorod. Gaertner painted the panorama in 1839 on commission from Friedrich Wilhelm III, working from Moscow during a tour of Russia that filled his late career with imperial sites.

title: Portrait of Edward Hicks Painting the Peaceable Kingdom
description: The elder Edward Hicks at his easel, brush poised over a version of his Peaceable Kingdom showing the lion, ox and child of Isaiah's prophecy. Thomas Hicks, Edward's younger cousin, painted the homage in 1839 when Edward was fifty-nine; the canvas entered the National Portrait Gallery in Washington.

title: The Fighting Temeraire tugged to her last berth to be broken up
description: The 98-gun veteran of Trafalgar is towed by a black steam tug along the Thames toward the breaker's yard, set against a smouldering sunset. Turner contrasts the pale, ghostly hulk with the squat industrial tug, mourning the passing of the age of sail.

title: The poor poet
description: A penniless poet huddles under an umbrella in his garret bed, scribbling verses while the roof leaks. Spitzweg's most famous Biedermeier image, now in Munich's Neue Pinakothek, distils the era's fondness for affectionate caricature of the eccentric outsider.

title: (Barcelona) Stromy Sea with Blazing Wreck - William Turner - Tate Britain
description: A late Turner oil sketch in which a burning ship is nearly engulfed by towering surf and smoke. Paint is scrubbed and scraped into vortices of orange and lead grey, rendering catastrophe as pure elemental force. The work belongs to the Tate Bequest of unfinished canvases that Turner left in his studio at his death.

title: (Barcelona) The New Moon; or, ‘I’ve lost My Boat, You shan’t have Your Hoop’ - William Turner - Tate Britain
englishTitle: The New Moon; or, 'I've lost My Boat, You shan't have Your Hoop'
description: A small seaside scene from Turner's late period, where two children quarrel over a lost boat and a hoop on a wide tidal shore beneath a pale new moon. The trivial human anecdote is set against an expansive luminous sky and estuary, characteristic of Turner's mature handling of atmosphere and light. The work entered the national collection through the Turner Bequest and is held at Tate Britain.

title: Architect’s Dream
description: A bearded architect reclines on the capital of a fluted column, looking out over a fantastic harbour lined with Egyptian pyramids, Greek temples, Roman aqueducts and a Gothic cathedral at the back. Cole painted the canvas in five weeks for Ithiel Town in 1840, after the New York architect commissioned a view of Athens; Town rejected it as too architectural and the painting is now in the Toledo Museum of Art.

title: Der Schmetterlingsjäger
description: A frock-coated naturalist tiptoes through tall grass with raised butterfly net, lost in Linnaean reverie. The collector-eccentric, beloved subject of Spitzweg's Biedermeier comedies, is here painted on a vertical panel that exaggerates the man's spindly absurdity.

title: Kuniyoshi Utagawa, Pilgrims in the waterfall
description: Devotees perform misogi, the Shinto cold-water purification rite, beneath a thundering cascade. Kuniyoshi exploits the vertical ōban format to dramatise the columnar fall of water, a theatrical staging that recalls his celebrated heroic and supernatural compositions.

title: Schinkel3
description: An imagined interior of the reception hall in Schinkel's projected royal palace for King Otto on the Athenian Acropolis, with polychrome painted walls and a coffered ceiling sheltering a colossal statue. Friedrich Wilhelm, Crown Prince of Prussia, suggested the commission in 1833; Schinkel submitted his drawings in 1834 and the scheme was never built.
credit: Schinkel: Werke der höheren Baukunst für die Ausführung erfunden von Schinkel, Berlin 1840, Taf. 9; reproduction picture postcard Staatliche Schlösser und Gärten, Berlin

title: Sun Setting over a Lake
description: Form is reduced to bands of gold, rose and slate water in a late, near-abstract evocation of dusk. Pictures of this kind, left in his studio at his death, anticipate by half a century the dissolutions of Impressionism.

title: The Slave Ship
description: A slaver flings the dead and dying from its hold as a typhoon rises over a blood-orange sea, painted in response to the Zong massacre and abolitionist debate. Turner dissolves moral horror into dazzling atmosphere, the figures and chains barely surfacing through churning paint.

title: Waves Breaking against the Wind
description: A pure marine, the canvas is given entirely to a churning sea raked by spray. Turner reportedly had himself lashed to a mast in storms; the picture's loose, scumbled paint claims that immediacy.

title: Chaos. The Genesis
description: An angel of God hovers in cruciform pose above the dark turbulent waters of creation, light tearing the cloud apart behind him. Aivazovsky painted Chaos in Rome in 1841, his early twenties; it earned him a gold medal from Pope Gregory XVI and now hangs at the Mechitarist monastery of San Lazzaro degli Armeni in Venice.

title: Christ on the Sea of Galilee
description: Christ asleep in the stern while his disciples haul at the sail and oars of a fishing boat pitched almost vertical by a green wave on the Sea of Galilee. Delacroix returned to the Gospel storm at least six times during his late career; this oil sketch is in the Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art in Kansas City.

title: Der Sonntagsspaziergang
description: A bourgeois family in their Sunday best parades down a country path under a parasol, the children straggling behind. Spitzweg captures the small comedies of Biedermeier ritual with affectionate, miniaturist precision.

title: Hatsuhana doing penance under the Tonosawa waterfall
description: From the series Lives of Wise Women and Virtuous Wives, Hatsuhana of the joruri play Hakone Reigen prays under the icy Tonosawa falls to obtain her crippled husband's revenge. Kuniyoshi treats the ascetic subject with characteristic dynamism, the cascading water rendered in steep blue parallel lines.

title: His Highness Muhemed Ali
description: The Albanian-born ruler of Egypt sits in a European armchair in turban and richly embroidered Ottoman dress, painted on Wilkie's late tour to the Near East. The Scottish painter died at sea on the return voyage from this commission, and J.M.W. Turner commemorated his burial in 'Peace - Burial at Sea'.

title: Karolina Lizius
description: The shoemaker's daughter Karolina Lizius gazes outward in modest dress, painted as one of the bourgeois sitters Ludwig I added to his Schönheitengalerie. Stieler, court painter in Munich, specialised in this restrained Biedermeier portrait formula: smooth finish, neutral ground, demure psychology.

title: Katerina Rosa Botsaris
description: The young daughter of a Greek War of Independence hero is shown in embroidered Greek costume, her dark hair loose beneath a tasselled cap. Stieler painted the portrait for Ludwig I of Bavaria's Schönheitengalerie, the Munich gallery of beauties in which the king collected idealised female likenesses.

title: Portrait of Alessandro Manzoni
description: The novelist Alessandro Manzoni, author of I Promessi Sposi, sits in sober dark dress against a neutral ground, fixing the viewer with a measured gaze. Hayez treats the literary patriot of the Risorgimento with the restrained likeness and crisp drawing of the Italian Romantic portrait tradition.

title: Campo Santo
description: A tall-masted barge drifts past the island cemetery of San Michele in the Venetian lagoon. Painted alongside its Royal Academy companion the Dogano, the work converts a place of burial into a study of pearled morning light.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"t/turner/2/2041turn"

title: Odalisque with Slave
englishTitle: Odalisque with Slave (Walters Art Museum, 1842; landscape by Jean-Paul Flandrin)
description: Commissioned by King Wilhelm I of Württemberg, the picture reclines an odalisque before a garden vista while a servant plays the lute. Ingres designed and largely painted it, with the landscape backdrop entrusted to his pupil Paul Flandrin.
credit: Walters Art Museum : Home page Info about artwork

title: Peace - Burial at Sea
description: Commemorates the sea burial of the painter David Wilkie off Gibraltar, the steamer's silhouette and inky black sails set against a flaring sun. Exhibited as a pendant to Turner's fiery 'War,' the picture pairs cool nocturnal calm with the warmth of mourning.

title: Portrait of Countess Julia Pavlovna Samoilova moving away from the ball with her adopted daughter Amazilia Pacini
description: Countess Yuliya Samoylova sweeps out of a masquerade ball in a crimson velvet wrap, her adopted daughter Amazilia Pacini at her side. Bryullov painted the heiress of the Skavronsky family three times; she had been his patron and muse since their meetings in Italy in the 1820s.

title: Samson and the lion
description: Samson straddles the lion and pries open its jaws, his musculature lit with the academic clarity Hayez absorbed from study after the antique. The Old Testament hero is staged as a single isolated figure, drawing on the sculptural Romanticism that linked the artist to Canova's circle.

title: Snow Storm: Steam-Boat off a Harbour's Mouth
description: A paddle-steamer engulfed by a vortex of snow, smoke and sea, exhibited with Turner's claim that he had been lashed to the mast to observe it. Critics dismissed the canvas as 'soapsuds and whitewash', but it remains his definitive statement on the elemental sublime.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"t/turner/2/2040turn"

title: The Temple of Segesta with the Artist Sketching
description: The unfinished Doric temple at Segesta in western Sicily rises above scrub-covered hills, with a tiny seated figure of the painter sketching at lower left. Cole worked the canvas up in 1843 from drawings made during his second European tour, and the picture entered the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.

title: The Voyage of Life: Childhood
description: An infant glides from a dark cavern in a gilded boat shaped like an hourglass, steered by a winged guardian angel through a lush spring landscape. First of four panels in the National Gallery's 1842 version of The Voyage of Life, a moral allegory of the soul's progress through earthly time.
credit: or; Picture taken at: National Gallery of Art, Washington, D.C., USA 3.-; National Gallery of Art, Washington, D. C., online collection

title: The Voyage of Life: Manhood
description: The traveller, now grown, clasps his hands in prayer as his rudderless boat plunges through a torrent of black rocks under storm clouds, the guardian angel watching from above. Third panel in Cole's 1842 second version of The Voyage of Life, painted in his Catskill studio after the New York set was sold off.
credit: National Gallery of Art, Washington, D. C., online collection

title: The Voyage of Life: Old Age
description: The voyager, white-bearded, drifts on a glassy black sea while his angel gestures upward toward a host of celestial spirits breaking through the clouds. Fourth and final panel of the National Gallery's 1842 set, completing Cole's allegory of the Christian soul's passage from infancy to eternity.
credit: National Gallery of Art, Washington, D. C., online collection

title: The Voyage of Life: Youth
description: The young traveller, now alone at the tiller, steers toward a shining cloud palace in the sky above a verdant river valley. Second panel in Cole's 1842 second version of The Voyage of Life series at the National Gallery of Art, painted after the original 1840 set passed into private hands.
credit: National Gallery of Art, Washington, D. C., online collection

title: Light and Colour
description: A vortex of golden light spirals around the figure of Moses inscribing Genesis, with a serpent and submerged figures at its rim. Turner conceived the picture as a pendant illustrating Goethe's theory of positive, light-giving colour.

title: Siege of Pskov by Polish king en:Stefan Batory
description: Russian defenders sally from a breach in the white walls of Pskov as Stefan Batory's Polish-Lithuanian army storms the city in 1581. Bryullov worked on this large historical canvas from 1839 until his death in 1852, leaving it unfinished; it hangs in the State Tretyakov Gallery in Moscow.

title: The Sun of Venice Going to Sea
credit: Google Arts & Culture — dwEYd5yKW43wWQ Tate Images ( http://www.tate-images.com/results.asp?image=N00535&wwwflag=3&imagepos=5 )

title: Wohnzimmer des Schlossermeisters C.F.A. Hauschild in Berlin
description: The sitting room of the Berlin locksmith C.F.A. Hauschild on Stralauer Strasse 49, with patterned wallpaper, framed prints stacked above the sofa, and a piano against the back wall. Gaertner, trained as a porcelain painter at KPM, made a speciality of Biedermeier-era interiors and Berlin street views.

title: (Barcelona) Lake Lucerne ; the Bay of Uri from above Brunnen - William Turner - Tate Britain
englishTitle: Lake Lucerne: The Bay of Uri from Brunnen
description:
A watercolour from Turner's late Swiss tours, when he returned repeatedly to Lake Lucerne in search of atmospheric subjects. From the heights above Brunnen the bay opens in pale washes of blue and pearl, mountains dissolving into the luminous haze that defined his final manner. The sheet belongs to a celebrated group of Swiss studies now held by Tate Britain.</curatorDescription>
<parameter name="reason">Artist field contained Wikimedia uploader "Didier Descouens". Title was the filename with a misleading "(Barcelona)" location prefix and museum tail. This is a known J. M. W. Turner watercolour from his late Swiss series, c. 1841.

title: A View of the Two Lakes and Mountain House
description: Morning mist lifts off the twin Catskill lakes as the white-pillared Catskill Mountain House perches on a cliff above. Cole lived in the village of Catskill from 1836 and painted this 1844 view of the famous hotel that had drawn tourists to the Hudson Valley since 1824.

title: Fishing Boats Bringing a Disabled Ship into Port Ruysdael
description: Boats tow a damaged sailing ship into the imaginary Dutch harbour of Port Ruysdael, Turner's homage to Jacob van Ruisdael. Painted late in his career, the canvas dissolves rigging and breaking sea into broad sweeps of grey, white and salt. It is one of several pictures in which Turner used invented Dutch place-names as a critical tribute.

title: FRANCESCO HAYEZ - Incontro di Giobbe ed Esaù
description: The painting illustrates Jacob's return to his homeland, asking forgiveness from his brother Esau for having deceived his birthright. Biblical subjects had a lot of luck around the mid-nineteenth century, as the suffering of the Jewish people recalled the Italian political situation.

title: Rain
description: A Great Western Railway locomotive races across Maidenhead Bridge through curtains of rain, the iron viaduct dissolving into vapour and golden light. The picture is a defining statement of the modern industrial sublime, painted with palette knife and finger as much as brush.

title: Takiyasha the Witch and the Skeleton Spectre
description: A nishiki-e triptych staging the sorceress Takiyasha as she summons a colossal skeleton against the warrior Mitsukuni in the ruined Soma palace. Kuniyoshi compresses three full sheets into one continuous, theatrically lit scene drawn from the gothic literature of late Edo.

title: Van Tromp
description: The Dutch admiral Maarten Tromp puts his ship about in heavy weather, a subject Turner returned to repeatedly in his last decade. The picture extends his admiration for the seventeenth-century Dutch marine tradition into a high-key, Romantic key.

title: Venice Quay
description: The Doge's Palace and the Riva degli Schiavoni shimmer through lagoon light in a late Venetian view. By his third trip to Venice in 1840 Turner was treating the city's stones as little more than coloured vapour.

title: Feminine Wave
description: A graceful, curling wave breaks in undulating tendrils against a void, conceived as the gentler counterpart to Hokusai's better-known 'Masculine Wave'. The print belongs to the artist's late mature exploration of water as pure pattern, where ukiyo-e line approaches abstraction.

title: Norham Castle
description: The Northumbrian border keep dissolving into rose and gold mist above the Tweed, a motif Turner painted repeatedly across his career. The late oil reduces architecture and cattle to translucent veils of pigment, anticipating modern abstraction.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"t/turner/2/206turne" http://www.tate.org.uk/art/artworks/turner-norham-castle-sunrise-n01981

title: Portrait of Alexandra Amalie von Bayern
dateCreated: 1845, replica of a portrait painted in 1838
description: A Schönheitengalerie portrait of Princess Alexandra of Bavaria, daughter of Ludwig I, rendered in Stieler's characteristic porcelain finish. The sitter is shown with the soft idealization the Munich court demanded of its gallery of beauties.
credit: originally uploaded to de.wikipedia by Thyra ( talk · contribs ) on 20 December 2007, 19:16 under the file name Stieler - Alexandra, Prinzessin von Bayern (Schönheitengalerie).jpg . ( +/− )

title: Portrait of Comtesse d'Haussonville
description: A society portrait of Louise de Broglie, comtesse d'Haussonville, that Ingres laboured over for three years and that now hangs in the Frick Collection. Mirror, ribboned slippers and porcelain are arranged with linear precision, while the sitter's improbably elongated arm exemplifies the artist's controlled anatomical license.

title: Portrait of Friederike Freiin Von Gumppenberg
description: A late entry in the Schönheitengalerie, depicting the Bavarian baroness with the soft chiaroscuro and idealized features Stieler used throughout the cycle. The portrait belongs to the long Munich project that gathered thirty-six women from across the social spectrum at Ludwig I's command.

title: The Balcony Room
description: An empty room, white curtains billowing at the open balcony door, a sofa half-glimpsed in a wall mirror. Menzel made the small oil for himself, capturing transient sunlight with the immediacy of a snapshot decades before plein-air Impressionism reached Berlin.

title: Battle of Vyborg Bay
description: Russian galleys and ships of the line break through the Swedish fleet trapped in Vyborg Bay in June 1790, smoke from broadside fire rolling across the Baltic. Aivazovsky painted the engagement in 1846 as part of a Naval Ministry commission documenting Russian victories at sea.

title: Boat Ride by Kumkapi in Constantinople
description: Caiques drift past the seawall at Kumkapi on the Sea of Marmara, with the silhouette of Constantinople rising behind. Painted in 1846 after Aivazovsky's travels through Ottoman waters, the canvas belongs to the long series of Bosphorus and Marmara views he produced for Russian and Turkish patrons.

title: Building Site with Willows
description: Menzel turns a humble Berlin construction site, fringed by drooping willows, into a study of weather and labour. The unposed subject and freshly observed light anticipate the realist vein the Prussian painter would pursue across decades of obsessive sketching from life.

title: Coffee-house by the Ortaköy Mosque in Constantinople
description: A waterfront coffee-house beside the domes and slender minarets of the Ortakoy Mosque on the European shore of the Bosphorus. Painted in 1846, the canvas predates the present Neo-Baroque mosque rebuilt by Nikogos Balyan in 1854, recording the older structure that stood on the site.

title: Noah's Ark
description: Pairs of lions, leopards, horses, oxen, and waterfowl plod up the gangplank into Noah's ark under a darkening sky, with the floodwaters already rising on the horizon. Hicks, a Quaker minister and self-taught sign-painter from Bucks County, Pennsylvania, adapted the composition from an 1844 Currier lithograph.

title: Pizarro Seizing the Inca of Peru
description: Painted when Millais was barely seventeen and exhibited at the Royal Academy, this dramatic history scene shows the conquistador wresting Atahualpa from his throne amid scattering attendants. The crowded composition and bright local colour announce the precocious draughtsmanship he would soon channel into the Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood.

title: Sea Battle at Navarino on October 20
description: Russian, British, and French squadrons under Admiral Codrington pound the Ottoman-Egyptian fleet at anchor in Navarino Bay on 20 October 1827, masts toppling and gunsmoke piling against the cliffs. Aivazovsky returned to the subject several times for the Naval Ministry, dramatising a decisive engagement of the Greek War of Independence.

title: The Battle of Revel
description: Russian ships of the line drive the Swedish fleet onto the rocks off Revel in May 1790, broken masts and shattered hulls littering the Baltic. Aivazovsky painted the action for the Naval Museum in St Petersburg, where it still hangs as part of his cycle of imperial sea victories.
credit: ( Original text: Naval museum of St. Petersburg, Russia. ), Original uploader was Pietje96 at en.wikipedia , (4 January 2010 (original upload date))

title: The Russian Squadron on the Sebastopol Roads
description: Black Sea Fleet warships ride at anchor in the roadstead of Sevastopol under a glassy sunset, the masts and yards of the squadron silhouetted against a pearl-coloured sky. Painted in 1846, the year Aivazovsky was appointed senior painter to the Russian Naval Staff and supplied with a studio at the fleet's home port.

title: Undine Giving the Ring to Massaniello
description: A fantastical pairing of the water-nymph Undine, drawn from de la Motte Fouqué's novella, with the Neapolitan fisherman-rebel Masaniello. Painted at seventy-one, the canvas dissolves narrative into a swirl of aquatic colour typical of Turner's late square-format mythologies.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"t/turner/2/208turne"

title: View of Constantinople by evening light
description: Galata Tower with its original conical roof rises over the Golden Horn as caiques drift on the Bosphorus in the last light of evening. Aivazovsky visited Constantinople repeatedly from 1845 onward, producing canvases for Sultan Abdulmecid I that earned him the Order of the Nishan-i Iftikhar.
credit: 1, The Athenaeum: Home - info - pic via wikipaintings.org 2. art-catalog.ru

title: Accusa segreta
description: A Venetian noblewoman pauses by the bocca di leone, the lion's-mouth letterbox into which secret denunciations were dropped under the Republic. Hayez, leader of Italian Romantic painting, often coded contemporary Risorgimento politics into such historical scenes, here rendered with his porcelain-smooth flesh and rich brocades.

title: At first glance he looks fierce, but he's really a nice person
description: A glowering giant's face is, on closer look, made up entirely of squirming naked men — a sly anatomical pun on the proverb in the title. Kuniyoshi produced such jigsaw figures to slip past Tempō-era censorship that restricted depictions of named actors and courtesans.

title: Home in the Woods
description: A pioneer family stands by their log cabin on the shore of a wilderness lake, the father returning with a string of fish as smoke rises from the chimney. Cole painted the canvas in 1847 for his Catskill patron; it now hangs at the Reynolda House Museum of American Art in Winston-Salem.
credit: The Athenaeum: Home - info - pic; Reynolda House Museum of American Art

title: Lola Montez
description: The Irish-born dancer who styled herself a Spanish noblewoman, painted at the height of her hold over Ludwig I of Bavaria. Her place in the Schönheitengalerie was itself a small political event, the affair contributing to the king's abdication the following year.

title: Prometheus Bound
description: The Titan Prometheus is chained to a crag of the Caucasus at dawn, an eagle wheeling above to tear at his liver, the sun rising behind distant snow-capped peaks. Exhibited at the National Academy of Design in 1847, Cole's late mythological piece adapts Aeschylus to the vertical drama of the Hudson River sublime.

provenance.collection: Fine Arts Museums of San Francisco
provenance.location: M. H. de Young Memorial Museum

title: Tamar
description: The biblical Tamar, daughter-in-law of Judah, is rendered as a brooding half-length figure veiled in shadowed reds. Hayez, the central painter of Italian Romanticism, treats Old Testament heroines with the same charged sensuality and theatrical chiaroscuro he brought to his patriotic allegories.

title: Barrikade in der Breiten Straße
description: A barricade of paving stones and overturned carts blocks the Breite Strasse in Berlin during the March 1848 revolution, a tricolour flag planted at the summit. Gaertner, the city's leading topographical painter, sketched the uprising on the spot and worked it up in oil that same year.

title: Battle of Çesme at Night
description: Ottoman ships burn in the bay of Cesme as the Russian fleet under Alexei Orlov destroys the Turkish line on the night of 25-26 June 1770. Painted in 1848 and now in the Aivazovsky National Gallery at Feodosia, the canvas belongs to the marine painter's cycle of naval victories commissioned during his years as official painter to the Russian Admiralty.

title: hanging scroll
description: A hanging scroll depicting the arhat Handaka Sonja, shaven-headed and large-eared, summoning a dragon from his begging bowl amid a coiling rain cloud. Kuniyoshi handles the Buddhist iconography in ink and pale colour with the muscular drawing he refined in his warrior prints.

title: In the Berkshires
description: A herdsman drives cattle along a country road through the rolling western Massachusetts hills, with farms and a steeple visible in the valley below. Inness painted the picture between 1848 and 1850 in the Hudson River School idiom of his early career, before his shift toward the Barbizon manner; it hangs in the Thyssen-Bornemisza in Madrid.
credit: Colección Carmen Thyssen-Bornemisza en depósito en el Museo Thyssen-Bornemisza

title: Menzel's sister Emilie
description: A small, intimate study of the painter's sister Emilie asleep in a chair, her head fallen to one shoulder beneath a lamp. Menzel's private domestic oils, made off the public radar, anticipate Impressionism in their sketchy handling and unsentimental observation of momentary light.

title: Self-portrait Karl Brjullow
description: Bryullov, in his sixtieth year, faces the viewer in a dark coat, his hand resting against a cushion, the long illness that would soon kill him visible in his pale features. He painted the self-portrait in Rome in 1848 during convalescence; it now hangs in the State Tretyakov Gallery.

title: Self-Portrait with Pipe
description: An early self-portrait from Courbet's Romantic-tinged youth, the painter shown smoking a long pipe with hooded eyes and a tilted head. Strong dark-on-dark modelling and a deliberately bohemian air announce the self-mythologising persona he would build through the 1850s.

title: The Cornell Farm
description: A panoramic view of James C. Cornell's prize Northampton, Pennsylvania farmstead, with rows of livestock paraded in the foreground and white outbuildings stretching to the horizon. Hicks painted the canvas in 1848 to commemorate Cornell's prizes at the Bucks County agricultural fair; it entered the National Gallery of Art in Washington in 1964.

title: Carl Spitzweg - Im Dachstübchen
description: The Garret or The Attic (c. 1840s). Private collection

title: Kagesue
description: Two mounted samurai surge through the rapids of the Uji in their famed race to lead the charge during the Genpei War. Kuniyoshi packs the triptych with churning water and twisting horses, exemplifying the warrior-print genre (musha-e) he revived in the late Edo period.

title: Portrait of Sophia Shuvalova
description: Sophia Andreevna Shuvalova, twenty years old and recently married to Count Alexei Bobrinsky, sits in a white silk gown against a backdrop of dark drapery. Bryullov, by then living in Italy on doctor's orders, completed this portrait in 1849, a few years before his death in Manziana.

title: Stormy sea at night
description: A three-masted ship rolls in heavy seas under a broken moon, its sails reefed against the swell, foam glowing pale where the waves crest. Aivazovsky painted dozens of nocturnal storm scenes throughout the 1840s, perfecting the thinly glazed translucent water that became his signature.

title: The Haunted Manor
description: An ivy-choked manor stands beyond a dark woodland pool that catches a livid sunset. Painted early in Hunt's career, the eerie stillness and minutely studied foliage signal the emerging Pre-Raphaelite commitment to truth-to-nature charged with literary mood.

title: The Wreck Buoy
description: A scarlet buoy bobs above a foundered hull as a low rainbow arcs over a ruffled sea. One of Turner's last completed oils, the picture reworks an earlier seascape into a meditation on hazard and salvage.

title: Boar Lane
description: A wet Leeds thoroughfare at dusk, gas lamps haloed in mist and shopfronts mirrored on the slick pavement. Grimshaw built a career on these meticulously observed urban nocturnes, balancing Pre-Raphaelite detail with a Whistlerian feel for atmospheric blue-greens.

title: Cats Suggested as The Fifty-three Stations of the Tōkaidō
description: Kuniyoshi, a noted cat lover, replaces every post town on the Tōkaidō highway with a cat whose pose or attribute puns on the station's name. The triptych is a tour de force of Edo wordplay (mitate) and ukiyo-e woodblock printing, made when actor prints had been restricted by Tenpō reform censorship.

title: Der Maler auf einer Waldlichtung
description: A plein-air painter has stretched out on his back beneath a propped umbrella in a forest clearing, paint box at his feet. The compact panel is a gentle self-mockery of the Romantic ideal of the artist communing with nature.
credit: Joachim Nagel: Carl Spitzweg. Belser, Stuttgart 2008, S. 11

title: Frederick the Great Playing the Flute at Sanssouci
description: Menzel reconstructs an evening concert at Sanssouci, with Frederick the Great playing flute beside C.P.E. Bach at the harpsichord and Quantz, Benda, and the Margravine Wilhelmine listening. Painted under Friedrich Wilhelm IV, it crowns the artist's long Prussian historical project.

title: Susanna at Her Bath
description: The biblical Susanna twists modestly at her bath, surprised by the elders whose presence is implied beyond the frame. Hayez handles the polished nude in the National Gallery, London, with a sculptural finish indebted to Canova and the warm tonalities of his Venetian training.
credit: the second upload from File:Francesco Hayez 054.jpg; -; National Gallery, London - online catalogue

title: Tänzerinnen in Blau
description: Four ballerinas in pale blue tutus stand backstage adjusting their costumes and bodices, their faces averted from the viewer. Degas worked the subject of dancers at rest from the 1870s onward; this canvas, traditionally dated to the late nineteenth century, hangs in the Pushkin Museum in Moscow.

title: The Church at Vétheuil
description: The Church Vétheuil

title: The Ninth Wave
description: Shipwrecked sailors cling to a splintered mast as the towering ninth wave — said in Russian seafaring lore to be the most destructive of a storm — rises beneath a luminous dawn sky. Aivazovsky completed the painting in 1850 in Saint Petersburg; it has stayed at the Russian Museum since the Imperial collection and is the defining canvas of Russian Romantic marine painting.

title: Mariana
description: Drawn from Tennyson's poem after the Shakespearean character, Mariana stretches wearily at her embroidery beside a stained-glass window, autumn leaves drifting onto the floor. Millais paints the heraldic glass and velvet gown with founding Pre-Raphaelite precision, every fibre and pane separately observed.
credit: Google Arts & Culture — 6wGvnPEiyH8RFA Also available at http://www.tate-images.com/results.asp?image=T07553&wwwflag=3&imagepos=41 .

title: Monet w1050
description: A Belle-Île seascape from Monet's 1886 Brittany campaign, where he confronted the Atlantic's dark, jagged cliffs under shifting weather. The palette tightens to slate, violet and bottle-green, with broken brushwork registering the swell against rock.

title: Monet w1054
description: Painted during the artist's ten-week stay on Belle-Île-en-Mer, the canvas wrestles with pyramidal sea-stacks and pounding surf. Monet worked in oilskins on the cliffs, layering short, scumbled strokes to capture spray and the heavy Atlantic light.

title: Monet w1056
description: Another study from the Belle-Île series, in which Monet returned again and again to the same outcrops to track changing weather. Cool blues and bruised purples dominate, the sea built up in dense, choppy strokes that mimic the swell itself.

title: Monet w1065
description: A motif drawn from Monet's Belle-Île campaign on Brittany's wild south coast, where granite needles meet a relentless sea. The painter mixed lead white into deep ultramarines to render foam, working in the open air against squalls that often interrupted the sittings.

title: Monet w1075
description: From the artist's mid-1880s output, this canvas shows the loosened, near-abstract handling Monet was developing on the Channel coast. Surface texture takes priority over contour, with the brushstroke itself conveying wind, weather and tide.

title: Monet w1089
description: A landscape from Monet's most prolific decade at Giverny, where the garden and surrounding meadows became his open-air laboratory. Light is registered in feathered, comma-shaped strokes that trade modeling for vibration of colour.

title: Monet w1120
description: Painted in the late 1880s, the canvas belongs to Monet's increasing tendency to dissolve subject into atmosphere. Broken touches of complementary colour set the picture humming, anticipating the serial method of the haystacks and poplars.

title: Monet w1155
description: A Giverny landscape from the years when Monet was systematizing his serial practice, returning to the same view under successive lights. Foliage is broken into flickering touches that read as foliage only at a distance.

title: Ophelia
description: Shakespeare's drowning Ophelia drifts among meadow flowers along the Hogsmill River in Surrey. Millais painted the riverbank botany on site over five months, then posed Elizabeth Siddal in a heated bathtub for the figure. Each bloom carries Victorian floral symbolism for grief, innocence and madness.

title: Poplars in the Sun
description: Part of Monet's poplar series on the banks of the Epte, painted from a flat-bottomed boat moored among the trees. The verticals march across the canvas in a near-decorative rhythm, sunlight filtered into juxtaposed greens, lavenders and rose.

title: Portrait of Princess Albert de Broglie
description: Pauline de Broglie is set against a tapestry-hung wall, her blue satin gown rendered with Ingres's near-fanatical attention to fabric. The portrait was painted late in his career and is now a centrepiece of the Robert Lehman Collection at the Metropolitan Museum.
credit: This file was derived from: Jean auguste dominique ingres princesse albert de broglie.jpg :

title: Porträt der Madame Moitessier
description: Madame Moitessier stands in black velvet and lace, a heavy gold bracelet anchoring her gloved wrist. Ingres laboured on his Moitessier portraits across more than a decade, prizing the linear contour and porcelain finish that define his late society style; this version belongs to the National Gallery of Art in Washington.
credit: National Gallery of Art, Washington, D. C., online collection

title: An Idyll
description: An early pastoral by Gérôme in the vein of his Néo-Grec circle, reaching back to Anacreontic and Pompeian models. Slender nudes, shallow stage-like space and porcelain-cool color place the picture closer to his Greek Interior than to his later Orientalist scenes.

title: Back View of Fuji from Dream Mtn in Kai Province
englishTitle: Back View of Fuji from the Dream Mountain in Kai Province
description: Hiroshige reverses the conventional southern view of Fuji, glimpsing the sacred peak from Kai Province on the mountain's far side. Part of his first Thirty-six Views series, the design uses graduated bokashi printing to layer mist, peak, and foreground.

title: Sokokura by Hiroshige1
englishTitle: Sokokura, from Seven Hot Springs of Hakone
description: A woodblock view of Sokokura, one of the seven hot springs of Hakone, with bathers and travelers gathered amid the steep wooded gorge. The print belongs to Hiroshige's series Hakone shichiyu zue, devoted to the spa villages prized by Edo-period travelers along the Tōkaidō.

title: Unter den Linden
description: Berlin's grand boulevard stretches past the equestrian statue of Frederick the Great, with the Königliche Oper on the left and the Stadtschloss closing the vista. Gaertner, the city's pre-eminent vedutista, charts the Prussian capital with architect's precision under a clear summer light.

title: Awa Province : Naruto Whirlpools
englishTitle: Awa Province: Naruto Whirlpools, from the series Famous Places in the Sixty-odd Provinces
description: A vertical ōban from the Famous Places in the Sixty-odd Provinces series, looking down on the swirling Naruto whirlpools that churn between Awa and Awaji. Hiroshige flattens the sea into concentric arcs of bokashi blue, framed by a steep cliff at left.
credit: Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, online database

title: Battle of sinope
description: Russian warships pound the Ottoman fleet at anchor in the harbour of Sinope, flames erupting from the wooden hulls against a black sky. Aivazovsky painted the November 1853 engagement, an early Crimean War victory for Admiral Nakhimov, from official accounts the year it occurred.
credit: ( Original text: Naval school, St. Petersburg, Russia. ) Original uploader was Pietje96 at en.wikipedia

title: Cornelis Springer
description: The Jodenbreestraat in Amsterdam, with the house once occupied by Rembrandt at number 4-6 reimagined in its supposed seventeenth-century guise, the Sint-Antoniesluis at right and the tower of the Zuiderkerk rising behind. Springer, a Romantic topographical painter, treated the city as a chain of historicising stage sets rather than the contemporary streetscape.

title: The Awakening Conscience
description: A young woman starts up from her lover's lap in a cluttered London parlour, her face caught at the instant of moral recognition. Hunt loaded the picture with Pre-Raphaelite symbolism, every object on the patterned wallpaper, the discarded glove, the cat at the table chosen to spell out the cost of a kept woman's situation.

title: The Order of Release 1746
description: A Highland wife presents a release order to a soldier guarding her wounded Jacobite husband, who collapses against her with their child asleep on his shoulder. Effie Ruskin posed for the wife — the sittings precipitated her separation from John Ruskin and eventual marriage to Millais.
credit: Transferred from en.wikipedia to Commons by Mattis . Original uploader was Paul Barlow

title: The Sleeping Spinner
description: A young spinner has fallen asleep at her wheel, distaff drooping in her lap. Courbet treats the rural genre subject with monumental gravity, applying paint thickly with knife and brush so that the homely interior carries the weight of a Salon picture.

title: Christ on the Sea of Galilee
description: Christ sleeps in the stern of a fishing boat while terrified apostles wrestle the sail against a green wall of water. Delacroix returned to the Gospel subject repeatedly in the 1850s, each version intensifying the chromatic clash between the storm and the calm figure asleep in its centre.

title: Das Ständchen
description: A hopeful suitor stands beneath a balcony serenading an unseen sweetheart, while neighbours watch from their windows. Spitzweg returned often to this nocturnal Ständchen subject, savouring the gap between Romantic gesture and small-town audience.

title: Roman Pilgrims
description: A group of Italian pilgrims rests on the road, products of Lewis's residence in Rome during the late 1830s before he settled in Cairo. The picture catalogues regional costume with the same ethnographic precision he would later turn on the Ottoman world. It marks his transition from Spanish to Mediterranean genre subjects.

title: The Finding of the Saviour in the Temple
Arab saddling his horse
description: A North African rider tightens the girth of his white horse against a backdrop of rocky terrain and pale sky. Drawing on sketches made during his 1832 mission to Morocco with the Comte de Mornay, Delacroix returned for decades to the Arab horseman as a Romantic exemplar of dignified physical action.

title: Arabian nights 3 by John Frederick Lewis
description: A finely worked Orientalist scene drawn from the Thousand and One Nights, set inside one of the tiled, latticed interiors Lewis studied during his decade in Cairo. He is best known for the jewel-bright watercolour technique that lets sunlight pick its way across carpets and costume.

title: Im Harem
description: An odalisque reclines under fretwork screens in a Munich painter's idea of a Turkish harem, the orientalist staffage rendered with Spitzweg's trademark twinkling humour. The artist drew his exotic detail entirely from prints and travel literature, never having visited the East.

title: Rear view of the Houses at Schloßfreiheit
description: The crowded rear façades of the middle-class houses lining the Schloßfreiheit drop straight to the Spree, washing visible from upper windows. Gaertner recorded the row in 1855; in 1896 the entire street was demolished to clear the site for the Wilhelmine Monument to Emperor Wilhelm I.
credit: Originally from Google Art Project. The Google Art Project image has since been edited or redone and is at [1] .

title: Rider Attacked by a Jaguar
description: A jaguar springs from a thicket onto the haunches of a rearing horse, its rider thrown back as the predator's claws sink into the animal's flank. Delacroix borrowed the motif from Rubens and the Stubbs lion-and-horse tradition, condensing the struggle into a tight vertical of intersecting muscle.

title: Rocks at Mouthier by Gustave Courbet
description: A close-up view of weathered limestone cliffs near the artist's native Franche-Comté, the river snaking through a narrow valley below. Courbet builds the rock face with palette-knife slabs of paint, asserting landscape as raw geological matter rather than picturesque scenery.

title: The intercepted love letter
description: A pair of conspirators in a courtyard puzzle over a love letter snatched from its addressee. The narrative anecdote, the costumed protagonists, and the pinpoint architectural detail are textbook Spitzweg, drawn from a stage tradition rather than direct observation.

title: A Frank Encampment in the Desert of Mount Sinai
description: A British traveller's tent camp pitched in the Sinai wilderness, with St Catherine's monastery faintly visible in the distance. Lewis drew on a decade of life in Cairo to render carpets, tasselled saddles and Bedouin retainers with miniaturist exactitude. The watercolour fuses Orientalist reportage with the topographical tradition.

title: Achille De Gas in the Uniform of a Cadet
description: The artist's younger brother Achille stands in the dark blue dress uniform of a French naval cadet, hand resting on a sabre hilt. Painted around 1856-57 while Degas was beginning his Italian study years, the canvas is held by the National Gallery of Art in Washington.

title: Male Nude
description: Male Nude Artist: Edgar Degas (French, Paris 1834–1917 Paris) Date: 1856 Medium: Oil on canvas Dimensions: 13 3/4 x 24 1/4 in. (34. 9 x 61.

title: Milton
description: A view of the Hudson Valley near Milton, New York, with grazing cattle in a meadow and the broad river opening behind. Inness was working in the wake of his European study trips, still close to the Hudson River School idiom before his later turn toward Barbizon-influenced softness; now in the Yale University Art Gallery.
credit: Yale University Art Gallery, Yale University, New Haven, Conn.

title: Monet w1001
description: From the mid-1880s, when Monet was extending his repertoire of coastal and rural motifs after settling at Giverny. The brushwork is densely woven, building landscape from short, directional strokes of contrasting hue.

title: Monet w1003
description: A mid-1880s landscape from Monet's expanded raisonné, painted as he consolidated the rapid, plein-air manner into a more deliberate decorative surface. Form yields to a tapestry of small coloured touches.

title: Monet w1016
description: A landscape entry in Monet's catalogue raisonné showing his characteristic divisionist-leaning brushwork of the period. Local colour is broken across complementary touches so the eye reassembles the scene at viewing distance.

title: Monet w1035
description: From Monet's Étretat campaigns of the 1880s, when he braved cliff ledges and rising tides to capture the chalk arches in changing weather. The handling marries graphic structure to looser, atmospheric water.

title: Monet w1042
description: A Normandy coast subject from Monet's prolific Étretat-era output, where rock, sea, and sky are unified by a high-keyed palette of blue, lilac, and creamy white. Brushwork follows the contours of swell and stone.

title: Monet w1179
description: An earlier landscape predating the high Impressionist style, with a more traditional, tonal handling than the artist's later work. Drawing remains visible beneath the paint, and the palette stays close to a Barbizon range of earths and greens.

title: Monet w1296
description: An early landscape from Monet's formative years, before the Impressionist breakthrough of the 1870s. The composition retains traditional perspectival depth, with paint laid more thinly than in the textured works of his maturity.

title: Monet w1563
description: A landscape held within Monet's Impressionist repertoire, where the optical mixing of small coloured strokes carries the work. Atmosphere takes precedence over drawing, the eye assembling the scene from a tissue of brushmarks.

title: Monet w1636
description: From Monet's later Giverny output, where landscape gives way to immersive fields of colour and reflection. The painter's brushwork loosens further, sacrificing legibility of motif to a unified surface vibration.

title: Monet w948
description: A very early work from Monet's teenage years in Le Havre, predating his formal training under Boudin and his move toward Impressionism. The handling is more conventional than his later production but already shows an interest in outdoor observation.

title: Monet w961
description: An adolescent piece from Monet's Le Havre period, made before he had committed to landscape painting in the open air. Drawing and tonal modelling still carry the work, with only hints of the looser facture he would soon develop.

title: Monet w962
description: An early Monet landscape painted while the artist was still a teenager working from nature in Normandy. The brushwork shows the influence of Boudin and the Barbizon school, foreshadowing the loose handling that would later define Impressionism.

title: Sumida River
englishTitle: Suijin Shrine and Massaki on the Sumida River, from One Hundred Famous Views of Edo
