description: From One Hundred Famous Views of Edo, the print frames the Sumida River through the trees of the Suijin shrine grove at Masaki. Hiroshige uses the steep foreground branches and high horizon characteristic of the late series to fold the viewer into the riverside scene.
credit: Image: http://collections.lacma.org/sites/default/files/remote_images/piction/ma-18199982-O3.jpg Gallery: http://collections.lacma.org/node/190172 archive copy at the Wayback Machine

title: Tempest by Sounion
description: A storm breaks over the headland of Cape Sounion on the southern tip of Attica, the ruined columns of the Temple of Poseidon picked out above churning sea. Aivazovsky, court painter to the Russian navy, treated the Aegean coastline as a stage for Romantic seascape rather than archaeological record.

title: The Lackawanna Valley
description: A reclining figure on a hillside looks down on the new Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad roundhouse outside Scranton, Pennsylvania, with a locomotive trailing smoke through cleared stumps. Commissioned by the railroad's first president as a promotional image, Inness's panorama frames American industrial expansion within a pastoral Hudson River idiom; now at the National Gallery of Art.

title: View of Constantinople and the Bosphorus
description: Caïques and Ottoman steamers drift on the Bosphorus beneath the silhouette of Constantinople, the domes and minarets of Süleymaniye and Hagia Sophia rising through golden haze. Aivazovsky visited the city several times in the 1840s and 1850s and made the Bosphorus panorama one of his recurring set pieces for Russian and Ottoman patrons alike.

title: Yoro Waterfall in Mino Province
englishTitle: Mino Province: Yōrō Waterfall, from Famous Views of the Sixty-odd Provinces
description: From the late series Famous Views of the Sixty-odd Provinces, this vertical print shows the Yōrō Falls of Mino plunging through a wooded ravine. Hiroshige exploits the tall format to stretch the cataract into a single white ribbon against deep green cliffs, with figures dwarfed at its base.

title: Bamboo Yards
description: An Autumn print from Hiroshige's One Hundred Famous Views of Edo, showing the bamboo yards along the Kanda River where poles were stacked vertically into stark, near-abstract patterns. The diagonal viewpoint and reduced palette typify the formal boldness of his final great series.

title: Egyptian Recruits Crossing the Desert
description: Painted after Gérôme's first journey up the Nile, the canvas shows conscripts being driven across the sand under guard. The high horizon, sharp shadows and ethnographic costume detail are characteristic of his fastidious Orientalist manner.

title: Justitia
description: A weathered statue of blindfolded Lady Justice stands with broken scales while a soldier loiters in shadow behind her, a wry Biedermeier comment on the gap between law and power. The panel was sold under Nazi duress by Jewish collector Leo Bendel and only restituted to his heirs in 2019.

title: Lake Nemi
description: The crater lake of Nemi in the Alban Hills south of Rome lies in deep shadow below a wooded ridge, a faint procession of trees marking the rim. Inness painted the site during his second Italian sojourn in 1856-57; the canvas is now in the Yale University Art Gallery.
credit: Yale University Art Gallery, Yale University, New Haven, Conn.

title: Plum Park at Kameido
englishTitle: Plum Garden at Kameido, from One Hundred Famous Views of Edo
description: A celebrated plum tree in the Kameido garden east of Edo, its blossoming branch thrust across the foreground while visitors stroll behind in a red-suffused dusk. Hiroshige's print from One Hundred Famous Views of Edo was later copied in oil by Van Gogh.

title: Sudden Shower Over Shin-Ohashi Bridge and Atake
englishTitle: Sudden Shower over Shin-Ōhashi Bridge and Atake, from One Hundred Famous Views of Edo
description: From One Hundred Famous Views of Edo, figures hurry across the Shin-Ōhashi bridge as a sudden summer downpour falls in fine engraved lines over the Sumida. The compressed perspective and slanting rain made the print a touchstone for European Japonisme; Van Gogh later copied it in oil.

title: Suido Bridge and Surugadai
description: From One Hundred Famous Views of Edo, Hiroshige's late masterwork-series, this Summer sheet looks down from the Suidobashi bridge over the Kanda aqueduct toward the scholar district of Surugadai. A giant carp streamer for Boys' Day floats in the foreground, a hallmark of his daring close-up framing.

title: The Coffee Bearer
description: A young Egyptian woman carries a brass coffee tray through a marble courtyard, ducking below the lintel of a sunlit doorway. Lewis stages the scene to showcase the architectural light effects he studied during his Cairo years. The metalwork, sash and tilework are executed with miniaturist watercolour precision in oils.

title: Utagawa Hiroshige
englishTitle: View of the Naruto Whirlpools in Awa Province
description: A vertical triptych charts the famed Naruto whirlpools off Awa province, the churning indigo eddies set beneath a banded sky. Hiroshige stretches the ooban format to give the tide its full vertiginous scale.

title: 20. The Entrance Gate In Enoshima
englishTitle: The Entrance to Enoshima in Sagami Province, from Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji
description: Plate twenty of Hiroshige's Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, showing pilgrims passing through the bronze torii at Enoshima with Fuji floating across Sagami Bay. The composition is built from flat overlapping silhouettes, a hallmark of late-Edo ukiyo-e landscape design.

title: 21. Lake In Hakone
englishTitle: The Lake at Hakone, from Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji
description: Plate twenty-one of the Thirty-six Views, with the dark glassy surface of Lake Ashi at Hakone reflecting Mount Fuji and the surrounding peaks. Hiroshige was a master of these mirror-symmetry compositions, splitting the sheet between solid landscape and its watery double.

title: 26. The Oi River Between Suruga and Totomi Provinces
englishTitle: The Ōi River between Suruga and Tōtōmi Provinces, from the series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji
description: Porters ford the broad shallows of the Oi River, with Fuji's cone framed beyond. Hiroshige drew the design for the Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji issued by Tsutaya Kichizo, deploying the bokashi gradient technique to suggest mist rising off the water.

title: 32. Dog Eye Pass
englishTitle: Inume Pass in Kai Province, from Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji
description: Hiroshige's view from Inume Pass in Kai Province looks down on a sea of cloud broken by Fuji's summit, plate 32 of his Thirty-six Views series. The composition compresses foreground rocks and distant peak into a single graphic plane, a hallmark of late-Edo landscape design.

title: 34. Kuroto Bay
englishTitle: Kuroto Bay in Kazusa Province, from Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji
description: Boats drift in Kuroto Bay with Fuji visible across the water, plate 34 of Hiroshige's Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji. The flat blue expanses and economical drawing of sails reflect the woodblock vocabulary that would soon enthral European Japonisme.

title: 36 Views of Mount Fuji - 18. The Sagami River
englishTitle: The Sagami River, from the series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji
description: Plate eighteen of Hiroshige's late Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, with the Sagami River winding through Kanagawa Province toward the snow-capped peak. The vertical ōban format compresses foreground rapids and distant cone into a single, telescoped view.

title: 36 Views of Mount Fuji - 19. The Seven-Ri Beach
englishTitle: Seven-Ri Beach in Sagami Province, from Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji
description: Plate nineteen of the Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, depicting Shichirigahama, the seven-ri stretch of coast in Sagami Province. Enoshima crouches on the horizon while Fuji floats beyond, the printer using bokashi gradient to fade sea into sky.

title: 36 Views of Mount Fuji - 33. Kogane Plain
englishTitle: Kogane Plain in Shimōsa Province, from Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji
description: A wide view across the Kogane plain in Shimosa, with Fuji blue on the horizon and grasses sketched in the foreground. From Hiroshige's Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, the print uses the bokashi gradation to soften sky and distance.

title: 36 Views of Mount Fuji- 23. The Sea off Satta
englishTitle: The Sea off Satta in Suruga Province, from Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji
description: Plate twenty-three of the Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji. Big stylised waves curl in the foreground off Satta Point on the Tōkaidō road, with Fuji rising serenely behind, an answer to Hokusai's earlier Great Wave composition.

title: 36 Views of Mount Fuji' - 36. The Hoda Coast
englishTitle: The Hoda Coast in Awa Province, from the series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji
description: The closing print of Hiroshige's Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji shows the rocky Hoda coast in Awa Province, Fuji floating across Edo Bay. Crisp keyblock outlines and indigo seas give the design the graphic clarity that defined his late style.

title: Fuji on the Left of Tokaido Road
englishTitle: Mount Fuji on the Left of the Tōkaidō Road, from Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji
description: Travellers move along the Tokaido highway as Mount Fuji rises to the left, a print from Hiroshige's posthumously published Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji. The composition layers near figures against a flattened distance, exploiting the woodblock medium's graded skies and crisp silhouettes.

title: Fuji sanjūrokkei Tōto ikkokubashi
englishTitle: Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji: Ichikobu Bridge in the Eastern Capital
description: Sheet from Hiroshige's late series Thirty-Six Views of Mount Fuji, showing Edo's Ikkoku Bridge with the sacred peak rising behind the city's tiled rooftops. The print uses the deep cobalt bokashi gradation Hiroshige favoured for sky and water, contrasting urban bustle below with serene distance.

title: Italian Landscape
description: Sailboats drift on the still water of Lake Maggiore beneath an alpine evening sky, distant peaks fading into haze along the Italian shore. Painted in 1858 during one of Aivazovsky's tours abroad, the canvas trades his usual Black Sea storms for the softer Lombard atmosphere of the lake district.

title: The Bellelli Family
description: Degas's aunt Laura Bellelli stands in mourning black with her two daughters in their Florence apartment, her husband Gennaro turned away in an armchair at right, a chalk portrait of her recently dead father pinned to the wall behind. Begun during the artist's 1858-59 stay with the family and completed in Paris, the canvas is now the centrepiece of the early Degas rooms at the Musée d'Orsay.
credit: Google Arts & Culture — CAEtElXoJtKBnQ RMN (Musée d'Orsay) / Gérard Blot This is a featured picture on the Persian language Wikipedia ( نگاره‌های برگزیده ) and is considered one of the finest images. See its nomination here . If you think this file should be featured on Wikimedia Commons as well, feel free to nominate it . If you have an image of similar quality that can be published under a suitable copyright license , be sure to upload it, tag it, and nominate it .

title: The courier in the Rosenthal
description: A village postman trudges along a sun-drenched lane in the Rosenthal, satchel slung at his hip. Spitzweg, a trained pharmacist who painted in his spare hours, made a career of these affectionately ironic small-town vignettes.
credit: Joachim Nagel: Carl Spitzweg. Belser, Stuttgart 2008, S. 31

provenance.collection: Museum für Kunst und Kulturgeschichte der Philipps-Universität Marburg
provenance.location: Museum für Kunst und Kulturgeschichte der Philipps-Universität Marburg

title: The lute player
description: A single seated figure tunes a long-necked lute in a dim Cairo interior, the strings catching a shaft of light. Gérôme uses the musician as a pretext for a study in muted tonality and meticulous costume detail.

title: The Otsuki Plain
englishTitle: The Plain of Ōtsuki in Kai Province, from Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji
description: Travellers cross the open plain of Otsuki with Fuji set against a pale sky, plate 31 of the Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji. Hiroshige favoured such low horizons to let the mountain dominate, balanced by the human-scale activity of road and field.

title: The Pine Forest of Mio
englishTitle: Miho Pine Grove in Suruga Province, from Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji
description: From Hiroshige's late Mount Fuji series, the spit of pines at Miho-no-Matsubara curls into Suruga Bay with Fuji on the far shore. The site is bound up with the noh play Hagoromo, and Hiroshige uses bokashi blues and the dense black of pine needles to set its quiet mood.

title: The Sea off the Miura Peninsula
englishTitle: The Sea off the Miura Peninsula in Sagami Province, from Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji
description: From Hiroshige's late Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji series, published shortly before his death. A foreground of dark, choppy water frames the distant cone of Fuji across the bay; the woodblock printer's bokashi gradients soften sky and sea into bands of graded blue.

title: The Teahouse with the View of Mt. Fuji
englishTitle: Teahouse with a View of Mount Fuji, from the series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji
description: From Hiroshige's Thirty-Six Views of Mount Fuji, travellers pause at a roadside teahouse while the snow-tipped volcano floats beyond. The graded blue sky and crisp foreground figures show the woodblock master's command of bokashi printing and his eye for the everyday rhythms of Edo travel.

title: The Vale of Rest
description: Two nuns dig a grave at twilight in a walled cemetery, one resting on her spade as a coffin-shaped cloud drifts overhead. Begun outdoors at Kinnoull near Perth, the painting marks Millais's shift from minute Pre-Raphaelite finish toward broader, mood-saturated landscape.

title: View At Rouelles
description: A youthful landscape of Rouelles in the Le Havre hinterland, often cited as Monet's earliest surviving oil. The careful, almost Corot-like handling of trees and stream marks the threshold before his conversion to outdoor, sketch-based painting.

title: Wild Goose Hill and the Tone River
englishTitle: Wild Goose Hill on the Tone River (Kōnodai, Tonegawa), from Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji
description: From Hiroshige's late Thirty-Six Views of Mount Fuji, the Tone River winds toward the distant snow cone past Wild Goose Hill. Migrating geese punctuate a sky printed in deep bokashi blue, the woodblock gradation that became the artist's signature atmospheric device.

title: Ingres Etude Bain Turc Louvre 1859
description: A preparatory drawing in the Louvre's Cabinet des dessins for Le Bain turc, the circular canvas Ingres completed at age 82. The sheet shows him reworking the languid female nudes he had drawn from life decades earlier into a single dense Orientalist tableau.

title: The Kiss
description: A young couple embrace on a stone staircase, the woman's blue gown and the man's red tights forming the colours of the French and Italian flags. Hayez's most popular canvas became a coded emblem of the Risorgimento and the alliance behind Italian unification.
credit: Web Gallery of Art : Image Info about artwork wga QS:P11807,"s-e.html?/html/h/hayez/6hayez"

title: Fox in the Snow
description: A red fox crouches over its prey in a frozen field, painted with the palette knife's broad, material slabs that Courbet championed in his Realist landscapes. The unsentimental subject and the granular, scraped whites of the snow strip the hunt scene of Romantic glamour.
credit: dallasmuseumofart.org; The AMICA Library; Dallas Museum of Art, online collection

title: Horses coming out of the sea
description: Two Moroccan grooms drive their horses out of the surf onto a stretch of North African beach, the animals shaking water from their flanks. Painted in 1860, three years before the artist's death, the canvas distils thirty years of Delacroix's Maghreb sketchbooks into a single concentrated motif; now at the Phillips Collection in Washington.

title: James Abbott McNeill Whistler
description: Plate from the Thames Set, made when Whistler took rooms at the Angel Inn to study London's working riverfront. A balcony view crowded with rigging, mooring posts and a pair of seamen, etched with the dense, descriptive line he later abandoned for atmospheric suggestion.

title: Schmetterlinge
description: A swirl of butterflies fills the sheet, drawn with finely observed wing markings and a decorative arabesque rhythm. Kaulbach, best known as a history painter, here turns to natural history as ornamental composition.

title: The Black Brunswicker
description: A young Brunswick cavalry officer takes leave of his sweetheart on the eve of Waterloo, her hand braced against the door he is determined to open. Millais paired the black death's-head hussar uniform against shimmering ivory silk to heighten the parting. Charles Dickens's daughter Kate modelled for the woman.

title: The Blue Grotto on Capri
description: Sunlight refracted through the submerged entrance of Capri's Grotta Azzurra fills the cavern with the cobalt glow that made it a Grand Tour pilgrimage site. The picture is in fact by Berlin landscapist Carl Friedrich Seiffert, who specialised in luminous Italian veduta.

title: The Oceanids
description: A wood-engraved fantasy of the Oceanid sea nymphs rising through dark surf. Doré, working largely as a print designer, deploys his trademark high-contrast hatching to model luminous bodies against deep velvety blacks, building atmosphere from tonal extremes rather than colour.

title: The Thames in Ice
description: Painted during the great freeze that gripped London in the winter of 1860, when Whistler was lodging at Wapping. A merchant ship sits locked among broken floes, its rigging set against a smoke-grey sky in the muted, almost monochrome palette he was developing for the river.

title: Young Spartans exercising
description: Four Spartan girls challenge four boys to a wrestling match in a bare landscape, with Lycurgus and a group of older citizens watching at right. Drawing on Plutarch's life of the legislator, Degas reworked the canvas across the 1860s and into later decades; the picture is now in the National Gallery, London.

title: Zeitungsleser im Hausgarten
description: A Biedermeier gentleman absorbs himself in his newspaper amid the trellised greenery of a small private garden. Spitzweg specialized in such gently humorous bourgeois vignettes, painted in rich enamel-like color, that catalogued the introspective civic culture of mid-nineteenth-century Munich.

title: Bemberg Fondation Toulouse - Self-portrait paintings by Henri Fantin-Latour
description: An early self-portrait by the painter best known for his hushed flower pieces and group portraits of the Parisian avant-garde. The dark ground and concentrated gaze owe much to his close study of seventeenth-century Dutch masters in the Louvre.

title: Symphony in White
englishTitle: Symphony in White, No. 1: The White Girl
description: Joanna Hiffernan stands full-length in a flowing white dress on a white drape, holding a single lily. Whistler's emphasis on subtle gradations of cream, ivory and pale flesh tones over storytelling helped lay the ground for Aestheticism's art-for-art's-sake credo.
credit: National Gallery of Art, Washington, D. C., online collection

title: Music in the Tuileries
description: A fashionable crowd in top hats and crinolines listens to a band in the Tuileries gardens, the canvas crowded with portraits of Manet's circle, including Baudelaire, Gautier and Fantin-Latour. The flat patches of black coats and abrupt cropping mark Manet's first decisive turn toward painting modern Parisian life.

title: Ovid among the Scythians
description: The exiled Roman poet Ovid reclines on the grass of the Black Sea steppe, offered milk and bread by Scythian herdsmen while their horses graze in the background. Delacroix exhibited a smaller version at the 1859 Salon and returned to the subject in 1862, the year before his death; the painting is now at the Metropolitan Museum of Art.
credit: Met Museum (Timeline of Art History); Metropolitan Museum of Art, online collection (The Met object ID 439631)

title: The Turkish bath
description: A circular tondo crowded with bathing women, drawn together from poses Ingres had refined across half a century of nudes. Painted in his eighties for Prince Napoléon, the work distils his lifelong fascination with sinuous contour and the Orientalist harem trope into a single hothouse composition.
credit: This file was derived from: Le Bain Turc, by Jean Auguste Dominique Ingres, from C2RMF.jpg :

title: Don Quijote illustrated by Gustav Dore III
description: Don Quixote rides out across the Spanish meseta with Sancho Panza behind, an illustration from Doré's monumental 1863 edition of Cervantes. The wood-engraved plates, cut by a battery of Parisian engravers, fixed the public image of the knight-errant for the next century.

title: Eduard Gaertner Berlin Bruederstrasse
description: The Brüderstraße on the Spreeinsel in Berlin-Mitte recedes between rows of plastered townhouses toward the tower of the Petrikirche. Gaertner painted the view in 1863, still working in the precise Berlin Biedermeier vedute mode he had practised since the 1820s.
credit: Photograph of the original painting by uploader (not that it mattered, but some Common admins have no idea about German copyright and delete it otherwise).

title: Eve of St Agnes
description: Drawn from Keats's poem, Madeline undresses by moonlight on St Agnes's Eve in the hope of dreaming of her lover. Millais painted the scene by night at Knole House using his wife Effie as model, working in the cool silvered palette characteristic of his later, looser Pre-Raphaelite manner.

title: Monet w24
description: A road by the Saint-Simeon farm near Honfleur, from Monet's earliest Normandy campaigns. The handling still carries the firm tonal modelling of Boudin and Jongkind, his coastal mentors, before the broken Impressionist stroke took hold.

title: Olympia
description: A reclining nude courtesan meets the viewer's gaze with cool defiance, attended by a Black maid bearing flowers from a client. Manet flattens form with stark lighting and sharp tonal contrasts, scandalising the 1865 Salon by transposing Titian's Venus into contemporary Parisian demi-monde.

title: Self-portrait by Edgar Degas
description: The young Degas, around twenty-nine, looks out from a dark ground in a black coat and high collar, his expression guarded and slightly aslant. Painted around 1863, the picture entered the collection of Calouste Gulbenkian and now hangs at the Gulbenkian Museum in Lisbon.
credit: Calouste Gulbenkian Museum in Selected work 30 from Self Portrait: Renaissance to Contemporary (Anthony Bond, Joanna Woodall, ISBN 978-1855143579 ).

title: The Christian Martyrs' Last Prayer
description: A Roman arena scene in which kneeling Christians pray as lions are released and crucified figures burn against the stadium walls. Gerome combines archaeological detail of the Circus Maximus with the polished academic finish typical of his Salon machines.
credit: Walters Art Museum : Home page Info about artwork

title: The Princess from the Land of Porcelain
description: Painted in London during Whistler's japonisme phase, the canvas dresses Christine Spartali in a loose kimono among Asian carpets and a folding screen. Frederick Leyland later acquired it and hung it in the dining room that became the Peacock Room, now reinstalled at the Freer Gallery.
credit: This file was derived from: James McNeill Whistler - La Princesse du pays de la porcelaine - Google Art Project.jpg :

title: A Seascape
description: A nocturnal Channel scene with moonlight breaking through cloud over distant sailing vessels. Made during Monet's formative summers on the Normandy coast, the picture follows the marines of Boudin and Jongkind, with feathery brushwork capturing reflected silver on dark water.

title: La Pointe de la Hève
description: An early Channel-coast view of the headland at Sainte-Adresse, painted when Monet was still working through the lessons of Boudin and the Barbizon school. Wide sky and tide-flat foreground show his lifelong fascination with the meeting of sea and weather.

title: Monet w 42
description: An early landscape from Monet's mid-twenties, when he was painting outdoors in the forest of Fontainebleau and along the Norman coast. The dark tonal range and tighter handling reflect his Barbizon-school roots before the lighter Impressionist palette emerged.

title: Preparation for the exam
description: An early academic study from Repin's student years, depicting young men absorbed in their books before an examination. The careful tonal modelling and observed gestures already show the eye for everyday human drama that would shape his later realist canvases.

title: Romaine Lacaux
description: A poised portrait of a Parisian ceramic-maker's young daughter, seated in a stiff white dress with a flower in her hand. Among Renoir's earliest signed works, it still carries the smooth finish of academic portraiture but already shows his sensitivity to reflected light on translucent fabric.

title: Spring Flowers
description: Peonies, hydrangeas, and lilacs spill from basket and pot against a darkened ground, painted with an almost botanical attentiveness. An early still life, it shows the young Monet weighing studio precision against the looser, light-driven handling that would soon define his work.

title: Symphony in White
description: Whistler's full-length portrait of his model and lover Joanna Hiffernan in a white muslin dress, holding a lily. Conceived as a study in tonal harmony rather than narrative, the picture became a touchstone for the Aesthetic movement's pursuit of art for art's sake.
credit: Whistler Symphony in White no 2 (The Little White Girl)

title: The Battle of the Kearsarge and the Alabama
description: The Confederate raider Alabama lists and burns under fire from the Union sloop Kearsarge off Cherbourg, smoke staining a blue Channel sea. Manet, who was reportedly close enough to watch French pilot boats return from the engagement, treats this American Civil War moment with a high horizon and broadly brushed water that anticipates marine Impressionism.
credit: From en.wiki; The Philadelphia Museum of Art

title: The Dead Christ with Angels
description: Two angels support the slumped body of the dead Christ, his pallid torso lit against shadow. Manet borrows a traditional Lamentation type but flattens modeling and exposes brushwork in a way that scandalized the 1864 Salon, where critics also faulted the placement of the side wound on the wrong flank.

title: Arnaut fumant
description: A standing Albanian irregular smokes a long-stemmed pipe, his costume bristling with daggers and embroidered braid. Gérôme treats the bashi-bazouk as a costume study, the kind of single-figure ethnographic exercise he repeated through the 1860s.

title: Bazille and Camille
description: A figure study made for Monet's lost large-scale Dejeuner sur l'herbe, showing the painter Frederic Bazille and his future wife Camille Doncieux among forest light. The brisk plein-air handling already announces the broken touch that would define Impressionism.

title: Destruction of Leviathan
description: God smites the sea-monster Leviathan with a sword, the beast writhing in the deep amid lightning-lit clouds. Doré's wood-engraved illustration appeared in his folio English Bible, blending Romantic sublimity with the dense cross-hatching that defined his commercial print style.

title: Gustave Courbet 029
description: A nude study in Courbet's signature register, modelled with the dense, kneaded paint and warm flesh tones of his mid-1860s work. The treatment privileges the tactile reality of the body over idealised form, characteristic of the Realist's frank handling of the figure.

title: La Pointe de la Hève at Low Tide
description: Wagons and figures cross the wet sand below the headland of La Hève near Le Havre, Monet's home town. Shown at the Salon of 1865 — his official debut — the canvas owes much to the marine realism of Boudin and Courbet.

title: Monet w58
description: An early landscape from Monet's pre-Impressionist years, before the broken-colour technique fully emerged. The handling still carries traces of Boudin and the Barbizon plein-air tradition that shaped his apprenticeship along the Normandy coast.

title: Still Life with a Carafe, Flowers and Fruit
description: A glass carafe, scattered fruit and a small bouquet are composed on a dark cloth in disciplined Salon order. Among Fantin-Latour's earliest mature still lifes, it shows the precise tonal modelling that drew Whistler's circle to his work.

title: The Artist in His Studio
description: An oil sketch on wood for an unrealised group portrait, showing Whistler at his easel with the models Joanna Hiffernan and Fumette behind him. The thinly brushed greys and creams demonstrate the tonal economy he was beginning to formulate as a programme.

title: The Ragpicker
description: A life-size Spanish-inspired portrait of a Paris chiffonnier propped on his stick, set against a neutral grey ground. Manet borrows the format of Velázquez's philosopher portraits to dignify a marginal modern Parisian.
credit: The Athenaeum: Home - info - pic; The Norton Simon Museum

title: Cleopatra and Caesar
description: Cleopatra steps from the unrolled carpet to confront Caesar at his writing table, the ancient anecdote staged with the polished historicism Gérôme made his trademark. Smooth porcelain finish, archaeologically researched props, and a controlled tonal palette anchor the picture in academic theatre.

title: Dans la forêt de Fontainebleau
description: Figures rest in the dappled clearing of the Forest of Fontainebleau, the wooded preserve south of Paris that drew the Barbizon and early Impressionist painters. Renoir's youthful palette is still rooted in earthy Courbet-like tonality before his shift to brighter spectral colour.

title: Flowers and Fruit
description: Roses, peaches and grapes are arrayed on a plain tabletop against a neutral ground. Fantin-Latour's still lifes, prized in England via his dealer Edwin Edwards, distil the Dutch tradition into quiet, almost photographic studies of bloom and bloom-bearing skin.

title: Garden at Sainte-Adresse
description: An ornamental garden at the Norman seaside resort where Monet's aunt and family summered. The bright flower beds, brisk handling and high horizon look forward to the celebrated Terrace at Sainte-Adresse painted the following summer at the same property.

title: Inada Kyuzo Shinsuke
description: A sheet from Yoshitoshi's series Eimei nijūhasshūku (Twenty-eight Famous Murders with Verse), produced with Yoshiiku in 1866–67. The print exemplifies the late ukiyo-e taste for muzan-e — bloody, theatrical scenes drawn from kabuki and historical legend.

title: Jo
description: A portrait of Joanna Hiffernan, model and lover of Whistler, gazing into a hand mirror as she draws her copper-red hair through her fingers. Courbet painted at least four versions, the dense impasto and earth-toned palette characteristic of his Realist studio practice.

title: Odalisque reading
description: A reclining harem figure pauses over a book, her bared shoulders and embroidered cushions rendered with the polished surfaces and erotic restraint Hayez brought to his Orientalist subjects. The smooth modelling and warm half-light reflect his long career as Milan's leading Romantic portraitist.

title: Spring Bouquet
description: An early still life of garden flowers crowded into a white porcelain vase, painted under the influence of Courbet and Monet. The dense, dark ground and weighty paint surface show Renoir before his Impressionist palette had fully lightened.

title: The Collector of Prints
description: A bearded amateur sits in a tightly packed Parisian study, a bundle of unmounted prints on his knees and folios of engravings stacked against the walls. Degas exhibited the canvas at the 1867 Paris Salon; it is now in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, an early example of his interest in the absorbed urban specialist.

title: The Sleepers
description: Two nude women lie entwined in dishevelled bedding, jewellery and a broken pearl strand scattered on the sheet. Commissioned by the Turkish diplomat Khalil-Bey, the canvas treats lesbian love with a frank realism that scandalised the Second Empire.

title: The Vision of The Valley of The Dry Bones
description: An engraving from Dore's illustrated Bible, depicting Ezekiel's vision in which scattered bones reanimate as a vast army. The artist exploits dense crosshatching and dramatic chiaroscuro to give the desolate plain a haunted, otherworldly atmosphere.

title: Valparaiso Harbor
description: Made during Whistler's eight-month visit to Chile, where he had travelled to observe the Spanish bombardment of the port. Warships ride on a flat blue bay beneath a softly graded sky, a dusk study that anticipates his Thames Nocturnes by a decade.

title: Woman with a Parrot
description: A reclining nude exhibited at the Salon of 1866, where Courbet's frank naturalism, tousled hair and unidealised flesh, scandalised critics expecting an academic Venus. The bird perched on her outstretched hand provides the slim mythological pretext. Now in the Metropolitan Museum of Art.
credit: Metropolitan Museum of Art, online collection (accession number 29.100.57)

title: (Venice) La distruzione del tempio di Gerusalemme -Francesco Hayez - gallerie Accademia Venice
englishTitle: The Destruction of the Temple of Jerusalem
description: Hayez stages the Roman sack of Herod's Temple as operatic Romantic history painting: collapsing columns, fleeing priests and a smoke-darkened sky. The vast canvas, now in the Gallerie dell'Accademia, was conceived as a meditation on tyranny that resonated with Italian audiences under Austrian rule.

title: Adolphe Monet in the Garden of Le Coteau at Sainte-Adresse
description: The painter's father sits in a straw hat among flowering plants in the family's seaside garden at Sainte-Adresse. Painted during the same productive Norman summer as the Regatta, the picture combines a tender domestic portrait with Monet's emerging interest in dappled outdoor light.

title: Garden of the Princess
description: From a high window of the Louvre, Monet looked across the Pont des Arts to the dome of the Institut and the formal parterre of the Garden of the Princess. One of three Paris views painted from the same elevated vantage in 1867, it shows top-hatted strollers and carriages reduced to crisp coloured marks.
credit: posted to Flickr as monet_garden_princess_1867 , by Flickr user ErgsArt

title: Glaçons à Bougival
description: A frigid winter scene of the Seine clogged with drift ice near Bougival, where Monet lived in straitened circumstances. Pale lavenders and chalky greys describe the freeze, his brush dragged dryly to suggest the glassy plates of broken ice.

provenance.collection: Department of Paintings of the Louvre

title: Idylls of the King 3
description: A wood-engraved illustration to Tennyson's Arthurian cycle, showing Edyrn travelling to Arthur's court with his lady and dwarf. Doré builds the scene from his characteristic stagecraft of looming forest and theatrical light, the dense black tonalities suited to the poem's medieval atmosphere.
credit: Enid , by Lord Alfred Tennyson . London: Edward Moxon & Co., 1868.

title: Jeanne-Marguerite Lecadre in the Garden Sainte-Adresse
description: Jeanne-Marguerite Lecadre, a relative, stands among flowering beds in the family garden at Sainte-Adresse near Le Havre. The picture's bright local colour and crisp shadows show Monet absorbing the lessons of Manet and Japanese prints.

title: Little Red Riding Hood
description: From Doré's celebrated illustrations to Perrault's Contes, the wood engraving stages the child's fateful meeting with the wolf among forest shadows. Doré pioneered cinematic tonal staging in printed fairy tales, and these designs shaped the visual imagination of the genre across Europe.

title: Monet w81
description: An early canvas predating Impressionism's public arrival, in which Monet is still negotiating his debt to Boudin and Jongkind. Already evident is his appetite for outdoor light and a loosened, atmospheric handling of sky and water.

title: Pierre-Auguste Renoir - Frédéric Bazille
description: Renoir portrays his fellow Impressionist Frédéric Bazille at work before an easel, brush poised over a still life of a heron. The picture is a touching record of the early Batignolles circle, painted shortly before Bazille's death in the Franco-Prussian War.
credit: Renoir, peintre du bonheur : 1841-1919 , de Gilles Néret, Köln, Taschen, 2001, p. 14. ISBN 9783822857410

title: Quai du Louvre
description: An early Parisian cityscape, painted from a balcony of the Louvre overlooking the Seine. Bustling figures, carriages, and the dome of the Pantheon are rendered with the high vantage and bright daylight that anticipate Monet's mature Impressionist manner.

title: Regatta at Sainte-Adresse
description: Sailboats and onlookers crowd the beach at Sainte-Adresse, the Norman resort where Monet spent the summer with relatives. The crisp horizontals and bright local colour are still indebted to Boudin and Jongkind, but already announce the open-air manner that Impressionism would soon codify.

title: Self-portrait
description: The artist meets the viewer's eye in a fur-collared coat, painted with the meticulous, hard-edged detail he championed. Hunt was a founding member of the Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood, and the picture's sober concentration befits his role as its theoretical anchor.

title: Street in Sainte-Adresse
description: An early view of the seaside resort north of Le Havre, where Monet stayed with his aunt during a formative summer. Architecture is still drawn with relatively firm contour, but the bright Norman light and high-keyed palette already point toward Impressionist practice.

title: The Horse Market
description: A bustling North African market scene rendered with Gérôme's characteristic ethnographic precision: tethered Arabian horses, robed traders, and sun-bleached architecture under a hot, even light. The picture belongs to the Haggin Museum's deep Gérôme holding, assembled by California financier James Ben Ali Haggin.

title: The kill of deer
description: A vast hunting picture, over five metres wide, in which hounds bring down a stag in deep snow under the eye of a mounted huntsman. Courbet draws on his Franche-Comté upbringing and the Flemish hunt tradition, scaling a popular subject up to the format of history painting in keeping with his Realist programme.

provenance.collection: Musée des Beaux-Arts et d'Archéologie de Besançon
provenance.location: Musée des Beaux-Arts et d'Archéologie de Besançon

title: Artists Sketching in the White Mountains
description: Three painters perch on a New Hampshire ridge, easels braced against the wind as they survey the valley below. The wry small canvas comments on the Hudson River School fashion for plein-air landscape, with Homer himself among the figures.

title: In the Summer
description: A dark-eyed young woman sits outdoors in a loose white blouse, her hair undone — the painter's model and lover Lise Tréhot cast as a summer bohémienne. The picture predates Renoir's full Impressionist break and still owes a debt to Courbet's full-bodied realism.

title: Interior
description: A lamp-lit domestic interior from Monet's youth, with figures gathered after a meal. Indoor subjects are unusual in his work; here the warm artificial light and dark-keyed palette betray a debt to the realism of Manet and Bazille more than to his later high-colour outdoor practice.

title: La Pie
description: A single black bird perches on a wattle gate in a snowbound Norman garden, casting a faint blue shadow on the drift. One of Monet's earliest essays in coloured shadow, the picture was rejected by the 1869 Salon and now hangs in the Musée d'Orsay.

title: La Porte d'Amont
description: The Upstream Gate, Etretat

title: La Siesta, Memory of Spain
description: A recollection of Doré's Spanish travels, figures resting under midday heat in a sun-bleached landscape. Better known as a wood-engraver, Doré painted ambitious oils late in his career, here applying the dramatic chiaroscuro of his book illustrations to a Romantic genre subject.

title: Monet w 106
description: A coastal scene from Monet's formative years on the Channel, when he was working alongside Boudin and Jongkind. The handling is broader than academic landscape of the period and already shows his interest in transient light over fixed topography.

title: Monet W108
description: A tender domestic study of the artist's infant son Jean asleep in his cradle, dating from the precarious early years of Monet's family life. The handling is broad and affectionate, sheets and shadow simplified into planes of cool grey.

title: Monet w109
description: An early work from the period before Monet settled into the Impressionist idiom, when he was still absorbing lessons from Boudin and the Barbizon school. The handling is firmer and the tonal range narrower than in his mature plein-air practice.

title: The Academy of Architecture
description: The brick cube of Schinkel's Bauakademie rises on the Spreeinsel, its rhythmic terracotta façade and the figures crossing the Schleusenbrücke caught in clear afternoon light. Gaertner painted Schinkel's school of architecture in 1868, four decades after its completion; the building was destroyed in 1945 and demolished in 1962.

title: The Birthday
description: Hunt's young wife Edith is portrayed in profile against a deep ground, adorned with elaborate jewellery and patterned fabrics gathered during the painter's eastern travels. The exacting detail of ornament shows his characteristic Pre-Raphaelite finish in an intimate domestic register.

title: The Luncheon
description: An ambitious early figure piece showing Monet's companion Camille and their son Jean at a sunlit table, with a visitor lingering at the garden's edge. Submitted to and rejected by the 1870 Salon, it announces the everyday subjects that would define Impressionism.

title: The Sea at Le Havre
description: A grey Channel seascape painted from the harbour Monet had known since childhood, with sailing vessels riding a low swell beneath broken cloud. The high horizon and economical palette anticipate the marines of the following decade.
credit: Wikipedia Loves Art at the Carnegie Museum of Art This photo of item # 53.22 at the Carnegie Museum of Art was contributed under the team name " dewey_decimals " as part of the Wikipedia Loves Art project in February 2009. Carnegie Museum of Art The original photograph on Flickr was taken by Moira Burke — please add a comment to the original Flickr page whenever a use has been made on Wikipedia or another project. Project galleries on Flickr: this institution , this team

title: View of Tiflis from Seid-Abaz
description: Tiflis, modern Tbilisi, spreads along the Kura river below the bluff of Seid-Abaz, its houses stepping up the slopes toward the surrounding Caucasian ridges. Aivazovsky toured the Caucasus in 1868 and produced a series of Georgian and Armenian townscapes, of which this is one.

title: At the Races in the Countryside
description: A landau parked at a country racecourse, the Valpinçon family attending to their newborn son under the shade of a parasol. Degas crops the carriage and horses with photographic abruptness, turning a polite outing into a study of asymmetric modern composition.

title: Boote
description: A study of moored rowing boats, the kind of riverside motif Monet repeatedly mined along the Seine. Water is rendered in horizontal slabs of broken colour, the hulls anchoring an otherwise nearly abstract surface.

title: Dervishes in Festive Attire
description: Two dervishes pose in vivid ceremonial garments studded with shells, beads, and embroidery. The careful ethnographic detail reflects Vereshchagin's Central Asian travels and his reportorial approach to Russian Orientalist subjects.

title: La Grenouillère
description: Bathers and rowboats cluster around the floating café on the Seine at Bougival, the spot where Renoir and Monet spent the summer of 1869 painting side by side. Broken touches of opaque colour on the water mark one of the foundational moments of Impressionism.

title: Long Branch
description: Two fashionable women in bustled dresses pause on a cliff at the Jersey Shore resort, parasols snapping in the Atlantic wind. Homer's bright, almost Impressionist palette captures the new postwar leisure culture with magazine-illustrator clarity.
credit: The AMICA Library; Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, online database

title: Monet w0145
description: A snow-bound landscape at sunset, a subject Monet returned to repeatedly through his career to test the chromatic limits of white. Pale pinks and lilacs warm the drifts as the low sun stains the horizon.

title: Monet w148
description: An early work from Monet's apprentice years, when his practice was still indebted to plein-air predecessors like Eugène Boudin. The brushwork is tighter and the subject more conventionally framed than in the mature Impressionist canvases.

title: On the Beach
description: Children and bathers cluster on a sunlit Atlantic strand, the composition organized in horizontal bands of sand, surf and sky. Homer's interest in the new American leisure shore renders the figures with quick, illustrational economy.

title: Selbstporträt im Alter von 78 Jahren
description: A late self-portrait at age seventy-eight, the Milanese master appraising himself with calm, unflattering directness. The restrained palette and tightly painted head reflect the academic rigour Hayez upheld at the Brera even as Romanticism gave way to verismo.

title: Still Life with Flowers and Fruit
description: An early still life arranging garden blooms alongside ripe pears and grapes on a draped surface. Painted before Monet committed fully to plein-air landscape, the canvas shows him testing dense impasto and saturated colour against the conventions of Salon still-life painting.

title: Still Life With Watermelon
description: An early student work made during Chase's Indianapolis years, the cut watermelon is laid out with the dark ground and dramatic highlights of the Munich-school tradition he would soon study at first hand. The picture predates his shift toward looser, brighter American Impressionism.

title: The Bridge at Bougival
description: Painted during Monet's lean Bougival period alongside Renoir, the composition hinges on the wooden river bridge cutting across the Seine. The handling is still relatively tight, but already shows the rapid notation of reflections that would soon define Impressionism.

title: The Sailboat
description: The Sailboat (Seascape)

title: The Seine at Bougival
description: Painted from the riverbank at the village that drew Monet, Renoir and Pissarro alike, the scene catches a row of moored boats and the mirror of the Seine. Quick, comma-shaped strokes record passing reflections rather than fixed contours.

title: The Wave
description: One of a series of stormy seascapes Courbet painted at Étretat in 1869, the breaking wave thickly built up with the palette knife. He treated water as solid matter, layering grey-green pigment against a leaden sky to register the weight rather than the glitter of the Channel.

title: The Wave
description: A breaking wave rears in heavy impasto under a brooding Channel sky, the horizon pushed high and the surf laid on with palette knife. Courbet painted dozens of these studies on the Normandy coast at Étretat in 1869, treating seascape as a study of matter rather than picturesque incident.

title: Barge Haulers on the Volga
description: Eleven harnessed labourers heave a barge upstream across a vast, sun-bleached Volga sandbar, their faces individuated portraits of exhaustion and stoicism. Repin's early masterpiece announced the social conscience of the Peredvizhniki, marrying academic figure construction to a panoramic Russian landscape.

title: Camille sitting on the beach at Trouville
description: Camille Doncieux on the beach at Trouville during the family's stay in the summer of 1870, painted in the open air with sand reportedly still embedded in the paint. The handling is rapid and sketch-like, capturing wind, light and the moment of leisure.

title: Eagle Head
description: Three young women emerge from the surf onto the Cape Ann shore, their wet bathing dresses clinging in a way that scandalized contemporary critics. Homer treats the scene as a study of weight, wind and waterlogged fabric rather than narrative incident.
credit: Metropolitan Museum of Art, online collection (The Met object ID 20011474)

title: en
description: Boats crowd the harbour mouth of the Norman resort of Trouville, where Monet honeymooned with Camille in the summer of 1870. The pictures from that holiday — sand still embedded in some of the canvases — were the last he made before fleeing the war to London.

title: Hôtel des roches noires. Trouville
description: Holiday-makers parade beneath a row of fluttering tricolours along the boardwalk of Trouville's grandest hotel. Painted on the eve of the Franco-Prussian War, the picture is a brisk exercise in plein-air reportage, with sand still trapped in the paint surface.

title: Monomakh's hunting
description: Grand Prince Vladimir Monomakh of Kievan Rus rests on the grass after a boar hunt, his retinue and dogs gathered around the kill. Painted in 1870 while Vasnetsov was still a student at the Imperial Academy, the picture anticipates his later turn toward medieval Russian history and bylina subjects.

title: Still Life with Hummingbird
description: A hummingbird hovers above a cluster of cut flowers and fruit on a dark ground. The dense Munich-trained shadows and tightly observed wings reflect Chase's early academic still-life manner before his later turn to airy Impressionist plein-airs.

title: Surikov-Horseman2
description: An alternate version of the Bronze Horseman composition, with Falconet's equestrian Peter the Great rearing on the Senate Square pedestal beside the Neva. Surikov produced the study in 1870 during his Academy years in St Petersburg, before the Moscow history paintings that would make his reputation.

title: The Beach at Trouville
description: Painted on the Normandy coast during Monet's honeymoon summer, the canvas shows two seated women — likely Camille Monet and a companion — under parasols on the windswept sand. Grains of beach are embedded in the paint, a documentary trace of the open-air method.

title: The boardwalk on the beach at Trouville
description: A breezy Norman seaside view from Monet's 1870 Trouville stay with Camille, days before the Franco-Prussian War sent him into London exile. Sand grains are reportedly embedded in the paint, evidence of true plein-air execution.

title: The Orchestra at the Opera
description: A view of the Paris Opera pit dominated by the bassoonist Désiré Dihau, with the legs and tutus of dancers cropped above the proscenium. Degas pioneers the abrupt foreground/background split and the off-axis viewpoint that would shape his ballet pictures for the next two decades.

title: The Shadow of Death
description: A Pre-Raphaelite vision of Christ as a young carpenter stretching after labor, his outflung arms casting a cruciform shadow across the workshop wall. Hunt painted the scene in Jerusalem to ground every tool, shaving and textile in archaeological accuracy.
credit: Originally from en.wikipedia ; description page is/was here . 2007-01-04 (original upload date). Original uploader was Paul Barlow at en.wikipedia

title: Houses by the Bank of the River
description: Painted during Monet's Dutch sojourn after the Franco-Prussian War, the canvas shows a row of green-shuttered houses reflected in the Zaan. Long horizontal brushstrokes mirror the calm of the Holland waterways that fascinated him.

title: In the Alpine High Valley
description: A small group winds along a high alpine track with the Wendelstein massif rising behind them. Late in his career Spitzweg loosened his touch under Barbizon influence, and the airy mountain palette here is closer to plein-air observation than to his earlier studio finish.

title: La Classe de danse
description: Dancers in white tutus practise at the barre and rest along the back wall of a rehearsal room at the rue Le Peletier opera house, ballet master Jules Perrot leaning on his cane in the centre. Degas worked the canvas between 1871 and 1874; it now hangs at the Musée d'Orsay and was a foundational picture of his ballet series.

title: La Zaan à Zaandam
description: Refugee from the Franco-Prussian war, Monet found in the Dutch waterways at Zaandam a flat horizon punctuated by sails and clapboard houses. Cool blues and ochre dominate the four-month Holland sojourn, in which he painted some two dozen views along the Zaan.

title: Méditation
description: Camille Doncieux, the painter's first wife, reclining on a sofa in quiet thought. The intimate domestic subject and muted tonal range belong to Monet's early-1870s figure painting, before his work shifted decisively outdoors toward pure landscape and atmospheric study.

title: Monet w182
description: An early-1870s landscape from Monet's Argenteuil period, when he settled on the Seine and refined the broken-stroke technique that would define Impressionism. Light is registered in short touches of unmixed colour laid wet-in-wet.

title: Nocturne: Grey and Gold
description: Westminster Bridge and the Thames vanish into a haze of grey-blue twilight, pierced by scattered gold lamplight. The painting belongs to Whistler's Nocturne series, in which musical titles signalled the priority of tonal harmony over narrative.

title: Portrait of Mlle. Hortense Valpinçon
description: Hortense, the young daughter of Degas's childhood friend Paul Valpinçon, leans against a table and steadies a half-eaten apple in her hand. Painted in 1871 at the family's Normandy estate of Ménil-Hubert on a remnant of striped mattress ticking when no proper canvas was at hand, the portrait is now at the Minneapolis Institute of Art.

title: Portrait of the Artist's Mother
description: Anna McNeill Whistler sits in profile in a London interior, bonneted and dressed in black against a pale grey wall hung with one of her son's etchings. The strict horizontal-vertical geometry and muted palette underscore Whistler's framing of a familial portrait as a tonal arrangement.

title: Prayer in the Mosque Alternative title
description: Worshippers prostrate themselves in long rows beneath the soaring arches of Cairo's Mosque of Amr, sunlight slanting across the columns and prayer mats. Gérôme's enamel-smooth Orientalism rests on direct study of Egyptian architecture from his repeated travels in the country.

title: Still life with fruit
description: Grapes, peaches and other fruit are heaped on a draped tabletop in a darkened interior. The Munich-school chiaroscuro and confident, loaded brushwork mark the young Chase's training in 1870s Bavaria.

title: The Champion Single Sculls
description: Eakins's friend Max Schmitt rests on his oars on the Schuylkill River at twilight, with the painter himself rowing in the middle distance. The composition is built from rigorous perspective studies of bridges and ripples, reflecting Eakins's Philadelphia commitment to anatomical and optical truth.

title: The Thames below Westminster
description: A view across the Thames toward the Houses of Parliament and Westminster Bridge, dissolved in river mist. Painted during Monet's wartime exile in London, the canvas anticipates by three decades his later Thames series, already setting silhouetted architecture against a pearly, fog-bound sky.

title: Variations in Pink and Grey: Chelsea
description: A Thames-side view from the years when Whistler lived on Lindsey Row and was reformulating landscape as colour harmony. Fishermen and barge-poles are reduced to slim vertical accents on a horizontal field of pearly grey water and dusty pink shore.

title: Windmills Near Zaandam
description: A girl walks the dyke path between Oostzaan and Zaandam, windmill sails turning over flat polder land. Painted during Monet's 1871 Dutch sojourn after his English exile, the picture's narrow tonal range catches a typical overcast Holland sky.
credit: Walters Art Museum : Home page Info about artwork

title: “And the Prayer of Faith Shall Save the Sick”
description: A late biblical genre piece taking its title from the Epistle of James, set within a sunlit Eastern interior. Lewis casts the scriptural episode in the Cairene domestic vocabulary he had perfected over decades. Mashrabiya light falls across patterned cushions and the bedside attendants in saturated colour.

title: Argenteuil
description: Sailboats lie along the bank of the Seine at Argenteuil, the suburban boating town where Monet settled after the Franco-Prussian War. Quick comma-strokes break the water and sky into the broken, prismatic colour that became the signature of early Impressionism.

title: Arrangement in Gray: Portrait of the Painter
description: A self-portrait built from narrow tonal intervals of grey, the painter emerging only as a darkened silhouette and pale face from a near-uniform field. The careful tuning of values exemplifies Whistler's musical analogies for picture-making.

title: Claude Monet - Argenteuil - 1872 - Musée d'Orsay
description: A view of the Seine at Argenteuil, the suburban boating town where Monet settled after the Franco-Prussian War. Sailboats and reflections on calm water became his central subject here, painted from a floating studio he converted from a small skiff.

title: Der Tanzsaal
description: Young ballerinas gather in a high-windowed Paris Opera rehearsal hall, one stretching at the barre while others wait their turn. Painted in 1872, the scene belongs to Degas's earliest series on the ballet, in which he treated the company's working spaces as a laboratory for studies of artificial light, mirrored geometry, and arrested movement.

title: Impression
description: The harbour of Le Havre at dawn dissolves into vapour, masts and cranes ghosted behind an orange sun whose reflections crackle across the water. Exhibited at the first independent show of 1874, its title supplied a hostile critic with the term 'Impressionism' that would name the movement.

title: Ivan Constantinovich Aivazovsky - Moscow in Winter from the Sparrow Hills
description: A snowbound panorama of Moscow viewed from the Sparrow Hills, the city spreading toward the horizon beneath low winter cloud. Painted in 1872 on a 46 by 72 cm canvas, the picture is a rare urban subject from Aivazovsky, whose practice was overwhelmingly marine.

title: Monet w 208
description: Painted in the early 1870s as Monet established the visual language of Impressionism, the picture trades finish for immediacy, applying paint in mosaic-like touches. Works of these years preceded and prepared the 1874 group exhibition that gave the movement its name.

title: Monet w 235
description: A river or harbour subject from 1872, the year of the famous Impression, Sunrise, sharing its concern with reflections, vapour, and the dissolution of form on water. The vibrating shorthand of small coloured strokes marks Monet's break with conventional finish.

title: Monet w197
description: An Argenteuil-era landscape from the years Monet shared the riverbank with Manet and Renoir. The brushwork is quick and divisible, the palette tuned to outdoor daylight rather than studio convention.

title: Monet w199
description: Springtime at Argenteuil, painted soon after Monet moved downriver from Paris in 1871. Blossoming trees and sunlit grass are caught in flickering strokes, the figures held lightly within an atmosphere of dappled spring light.

title: Monet w222
description: An Argenteuil scene from the year of the first Impressionist exhibition's gestation. Monet works en plein air, registering reflections on water and the play of leaves with rapid, divided touches.

title: Monet w224
description: A riverbank composition from Monet's Argenteuil years, where the Seine and its boats supplied an inexhaustible motif. The horizon sits low, leaving most of the canvas to sky and shimmering water.

title: Nocturne in Blue and Gold: Old Battersea Bridge
description: Old Battersea Bridge looms in silhouette over the Thames at dusk, its piers stretched into a near-Japanese vertical. Whistler reduced river, sky, and timber to a few veils of blue and gold, treating the cityscape as an arrangement of tones in line with his Aesthetic credo.

title: On the Beach -- Two Are Company
description: A wood engraving after Winslow Homer published in Harper's Weekly, depicting a flirtation interrupted on a New England beach. Homer's Reconstruction-era illustrations chronicled American leisure with a wry observational eye.

title: Pollice Verso
description: A staged Roman amphitheatre scene in which a victorious mirmillo stands over his fallen opponent and looks up at the Vestals' thumbs-down verdict. Gérôme drew on his own collection of antique armour for the gladiators' helmets and helped fix Hollywood's mental image of the arena.

title: Pont-Neuf
description: Pedestrians and carriages cross Paris's oldest bridge under a clear summer sky, the Seine glittering between embankments. Renoir's brother Edmond reportedly delayed passersby in conversation so the painter could capture them in rapid, sun-drenched touches.

title: Regattas at Argenteuil
description: Sails crowd the Seine basin at Argenteuil, doubled in vivid downward strokes that read almost as flames on the water. The painting's loose vertical reflections were among the works that helped define the Impressionist handling of moving light on water.

title: Springtime
description: A young woman, almost certainly Camille, sits reading in dappled shade beneath flowering trees. Pink-white blossoms and green foliage are dissolved into a single shimmering screen of broken touch, an early statement of Monet's plein-air figure painting.

title: Still Life
description: An early domestic still life from Monet's Argenteuil years, when he briefly turned from landscape to tabletop subjects. A lacquered tray, porcelain cups and a polished kettle are arranged with Japoniste restraint, the gleaming surfaces reflecting his admiration for Manet and for Edo lacquerware.

title: The Biglin Brothers Racing
description: Professional oarsmen John and Bernard Biglin pull in unison in their pair-oared shell during a five-mile race on the Schuylkill River, watched by crowds along the Philadelphia shore. Eakins, an avid rower himself, worked the picture up from drawings and precise perspective studies after attending the contest on 20 May 1872. Now at the National Gallery of Art.

title: The Highway Bridge under repair
description: The road bridge at Argenteuil propped on temporary timber scaffolding after wartime damage. Monet treats the construction site as a fully serious motif, the geometry of beams and trestles balanced against the soft Seine below.

title: The Petit Bras of the Seine at Argenteuil
description: A quiet backwater of the Seine fringed by bare poplars and reflected on a glassy surface. Painted in the first weeks of Monet's settlement at Argenteuil, the canvas balances delicate atmospheric grey-blues against incipient Impressionist touch.

title: A Lady Receiving Visitors
description: A harem interior in Cairo, where a seated lady greets her guests amid mashrabiya screens and a sun-dappled mosaic floor. Lewis lived a decade in an Ottoman house in the city and made the filtered light through latticed windows his signature subject. Every textile, slipper and tile is rendered in jewel-bright watercolour clarity.

title: A Walk in the Meadows at Argenteuil
description: Figures stroll through tall summer grass beside the Seine at Argenteuil, the village where Monet lived from 1871 to 1878. The high horizon and broken touch dissolve foreground wildflowers into a tapestry of pure colour, a defining experiment of his Argenteuil years.

title: American Shipping off the Rock of Gibraltar
description: An American three-master rides at anchor in the calm waters off the Rock of Gibraltar, the limestone bulk rising behind it under a clear southern sky. Painted in 1873 by Aivazovsky, principal painter of the Russian Navy, the canvas belongs to his long series of marine views worked entirely from memory in the Feodosia studio.

title: Autumn on the Seine
description: Riverside trees in russet and gold are doubled in the still surface of the Seine. Painted from the bank at Argenteuil, the picture exploits Monet's preferred device of mirrored reflection, the upper and lower halves of the canvas answering one another in horizontal bands.

title: Ballettprobe
description: Dancers warming up in the rehearsal room, observed from a raked corner viewpoint that pushes the orchestra rail into the foreground. Degas favoured these unguarded moments of preparation over performance, where artificial light, pastel-keyed tones and oblique geometry could be studied at leisure.

title: Boys in a Dory
description: Watercolor; Drawings

title: Breezing Up
description: A catboat heels in stiff wind off the Massachusetts coast, three boys and a fisherman crowded along the windward rail. Homer reworked the composition over two years, settling on the diagonal mast that turns a leisure scene into an emblem of post-Civil-War optimism.

title: Confusion of Tongues
description: An illustration to Genesis 11 from Doré's English Bible, depicting the workers scattering as the Tower of Babel founders mid-construction. Doré stages the scene with vertiginous architecture and a gulf of stormy sky, exploiting the dense black hatching of wood-engraving to dramatise divine judgement.

title: Cow Boys
description: Two young cattle drovers in straw hats lean on a rail fence, watching their herd from a sun-soaked pasture. Often catalogued as Cow Boys, the canvas typifies Homer's Gloucester-era interest in agrarian boyhood as an emblem of postwar American innocence.
credit: Ball State University Libraries: Digital Media Repository

provenance.collection: David Owsley Museum of Art Ball State University

title: Dad's Coming!
description: A boy perched on an overturned dory watches the horizon while his mother and infant sister wait beside him on the beach. The hopeful title masks Homer's familiar coastal anxiety, as the absent father's sail is nowhere yet visible.
credit: National Gallery of Art, Washington, D. C., online collection

title: Girl in the Hammock
description: A woman reclines in a slung hammock with a book, her white dress catching dappled light through the canopy. Homer's flattened design and decorative pattern of leaves reflect his exposure to contemporary Japanese prints.

title: Jacob Wrestles with the Angel
description: A wood-engraved illustration from Doré's English Bible (1866), depicting Genesis 32 — Jacob struggling through the night with a divine adversary at the ford of the Jabbok. The dense black hatching and theatrical lighting are hallmarks of Doré's Romantic graphic style.

title: Masked Ball at the Opera
description: Top-hatted men press around costumed women in dominoes beneath the colonnaded foyer of the old Paris Opéra on rue Le Peletier, painted only months before the building burnt down. Manet compresses the crowd into a frieze of black coats, reading the bourgeois carnival as a study in modern social ritual.

title: Monet w 272 Apple Trees in Bloom
description: Apple trees in full blossom, their pinkish-white canopies set against fresh spring green and dabbed in short broken strokes. The subject was a favourite of the early Impressionists, who valued orchards as outdoor studios where colour and light could be studied together.

title: Monet w 290 autumn effect in argenteuil
description: A view along the Seine at Argenteuil, where Monet was based through much of the 1870s, painted at the moment when foliage flares into copper and gold. The water carries the autumn colour back as a lattice of broken reflections, a hallmark of his river pictures from these years.

title: Monet w265
description: A landscape from the years Monet rented the house at Argenteuil that became a hub for his circle. Light is treated as the true subject, with grass, water and sky fused by a single weather and hour.

title: Naked Woman Lying on a Couch
description: An unidealised nude sprawls across a rumpled divan, her clothing tossed over the chair beside her. Painted early in Caillebotte's career, the canvas treats the female body with a candid, almost photographic objectivity that was startling to Salon-trained eyes.

title: Railroad Bridge
description: A modern iron rail bridge strides across the Seine on concrete piers, a small steam train trailing white smoke above sailing boats. Monet repeatedly painted this junction of leisure and industry during his Argenteuil years.

title: Rainbow
description: A rainbow arches above a shipwreck and lifeboat tossed in heavy seas, survivors pulling at the oars while the sky breaks open behind them. Painted in 1873 and now in the State Tretyakov Gallery, the canvas is one of Aivazovsky's signature meditations on rescue at sea, salvation hinging on a sliver of coloured light.

title: Selbstporträt
description: A young Vasnetsov, twenty-five and recently arrived in Saint Petersburg from the Academy, looks out with a thin moustache and dark coat against a neutral ground. The 1873 self-portrait is in the Tretyakov Gallery, the same Moscow institution whose façade Vasnetsov would design three decades later in his Russian Revivalist mode.

title: Ships in a Harbor
description: Ships in a Harbor

title: The Artist's Garden in Argenteuil
description: A corner of Monet's Argenteuil garden ablaze with dahlias, with the painter's house glimpsed beyond a wooden fence. The canvas — long associated with a similar work by Renoir painted alongside Monet — applies broken Impressionist touches to translate the heat of late summer.

title: The Four Leaf Clover
description: A young woman in a wide-brimmed hat searches a meadow for the proverbial lucky clover, her downturned head shaded by the brim. Homer turns a slight pastoral conceit into a study of summer light filtered through straw.
credit: Bridgeman Art Library : Object 241624; Detroit Institute of Arts

title: The Luncheon
description: An intimate domestic interior showing the remains of a meal at the Monets' Argenteuil house, with the artist's first wife Camille and son Jean implied in the staging. Light pours across linen, glassware, and fruit in a quietly Manet-inflected still life.

title: The Railway
description: Victorine Meurent, in dark blue with a sleeping puppy in her lap and an open book, sits before the iron railings above the cutting of the Gare Saint-Lazare; beside her, a child in white watches a passing train betrayed only by its cloud of steam. Exhibited at the Salon of 1874 and now at the National Gallery of Art in Washington, the picture was Manet's last of his favourite model.

title: The Railway Bridge in Argenteuil
description: The iron railway bridge at Argenteuil cuts across the Seine in flat planes of pale stone, a steam train trailing white smoke above. Monet treats modern infrastructure as a legitimate motif of plein-air painting, balancing its industrial geometry against the soft river bank.

title: Wild Poppies Near Argenteuil
description: Camille and the young Jean Monet wade through high summer grass at Argenteuil, scarlet poppies dotted across the field in dabs of vermilion. A second figure-pair higher on the slope mirrors the first, knitting two moments into one composition.

title: Boating
description: A boater in straw hat and crisp whites holds the tiller while his companion lounges in the prow against a wall of saturated blue water. The radically cropped composition and high horizon reveal Manet's debt to Japanese prints and his summer at Argenteuil with Monet.

title: Canoeists near Argenteuil
description: Sailboats and rowers drift on the Seine at Argenteuil, the Parisian suburb where Monet lived through the early 1870s and turned regatta-day leisure into a recurring subject. Quick comma-strokes describe water and rigging with equal economy.
credit: L'Évasion des Sens : MONET_Canotiers à Argenteuil

title: Fishing boats leaving the harbor
description: Sail-rigged fishing boats slip out of Le Havre on a misty morning, the harbour walls and shipping reduced to muted silhouettes. Monet painted the port of his boyhood repeatedly in the early 1870s, and works of this kind directly preceded Impression, Sunrise of 1872.

title: Le Bassin du Commerce
description: A canvas of Le Havre's commercial basin, the harbour from which Monet had launched Impression, Sunrise two years earlier. Painted with rapid broken touches, the work continues his investigation of Channel-port atmospheres, where masts, smoke and reflected light become almost interchangeable.

title: Le Pont d'Argenteuil
description: The road bridge at Argenteuil, rebuilt after the Franco-Prussian War, frames moored sailboats on the Seine. Monet used the same bridge in several canvases of 1874, varying the viewpoint and weather to test how a single motif behaves under changing light.

title: Monet w 338
description: Painted during the year of the first Impressionist exhibition, this work shows Monet's mature open-air method fully formed. Pigment is laid down in distinct touches that resolve into atmosphere only at viewing distance, refusing the smooth surface prized by the Salon.

title: Monet w327
description: A mid-1870s landscape from the Argenteuil years, painted as Monet pushed his palette toward purer, lighter chromatic notes. The brushwork is short and patchy, more interested in vibration than in contour.

title: Moonlight
description: A study of figures on a darkened shore under a low moon, painted in oil with the heavy tonal contrasts Homer favored after the Civil War. Silvered light on water dominates the otherwise nearly silhouetted forms.
credit: The Athenaeum: Home - info - pic; Fenimore Art Museum

title: Pont Argenteuil Monet 1
description: Sailing boats line the basin at Argenteuil beneath the highway bridge, their masts reflected in the broken blue water of the Seine. The picture belongs to the suburban riverscapes that defined the early Impressionist summers of 1872 to 1874.

title: Répétition d'un ballet sur la scène
description: Dancers in tutus drift through a stage rehearsal, one yawning behind a flat, the ballet master and observers grouped in shadow at the wings. The Metropolitan's version, in oil thinned to a near grisaille, is one of three closely related compositions Degas worked on around 1874, the largest of which appeared in the first Impressionist exhibition that April.

title: Self-portrait
description: Aivazovsky, in his late fifties and at the height of his European reputation, faces the viewer in dark formal dress with a sober, level gaze. Painted in 1874 at the request of the Accademia di Belle Arti in Florence, the canvas entered the Uffizi self-portrait collection alongside Orest Kiprensky as only the second Russian artist so honoured.

title: Snow at Argenteuil
description: A muffled village street under fresh snow, part of Monet's sustained study of Argenteuil winters. The white ground is laid in with cool blues and lilacs rather than pure white, a decisive Impressionist break from academic monochrome.
credit: Google Art Project works from the Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art

title: Summer
description: Camille and Jean lie among long grass and poppies under a high summer sky. The picture belongs to a small group of figure-in-meadow compositions Monet made at Argenteuil, treating the family as colour incidents within a continuous field of warm growth.

title: The Geese
description: Geese gather at a farmyard pond in this rural scene from Monet's Argenteuil years, painted at the moment Impressionism crystallised around the first group exhibition. The whitewashed wall and reflecting water carry the picture's main optical work, dappled with quick, flickering touches.

title: The North-West Passage / Die Überfahrt nach Nord-West / Le Passage du Nord-Ouest
description: An old sea captain sits stiffly by a window while his daughter reads aloud from a logbook, a Union Jack draped across his knees. Millais distilled Britain's Arctic ambitions into domestic drama; the canvas became one of the most reproduced images of Victorian patriotic sentiment.

title: The Rehearsal Onstage
description: Dancers in white tutus rehearse on a near-empty stage while a ballet master gestures and a knot of men in dark coats watches from the wings. The Metropolitan's pastel and gouache version, painted around 1874, exploits the high vantage of an opera box to push the floor up against the picture plane in a way Degas had absorbed from Japanese prints.
credit: Metropolitan Museum of Art, online collection (The Met object ID 110000595)

title: The Windmill on the Onbekende Gracht
description: A brick polder mill stands across one of Amsterdam's quieter canals, its sails set against a wind-swept Dutch sky. Monet painted it during his autumn 1874 Dutch trip, a return to the country he had first sketched while waiting out the Franco-Prussian War.
credit: Bridgeman Art Library : Object 129973; Museum of Fine Arts, Houston, online collection

title: The Zuiderkerk
description: A view up the Groenburgwal canal toward the spire of the Zuiderkerk, painted during Monet's brief Dutch sojourn. The canvas already carries the rapid, broken brushwork of nascent Impressionism, dissolving brick facades and water into vibrating coloured strokes.

title: A Corner of the Apartment
description: An interior view of the Monet family's Argenteuil home, with young Jean standing at the end of a darkened hallway between hanging plants and curtained light. The painting marks one of Monet's rare domestic interiors, balancing silhouetted shadow against a glowing window.

title: Au Café-concert : La Chanson du chien
description: A café-concert singer leans forward at the footlights, her gloved hands shaped like a dog's paws as she performs the popular novelty song known as the Chanson du chien. Worked up between 1875 and 1877 in gouache and pastel over a monotype base, the sheet belongs to a group of small night-life scenes Degas made of the open-air café-concerts along the Champs-Élysées.

title: Bartolomeo Magagnosco by John Singer Sargent 1875
description: A pencil head-and-shoulders study of Bartolomeo Magagnosco, inscribed Nice, January 1875, when Sargent was nineteen and travelling on the Riviera with his family. Now in the Philadelphia Museum of Art, the sheet shows the assured contour drawing that underpinned the oil portraits with which Sargent would debut at the Paris Salon two years later.

title: Camille au métier
description: An intimate domestic scene of Monet's first wife, Camille Doncieux, seated at an embroidery frame in their Argenteuil home. The painter treats the patterned tapestry, dress, and wall hangings as a single woven field of colour, dissolving figure and interior into a continuous surface of touches.
