title: Camille Monet and a Child in the Artist's Garden in Argenteuil
description: Camille Monet and a Child in the Artist's Garden in Argenteuil

title: Étretat
description: The Normandy cliffs and one of the three great natural arches at Étretat rise above a tidal beach where small fires of burning kelp send up white plumes of smoke. Painted by Inness during his European travels of the early 1870s, the canvas is in the Wadsworth Atheneum in Hartford and belongs to his panoramic, atmospheric phase before the late Swedenborgian landscapes.
credit: The Athenaeum: Home - info - pic; Wadsworth Atheneum

title: In a café or L’Absinthe
description: The actress Ellen Andrée and the engraver Marcellin Desboutin sit side by side at a marble café table, the woman staring blankly past a tall glass of cloudy absinthe. Originally exhibited under the title Dans un café and reset as L'Absinthe at its London showing of 1893, the picture was painted at the Nouvelle-Athènes in Pigalle and is now in the Musée d'Orsay.

title: La Yole - The Skiff - Renoir
description: Two young women row a vivid orange skiff on the Seine at Chatou, the river populated by sailboats and a distant railway bridge. Renoir's complementary contrast of cobalt water and chrome-orange hull, applied in feathered touches, captures the leisurely Impressionist suburb of the 1870s.

title: Le Pont d` Argenteuil - Claude Monet
description: A view of the road bridge at Argenteuil, the Seine town that became the Impressionist headquarters in the early 1870s. Monet records the pleasure boats and tree-lined bank with quick comma-strokes, the rebuilt iron-and-stone span symbolising the post-war modernity of suburban leisure.
credit: MNBA logo This file, part of the Collection of the Fine Arts Museum, was provided to Wikimedia Commons thanks to an agreement between the Museo Nacional de Bellas Artes and Wikimedia Argentina .

provenance.collection: National Museum of Fine Arts, Argentina
provenance.location: National Museum of Fine Arts, Argentina

title: Man in a Toque; Self-Portrait
description: Gauguin, in his late twenties and still a Paris stockbroker, looks out from beneath a soft toque in muted browns and greys. Painted around 1875 to 1877, the small canvas is the earliest known self-portrait of an artist whose face would become one of the most painted subjects in his late Polynesian work; it is in the Harvard Art Museums.

title: Meadow with Poplars
description: Poplars near Argenteuil, painted in the suburban Seine landscape that nourished Monet's early Impressionist breakthrough. Vertical trunks divide the field into rhythmic intervals, a compositional device he would push further in the 1891 Poplars series.

title: Monet w357
description: An outdoor canvas from 1875, when Monet was at the technical heart of his Argenteuil period. Forms are dissolved into juxtaposed strokes of warm and cool, with shadow rendered in colour rather than black.

title: Monet w368
description: A landscape made the year Monet's family was forced from their Argenteuil house by mounting debts. The picture nevertheless shows the confident high-key palette he had perfected on the Seine.

title: Monet w386
description: A garden or riverbank motif from 1875, executed in the loose, sun-flecked manner Monet had refined at Argenteuil. Pigment is laid in short directional strokes that read as foliage at viewing distance.

title: Mr and Mrs Edwin Edwards
description: The English etcher and printer Edwin Edwards sits at his desk while his wife Ruth stands behind him, both rendered in Fantin's habitual sober blacks. The Edwardses were the artist's closest patrons, channelling his still lifes into the lucrative London market.

title: Nocturne
description: Part of Whistler's celebrated Nocturne series, in which the painter pared the Thames down to washes of dusky blue and pewter. The work treats landscape as a tonal arrangement, anticipating the abstract sensibilities Whistler championed in his Aesthetic writings.

title: Nocturne in Black and Gold: The Falling Rocket
description: Showers of golden sparks fall through a smoky night sky above the Cremorne Gardens fireworks. The thinly washed, near-monochrome surface so provoked John Ruskin that his attack triggered the famous 1878 libel trial.

title: Place de la Concorde
description: Ludovic-Napoléon Lepic, cigar in hand and umbrella tucked under his arm, strides across the windswept square with his two daughters and a borzoi, a solitary man cropped at the left edge. Painted in 1875 and now at the Hermitage by way of the Gerstenberg collection and Soviet trophy art transfers, the picture places Lepic's silhouette over the statue of Strasbourg, then a recent emblem of loss to Prussia.

title: Portrait of Dr. Samuel D. Gross
description: A monumental scene of surgeon Samuel Gross presiding over an operation before his medical students at Jefferson College. Eakins records the bloodied hand, the chloroformed patient and the rapt amphitheatre with uncompromising realism, anchoring American painting in the lecture-hall light of modern science.

title: Red Boats
description: Sailing skiffs with vermilion hulls cluster against the willow-lined bank of the Seine at Argenteuil, where Monet kept his studio boat. The flickering reflections and high-keyed palette typify the river scenes he painted alongside Renoir and Manet during the suburb's pivotal Impressionist summers.

title: Renoirgarden
description: A woman shaded by a parasol stands amid blossoming flowerbeds, her figure dissolving into the surrounding foliage. Renoir uses fragmented, comma-like brushstrokes and unmodulated touches of pure colour to fuse figure and garden into a single shimmering field of sunlight.

title: The grand canal of Venice
description: Painted on a Venetian visit alongside Monet, the canvas captures the Grand Canal in shimmering broken touches of blue, white and ochre. Striped mooring posts cut vertical accents through the rippling water, marking Manet's most overtly Impressionist experiment.

title: The Iron Rolling Mill
description: A grimy panorama of the Königshütte rolling mill in Upper Silesia, with workers wrestling glowing iron under shafts of furnace light. Menzel spent months on site making hundreds of drawings, producing one of the first ambitious European paintings to take heavy industry as its subject.

title: The Studio Boat
description: Monet's floating studio, a converted boat moored on the Seine that let him paint from the water itself. Manet had recorded him at work in it; here the vessel becomes the subject, half-shaded under a bank of trees.

title: The Yerres
credit: Sidney and Lois Eskenazi Museum of Art Provenance Project

title: Train in the Snow
description: A locomotive idles at the Argenteuil station, its dark bulk and red signal lamps set against snow and bare trees. Monet returned often to the new railway as a subject, treating engine smoke and winter light as kindred atmospheric phenomena; the canvas is now at the Musée Marmottan Monet, Paris.

title: View of Argenteuil - Snow
description: Snow lies along the riverbank at Argenteuil, with the white plain crossed by a lone walker and faint footprints. Monet's winter pictures from this period set warm rooftops and clothed figures against muted blue-grey snow.
credit: The Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art, Kansas City

title: A Parisian Lady
description: A near-life-size portrait of the actress Ellen Andrée in fashionable street dress, her black silhouette set against a flat ground in Manet's signature manner. The picture pursues the figure of the modern Parisienne championed by Baudelaire rather than a sitter's likeness.

title: Acrobats. Festival in a Paris suburb
description: Tightrope walkers and tumblers entertain a working-class crowd at a Sunday fête on the edges of Paris. Painted in 1876 to 1877 during Vasnetsov's Paris stay, the picture was shown at the Salon of 1877 and now hangs in the Tretyakov Gallery, an Impressionist-tinged genre subject from the years just before he turned to Russian folklore.
credit: Scanned from A. K. Lazuko Victor Vasnetsov, Leningrad: Khudozhnik RSFSR, 1990, ISBN 5-7370-0107-5

title: Aivazovsky by Bolotov
description: Ivan Aivazovsky, full-bearded and in dark formal coat, is shown by his fellow academician Dmitry Bolotov in a sober three-quarter view. Painted in 1876, when Aivazovsky had been principal painter of the Russian Navy for thirty years, the portrait belongs to a small group of likenesses Bolotov made of senior figures of the Imperial Academy of Arts.

title: Bal du moulin de la Galette
description: A bustling Sunday afternoon at a Montmartre dance garden, where dappled sunlight filters through the trees onto crowds of working-class Parisians. Renoir's loose, broken brushwork captures shifting light and lively conversation, treating modern leisure as a worthy subject for monumental painting.

title: Carlo Pellegrini
description: Carlo Pellegrini, the Italian-born caricaturist who signed his Vanity Fair plates as Ape, is shown three-quarter length in a soft hat and overcoat. Worked in mixed watercolour, oil and pastel on paper around 1876 to 1877 and inscribed à vous, the sheet was Degas's return present after Pellegrini had painted him in London; it is in the National Gallery, London.
credit: Originally from en.wikipedia ; description page is/was here . Original uploader was Jack1956 at en.wikipedia 2007-10-11 (original upload date); National Gallery, London - online collection

title: Dans la prairie
description: Camille Monet reads in a meadow strewn with poppies and daisies, her parasol propped beside her. Monet's broken brushwork dissolves figure and field into a single screen of high-keyed colour, a Giverny-era exercise in the Impressionist treatment of figures outdoors.

title: Dore-I had done a hellish thing
description: A wood-engraving from Doré's late illustrated edition of Coleridge's Rime of the Ancient Mariner, showing the sailor clinging to the rigging after slaying the albatross. Dense parallel hatching builds the storm-charged sea and the cramped vertigo of the crow's nest.

title: Einzug des Kronprinzen Friedrich Wilhelm von Preußen in Jerusalem 1869
description: Crown Prince Friedrich Wilhelm of Prussia enters Jerusalem in 1869

title: Evening at Argenteuil
description: Evening at Argenteuil, in which the Seine carries the warm pinks and lilacs of a fading sky. Sailboats are noted with a few economical strokes, the picture organised entirely by horizontal bands of reflected light.

title: Fin d'arabesque
description: A solo dancer holds the final pose of an arabesque, her right arm extended with a bouquet, her gaze inclined toward her supporting shoulder while other ballerinas wait behind a stage flat. Identified as the Spanish étoile Rosita Mauri, the 1876 sheet is in pastel, essence and oil on paper and belongs to the Musée d'Orsay.

title: Flowers in a Rococo Vase
description: An exuberant bouquet spills from an ornate Rococo vase, painted with the broken touches and shifting planes that mark Cézanne's early move beyond Impressionism. The composition tilts the vessel forward, pressing pigment-laden blossoms against a darkened ground in dense, sculptural facets.

title: Google Art Project levels adjustment 2
description: Repin's graduation piece for the Imperial Academy of Arts depicts the Novgorod merchant-hero Sadko in the underwater kingdom of the Sea Tsar, choosing a bride from a procession of foreign maidens. Painted in Paris, it earned him a gold medal and signalled an early turn toward Russian folkloric subject matter.

title: Hunting
description: A hunting scene from 1876, an unusual subject for Monet, who almost never painted narrative motifs. It belongs to the decorative panels commissioned by Ernest Hoschede for the chateau de Rottembourg at Montgeron.

title: Le bateau atelier
description: Monet's floating studio, the converted boat he commissioned in Argenteuil so he could paint the Seine from on the water itself. Reflections of hull, mast, and bankside trees fragment across the surface in short broken strokes, the picture as much about looking from the boat as at it.

title: Le bateau-atelier - MAH Neuchâtel
englishTitle: The Studio Boat (Musée d'Art et d'Histoire, Neuchâtel)
description: The floating studio Monet had built at Argenteuil, a small cabined skiff that let him paint directly on the Seine. Reflections double the boat in rippling vertical strokes, an image of the artist's working method as much as a landscape.

title: Monet w397
description: A canvas from the year of the second Impressionist exhibition, where Monet showed eighteen works. The brushwork is confidently shorthand, atmosphere carried by colour temperature rather than line.

title: Monet w419
description: The Pond at Montgeron, painted at the country estate of the collector Ernest Hoschede, who commissioned a group of decorative panels from Monet. Reflections on still water already prefigure the Giverny obsession to come.

title: Moving House
description: An elderly couple shoulder a heavy sack of belongings across a Moscow back street in late winter, a small dog following at their heels. Painted in 1876 and acquired for the Tretyakov Gallery, the canvas is one of Vasnetsov's early Realist genre scenes from the years before he turned to bogatyrs and folk subjects.
credit: Scanned from: A. K. Lazuko Victor Vasnetsov , Leningrad: Khudozhnik RSFSR, 1990, ISBN 5-7370-0107-5

title: On the Banks of the Nile
description: A late riverside scene from Upper Egypt, with figures and pack animals drawn up on a sunlit bank above the Nile. Painted long after Lewis's return to England, it draws on the cache of Cairo sketchbooks he mined for the rest of his career. The high horizon and clear ochre palette typify his desert manner.

title: Portraits in the Countryside
description: Caillebotte's mother, aunt, cousin, and a family friend sit reading and sewing on the lawn at the family's Yerres estate, viewed from above through a steep garden perspective. The bourgeois leisure scene combines Impressionist plein-air light with Caillebotte's almost geometric staging of figures in space.

title: Song of the Lark
description: A young farmer pauses with his scythe at twilight, head tilted toward the unseen call of a lark. Painted shortly after the Civil War, the work distills Homer's interest in rural American labor and the silent intervals that punctuate it, rendered in a low-keyed palette of dusk.
credit: The Athenaeum: Home - info - pic; Chrysler Museum of Art, search: 83.590; Google Art Project works from the Chrysler Museum of Art

title: Sunny Day. Spring
description: Bare birches and a softening crust of snow at the edge of a Moscow suburb, painted by Levitan as a sixteen-year-old student at the Moscow School of Painting, Sculpture and Architecture. The small 1876 oil is among the earliest surviving works by an artist who would become the central figure of the Russian mood landscape, the so-called peizazh nastroeniya.

title: The Standing Bearer
description: A standard-bearer in Cairo unfurls the green banner of the Prophet before a mosque facade, surrounded by attentive figures. Gérôme stages the ceremony like a frieze, using crisp profile poses and tile patterns rendered with near-photographic care.

title: turf bench
description: A relaxed open-air group portrait of Repin's wife, daughters, and in-laws gathered on a turf bench in the family garden. Painted during his summers in Krasnoye Selo, it shows him adapting Russian realism to a freer, sun-warmed plein-air idiom.

title: Arrival of the Normandy Train
description: Steam billows beneath the iron-and-glass shed of the Gare Saint-Lazare as a locomotive pulls in from the Normandy line. One of twelve canvases Monet made of the station in 1877, the series treated industrial vapour as a modern equivalent of mist on the Seine.

title: Artlib gallery-13875-o
description: A requiem on a frozen plain: a priest swings a censer over a field of fallen Russian soldiers after the Russo-Turkish War. Vereshchagin painted the scene from direct experience as a war correspondent, part of his unsparing campaign against martial glamour.

title: Boating on the Yerres
description: A solitary oarsman pulls down the Yerres river near the artist's family estate, the viewpoint set startlingly low and close to the rower's straining body. Caillebotte's boating scenes treat leisure with the engineer's eye for mechanism, anticipating the cropped framing of modern photography.

title: Danceringreen
description: A ballet dancer in a green tutu adjusts her costume in the wings, captured from Degas' habitual cropped, off-axis vantage. Pastel hatching layers powdery greens and pinks, a chromatic shorthand the artist refined throughout his Opéra de Paris series.

title: Extérieur de la gare Saint-Lazare
description: Part of Monet's 1877 Gare Saint-Lazare series, the first concerted Impressionist meditation on industrial modernity. Steam, sunlight, and iron architecture dissolve into one another, the locomotive yard reframed as a study in coloured vapour.

title: Flowered Riverbank
description: A bank of the Seine near Argenteuil shimmers under summer foliage and scattered blossom. The high-keyed greens and broken touch are characteristic of Monet's most concentrated Impressionist years, when he and Renoir painted side by side along the river.

title: Market at Jaffa
description: A bustling market square in Ottoman Jaffa rendered with Bauernfeind's near-photographic precision, every robe, awning and stone of the citadel sharply observed. A trained architect turned Orientalist painter, he based such scenes on extensive study trips and on-site sketches in the Levant.

title: Monet w421
description: A landscape in Monet's mature Argenteuil-into-Vetheuil manner, with foliage rendered as a mosaic of small directional touches. Local colour is constantly inflected by reflected light from sky and ground.

title: Paris Street in Rainy Weather
description: A wet-cobbled Place de Dublin in Haussmann's rebuilt Paris, viewed from Rue de Moscou. Caillebotte, the Impressionists' patron and engineer, here departs from their feathery touch for a cool, photographic precision, deploying steep perspective and a near-life-size foreground couple.

title: Pond at Montgeron
description: Painted at the Hoschedé estate of Rottembourg, where Monet was commissioned to produce four large decorative panels, a still pond mirrors poplars and a strolling figure in flickering verticals of green. The Montgeron sojourn deepened the relationship that would, after Camille's death, lead to his second marriage with Alice Hoschedé.

title: Portrait of a Man
description: A bearded sitter in a dark coat fills the canvas at three-quarter length, hands hidden, the background washed in a flat warm grey. Dated 1877 and measuring 79 by 59 cm in oil on canvas, the portrait is in the Sterling and Francine Clark Art Institute in Williamstown, part of the deep Clark holding of Degas built up between 1911 and 1921.

title: Portrait of Frances Sherborne Ridley Watts
description: Fanny Watts, a childhood friend of Sargent from the family's Roman years, sits half-turned in a dark dress whose row of buttons winds along her body. The 1877 oil was the first picture Sargent submitted to the Paris Salon, where it was accepted while he was still a pupil of Carolus-Duran; it is in the Philadelphia Museum of Art.

title: Portrait of the painter Vasily Ivanovich Surikov
description: Vasily Surikov, the future painter of the Boyarynya Morozova and the Streltsy, sits in dark coat and full beard against a neutral wash, painted by his older Itinerant colleague Ilya Repin. The portrait is a record of friendship between two of the central figures of the Peredvizhniki, made at the start of Surikov's career as a history painter.

title: Porträt der Jeanne Samary
description: The Comédie-Française actress Jeanne Samary leans forward with parted lips and luminous eyes, her pink dress dissolving into the rosy ground. Renoir's brush builds the portrait almost entirely from warm, transparent layers of colour.

title: The Gare Saint-Lazare; Arrival of a Train - 1877
description: A locomotive pulls under the iron-and-glass shed of the Gare Saint-Lazare, steam rolling up to merge with the smoke-stained light. Part of a twelve-canvas series for which Monet secured permission to set up his easel inside the working terminus.

title: The Plum
description: A young woman sits alone at a café table, an unlit cigarette between her fingers and a brandy-soaked plum before her. Manet captures the suspended boredom of modern Parisian leisure with loose brushwork and a muted palette of pinks, creams and pale lilacs.

title: Bosphorus
description: Caïques and sailing barges drift on the calm waters of the Bosporus below the silhouette of Constantinople, lit by a low Mediterranean sun. Painted in 1878, the canvas belongs to the long series of Bosphorus views that Sultan Abdul Hamid II would acquire directly from Aivazovsky, eventually accumulating around forty works by the artist for the Ottoman court.

title: Bouquet de glaïeuls
description: A bouquet of gladioli, from the brief stretch of still life Monet produced after settling at Vetheuil. The blossoms are massed in vertical accents of red and pink, paint laid on thickly to register petal against petal.

title: Café Singer
description: A café-concert performer leans forward mid-song, mouth open, her gloved hand suspended before her face to mark the physical effort of projection. The 1878 pastel on canvas, now at Harvard's Fogg Museum, belongs to Degas's run of theatre subjects in which he and Mary Cassatt were testing pastel against the glare of gas footlights.

title: Dancer Taking a Bow
description: A ballerina holds a low curtsy at the front of the stage, bouquet in hand, the corps blurred behind her in the footlight haze. Degas returned obsessively to such after-performance moments around 1878, drawn to the gap between drilled spectacle and momentary stillness.

title: En route pour la pêche
description: Breton women and children file across the tidal flats of Cancale at low water, baskets balanced on shoulders. The Salon-scale picture established the twenty-two-year-old Sargent in Paris and won a second-class medal in 1878. The wet sand mirrors a high pearly sky in long horizontal bands of grey-blue.
credit: National Gallery of Art, Washington, D. C., online collection

title: La Seine à Vétheuil
description: The Seine at Vétheuil, the riverside village where Monet settled in 1878 after leaving Argenteuil. Soft poplars and reflections built up in short, drily loaded strokes typify the more sober palette of his late-1870s landscapes.
credit: Collection Olivier Senn, Taken on 15 May 2019

provenance.collection: MuMa Museum of modern art André Malraux
provenance.location: MuMa Museum of modern art André Malraux

title: Landscape at Saint-Ouen
description: An early landscape from the industrial outskirts north of Paris, painted before Seurat formulated his pointillist method. Loose, almost Corot-like brushwork registers river, sky and bank in muted tones, a quiet rehearsal for the rigorous technique to come.

title: Monet w502
description: A landscape from the Vetheuil years, when Monet, recently widowed, painted the small Seine village and its surrounding fields in all weathers. The handling is rougher and more searching than his Argenteuil work.

title: Notes Nocturne lithograph by James McNeill Whistler 1878
description: A single boatman crosses the Chelsea Reach of the Thames, with the Battersea factories and a church spire dissolved into atmospheric tusche washes. Whistler executed this second lithotint of 1878, the year of the Ruskin libel trial, working from memory on the stone in the Wellington Street printing offices rather than at the riverside.

title: On the Stile
description: A young woman pauses at a wooden stile separating two pasture fields, her gaze turned away from the viewer. The painting belongs to Homer's Houghton Farm idylls, where rustic labor is filtered through the conventions of the genteel illustration.
credit: National Gallery of Art, Washington, D. C., online collection

title: Portrait of Henri Michel-Lévy
description: The painter Henri Michel-Lévy stands in his studio leaning against his own canvases, a slack mannequin collapsed on the floorboards beside an open paintbox. Degas exhibited the 1878 portrait, now at the Calouste Gulbenkian Museum in Lisbon, at the fourth Impressionist exhibition under the title Artist in his Studio.

title: Portraits at the Stock Exchange
description: The banker Ernest May, top-hatted and pince-nez'd, listens to a colleague leaning over his shoulder while the trading floor blurs into faceless agitation behind them. Degas painted his collector and admirer in 1878,79, applying Edmond Duranty's call for portraits that read a sitter's profession in his bearing.

title: Stilleben mit Chrysanthemen
description: A still life of chrysanthemums in a glazed pot, painted at Argenteuil during a season when Monet turned indoors to floral subjects. Loose, prismatic touches break the petals into shimmering points of colour, treating the bouquet with the same outdoor optics he brought to his river views.

title: The Green Hill
description: A small group of figures crosses the slope of a sunlit New England hillside, the composition reduced to broad bands of grass, sky and shadow. The work belongs to Homer's late-1870s rural idylls, balancing illustration and quiet landscape observation.
credit: National Gallery of Art, Washington, D. C., online collection

title: The Milk Maid
description: A young woman in a bonnet and apron carries a brimming pail through a sunlit pasture. Homer's loose, summery handling belongs to the Houghton Farm watercolours and oils that distilled American rural life in the post-Civil War decade.
credit: National Gallery of Art, Washington DC

title: The Rainbow
description: A rainbow arcs across a clearing sky as the storm clouds drift off the meadow and a low sun catches the wet grass. The 1878 canvas at the Indianapolis Museum of Art belongs to Inness's late storm series, in which the Swedenborgian painter treated the rainbow as a recurring emblem of spiritual presence.

title: The Reaper
description: A solitary harvester swings his scythe through tall grain under a high summer sun, the field's ochre stalks brushed with rapid, almost graphic strokes. The watercolor belongs to Homer's Houghton Farm period, when he reworked rural American labor in the lean, light-keyed manner he had absorbed during his recent stay in Cullercoats.

title: The Road of the War Prisoners
description: Vasily Vereshchagin (Russian, 1842-1904). The Road of the War Prisoners, 1878-1879. Oil on canvas, 71 1/4 x 117 11/16 x 2 1/4 in.

title: Vétheuil in Winter
description: Drift ice clogs the Seine beneath the half-frozen village, painted during the brutal winter of 1879-80 when the river broke up in spectacular fashion. The chalky palette of bone-white and pewter records one of the coldest seasons of the century.

title: Warm Afternoon
description: A young woman in a sunbonnet sits on the warm grass of a hillside pasture, a study of stillness and rural reverie. Painted during Homer's Houghton Farm summers, the watercolor shows the artist's command of transparent washes and reserved white paper, qualities that helped redefine the medium's ambitions in America.
credit: National Gallery of Art, Washington, D. C., online collection

title: Winners
description: Drawn from Vereshchagin's Balkan series, the painting confronts the aftermath of battle as scavengers strip the bodies of the fallen. The Russian realist refused to glamorize war, building documentary detail into a deliberately disquieting field of corpses and crows.

title: At the Café
description: Patrons crowded along the marble counter of a Parisian brasserie, observed with the cool detachment Manet brought to modern social life. Sketchy contours, a high horizon and the cropped figures at the edges signal his late, increasingly Impressionist-inflected handling.

title: At the Père Lathuille Restaurant
description: On the terrace of a fashionable suburban restaurant, the proprietor's son leans intimately toward a lady lunching alone. Painted en plein air during Manet's late embrace of Impressionist technique, the canvas glows with dappled sunlight and feathery, summery greens.

title: Banks of the Seine at Lavacourt
description: The Seine winds past the village of Lavacourt across from Vétheuil, where Monet lived from 1878. The riverbank views he painted there mark the brightening palette and broken brushwork of his fully mature Impressionism, made under the strain of his wife Camille's final illness.
credit: Photo I took at the Frick Art Museum

title: Degas
description: Two dancers rest between exercises in tutus and bodices, one adjusting her shoulder strap while the other stands behind her. The 1879 sheet, pastel and gouache on paper at roughly 46 by 67 cm, belongs to Degas's long preoccupation with the lulls of the rehearsal room rather than the polished performance.

title: Garden under Snow
description: A snow-covered Paris garden seen from the window, the bare branches and low wall reduced to muted whites, blues and umbers. Gauguin painted the small canvas in 1879, still a stockbroker and Sunday painter under Camille Pissarro's tutelage; it now hangs in the Budapest Museum of Fine Arts.

title: Girl and Laurel
description: A young woman in a straw hat stands among flowering mountain laurel, her face shaded against the New England summer light. The composition belongs to Homer's mid-career sequence of solitary rural figures absorbed in landscape.

title: Grand Duchess Sofia at the Novodevichy Convent
description: Repin depicts the deposed regent Sofia Alekseyevna confined at Novodevichy Convent in 1698, her glare turned outward as a hanged Streltsy is glimpsed through the barred window. The picture compresses defeat, fury, and political claustrophobia into a single suffocating cell.

title: In the Conservatory
description: A fashionable Parisian couple — Monsieur and Madame Guillemet — pause among hothouse foliage, their hands almost meeting on a garden bench. Manet exhibited the canvas at the 1879 Salon, where its crisp drawing and modern subject bridged his Realist roots and Impressionist company.
credit: Curves adjusted from File:In the Conservatory.jpg . Originally: Google Arts & Culture: Home - pic 7 th level of zoom out of 8. Scaled down.

title: James Abbott McNeill Whistler
description: A small etching from Whistler's Venice set, produced after the artist arrived in the city following his bankruptcy. Sparing, calligraphic line on laid paper sketches a moored vessel against open water, the unworked paper standing in for sky and reflection.

title: La route de Vétheuil
description: A snow-effect view of the road leading into Vétheuil, the Seine-side village where Monet lived from 1878. The picture belongs to his series of winter landscapes painted en plein air, the broken brushwork registering the muted blues and lilacs of low northern light on settled snow.

provenance.collection: Museum of Fine Arts, St. Petersburg, Florida, USA
provenance.location: Museum of Fine Arts, St. Petersburg, Florida, USA

title: Louise Jane Jopling
description: The painter and writer Louise Jopling, herself a celebrated society figure, presented in a slim black gown against a muted ground. By this date Millais had moved well beyond his Pre-Raphaelite beginnings into a fluent, Velázquez-inflected portrait manner aimed squarely at fashionable London.

title: Marie Buloz Pailleron
description: A portrait of the writer Marie Buloz Pailleron painted out of doors at the family estate of Ronjoux, an unusually plein-air approach for a society commission. Sargent, then a young pupil of Carolus-Duran, sets her white dress against deep summer foliage in fluid, Manet-like brushwork.

title: Miss La La at the Cirque Fernando
description: The mixed-race acrobat Anna Olga Albertina Brown, billed as Miss La La, hangs by her teeth from a rope below the Cirque Fernando's painted dome. Degas attended several performances in January 1879 and produced sketches and an oil study before this canvas, his only circus subject, went on view at the Fourth Impressionist Exhibition.

title: Monet w526
description: A riverside motif in Monet's Vetheuil-period idiom, with broken touches of green, ochre and blue building both bank and water. The picture is held together by a single envelope of weather rather than firm drawing.

title: Plum Trees in Blossom
description: An orchard at Vétheuil seen through a haze of white spring blossom. Monet treats the subject — long established in Japanese printmaking, which he collected — as an all-over screen of pale flecks against pale ground, the trees almost dissolving into the field.

title: Poppy Field near Vétheuil
description: Crimson poppies scatter through summer grass on the slopes above Vétheuil, where Monet lived in straitened circumstances after leaving Argenteuil. The motif of wildflowers as red dabs against green became a signature device, repeated through the late 1870s.

title: Sokolniki. Autumn
description: A woman in black walks a damp avenue through Moscow's Sokolniki park as wet yellow leaves and bare birches close in on either side. Levitan was nineteen and living in Saltykovka, having been expelled from Moscow in an anti-Jewish edict, when Pavel Tretyakov bought the canvas, the first Levitan to enter the Tretyakov collection.

title: Still Life with Pheasants and Plovers
description: Game birds laid out on a bare table in muted earth tones, a rare still life from a year of personal hardship for Monet following his wife Camille's death. The handling is broader and more sober than his contemporary garden pictures.

title: Susanna and the Elders
description: The Danish painter takes up the biblical bather in a polished academic idiom learned in Bonnat's Paris atelier. Susanna is set against a shadowed garden wall, the elders pressed close to a single edge of the canvas to sharpen the moment of intrusion.

title: The Doorway
description: Print; Prints

title: The Millinery Shop
description: A milliner in a green wool dress and long gloves leans across a counter, inspecting a wide-brimmed hat with both hands; the unsold stock crowds the foreground. Degas reworked the canvas between 1879 and 1886; x-rays show he reduced the trim and ornament until the figure's class, customer or worker, became deliberately unreadable. The painting entered the Art Institute of Chicago in 1933.

title: The Road to Vétheuil
description: A rutted country road leads the eye between hedgerows toward the village rooftops on the Seine. Painted soon after Monet settled at Vétheuil following financial collapse in Paris, the canvas favours dry, broken brushwork over tonal finish.

title: Van gogh f1040 jh100
description: An early drawing from the Borinage period, when the artist was working as a lay preacher among Belgian coal miners and teaching himself to draw from manuals and Millet prints. The sheet's dense, laborious hatching reflects his self-taught struggle with the figure.

title: Vase of Flowers
description: An early still life painted while Seurat was still absorbing Barbizon and Impressionist precedents. The dense impasto and earthy palette show him before the systematic divisionism of dots that would define his mature work later in the decade.

title: Vétheuil
description: The riverside village rises from the Seine to its squat Romanesque church, mirrored in the slow water. Monet painted dozens of variants of this view during his impoverished Vétheuil years, working out of a small studio boat.

title: Woman in Street Clothes
description: The actress Ellen Andrée stands in everyday street dress, her face cast in shadow beneath a small hat. Degas drew this 1879 pastel as part of his series of modern Parisiennes, the same sitter whose absinthe-stupor he had captured for In a Café three years earlier.

title: Woman with a Pearl Necklace in a Loge
description: A young woman in pale evening dress sits in a theatre box, her image doubled in the curving mirror of the loge behind her. Cassatt was the only American invited to exhibit with the French Impressionists, and her theatre series adopts Degas's spatial play with reflection and electric light.

title: 100 Aspects of the Moon - 67
description: Minamoto no Tsunemoto draws his bow on a sika deer that has wandered into the imperial palace grounds, an autumn incident recorded in the year 932. From the One Hundred Aspects of the Moon, the design contrasts the courtier's taut profile with a low harvest moon hanging over palace eaves.

title: After Igor Svyatoslavich 's fighting with the Cumans
description: The young prince Igor Svyatoslavich and his slain warriors lie as though sleeping among bells, daisies and forget-me-nots on the southern steppe, with vultures circling against a rising moon. Vasnetsov drew the subject from the medieval Tale of Igor's Campaign and showed the canvas at the eighth Peredvizhniki exhibition in 1880, where Repin praised its solemn poetry and Stasov attacked it as academicism.

title: Autumn Landscape
description: A path winds through bare birches and yellowed grass under an overcast autumn sky, a single figure receding along it. Painted in 1880 and held at the Tver Regional Picture Gallery, the canvas belongs to Levitan's earliest run of mood landscapes, in which he began to load weather and season with quiet human feeling.

title: Balcony
description: Two top-hatted men gaze down from the wrought-iron balcony of the artist's apartment at 31 Boulevard Haussmann, the same Parisian vantage point Caillebotte used in several canvases of the period. The plunging perspective and modern bourgeois subject typify his engagement with Haussmann's reshaped city.

title: Bouquet of Mallows
description: A loose still life of pink mallows arranged in a glass vase, painted at Vetheuil during a difficult personal year for Monet. The tabletop dissolves into rapid, comma-like strokes that anticipate the all-over surface of his late garden pictures.

title: By the Water or Near the Lake
description: A young woman in a straw hat leans by a sun-dappled lake, the foliage dissolved into iridescent strokes of green and pink. The picture exemplifies Renoir's sociable, plein-air Impressionism of the early 1880s.

title: Clear Sailing
description: A small watercolor study of a sailboat on open water, painted with Homer's characteristic economy of wash. Sky and sea are summarized in a few transparent layers, leaving the white paper to carry the brightness of the canvas sail.
credit: Philadelphia Museum of Art, online collection

title: Five O'Clock Tea
description: Two women take afternoon tea in a Philadelphia parlour, the silver service gleaming in the foreground while the visitor lifts her cup to obscure her face. Cassatt presents bourgeois female ritual with an Impressionist's looseness of touch, emphasising decorative still-life passages over narrative.

title: Flying Carpet
description: Ivan Tsarevich rides a flying carpet through the night sky over a misty river, the caged Firebird glowing in his hand. Savva Mamontov commissioned the canvas in 1880 to decorate the boardroom of the Donetsk Railway, hoping the folk subject would conjure the romance of travel; the directors rejected it as too whimsical and Mamontov kept it for himself.

title: Francis Brooks Chadwick
description: A bust-length oil sketch of the Boston-born painter Francis Brooks Chadwick, set on a small panel just under fourteen inches high. Sargent painted his friend in Haarlem in 1880, where the two had travelled with Ralph Wormeley Curtis to study the Dutch masters at first hand.

title: Jerusalem Artichoke Flowers
description: Yellow blooms of helianthus rise on tall stems in a thicket of green, the canvas worked in feathery, broken touches. Painted at Vétheuil during a fertile garden period, it shows Monet's habit of treating cultivated flowers as motifs for studies in light and saturated colour.
credit: National Gallery of Art, Washington, D. C., online collection

title: L'homme au balcon
description: A top-hatted bourgeois leans on the wrought-iron railing of a Haussmann balcony, surveying the boulevard below. Caillebotte, an engineer by training, repeatedly used the steep diagonal of Paris's new avenues to investigate the modern viewer's detached urban gaze.

title: La debacle - Monet w562
description: The breakup of ice on the Seine after a hard winter near Vétheuil, with floes drifting past bare riverbanks. Monet returned to this motif repeatedly in 1880, using broken brushwork to register the shifting interplay of water, ice and reflected sky.

title: Le déjeuner des canotiers
description: Renoir's friends gather on the terrace of the Maison Fournaise at Chatou, lingering over wine and fruit after a row on the Seine. The composition weaves portraiture, still life, and shimmering river light into one celebrated image of modern leisure.

title: Madame Ramón Subercaseaux
description: The Chilean diplomat's wife is shown seated at a piano in an interior of pale silvery tones, her loose white dress catching the light. The composition belongs to Sargent's early Parisian period and was admired at the 1881 Salon.

title: Mary Cassatt Self-Portrait
description: Cassatt poses fashionably dressed, sketchbook angled away from view, her face partly in shadow as she meets the viewer's gaze. She made the small gouache and watercolour over graphite around 1880, a year after first exhibiting with the French Impressionists; it now belongs to the National Portrait Gallery in Washington.

title: Monet w579 springtime in vetheuil
description: A blossoming orchard at Vetheuil, the Seine village where Monet lived after Argenteuil. Loose feathered brushwork builds the white spring foliage against soft greens, the palette typical of his early move toward broken colour and atmospheric light.

title: Monet w601
description: A landscape from Monet's Vetheuil period, when he worked obsessively along the Seine's bends. The brushwork is rapid and atmospheric, recording weather rather than topography in the manner that defines his mature outdoor practice.

title: Monet w611
description: A study of willows along the riverbank, a recurring Vetheuil motif. Trailing branches are stroked in vertical green dashes against reflective water, the composition built almost entirely from flickering verticals and horizontals of broken colour.

title: Monet w646 jetty at fecamp in rough weather
description: The Norman fishing port of Fecamp under storm conditions, painted on one of Monet's coastal campaigns. Choppy water and a bleached sky are scumbled with quick palette-knife passages, recording the weather as much as the harbour's architecture.

title: Poppy Field
description: A field of red poppies set against summer greens, the kind of motif Monet revisited near Vetheuil and Giverny. Dabs of vermilion are scattered with calligraphic ease across a haze of grass, demonstrating his interest in saturated complementary colour.

title: Portrait of Mademoiselle Irène Cahen d'Anvers
description: The eight-year-old daughter of a Parisian banking family sits in profile, her copper hair flowing loose against a soft blue-green ground. Renoir's feathery brush captures both the child's reverie and the upholstered comfort of haute-bourgeois life.

title: Religious Procession in Kursk Province
description: A vast religious procession winds across a sunburnt steppe, sweeping clergy, peasants, gendarmes, and crippled pilgrims into a single dust-clouded cross-section of imperial Russian society. Repin's panoramic canvas is a touchstone of Peredvizhniki social realism.

title: Small Lake with Boat
description: An early oil sketch on cardboard from Munch's teenage years, depicting a still pond with a moored rowboat. The plein-air naturalism, painted before his Symbolist breakthrough, shows him absorbing Norwegian landscape conventions in compact, atmospheric form.

title: Study of a Nude
description: An academic life study from Gauguin's early years, predating the Tahitian primitivism for which he is now remembered. The figure is modelled with conventional tonal shading, evidence of the studio training he would soon discard for synthetism.

title: The Embroiderer Alternative title: French: La Brodeuse Mette Gauguin
description: Gauguin's wife Mette Sophie sits at a small table bent over her sewing, the dense brushwork drawn from Camille Pissarro's example. The 116 by 81 cm canvas, painted in 1880 while Gauguin was still a successful stockbroker, hangs at the Foundation E. G. Bührle in Zurich and is catalogued as Wildenstein 65.

title: The Seine at Lavacourt
description: A panoramic view of the Seine at Lavacourt, opposite his Vétheuil home, submitted to the 1880 Salon as a calculated bid for official recognition. The handling is unusually controlled, the river a broad mirror of pearly cloud.

title: The Wailing Wall
description: Worshippers gather at the Western Wall in Jerusalem, the great Herodian ashlar towering over them in raking sunlight. Gérôme based the picture on photographs and sketches from his Near Eastern travels, deploying the polished academic finish that defined his Orientalist output.

title: Two Boys Watching Schooners
description: Two barefoot boys perch on a grassy headland, gazing seaward at distant schooners drifting across a flat New England bay. The watercolor pares the scene to bands of sky, water, and sunlit turf, characteristic of Homer's Gloucester summers and his interest in childhood as a vantage on the wider working coast.
credit: Art Institute of Chicago : online database: entry 16803

title: Venetian Onion Seller
description: A street vendor stands in the cool gloom of a Venetian calle, a string of onions slung from her hand. The picture belongs to Sargent's early Venetian campaigns of 1880-82, when he prowled working-class quarters off the tourist routes. Tonal greys and a single shaft of light recall Velazquez, whom he had recently studied in Madrid.

title: Vétheuil
description: A view of the Seine-side village of Vétheuil, where Monet settled with his struggling household in 1878. He renders the church and clustered roofs through a screen of shimmering river reflections, treating the whole town as a single envelope of haze and light.

title: View of Vétheuil
description: The riverside village climbs from the Seine to its Gothic church tower, viewed from a boat moored among reeds. Monet rented a house at Vétheuil in 1878 and worked tirelessly along this stretch of water following Camille's death.

title: A forgotten soldier
description: A monumental anti-war canvas by the Russian battle painter Vereshchagin, showing a fallen soldier abandoned on the battlefield as carrion birds gather. The work is part of the artist's unflinching cycle exposing the human cost of imperial conflict.
credit: kunstkopie; Bridgeman Art Library : Object 266195; artpoisk.info; vereschagin.com.ua

provenance.collection: V. V. Vereshchagin Mykolaiv Art Museum
provenance.location: V. V. Vereshchagin Mykolaiv Art Museum

title: After the attack. Plevna
description: Vereshchagin painted the carnage of the Russo-Turkish siege of Plevna from first-hand experience as a war correspondent attached to the Russian army. The unsentimental documentary realism he made his trademark exposes the human cost behind official communiqués of imperial conquest.

title: Alenushka
description: A barefoot peasant girl sits hunched on a grey stone by a dark forest pond, her chin on her knees and her hair undone. Vasnetsov painted the orphan heroine of the Russian fairy tale Sister Alyonushka and Brother Ivanushka at Abramtsevo in 1881, using a local girl with grieving eyes as the model.

title: Alice Hoschedé au jardin
description: Alice Hoschedé, who would become Monet's second wife, stands among foliage at Vétheuil. The portrait belongs to a small group of garden figures from this transitional period, in which Monet treats the sitter as one luminous accent within a tangle of green.

title: Bei Fécamp
description: A view near Fecamp on the Normandy coast, where Monet painted from the chalk cliffs in early 1881. Salt air and grey-green sea are rendered through agitated, short brushstrokes, the palette muted toward the silver tones of the Channel.

title: Boat Lying at Low Tide
description: A stranded fishing boat tilts on the Normandy beach at Fécamp, its hull dark against shimmering wet sand and a high pearl sky. The on-the-spot rendering shows Monet's growing interest in the sea coast, a subject he would mine across the next two decades.

title: Bouquet of Sunflowers
description: A dense bouquet of sunflowers arranged in a glazed vase, painted in Vétheuil years before Van Gogh took up the same motif in Arles. Monet builds the heavy heads from short, comma-like strokes of chrome yellow and ochre, contrasting their warmth against a cool blue-grey ground.

title: Champ de coquelicots
description: A sun-flooded meadow of red poppies near Vétheuil, where Monet lived after Argenteuil. The horizon is pushed high so the field reads as a near-flat carpet of broken colour, a structure he would return to throughout his rural landscapes.

title: Dr. Pozzi at Home
description: The celebrated Parisian gynecologist Samuel Pozzi stands full length in a flame-red dressing gown, fingers tugging at his collar and sash. Sargent's bravura essay in monochrome scarlet was painted in the sitter's own apartment and announced the young American's arrival in Parisian society.

title: Heroes
description: The three bogatyrs Dobrynya Nikitich, Ilya Muromets and Alyosha Popovich sit mounted at the edge of the steppe, scanning the horizon for enemies. Vasnetsov worked on the nearly 3 by 4 metre canvas for almost twenty years, finishing it in 1898 in the rebuilt barn-studio Savva Mamontov had given him at Abramtsevo; Pavel Tretyakov bought it for his gallery as soon as it was done.

title: John Newman
description: Cardinal Newman, leader of the Oxford Movement and convert to Rome, sits in scarlet biretta and mozzetta near the end of his life. Millais paints the theologian with the brisk, grand-manner brushwork of his late society portraiture. The picture was commissioned soon after Newman received the cardinal's hat from Leo XIII.

title: La Seine à Vétheuil
description: A bend of the Seine at Vétheuil, the village where Monet lived through the bleakest years of his middle career. The river, opposite bank and sky are resolved into three horizontal bands of broken colour, a structural simplicity that points toward his coming serial work.

title: Lydia at the Tapestry Loom
description: Cassatt's elder sister Lydia, often her sitter in these years, leans into her work at a vertical tapestry loom in soft afternoon light. The picture belongs to the artist's series of women absorbed in domestic occupations, painted with the loose Impressionist touch she had absorbed in Degas's circle.

title: Monet w649
description: A coastal or riverside study from 1881, the year Monet divided his time between Vetheuil and the Normandy cliffs. Quick wet-on-wet strokes capture transient light, with no preparatory drawing visible beneath the painted surface.

title: Monet w651 morning by the sea
description: Dawn light over the Channel, painted during one of Monet's Normandy seasons. Pearly pinks and pale blues are layered in horizontal sweeps, anticipating the obsessive serial study of changing light that would define his later Rouen and Houses-of-Parliament campaigns.

title: Monet w653
description: A landscape from Monet's intensely productive 1881 season, when he worked between Vetheuil and the coast. The picture relies on tonal harmonies rather than line, the surface built up from short, dragged strokes of broken colour.

title: Monet w658
description: A landscape from 1881, the year Monet was preparing to leave Vetheuil for Poissy. The brushwork remains feathery and fragmented, recording the play of light over foliage and water in the manner he had refined through the previous decade.

title: Monet w662
description: An outdoor study from Monet's 1881 campaign, painted with the rapid, broken touch he had perfected at Argenteuil and Vetheuil. Saturated greens and lavender shadows show his consistent attention to the temperature of light.

title: Monet w664
description: A Vetheuil-era landscape worked entirely en plein air. Monet builds the scene from short, parallel strokes of broken colour, layering complementary hues to register the vibration of sunlight rather than to outline objects.

title: Monet w668
description: A landscape from the early 1880s, when Monet was still working the Seine valley around Vetheuil. The handling favours atmospheric unity over topographic detail, with soft transitions between sky, foliage and water.

title: Monet w678 lane in ile st martin
description: A path on the Ile Saint-Martin near Vetheuil, a small island in the Seine where Monet often set up his easel. Dappled summer light filters through trees in flickering touches of yellow and green, the composition framed by the receding lane.

title: Monet w679
description: An outdoor landscape from Monet's Vetheuil years. The picture is constructed from short, parallel strokes that knit foliage, sky and water into a single shimmering field, a technique central to Impressionist landscape practice.

title: Monet w683
description: A landscape from 1881, when Monet was producing canvases at high speed for the dealer Durand-Ruel. The handling is quick and confident, with thin scumbles allowing the light ground to glow through the upper layers of paint.

title: Monet w684
description: A landscape from Monet's final Vetheuil season, painted with the rapid, fragmented touch he had honed throughout the 1870s. The surface registers atmosphere as a single tonal envelope rather than a sequence of described objects.

title: Monet w691
description: A landscape from 1881, the year Monet worked between the Seine valley and the Normandy coast. Broken brushwork and a high-keyed palette dissolve the motif into pure light, in the spirit of the earlier Argenteuil pictures.

title: Monet w694
description: An outdoor study from 1881, made during one of Monet's most prolific years. The handling shows the mature Impressionist economy: no preliminary drawing, only short, directional strokes of complementary colour worked wet into wet.

title: Monet w700 near vetheuil
description: A view of the countryside surrounding Vetheuil, the Seine village Monet had occupied since 1878. Soft greens and lavender shadows are stroked in feathery, parallel touches, the composition closer to a tonal study than a topographic record.

title: Morning of Execution of Streltsy
description: Condemned streltsy in white death shirts hold lit candles in carts before the Kremlin wall, watched by their wailing families and by Peter the Great mounted at the right, as the gallows wait at Lobnoye Mesto. Surikov set his 1881 canvas on Red Square in the autumn of 1698, after the second streltsy revolt; Tretyakov bought it from the ninth Peredvizhniki exhibition almost as soon as it opened.

title: Mr. Carlyle delivering the address on his installation as Lord Rector of Edinburgh University
description: A wood-engraved illustration documenting Thomas Carlyle's rectorial address at Edinburgh, reproduced for a mass readership in the Illustrated London News. Such press engravings were the period's chief vehicle for circulating images of public events before photographic reproduction took over.

title: Nocturne in Rosa und Grau
description: A Nocturne in pink and grey, in which a stretch of river or shoreline dissolves into a few atmospheric washes. Whistler used these musical titles to insist that subject mattered less than the harmony of tones — the central tenet of his Aestheticist programme.

title: On the Terrasse
description: Two girls in flowered hats sit on a Chatou terrace overlooking the Seine, a basket of wool spilling between them. The picture is among Renoir's most ambitious figure compositions, set against a softly broken backdrop of foliage and river.

title: Temps calme
description: The Channel at Pourville under settled weather, painted during Monet's first sustained Norman coast campaign. Long horizontal bands of beach, sea and sky are differentiated almost entirely by close-valued blues and pearly greys.
credit: Artbook: Rudolf Staechelin’sche Familienstiftung Basel (Hrsg.): Nafea, die Sammlung Rudolf Staechelin, Basel .

title: The Burning of the Turkish Flagship by Kanáris
description: The 84-gun Ottoman flagship Mansur al-liwa explodes in red flame off the coast of Chios while Konstantinos Kanaris steers his fireship clear in the foreground. Aivazovsky painted the night attack of 6,7 June 1822, a Greek reprisal for the massacre of Chios during the War of Independence; the 162 by 223 cm canvas hangs in the National Gallery in Athens.

title: The Hut in Trouville
description: A tarred fisherman's hut stands above the bared sands of the Normandy coast, painted on a windy summer return to Trouville. Quick, scrubbed strokes record the silvered tideline and the lift of grasses on the dune, hallmarks of Monet's plein-air practice.

title: The Piazza San Marco
description: Renoir's view of Venice's central square dissolves the basilica's Byzantine facade into shimmering touches of pink, gold, and blue. Painted during his Italian journey, the canvas treats architecture as an Impressionist screen of light, with figures and pigeons scattered across the sunlit pavement.

title: The poor fisherman
description: A gaunt fisher stands in his moored skiff while a woman gathers flowers and an infant sleeps on the bank, the scene reduced to chalky, almost frescoed planes of pale color. The austere composition and melancholic mood made the picture a touchstone for Symbolist painters and the young Picasso.

title: The Sea in Fécamp
description: Das Meer bei Fécamp

title: Wheatfield
description: A summer wheatfield treated as an almost abstract field of warm strokes under a high sky. The subject anticipates the haystacks Monet would begin painting in series a decade later, where the same agrarian motif became a vehicle for studying changing light.

title: Abelard and his Pupil Heloise
description: The medieval philosopher tutoring his young pupil in a richly furnished Parisian interior, the doomed pair already absorbed in one another. Blair Leighton — not the Frederic Leighton credited here — favoured this kind of fastidiously costumed romantic-historical anecdote.

title: Arnaut Blowing Smoke at the Nose of His Dog
description: A Balkan mercenary in Ottoman service exhales pipe smoke into the muzzle of a patient hound on a sunlit Cairo street. Gérôme's enamel-smooth surface and ethnographic exactitude are typical of his late Orientalist studies of idle, picturesque soldiery.

title: Before the Race
description: Thoroughbreds and jockeys mill restlessly along the rail before the start, presented in a scatter of angled poses rather than a single tableau. Degas painted the small panel between 1882 and 1884, one of three identically titled canvases that drew on the stop-action horse photography then being published by Eadweard Muybridge. Henry Walters bought it in 1910 for the museum in Baltimore.
credit: Walters Art Museum : Home page Info about artwork

title: Charlotte Dubourg par Fantin-Latour
description: Fantin-Latour's sister-in-law sits in dark dress against a neutral ground, hands loosely clasped. The portrait carries the muted tonality and quiet psychological focus the artist learned from his admiration of the Old Masters and his friendship with Whistler; it now hangs in the Musée d'Orsay.

title: Cliff Walk at Pourville
description: Two women in white stand on a wind-swept Channel cliff above sailing boats, their parasols echoing the curve of clouds and grass. Painted during a working summer at Pourville in 1882, the canvas balances figural anchor against the broad Norman sky.

title: Cliffs at Pourville
description: One of Monet's 1882 views from the Norman village of Pourville, where he worked along the cliff path between Dieppe and Varengeville. Tall grasses are whipped into rapid green-and-violet strokes, the Channel pushed to a high horizon so that the cliff and sky carry most of the picture's air.

title: Cliffs near Dieppe
description: Chalk cliffs rear above a narrow band of restless sea, the grasses on top whipped by a Channel wind. Monet spent the spring of 1882 working at Pourville and Varengeville, applying short, dragged strokes to capture the fissured stone and saline atmosphere of the Norman coast.

title: Cliffs near Pourville
description: A Norman coastal scene capturing the chalk cliffs of Pourville under shifting summer light. Monet sets a high horizon and broken brushwork against the sea, dissolving rock and water into a single atmospheric weave typical of his Normandy campaign.
credit: Rijksmuseum Twenthe https://www.rijksmuseumtwenthe.nl/content/355 Previously: Cloude Monet, Falaises près de Pourville (1882) , adagio808 from Enschede, The Netherlands, 2009-06-25 15:23

title: Église de Varengeville
description: The Norman cliff-top church catches early sun above a mist-veiled coastline near Dieppe. Monet worked on the Varengeville motif repeatedly during his 1882 stay, treating the small chapel as a study in shifting maritime light.

title: El Jaleo
description: A near life-size scene of a flamenco dancer mid-stride before a row of seated musicians, lit by raking footlights that cast huge shadows on the back wall. Sargent worked the picture up from sketches made in Spain, marrying Velázquez's tonal economy to a thoroughly modern sense of theatrical staging.

title: Eugen von Blaas Bildnis Arthur Graf Berchtold 1882
description: A formal portrait of Arthur Graf Berchtold, a Hungarian magnate and member of the Imperial Diet, posed with the upright bearing of a statesman. De Blaas, better known for genre scenes, here demonstrates his society-portrait register with crisp tailoring and a sober palette.

title: Fisherman's Cottage on the Cliffs at Varengeville
description: Fisherman's Cottage on the Cliffs at Varengeville

title: Fishermen on the Seine at Poissy
description: Anglers in small boats work a quiet stretch of the Seine framed by leafy banks, painted from Monet's floating studio. The Poissy years were unhappy ones, but they yielded several of his most luminous river scenes in delicate greens and silvers.

title: Flowers in a Crystal Vase
description: A late still life painted in Manet's final months, when illness confined him to small flower pieces brought by visitors. Carnations and clematis are set in a faceted crystal vase, the brushwork economical yet luminous against a darkened ground.

title: Foggy Morning at Pourville
description: Mist swallows the Norman cliffs above Pourville, where Monet spent the summer of 1882 pursuing the dissolving effects of marine atmosphere. Pale lavenders and silvered greens are knit together in short, parallel strokes, leaving the horizon as little more than a suggestion.

title: Girl Carrying a Basket
description: A young woman trudges along a windswept English coast with her basket, painted during Homer's stay at the fishing village of Cullercoats. The Northumbrian sojourn shifted his palette toward greyed blues and ochres and gave his figures the weathered seriousness that marks his late marines.
credit: National Gallery of Art, Washington DC

title: June
description: Cattle graze in a sunlit New Jersey pasture under a broad green canopy, with the white spire of a Montclair church showing through the trees. Inness painted the canvas in 1882, soon after renting the Dodge estate in Montclair where he would settle for the rest of his life; the work entered the Brooklyn Museum and remains an early example of his Barbizon-rooted American manner.

title: Knight at the Crossroads
description: A bogatyr in heavy armour halts his horse before a moss-covered boulder on a darkening steppe, ravens perched among the bones of earlier travellers. The stone's old Cyrillic inscription warns that going straight ahead means no return; Vasnetsov drew the text from byliny he collected for the patron Savva Mamontov, reworking an earlier composition for the 1882 version now in the State Russian Museum.

title: La maison du pêcheur
description: A modest fisherman's cottage perched above the Norman coast, painted during Monet's productive campaigns at Pourville and Varengeville. Broken brushwork dissolves cliff, sea, and sky into a single weathered atmosphere, the cottage anchoring the composition against the windblown grass.

title: Lady with the Rose
description: Charlotte Louise Burckhardt, the twenty-year-old daughter of a Swiss merchant in the artist's Paris circle, stands against a flat grey ground holding a single pink bloom. Sargent painted the silhouette and tonal restraint in conscious homage to Velazquez, whom his teacher Carolus-Duran had urged him to study; the canvas drew acclaim at the 1882 Salon and now hangs in the Met.

title: Low Tide at Pourville
description: Exposed sand flats stretch beneath the chalk cliffs of the Normandy fishing village, painted on one of Monet's productive 1882 campaigns along the coast. Quick, broken brushwork captures the shifting light and damp air, and X-rays reveal an earlier composition lying beneath the beach.

title: Monet w 763 the path
description: A garden or woodland path drawing the viewer between flanking masses of foliage, painted with the interwoven greens and lilacs typical of Monet's Giverny work. The motif reduces landscape to a corridor of pure colour and dappled shade.

title: Monet w706
description: A landscape from 1882, when Monet had relocated to Poissy and was making frequent trips to the Normandy coast. The brushwork remains rapid and fragmentary, the palette tuned to the silver-grey light of the lower Seine.

title: Monet w712 low tide at pourville
description: Exposed beach and chalk cliffs at Pourville, the small Normandy resort where Monet worked through the spring of 1882. Glistening wet sand is stroked in pale lavenders and ochres, capturing the broad horizontal sweep of the Channel coast at low water.

title: Monet w717
description: A coastal scene from Monet's 1882 Normandy campaign at Pourville and Varengeville. Sea, sky and cliff are unified by a silvery palette and short, directional strokes, evidence of his close attention to the changing light of the Channel.

title: Monet w724
description: A landscape from the 1882 Normandy season, when Monet was shuttling between Pourville and his rented house at Poissy. Cliff and sea are simplified to broad zones of broken colour, the handling more atmospheric than descriptive.

title: Monet w736
description: A coastal subject from 1882, the year of Monet's intensive Pourville and Varengeville campaigns. Broken brushwork and a cool, salt-bleached palette register the particular light of the Normandy cliffs above the Channel.

title: Monet w752
description: A landscape from 1882, painted with the swift, confident touch Monet had refined over a decade of plein-air work. The surface is built up from short directional strokes that suggest weather and time of day before they describe place.

title: Monet w753
description: A coastal study from Monet's prolific Normandy campaign, executed with the broken-touch brushwork that defines his early-1880s plein-air practice. Cliffs, sea, and weather are reduced to chromatic vibrations, the palette tilted toward cool greens and pearly greys.

title: Monet w757
description: Painted during Monet's repeated stays on the Channel coast, the canvas tracks the play of light across rock and water with rapid, scumbled strokes. Form gives way to atmosphere, an approach that anticipates the artist's later serial investigations.

title: Monet w759
description: One of dozens of seascapes Monet produced from rented quarters along the Normandy shore, where weather shifts dictated his working day. The composition relies on a high horizon and a textured, comma-stroke sea typical of his Pourville and Étretat campaigns.

title: Monet w764
description: A Channel-coast motif handled with the loose, weather-driven facture Monet refined in the early 1880s. Sky and sea are knit together by repeated short strokes, the pigment kept high-keyed to register passing light.

title: Monet w767
description: From Monet's Normandy production, the scene captures the headlands and shifting maritime light he chased obsessively that decade. The handling is brisk and granular, with chalky lilacs and greens laid wet-into-wet.

title: Monet w772
description: Another Channel-coast view from Monet's 1882 campaign, with cliffs cropped tight and the sea pushed nearly flat against the picture plane. The brushwork remains unblended, each stroke registering a separate observation of colour and weather.

title: Monet w776
description: A coastal subject from Monet's intensive Normandy season, painted in the open air against quickly changing conditions. Greens, mauves, and cream whites are dragged across the surface in the loose impasto he had by then made his signature.

title: Monet w778a
description: Painted on the Normandy shore, the work belongs to a string of cliff and sea studies in which Monet tested how far light could dissolve solid form. The stroke is rapid, the palette cool and slightly chalky.

title: Monet w787
description: From Monet's Pourville-Varengeville orbit, where he repeatedly framed the Channel through cliffs and scrubby vegetation. The surface is built up in short, directional strokes that encode wind, haze, and tide.

title: Monet w807
description: A Normandy seascape carrying the high-keyed, broken-touch language Monet had perfected by the early 1880s. Distance is implied not by linear perspective but by graded warmth and saturation across the brushwork.

title: Monet w812 vase of chrysantemums
description: A still life of chrysanthemums massed in a vase, treated with the same broken-touch brushwork Monet brought to landscape. The flowers register as bursts of pigment rather than carefully drawn forms, the background kept tonal so colour can dominate.

title: Monet w816
description: A Channel-coast study from the run of seascapes Monet produced in 1882, painted on site through bracing weather. Sea, cliff, and sky are unified by a quick, granular touch and a restricted, salt-bleached palette.

title: Monet w922
description: A close study of jonquils, the yellow blooms set against muted greens to make colour the principal subject. Monet treats the flowers with quick, loaded strokes, the kind of small still life he often painted between larger landscape campaigns.

title: Portrait of Dora Wheeler
description: Dora Wheeler, a designer trained alongside Chase in Munich, sits in a blue gown amid the embroidered hangings of her mother Candace's Associated Artists studio. The portrait won a medal at the 1883 Paris Salon and helped establish Chase's reputation for atmospheric, aesthetic-movement interiors.

title: Portrait of Père Paul
description: A rare portrait by Monet, depicting the white-aproned cook of the Hôtel Blanche at Pourville. Painted during the same Normandy stay that produced the cliff-walk pictures, it captures the chef's ruddy face and twin chins in dense, almost caricatural impasto.

title: Road at La Cavée
description: A sunken Norman lane cuts down toward the sea at Pourville, where Monet spent productive months in 1882. Banks of grass and gorse frame a small triangle of bright Channel water, a composition organised by the steep diagonal of the path.

title: Sarkizova Ann
description: Anna Nikitichna Burnazyan-Sarkisova, the painter's second wife, gazes out from a semi-transparent veil that softens the dark ground behind her. Aivazovsky married Anna in 1882, nearly forty years his junior; the portrait hangs in the Aivazovsky Art Gallery in Feodosia, a rare exercise in formal portraiture from a painter best known for storms at sea.

title: Studio Interior
description: William Merritt Chase (American, 1849-1916). Studio Interior, ca. 1882.

title: The Church at Varengeville
description: The little Saint-Valéry church perches on its eroding clifftop at Varengeville-sur-Mer, painted from the gully below with the Channel framed beyond. Monet returned to the motif from several angles during his 1882 Pourville stay, treating the building as a fixed point against shifting weather.

title: The Church of Varengeville
description: The medieval clifftop church of Saint-Valery at Varengeville, silhouetted against the Channel sky. Monet returned to this motif repeatedly in 1882, treating it as a study in tonal envelope, here flushed with the warm rose and orange of evening.

title: The Daughters of Edward Darley Boit
description: Four sisters stand in the dim foyer of the Boit family's Paris apartment, the youngest seated on the rug, the eldest pair half-swallowed by shadow beside a pair of monumental Japanese vases. Sargent borrowed the deep recessive space and palette directly from Velazquez's Las Meninas, which he had copied in Madrid in 1879; the picture entered the MFA Boston in 1919.
credit: http://www.mfa.org/collections/object/the-daughters-of-edward-darley-boit-31782 This is a retouched picture , which means that it has been digitally altered from its original version. Modifications: As much of the unfree frame was removed as possible, lossless JPG crop . The original can be viewed here: John Singer Sargent 001.jpg : . Modifications made by Keraunoscopia .

title: Waiting
description: A young dancer in tutu bends to clasp her ankle on a wooden bench at the Paris Opera, beside a chaperone in black with a furled umbrella. Degas worked the pastel in steep perspective on paper, jointly held since 1983 by the Norton Simon Foundation in Pasadena and the J. Paul Getty Museum, one of the earliest of his more than two hundred backstage ballet studies.

title: White Lilacs in a Glass Vase
description: A bouquet of white lilacs leans from a clear glass vase against a darkened ground, the flowers worked in loaded, gestural strokes. The picture belongs to the small floral still lifes Manet painted at the very end of his life, when illness had reduced his ambitions to flowers brought by visitors.

title: Agitated Sea at Etretat
description: Heavy surf breaks against the Normandy chalk cliffs at Etretat, the famous arches receding behind a churn of jade and white. Monet returned repeatedly to this stretch of coast in the early 1880s, working on multiple canvases at once to chase shifting light; this one hangs in the Musée des Beaux-Arts de Lyon.
credit: Consulter cette image photographiée par Gilles Alonso spécialiste de la photo en gigapixel en très haute définition (+1 milliard de pixels)

provenance.collection: Museum of Fine Arts of Lyon
provenance.location: Museum of Fine Arts of Lyon

title: At the beer garden
description: A crowded Munich beer garden seethes with waitresses, top hats and bourgeois families under the chestnut trees. Menzel, the chronicler of modern German urban life, packs the canvas with the sharp-eyed, almost photographic detail he gathered in pocket sketchbooks.

title: Bemberg Fondation Toulouse - Bateaux sur la plage à Etretat - Claude Monet - 1883 65x81 Inv.2077
englishTitle: Boats on the Beach at Étretat
description:
Monet paints fishing boats hauled up beneath the chalk cliffs of Étretat, a Norman coast he returned to repeatedly in the 1880s. The pale beach and overcast sea are built from short, broken strokes that record shifting weather rather than narrative incident. The canvas now resides at the Bemberg Foundation in Toulouse.</curatorDescription>

The pale beach and overcast sea are built from short, broken strokes that record shifting weather rather than narrative incident. The canvas now resides at the Bemberg Foundation in Toulouse.

title: Chase mrs meigs piano organ 1883
description: Mrs. Meigs is shown at her piano-organ in a richly furnished aesthetic interior, her white dress glowing against dark panelling. Chase exhibited several such society portraits in the early 1880s, deploying the bravura tonal handling he had absorbed from Frans Hals and Velázquez.

title: Children on the Seashore
description: Painted on the rocky beaches of Guernsey, where Renoir summered in 1883, the canvas shows small bathers playing among warm ochre boulders. The Channel light prompts a brighter, drier palette and the firmer drawing of his transitional period.

title: Christian IX of Denmark with his family
dateCreated: between 1883 and 1886 ( Prince Valdemar of Denmark (Christian's son) married Princess Marie of Orléans on 20 October 1885. If she is not here, the painting should have been made before that date.)
description: Tuxen assembles Christian IX — the so-called father-in-law of Europe — with his children and royal grandchildren in the garden hall of Fredensborg Palace. Commissioned for the king's golden wedding anniversary, the group portrait records the Danish dynastic ties that linked the courts of Britain, Russia, and Greece.

title: Crab Fishing
description: Two figures lean from a beached dory to lift a crab pot, painted during Homer's productive Gloucester summer. The watercolor balances loose washes of harbor light with sharper notations of rope, basket and net.
credit: Bridgeman Art Library : Object 247063; The Athenaeum: Home - info - pic; Worcester Art Museum

title: Dance at Bougival
description: A young couple turns on the floor of a riverside dance hall outside Paris, the woman's pink bonnet glowing against the dappled crowd. Renoir worked from sittings with Suzanne Valadon and Paul Lhote to fix Impressionist plein-air light into a tightly composed figural scene.

title: Fujiwara no Yasumasa Playing the Flute by Moonlight
description: A late triptych by Yoshitoshi shows the Heian courtier Fujiwara no Yasumasa playing his flute on a moonlit moor while the bandit Hakamadare, disarmed by the music, looks on. Long stretches of muted ground and the cool autumnal palette demonstrate Yoshitoshi's reformed late style for the Meiji woodblock market.
credit: Image: http://collections.lacma.org/sites/default/files/remote_images/piction/ma-31808204-O3.jpg Gallery: http://collections.lacma.org/node/191379 archive copy at the Wayback Machine

provenance.collection: Los Angeles County Museum of Art

title: Georges Seurat
englishTitle: Seated Nude (study for Bathers at Asnières, 1883)
description: A preparatory oil study for one of the bathers in Une Baignade, Asnieres, the large canvas that announced Seurat's ambitions in 1884. Built from broad criss-crossed strokes in the conté-drawing manner he called balayé, it precedes his fully developed pointillist technique.

title: Khnopff
description: A figure buries her face in her hand as a half-glimpsed pianist plays in the corner, the music itself unseen. Khnopff, a founding Belgian Symbolist, isolates inwardness and silence with his characteristic muted palette and severe, almost photographic restraint.

title: Les Terrassiers
description: Labourers at work levelling earth, a subject from the industrial fringes of Paris that Seurat tackled in his early career. The broad balayé brushwork and sober palette precede the ordered dots of his pointillist maturity.

title: Madame X
description: Virginie Gautreau stands in profile in a black satin gown, her lavender-powdered skin set against a brown ground in a near-monochrome scheme.
