credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 37: Siphonophorae (see here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Siphonophorae 59
description: A Forskalia-like siphonophore dissected layer by layer, from intact colony to stripped polyp clusters. The sequence reveals the modular construction of a pelagic cnidarian, with each zooid specialized for swimming, feeding, or reproduction.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 59: Siphonophorae (see here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Siphonophorae 7
description: Mature and immature Epibulia and Rhizophysa colonies shown alongside cross-sections of their gas bladders. The plate emphasizes the apical pneumatophore that allows these chains of polyps to drift just below the sea surface.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 7: Siphonophorae (see here , here )

title: Haeckel Siphonophorae 77
description: Praya and Bassia colonies displayed as chains of paired swimming bells with trailing reproductive medusae. Haeckel uses the bilateral nectophores to convey the streamlined hydrodynamics of calycophoran siphonophores.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 77: Siphonophorae (see here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Spirobranchia
description: Brachiopod shells from the inside, with internal spiral lophophore supports visible in fossils such as Spirifer and Cyrtina. The plate doubles as a paleontological reference, juxtaposing Paleozoic forms to show the calcified scaffolding of the feeding organ.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 97: Spirobranchia (see here , here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Spumellaria
description: Spherical and spindle-shaped radiolarian skeletons with concentric latticework and radiating spines. The plate isolates the polycystine forms whose silica architecture inspired Haeckel's broader argument that nature is intrinsically geometric.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 91: Spumellaria (see here , here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Spyroidea
description: Two-chambered radiolarian skeletons rendered as miniature cages, each with a sagittal constriction and ornamental feet. The composition catalogs the helmet-like Nassellaria forms drawn from Challenger expedition microfossil samples.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 22: Spyroidea (see here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Stauromedusae
description: Stalked jellyfish rendered as goblet-shaped medusae anchored by adhesive feet, including Haliclystus auricula clinging to algae. The plate captures these unusual sessile cnidarians from side and base views.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 48: Stauromedusae (see here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Stephoidea
description: Ring-shaped radiolarian skeletons with single, double, or triple silica hoops, presented as crowns and lattices. The plate centers on simple-ringed Nassellaria, showing how minimal skeletal motifs can scaffold a living single cell.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 71: Stephoidea (see here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Teleostei
description: Bizarrely formed bony fish, including seahorses, the leafy sea dragon Phycodurus eques, and the antennated frogfish Antennarius striatus. The plate emphasizes camouflage and modified fins that disguise these teleosts as drifting weed.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 87: Teleostei (see here , here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Tetracoralla
description: Solitary and colonial rugose corals shown as polished cross-sections and side views, including the horn-shaped Omphyma turbinata. The plate is essentially paleontological, displaying the four-fold septal symmetry of an extinct Paleozoic order.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 29: Tetracoralla (see here , here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Thalamophora 12
description: Miliolid foraminifera arranged as porcelain-like shells with looping chambers, including Quinqueloculina and Cornuspira. The plate magnifies these microscopic shelled protists to reveal the sequential coiling that defines the order.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 12: Thalamophora (see here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Thalamophora 81
description: Lagenid foraminifera shown as flask- and bottle-shaped tests with single apertures, ornamented by ribs, spines, and squamose plates. Haeckel groups the variety to highlight how a basic vase form can be elaborated into dozens of species.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 81: Thalamophora (see here , here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Thalamphora
description: Elongate foraminifera with stacked or alternating chambers, including Nodosaria, Uvigerina, and Bolivina. The plate concentrates on multilocular benthic forms whose calcareous tests accumulate to build deep-sea sediments.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 2: Thalamophora (see here , here )

title: Haeckel Thoracostraca
description: A symmetrical plate of shrimp-like crustaceans, juxtaposing transparent adult Lucifer and Penaeus species with their nauplius and mastigopus larval stages. Haeckel uses the layout to argue visually for embryological recapitulation, treating the developmental sequence as ornamental composition.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 76: Thoracostraca (see here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Thuroidea
description: Sea cucumbers and their larvae arranged on a dark ground, showing Phyllophorus and Synapta alongside successive auricularia stages. The plate pairs adult body plans with their drifting planktonic young to emphasize life-cycle continuity within Holothuroidea.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 50: Thuroidea (see here , here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Tineida
description: A study of plume and leaf-mining moths in which Alucita and Pterophorus species spread their feathered wings into near-radial patterns. Magnified wing-scale details at the margins underscore the geometric microstructure beneath the apparently dusty surfaces.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 58: Tineida (see here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Trachomedusae
description: Bell-shaped trachymedusae are drawn from above, beside, and beneath, with the long manubrium of Geryonia trailing like a clapper. The transparent tissues let internal gonads and radial canals show through, turning anatomy into a chandelier-like ornament.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 26: Trachomedusae (see here , here and here )

title: Haeckel Trochilidae
description: Twelve hummingbird species, including the Sword-billed and Booted Racket-tail, are arrayed against black to display iridescent gorgets, crests, and tail streamers. Drawn from millinery skins, the postures are decorative rather than observational, foregrounding plumage geometry over flight behavior.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 99: Trochilidae (see here , here and here and Biodiversity Heritage Library )

title: Haeckel Tubulariae
description: Solitary and budding hydromedusae such as Sarsia and Coryne float across the page, several shown in the act of releasing free-swimming medusae from polyp colonies. The plate compresses an entire alternating life cycle into a single ornamental field.
credit: Kunstformen der Natur (1904), plate 6: Tubulariae (see here , here )

title: Houses of Parliament
description: One of nineteen views of the Houses of Parliament that Monet worked on from a balcony at St Thomas' Hospital across the Thames. Westminster's Gothic silhouette is silhouetted against a sun-soaked fog, the river burning with reflected colour as atmospheric haze flattens detail into pure tonal envelope.

title: London
description: Part of Monet's Houses of Parliament series painted from his window at St Thomas's Hospital, the canvas dissolves the Gothic Revival silhouette into mauve and orange vapour. The campaigns of 1899–1904 used the Thames fog as a coloured veil through which Monet tracked the changing hours.

title: Nymphéas
description: Pads of green and lavender float across a pond surface that fills the canvas, sky and bank registering only as reflections among the lilies. With this 1903-08 series Monet refined the immersive water-garden vision that would culminate in the Orangerie cycles.
credit: flickr.com; Sotheby's London,19 June 2007, L07007, lot 7

title: Portrait of Painter Peder Severin Kröyer
description: Tuxen depicts his fellow Skagen colonist Krøyer at work, palette in hand, eyes fixed on an unseen sitter. The portrait commemorates a friendship between the two leading Danish naturalist painters, set down a few years before Krøyer's mental collapse.

title: Sharing the News
description: A cluster of Venetian women pause from their chores to read aloud from a letter, faces tilted in shared attention. De Blaas mines the city's working-class courtyards for these intimate everyday vignettes, polished with the slick academic technique that earned him Belle Epoque popularity.

title: The Flirtation
description: Two young Venetians exchange glances across a sunlit doorway, the woman's costume crisp with embroidered linen and a flowered shawl. De Blaas built his career on such genre scenes of working Venice, prized in Edwardian salons for their sparkling finish and gentle theatrics.

title: The Houses of Parliament
description: The Gothic silhouette of Westminster dissolves into a haze of violet and orange across the Thames. Painted from a terrace at St Thomas's Hospital, the canvas belongs to Monet's London series, in which he tracked the same motif under shifting fog, smoke and sun.

title: Waterloo Bridge
description: Part of Monet's London Thames series, the bridge dissolves into industrial mist warmed by low sun. Smokestacks beyond the river emit plumes that fuse fog, water, and sky into a unified veil of orange and violet.

title: Wounded Amazon
description: A bare-breasted Amazon staggers from the field clutching her side, her body silhouetted against a stormy ground in von Stuck's customary bituminous palette. The classical subject is treated with the muscular Symbolist eroticism he made the signature of the Munich Secession.

title: Yamamoto 1904
description: A fisherman bends to his work in a small skiff, rendered in flat planes of color and direct gouged lines. The print is a foundational image of Japan's sosaku-hanga (creative print) movement, in which the artist designed, carved, and printed the block himself rather than relying on the traditional ukiyo-e workshop division of labor.

title: Aged Phoenix
description: A withered, balding phoenix stands on stick legs, the grotesque bird rendered in fine etched line on zinc plate. Plate 9 of the Inventionen cycle of eleven satirical etchings made between 1903 and 1905, the work is held by the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum and was first shown at the 1906 Munich Secession.

title: Autoportrait
description: Delaunay portrays himself in a high-collared coat, the brushwork still indebted to the divisionist palette he was absorbing from Seurat and Signac. Painted between 1905 and 1906, before his shift toward Orphism and the Eiffel Tower series.

title: Boris Kustodiev self-portrait
description: Kustodiev paints himself in hunting dress under the title On the Hunt, rifle and gear marking the rural retreats he favoured around the Volga. The 1905 canvas is held by the State Russian Museum in Saint Petersburg.

title: Édouard Manet by Henri Fantin-Latour
description: Manet stands three-quarter length in dark coat and top hat, gloves and cane in hand, framed against an austere studio ground. Fantin-Latour's portrait, the basis for his role in the group canvas Hommage à Manet, presents the Impressionist forerunner with the dandified self-possession his contemporaries described.

title: Eugen von Blaas - Plauderei - 1905
description: Two women lean together over a parapet in animated chatter, the title's German for 'small talk' framing the scene as anecdote rather than narrative. De Blaas relishes the textile detail, from the patterned shawl to the starched apron, in his typical lustrous, salon-ready finish.

title: Female Nude with Foliage Shadows
description: A standing female nude is dappled by the shadows of overhanging leaves, the figure modelled in loose strokes on a rough ground. Painted in oil on cardboard in 1905, the early canvas now in the Kirchner Museum Davos predates the formal founding of Die Brücke later that year in Dresden.

title: In the Water by Eugen von Blaas
description: Venetian girls hike up their skirts to wade in the lagoon shallows, a favourite genre subject of Eugen von Blaas. The Austrian-Italian academician built his career on these sun-warmed scenes of Adriatic peasant life, rendered with porcelain finish and bright local colour.

title: Moonrise: Soldier and Maiden
description: A soldier and a young woman stand in a wooded clearing under a rising moon, the figures pressed close in the half-light. Painted in 1905 during Kirchner's Dresden student years, the canvas entered the Museum of Fine Arts, Houston as accession number 98.286.

title: Portrait of Ashbury Wright Lee
description: The elderly Philadelphian Ashbury Wright Lee is shown three-quarter length in a dark coat, the loose handling of the face typical of Eakins's late portraiture. Painted around 1905, the canvas belongs to the unsparing commissioned likenesses Eakins produced for friends and acquaintances in his final productive decade.

title: Portrait of Maria Yermolova
description: The actress Maria Yermolova stands full length in a black gown, the floor mirror at her side multiplying the columnar silhouette. Commissioned in 1905 by Moscow's literary and artistic community to mark her thirty-fifth anniversary at the Maly Theatre, Serov worked over thirty-two sittings at her Tverskoy Boulevard residence; the painting is now in the Tretyakov Gallery.

title: Portrait of the Writer Maxim Gorky
description: Maxim Gorky leans forward in a tieless dark shirt, his thin moustache and untidy hair signalling the workman writer he cultivated as a public persona. Serov painted the portrait in 1905, the year of the first Russian revolution, in which Gorky was briefly imprisoned for revolutionary agitation.
credit: http://podol.ru/serov/ PDF (for version uploaded on 10 January 2014)

title: The Open Window
description: The view from Matisse's hotel window at Collioure looks out through pots of climbing flowers to a harbour of sailboats under pink and green water. Painted in 1905 and shown at the Salon d'Automne that autumn, the canvas was bequeathed in 1998 to the National Gallery of Art, Washington from the estate of Mrs John Hay Whitney.
credit: Retrieved from National Gallery of Art, USA , 25 December 2007.

title: The Struggle for Woman
description: Two nude warriors lock in combat over a sprawling female nude, a Symbolist allegory of erotic rivalry typical of von Stuck's Munich Secession output. Hard contour, bronzed flesh and a smouldering ground push the mythic theme toward late nineteenth-century decadence.

title: Water Lilies
description: An early canvas in the great water-lily cycle Monet pursued at his Giverny pond for the last three decades of his life. The horizon has already vanished; only floating pads, reflected sky and submerged depth remain, organised purely by colour.
credit: Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, online database

title: Dancers
description: Two figures swing through a loose woodcut composition, the angular limbs and reduced palette typical of the Brücke group's early experiments. Made in 1906, the year after Kirchner co-founded Die Brücke in Dresden, the print is held by the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum.

title: Doris with Ruff Collar
description: Doris Große sits in a stiff white pleated ruff, her face turned slightly aside in a pose borrowed from old-master portraiture. The model, whom Kirchner nicknamed Dodo, was his lover and principal sitter from around 1904 until 1911; the circa-1906 canvas entered the Thyssen-Bornemisza collection in 1961 as one of the Baron's first modern acquisitions.

title: Portrait of Jean Metzinger
description: Jean Metzinger sits in profile in a blue hat against a stylised floral backdrop, a tulip pinned to his lapel. Also known as L'homme à la tulipe, the 1906 portrait was painted while Delaunay was working through Neo-Impressionist divisionism, before either sitter or artist turned to Cubism.

title: Salome
description: Salome dances before a moonlit sky, the platter bearing the head of the Baptist held up by a grinning attendant. Von Stuck stages the subject with bare midriff, jewelled adornments and the brooding theatricality favoured by fin-de-siècle Munich Symbolism.
credit: Eva Mendgen: Franz von Stuck 1863–1928. Benedikt Taschen Verlag, Köln 1994; ISBN 3-8228-8953-9

title: Salome
description: Franz von Stuck stages Salome in dark, lurid Symbolism: the dancer raised in ecstasy beneath jewelled veils while a servant hoists the Baptist's head into shadow. The picture distils the Munich Secession's fascination with the femme fatale.

title: Sten'ka Razin
description: The Cossack chieftain Stepan Razin sits brooding in a fur-lined coat aboard a strug, his crew rowing out across the wide Volga. Surikov first sketched the subject in 1887 and only finished the 318 by 600 cm canvas for the 1906 exhibition, returning to repaint Razin's face around 1910. The painting hangs in the State Russian Museum, St Petersburg.
credit: Originally uploaded on en:Image:Surikov1906.jpg on 15:56, 15 February 2005 by en:user:Ghirlandajo with a caption; Vasily Surikov . Sten'ka Razin (1906). The Russian Museum , St Petersburg

title: Two Human Beings
description: A man and woman stand side by side on a stony shore, facing the sea but never one another. Munch returned to this image of unbridgeable distance for decades in paintings and woodcuts, here rendered in blunt blocks of beach grey, surf white and brooding water.

title: Water Lilies
description: Lily pads float in even rhythms across green-blue water, with a pale band of sky-reflection running along the upper edge. The picture comes from the first mature group of Nymphéas exhibited by Durand-Ruel in 1909.

title: Water Lilies by Monet
description: An overhead view of the Giverny pond, dotted with discs of pink and white lilies. Cool blues and greens shift toward lavender where the surrounding foliage is mirrored in still water, with no sky visible above the bank.

title: Waterlilies
description: A horizontal screen of lily pads hovers over reflected sky on the Giverny pond. By 1906 Monet had abolished the bank entirely, treating the water as a self-contained world the eye could enter at any point.

title: Bathing Men
description: Three nude men stride from the surf in a frieze-like composition, painted on the German island of Warnemünde. Munch celebrated sun, sea and male vigour with vehement verticals of brushwork, part of a triptych on the ages of man now in Helsinki's Ateneum.

title: Giambattista Pittoni
description: Bartolomeo Nazari shows his fellow Venetian Giambattista Pittoni at the easel, the leading Rococo history painter of the lagoon city. The portrait survives in the Museo Correr and was reproduced in Laura Coggiola Pittoni's 1907 monograph Dei Pittoni, Artisti Veneti. Pittoni would later co-found the Venetian academy in 1750 and succeed Tiepolo as its president.
credit: Original source: Museo Correr, Venice Intermediate source: Laura Coggiola Pittoni (1907). Dei Pittoni, Artisti Veneti . Bergamo: Istituto Italiani d'Arti Grafiche. Immediate source: https://archive.org/stream/deipittoniartist00pitt#page/24/mode/1up

title: Nymphéas
description: From the Giverny series, the Japanese-style pond seen close-up with no shore in sight. Lily pads punctuate broad zones of mauve and green reflection, the painted surface oscillating between water-skin and pure abstraction.

title: Pond with Water Lilies
description: A vertical Giverny canvas in which the lily pond is rotated almost into pure surface pattern. Pinks and violets float over deep greens, the brushwork loose enough that the pads sometimes read as drifting clouds of pigment.

title: Portrait of Henriette Girshman
description: Henriette Girshman stands in her boudoir, hand poised in front of a mirror that doubles the room behind her. Painted in 1907 in oil on canvas at 140 by 140 cm, Serov's portrait borrows the reflected-space conceit of Velázquez's Las Meninas and now hangs in the Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow.

title: Still Life with a Parrot
description: A green parrot perches above a table of fruit and crockery rendered in dense, saturated patches of orange and complementary hues. Painted in the first half of 1907, the canvas marks the high point of Delaunay's divisionist phase and his engagement with Chevreul's colour theories. A second, more mosaic-like version is in the Thyssen-Bornemisza Museum, Madrid.

title: The Chess Game
description: Two friends bend over a board in a sun-shot garden during one of Sargent's Alpine summers in the Simplon. The painter spent these holidays sketching members of his travelling party in shawls, hats and Kashmiri textiles. The watercolour-like oil handling and high-keyed greens are typical of these informal late landscapes.

title: The Snake Charmer
description: A dark silhouetted figure pipes serpents from a moonlit jungle on a riverbank, commissioned by the mother of Robert Delaunay. Rousseau, a self-taught customs officer, never left France; his jungles were composed from the Jardin des Plantes, picture books and dream, layered in his deliberate, flattened naïve manner.

title: The Song
description: A late portrait by the American Impressionist of a young woman absorbed in performance, rendered with the fluid brushwork and rich tonal harmonies Chase admired in Velazquez. The dark, atmospheric ground throws the figure's pale skin and parted lips into intimate relief.

title: Water Lilies
description: Water Lilies, 1907, 19. 170

title: Water Lilies
description: An early canvas from the Water Lilies series begun in earnest after 1903, when Monet shifted from views of the Japanese bridge to the pond's surface alone. Floating pads anchor a shimmering ground in which clouds and willows are fused as reflection.

title: Waterlilies
description: Clusters of lilies drift on a pond shot through with violet and rose reflection, the pads rendered in short, scumbled strokes. The 1907 group is among Monet's most chromatically daring before his cataracts began to dull his vision.

provenance.collection: Kawamura Memorial DIC Museum of Art
provenance.location: Kawamura Memorial DIC Museum of Art

title: Female Nude
description: A woman sits with her back to the viewer, the volumes of shoulder and hip cut into broad black slabs. Kirchner produced the woodcut in 1908, printed on blotting paper at roughly 19 by 15 inches, while consolidating the rough-hewn vocabulary of the Brücke group around the studio at Dresden. The impression is in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.

title: Le Palais Ducal
description: The Doge's Palace rises from the Venetian lagoon in dissolving pinks and aquamarines, painted during Monet's two-month stay in the city. The facade is treated less as architecture than as a screen for refracted light, with broken brushwork knitting stone, water and sky into a single luminous fabric.

title: Monet w1725
description: A late canvas from Monet's Giverny years, one of the water-garden compositions in which the pond surface dissolves into a near-abstract field of reflected sky and floating blooms. Loose, layered brushwork builds colour without a fixed horizon, anticipating the immersive Grandes Decorations.

title: Monet w1726
description: One of the water-lily paintings made in the studio at Giverny, where Monet returned obsessively to the pond he had dug himself. The viewpoint is tilted down so the surface fills the frame, broken only by floating pads and the soft mirror of overhanging willows.

title: Nudes
description: Two figures lean against a stove in the bare interior of Kirchner's Dresden studio, their bodies sketched in quick, angular contours. The painting belongs to the cycle of studio nudes Kirchner produced around 1908, part of the Brücke programme of working from unprofessional, freely posed models. The canvas is in the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum, New York.

title: Portrait of Almina Daughter of Asher Wertheimer
description: Almina Wertheimer poses cross-legged in Persian costume, a long-necked sarod balanced across her lap. Painted in 1908 when the sitter was about twenty-two, this was the last of Sargent's nine portraits of the Wertheimer family, bequeathed to the British nation in 1922 and now in Tate.

title: Terror Antiquus
description: Lightning splits a darkening sky over the Aegean as an archaic kore smiles enigmatically in the foreground, the Acropolis and the citadels of Mycenae and Tiryns flickering below. Bakst built the 250 by 270 cm canvas after a 1907 trip to Greece with Serov, aiming at an apocalyptic fable of ancient cataclysm. It won a gold medal at the 1910 Brussels Exposition Universelle and entered the State Russian Museum.

title: The Grand Canal
description: Looking down the Grand Canal toward Santa Maria della Salute, Monet renders Venice as drifting reflections of pink and turquoise on water. The view comes from his only visit to the city, in autumn 1908, which yielded a late series exhibited at Bernheim-Jeune in 1912.

title: The Watercarrier
description: The Italian-Austrian painter de Blaas specialised in genteel scenes of Venetian life, here a young woman pausing with her copper water vessel. His glossy academic finish made such picturesque subjects popular with late-nineteenth-century international collectors.

title: Water Lilies
description: Lily blossoms sit like white embers on a deep mauve pond, the surface broken only by their slow geometry. The canvas dates from Monet's last full-sighted summers at Giverny before cataract surgery would alter his colour sense.

title: Water-Lilies
description: A canvas from the second great wave of Nymphéas pictures, painted as Monet exhibited forty-eight pond views at Durand-Ruel's Paris gallery. Pads drift across reflections of cloud and sky, the water surface flattened into a pure field of colour with no horizon to orient the viewer.

title: William Rush Carving His Allegorical Figure of the Schuylkill River
description: The Philadelphia sculptor William Rush works at his studio bench, carving an allegorical female figure of the Schuylkill River from a wooden block while the nude model stands posed nearby. Eakins returned to the 1877 composition in 1908, the only subject he is known to have reworked in his career. The canvas is in the Brooklyn Museum.
credit: Online Collection of Brooklyn Museum ; Photo: Brooklyn Museum, 39.461_SL1.jpg

title: Bathers at Moritzburg
description: Yellow-orange bodies wade and sprawl beside cobalt water at the Moritzburg lakes outside Dresden, where Kirchner and the Brücke painters spent summer weeks bathing naked from 1909 onward. Begun in 1909, the canvas was repainted in 1926 in lighter, more even tones. It is now in Tate Modern, London.

title: Promenade Along the Volga
description: Townsfolk in summer hats and dresses stroll along the Volga embankment at Tutaev, the white-walled Romanov-Borisoglebsky churches rising behind them. Painted in 1909 in oil on canvas at 100 by 125 cm, the work marks Kustodiev's turn toward provincial merchant life as a subject. The picture is in the State Russian Museum.

title: Saint-Séverin No. 3
description: The ribbed vaults and ambulatory columns of Saint-Séverin in the Latin Quarter buckle inward as if pulled by the weight of stained-glass light. Delaunay made seven canvases of the Gothic church between spring 1909 and early 1910, and this 114 by 89 cm oil belongs to that series. It now hangs at the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum.

title: The Eiffel Tower
description: An early treatment of the iron tower that would obsess Delaunay for decades, viewed from below and toppling against a turbulent sky. The fractured planes and sharp diagonals translate Cubist analysis into a celebration of modern engineering.

title: Vesterhavet i storm. Efter solnedgang. Højen
description: A view of the North Sea at Højen on the northern tip of Jutland, painted near Tuxen's home at Skagen. Associated with the Skagen painters, Tuxen here forsakes the colony's clear summer light for a churning storm twilight, with thick impasto registering wind-driven spray.

title: Albert Gleizes
description: A seated woman in a heavy blue dress holds a bowl of phlox beside a window opening onto a faceted landscape. Gleizes signed the canvas 'Alb Gleizes 10' and showed it in Room 41 of the 1911 Salon des Indépendants, the public debut of group Cubism, and again at the 1913 Armory Show. The 81 by 100 cm oil now belongs to the Museum of Fine Arts, Houston.

title: Ballettfigurine zu: Feuervogel
description: A costume study for the Firebird, the legs braced wide in pointed slippers and the bodice flaring into orange and gold plumage. Bakst was brought in to redesign three of the costumes for Stravinsky and Fokine's Firebird, premiered by Diaghilev's Ballets Russes at the Paris Opéra on 25 June 1910 with sets by Alexander Golovin.

title: Crow and blossom by Ohara Koson
description: A solitary crow perches on a flowering branch, the bird's blue-black plumage set against pale petals. Koson's shin-hanga woodblock print refines Edo-period kachō-e bird-and-flower conventions for early-twentieth-century export collectors, prizing economical line and atmospheric ground.
credit: Woodblock print circa 1910 by Ohara Koson (1877-1945)

title: Ernst Ludwig Kirchner Spielende nackte Menschen 1910-1
description: Figures wrestle and tumble naked beneath a tree, limbs flattened into broad colour planes of pink, blue and acid green. Painted in 1910 at 77 by 89 cm, the canvas grew out of the Brücke summers at the Moritzburg lakes and now hangs in the Pinakothek der Moderne, Munich.

title: Kustodiyev fair
description: A provincial Russian fair in full swing, traders' awnings and lacquered toys crowding a wooden square under a summer sky. Painted in 1910 and held by the Nizhny Novgorod State Museum of Fine Arts, the canvas grew out of Kustodiev's Volga travels and his fascination with market days as folk theatre.

title: Negro boy by L.Bakst
description: Costume study of a boy attendant, drawn in pencil, watercolour and silver paint on laid paper, 29 by 15.5 centimetres. The 1910 sheet is held by the MAGMA collection and belongs to Bakst's high Ballets Russes period, when his orientalist costume designs for Schéhérazade and Cléopâtre were reshaping European stage design.

title: Portrait of Ida Rubinstein
description: The dancer Ida Rubinstein reclines nude on a strip of blue cloth, her limbs elongated into the silhouette of an Assyrian relief. Serov painted her in Paris in summer 1910 after seeing her perform Zobeide in Scheherazade and the title role in Cléopâtre for Diaghilev's first Saisons Russes. The canvas is in the State Russian Museum.

title: Rape of Europa
description: Europa rides the white bull across a flat green sea, dolphins curling around their wake. Worked up at Serov's Finnish summer cottage in 1910 in tempera on cardboard at 71 by 98 cm, the picture builds on sketches made during his 1907 trip to Greece with Bakst. It hangs in the State Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow.

title: Self-portrait
description: Malevich confronts the viewer in a heavy crimson coat, ringed by red-outlined female nudes in the background. The 27 by 27 cm gouache, dated to 1910,1911, marks his transition from the icon-derived figures of his early Symbolist works toward a more declarative, primitivist palette. It belongs to the State Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow.

title: Water Lilies
description: Held by the Musée Marmottan Monet, which inherited the artist's studio holdings, this Nymphéas frames the pond as an unbroken field of reflected light. Pads cluster as horizontal accents across deep blues and rose, the composition organised by colour weight rather than perspective.

title: Champs de Mars: The Red Tower
description: The Eiffel Tower rises in fractured red and ochre planes above the Champ de Mars. Delaunay's Orphic Cubism dismantles the engineered iron icon into prismatic facets, part of his sustained series treating the tower as a modern motif of Parisian light and movement.

title: Eiffel Tower
description: Painted at the height of Delaunay's Cubist phase, the tower lurches and splinters as if seen simultaneously from multiple vantage points. Surrounding buildings collapse inward, dramatising the giddy modern experience of urban scale.

title: Floorpolishers
description: Three peasants kneel and lunge with floor brushes across a strip of yellow parquet, their bodies thickened into block-like volumes. Catalogued as Nakov F-196, the 78 by 71 cm gouache on paper was shown at the Donkey's Tail exhibition in Moscow in March 1912 and now belongs to the Stedelijk Museum, Amsterdam.

title: Juan Legua
description: A seated man in dark suit and stiff collar tilts back in his chair, face splintered into a small grid of facets while the body remains legible. Painted in 1911 at 55 by 46 cm, the canvas is one of Gris's earliest Cubist portraits, the sitter a Spanish journalist living in Paris who likely used Juan Legua as a pen name. It is at the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.

title: Le Dieu Bleu Nijinsky
description: A standing figure with blue-painted skin stretches the arms wide in a hieratic pose, the hips wrapped in patterned silks. Bakst's 1911 costume design was made for Vaslav Nijinsky as the title role of Le Dieu bleu, the Cocteau-Hahn-Fokine ballet that Diaghilev premiered at the Théâtre du Châtelet on 13 May 1912. The look drew on visiting Cambodian and Siamese court dancers Bakst had studied in St Petersburg.

title: Paysage à Cassis
description: The terraced hills above Cassis stack up in flat patches of pink, ochre and pine green under a Mediterranean light. Painted in December 1911 in oil on canvas at roughly 50 by 62 cm, the landscape belongs to the brief Fauve-derived phase Picabia ran through before swinging into the Section d'Or Cubism of 1912.

title: Portrait of Jacques Nayral
description: The writer Jacques Nayral stands three-quarter length in Gleizes's garden at Courbevoie, the foliage broken into the mobile facets of an early Cubist scheme. The 162 by 114 cm canvas was shown at the 1911 Salon d'Automne and reproduced in Du Cubisme, the manifesto Gleizes wrote with Metzinger in 1912. Tate acquired the picture in 1979.

title: Portrait of Princess Olga Orlova
description: Princess Olga Orlova sits in a wide-brimmed hat and dark fur stole, one well-groomed hand resting on the arm of a chair. Painted in 1911 at 237 by 160 cm in canvas and tempera, the portrait was shown to acclaim at the Esposizione Internazionale di Roma; the sitter disliked it and donated the picture to the Alexander III Museum, now the State Russian Museum, in 1912.

title: Recoveredgleizes
description: A Cubist landscape of Meudon with a small figure threaded through faceted houses, trees, and a winding path. Gleizes exhibited Le Chemin (Paysage à Meudon) at the 1911 Salon des Indépendants, the show where the Salle 41 hang first announced Cubism as a public movement.

title: Repose
description: A languid female figure reclines on a sofa, head turned away, wrapped in shimmering ivory satin and gauze. Sargent's niece Rose-Marie Ormond was the model for several such drapery studies in the years before the First World War. The picture is essentially a virtuoso exercise in painting white folds against deep shadow.

title: Street with church in Kandern
description: A village street in the Black Foothills opens toward the parish church, the planes of road, façade, and sky reduced to firm coloured patches. Painted during Macke's Kandern period, the scene shows him absorbing Cézanne and the early Blaue Reiter palette before his shift to fully saturated colour.

title: The Woman
description: Eve panel from a triptych on the Fall, with Adam and the serpent occupying the flanking compartments. Byam Shaw extends the late Pre-Raphaelite manner of Burne-Jones and Rossetti into the Edwardian era, with hothouse colour and stylised vegetation. The figure is set against a tapestry of curling leaves and ripe fruit.

title: Window on the City No. 3
description: Faceted Parisian rooftops and the silhouette of the Eiffel Tower dissolve into a grid of prismatic colour. Painted across 1911-12 and now at the Guggenheim, Window on the City No. 3 belongs to Delaunay's Fenêtres series, the first sustained experiment in what Apollinaire would name Orphism.

title: Albert Gleizes
description: Cubist footballers lunge across the canvas in a tangle of jersey stripes, limbs, and faceted ground plane. Oil on canvas, 225.4 x 183 cm, the work entered the National Gallery of Art in Washington as one of Gleizes's largest Salon-scale figure compositions of 1912-13.

title: Francis Picabia
description: A near-square canvas of nearly two and a half metres on each side, dissecting a mountain spring into broad facets of ochre and grey-green. Picabia showed La Source at the 1912 Salon d'Automne in Paris; the picture later entered the Museum of Modern Art in New York.

title: Francis Picabia
description: Robed penitents and processional banners pulse through a Sevillian street in a Cubist-Orphist lattice of cones and curves. Inspired by Picabia's travels in Spain, the square canvas was shown at the 1912 Salon de la Section d'Or and travelled to the 1913 Armory Show; it now hangs at the National Gallery of Art, Washington.

title: Harvard Theatre Collection - Bakst
description: Watercolour set design for Act I of Daphnis and Chloe, with a wooded grove and rocky outcrop sketched in pale washes. Bakst made the drawing in 1912 for the Ballets Russes production choreographed by Fokine to Ravel's score; the sheet survives in the Harvard Theatre Collection at Houghton Library.
credit: MS Thr 414.4 (9), Harvard Theatre Collection , Houghton Library, Harvard University

title: L'Homme au Balcon
description: A tall, narrow Cubist portrait of the doctor Théo Morinaud on a Paris balcony, the city beyond him fragmented into stacked facets. Oil on canvas, 195.6 x 114.9 cm, the picture entered the Philadelphia Museum of Art via the Louise and Walter Arensberg Collection in 1950.

title: Les Baigneuses
description: Cubist bathers stand and recline along a river bank rendered as a shallow stage of interlocking planes. Oil on canvas, 105 x 171 cm, Les Baigneuses entered the Musée d'Art Moderne de la Ville de Paris after being shown at the 1912 Salon de la Section d'Or, the exhibition that defined the Puteaux group.

title: Nollendorfplatz
description: Trams curve around the Berlin square of Nollendorfplatz under a steep, tipped-up perspective, with hurrying figures pressed against the kerb. Kirchner began his Berlin street pictures shortly after the Brücke group relocated from Dresden; the canvas is now held by Stiftung Stadtmuseum Berlin.

title: Portrait of Pablo Picasso
description: A Cubist portrait of Picasso seated with a palette, his face and jacket broken into pale blue and ochre facets. Painted in 1912 and now at the Art Institute of Chicago, Gris inscribed the canvas 'Hommage à Pablo Picasso', framing his own analytic style as both tribute and challenge to the older master.

title: Self-portrait
description: Kustodiev paints himself in fur cap and overcoat against a snowy Russian street, hand to chin in a moment of pause. Commissioned in 1912 for the Uffizi self-portrait gallery in Florence, the picture places the artist within the Russian merchant world he was making his subject.

title: Slavs in their Original Homeland: Between the Turanian Whip and the Sword of the Goths
description: The opening canvas of Mucha's Slav Epic shows a couple cowering in a moonlit field while spectral horsemen ride overhead, embodying the early sufferings of the Slavic peoples. Mucha's tempera-and-oil technique on huge canvas gives the symbolist scene a pale, dreamlike pallor distinct from his Art Nouveau posters.

provenance.collection: museum collection of the Prague City Gallery

title: The Tiger
description: A crouching tiger fractured into prismatic facets of yellow and black, its body locked into the surrounding crystalline landscape. Marc, co-founder of Der Blaue Reiter, treated animals as emblems of an unfallen spiritual world, here borrowing Cubist faceting to fuse predator and habitat into a single restless rhythm.

title: Windows Open Simultaneously
description: A small 1912 oil in which the Eiffel Tower dissolves into a grid of translucent green, pink and ochre prisms, identifiable only by its tapering silhouette. Acquired by the Tate and measuring 45.7 by 37.5 cm, the panel belongs to Delaunay's Simultaneous Windows cycle, the founding works of Orphism.

title: Cliff Dwellers
description: Tenement crowds spill from fire escapes, stoops, and laundry-strung windows on a sweltering summer evening on Manhattan's Lower East Side. Painted in May 1913 and now at the Los Angeles County Museum of Art, the canvas belongs to Bellows's Ashcan record of immigrant New York.

title: Edtaonisl
description: Three metres square, the canvas threads abstract bands of rose, blue, and ochre around a memory of a dancer and a watching cleric seen on Picabia's Atlantic crossing. The invented title interleaves the French words étoile and danse; the picture was shown at the 1913 Armory Show and is now at the Art Institute of Chicago.
credit: MoMA , see also Art Institute of Chicago

title: Jealousy
description: A bearded man stares from the foreground in green-tinged pallor while behind him a woman in red plucks fruit beside another suitor. Munch returned to the jealousy motif repeatedly, treating it as a Garden-of-Eden parable charged with autobiographical anxiety.

title: L'Équipe de Cardiff
description: Cardiff rugby players leap for the ball beneath a Ferris wheel, an aeroplane, and a luminous advertising hoarding for Astra. Oil on canvas, 326 x 208 cm, the picture entered the Musée d'Art Moderne de la Ville de Paris as the largest of Delaunay's three Équipe de Cardiff variants from 1912-13.

title: L'Homme en hamac
description: A reclining figure swings in a Cubist hammock, the suspending ropes and surrounding garden broken into faceted planes of green and ochre. Oil on canvas, 130 x 155.5 cm, the picture entered the Albright-Knox Art Gallery in Buffalo after its 1913 debut at the Galerie La Boétie Salon de la Section d'Or.

title: La Pisanella by L. Bakst 06
description: Set design for the Port of Famagusta, the Cypriot harbour from Gabriele d'Annunzio's play La Pisanelle ou la Mort parfumée. Bakst made the watercolour in 1913 for Ida Rubinstein's production at the Théâtre du Châtelet, staged by Vsevolod Meyerhold with music by Ildebrando Pizzetti.

title: Picabia starDancer
englishTitle: Star Dancer on a Transatlantic Steamer
description: A music-hall dancer dissolves into prismatic shards of pink and blue aboard a transatlantic steamer. Painted in 1913 on Picabia's voyage to New York for the Armory Show, the watercolour translates Cubist faceting into the chromatic energy he would soon name Orphism.

title: Portrait de l’éditeur Eugène Figuière
description: The publisher Eugène Figuière sits behind a desk stacked with books and journals, surrounded by Cubist planes that name his most important authors. Oil on canvas, 143.5 x 101.5 cm, the portrait was painted to mark Figuière's publication of Gleizes and Metzinger's manifesto Du Cubisme in 1912; it hangs at the Musée des Beaux-Arts de Lyon.

title: Portrait of Mikhail Matyushin
description: A faceted Cubo-Futurist portrait of the composer and painter Mikhail Matyushin, his head dispersed into intersecting metallic planes against a fragmented backdrop. Painted in 1913 and held by the State Tretyakov Gallery, the canvas dates from the year Malevich and Matyushin collaborated on the Futurist opera Victory over the Sun.

title: Promenade
description: Strolling figures pass beneath trees on a sunlit avenue, simplified into faceless silhouettes against blocks of pure colour. Macke, a central member of Der Blaue Reiter, used such promenade scenes to translate everyday Rhineland leisure into the prismatic colour planes he absorbed from Delaunay's Orphism.

title: Samovar
description: A Russian samovar dissected into cylindrical and conical facets of grey, ochre, and tin. Painted in 1913 and now at the Museum of Modern Art in New York, the still life sits between Malevich's Cubo-Futurist machine subjects and the radical abstraction he would unveil as Suprematism two years later.

title: Sand Hills near Grünau
description: Pale dunes outside the Berlin suburb of Grünau roll in jagged ridges under a sharp blue sky, with a few small figures scattered across the slope. Kirchner painted the picture in 1913 during a summer excursion from his new Berlin studio; the canvas was photographed for the Google Art Project from a German museum collection.

title: Seiltänzerin
description: A tightrope walker poised above a fairground crowd, the scene built from interlocking translucent diamonds of colour. Painted in the artist's most prolific year, the composition shows Macke fusing his Blaue Reiter sensibility with the prismatic geometry he had absorbed from Robert Delaunay in Paris.

title: Street
description: Two cocottes in feathered hats and fur stoles stride down a Berlin pavement, a crowd of dark-suited men pressing past on either side. Oil on canvas, 120.6 x 91 cm, the picture belongs to Kirchner's Berlin Strassenbilder cycle of 1913-15 and is held by the Museum of Modern Art in New York.
credit: Kirchner and the Berlin Street MoMA

title: The Knife Grinder or Principle of Glittering" Hungarian: A késélező The Knife Grinder
description: A grinder pumps his treadle wheel on a tenement stair, his hands and the spinning blade multiplied into repeated facets to suggest motion. Malevich gave the canvas the subtitle Principle of Glittering and showed it in 1913 alongside the Russian Cubo-Futurists; it now belongs to the Yale University Art Gallery.

title: The Prince Out Hunting Sees the Castle Where the Princess Lies Sleeping
description: A young prince reins in his horse at the edge of a forest, gazing across a moat to a turreted castle wrapped in briars. Bakst painted the panel between 1913 and 1922 for James de Rothschild's Sleeping Beauty cycle at Waddesdon Manor, where the National Trust still keeps the series.

title: The Princess and the Court Fall Asleep for a Hundred Years
description: Courtiers slump into a hundred-year sleep around the dais where the princess lies, drapery and tapestries already softening into the dust of long quiet. Bakst painted the panel between 1913 and 1922 as part of his Sleeping Beauty cycle for James de Rothschild at Waddesdon Manor, now held by the National Trust.

title: The Princess Pricks Her Finger on a Spinning Wheel
description: The princess recoils at the moment the spindle pierces her finger, the old crone leaning over the wheel in a shadowed tower chamber. Bakst painted the panel between 1913 and 1922 for James de Rothschild's Sleeping Beauty cycle at Waddesdon Manor, where the National Trust still keeps the series.

title: The Sleeping Beauty: The Prince Discovers the Princess and Wakes Her with a Kiss
description: The prince leans over the sleeping princess on her canopied bed, the moment of waking fixed in a swirl of brocade and Bakst's ornamental palette. Painted between 1913 and 1922 as the seventh panel in a Sleeping Beauty cycle commissioned by James and Dorothy de Rothschild, with members of the Rothschild family modelling for the characters. The panels were installed in the Bakst Room at Waddesdon Manor in 1995.

title: Two Women with a Washbasin; The Sisters
description: Erna and Gerda Schilling stand by a washbasin in a Berlin interior, one bending forward to dip her hands while the other looms behind in pointed silhouette. Kirchner painted the dancer sisters repeatedly during his Berlin period; the canvas is in the Städel Museum, Frankfurt, with sharp pink and green complementaries pitched against the city's nervous tempo.

title: Udnie
description: Curving metallic planes and tubular forms hurtle across a near-square canvas almost three metres on each side. Picabia painted Udnie in 1913 after watching Polish dancer Stasia Napierkowska perform on the ship carrying him to the Armory Show; the picture now hangs at the Musée National d'Art Moderne, Centre Pompidou, Paris.
credit: Photograph Coldcreation at MNAM, Centre Pompidou, Paris (Feb. 2014)

title: Weeping Nude
description: A naked woman sits on the edge of a bed, head bowed into her hands, the room dissolving in nervous strokes around her. Munch left the figure raw and unidealised, channelling psychological collapse through agitated brushwork rather than narrative detail.

title: Zmei Gorinich
description: The bogatyr Dobrynya Nikitich strikes at the coiling seven-headed dragon Zmey Gorynych on the rocky banks of the Puchai river. Begun in 1913 and completed in 1918, Vasnetsov's late folkloric canvas reworks the bylina cycle of Russian heroic poems he had been mining since the 1880s.
credit: CD-ROM "Государственная Третьяковская галерея".Издание 2-е; Допол. Издательство: AlexSoft, 2004

title: Albert Gleizes
description: Faceted planes assemble into the seated figure of the composer Florent Schmitt at the keyboard. Gleizes executed the pastel between 1914 and 1915 at 36 by 27 centimetres, the small format and chalky medium softening the angular Cubist syntax he had codified with Metzinger in 'Du Cubisme' three years earlier.

title: In Russia. Soul of the people
description: An expansive procession of Russian people - peasants, monks, soldiers and intelligentsia - moves across a northern landscape in search of spiritual truth. Nesterov treats his pre-revolutionary allegory in luminous, restrained colour, blending Symbolist mood with Orthodox iconographic gravity.

title: Kustodiev Renee Notgaft
description: Renée Ivanovna Notgaft sits in a contemplative half-length pose, her dress and bare shoulders set against a darker backdrop. Kustodiev painted the portrait in 1914, the year before his spinal illness confined him to a wheelchair and pushed him toward the bright, festive Russian subjects of his late work.

title: Le Matin clair aux saules
description: Pale lilies float on a luminous pond crossed by the trailing reflections of weeping willows. The panel forms part of the Grandes Décorations cycle Monet painted at Giverny for the oval rooms of the Musée de l'Orangerie in Paris, where pond, sky and bank dissolve into a continuous surface.

title: Les Deux saules
description: Two weeping willows frame the composition like proscenium curtains, their trunks pale against drifts of pink and blue water. The mural-scale study belongs to Monet's late Giverny project conceived as continuous, all-encompassing decoration.

title: Les Nuages
description: Banks of cloud are reflected on the still pond surface, the lilies riding across them like islands. Painted as Monet wrestled with cataracts, the panel forms part of his bequest of mural-scale Décorations to France.

title: Matin
description: Pale dawn light catches the lily pads on the Giverny pond, the water dissolving into broad horizontal sweeps of mauve and cream. The work belongs to the great cycle Monet developed in his late, near-blind years for the Orangerie ovals.

title: Monet w1781
description: A Giverny pond study built up in long, weighted strokes of violet, green and pink. Monet works without a horizon line, letting reflected light and lily pads alone organise the picture plane.

title: Monet w1786
description: Part of the sustained water-lily project that occupied Monet's final two decades. The handling is broader and more gestural than his earlier Impressionist work, the pigment scrubbed and dragged to evoke shifting water and weather.

title: Nymphéas avec reflets de hautes herbes
englishTitle: Water Lilies, Reflections of Tall Grass
description: From the late Nymphéas cycle, the canvas dissolves the lily pond into floating pads, drowned grasses, and reflected sky. Working at monumental scale in his Giverny studio, Monet abandoned the horizon altogether to let surface and depth fuse into a single chromatic field.

title: Omphale
description: The Lydian queen Omphale stands draped in the lion-skin of Hercules, who served her in bondage as punishment for murder. Byam Shaw, a late Pre-Raphaelite, treats the mythological role-reversal with jewel-toned costume detail and decorative outline drawn from his Birmingham School training.

title: Portrait of an Army Doctor
description: Broad overlapping planes and intersecting diagonals reassemble Major Mayer-Simon Lambert, regimental surgeon in charge of the military hospital at Toul. Gleizes painted the canvas between 1914 and 1915 while serving in the garrison there; it now hangs in the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum, New York, and at least eight preparatory sketches survive.

title: Reflets d'arbres
description: Inverted trees and clouds shimmer in the pond, lily pads punctuating the surface as the only signal of where water meets reflection. The picture pushes Monet's late style toward near-abstraction.

title: Reflets verts
description: Floating pads drift across a mirror of green leaf-shadow, with no sky or bank to anchor the view. The canvas is a study toward the Grandes Décorations Monet eventually donated to the French state for the Orangerie.

title: Reservist of the First Division
description: Cubo-Futurist fragments of a soldier's ear, moustache and cap collide with pasted printed paper, a postage stamp and a real thermometer affixed to the canvas. Malevich produced this assemblage in the autumn-winter of 1914 at 53.7 by 44.8 centimetres; it entered the Museum of Modern Art, New York, after the Berlin works left in Hugo Häring's care were acquired in 1935.

title: Water Lilies
description: Water Lilies

description: Water Lilies

title: Woman with animals
description: Madame Raymond Duchamp-Villon sits in a large armchair with her dog and two cats, wedding band and beads picked out among the shifting Cubist planes. Gleizes finished the nearly two-metre canvas in February 1914 and showed it at the Salon des Indépendants that spring; the work passed through Marcel Duchamp's collection and has been at the Peggy Guggenheim Collection in Venice since 1940.

title: Albert Gleizes
description:
A returning poilu, rifle and pack flattened into Cubist scaffolding, appears in this wood engraving captioned 'Retour de Bois-le-Prêtre'. Gleizes contributed the print to issue 20 of Le Mot on 1 July 1915, the wartime Parisian weekly co-edited by Paul Iribe and Jean Cocteau, while the artist was himself serving at Toul.</curatorDescription>
