title: Albert Gleizes
englishTitle: Sketch for the Portrait of Jean Cocteau
description: A schematic head-and-shoulders study of the young Jean Cocteau, reduced to a few angled planes and contour lines in Gleizes' Cubist idiom. Drawn during the artist's military service at Toul, it was reproduced in Josep Maria Junoy's Catalan avant-garde review Troços in October 1917.

title: Anisimov Alexander Ivanovich
description: The icon historian Alexander Ivanovich Anisimov is shown seated, hand resting near a book, in muted greys against a sober wall. Kustodiev painted the portrait in 1915 from his wheelchair after spinal surgery; Anisimov was a leading scholar of medieval Russian painting and would later be arrested and shot in the Stalinist purges.

title: Composition for "Jazz
description: Bright wedges of colour pivot around tilted black bars in a square 73-centimetre composition. Gleizes painted the work in 1915 on cardboard now mounted to Masonite during his stay in New York; it entered the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum as part of the founding Cubist holdings.

title: Fantômas
description: A Synthetic Cubist still life of pipe, newspaper and glass, with the words FANTOMAS and LE JOURNAL legible across the fragmented planes. Painted in 1915 and held in the Chester Dale Collection at the National Gallery of Art, Washington, the title cites the popular pulp anti-hero of Souvestre and Allain's serial novels.

title: Goyō Hashiguchi
description: A young woman freshly emerged from the bath gathers her loosened hair, skin warm against the cool indigo of her robe. Hashiguchi, a leading shin-hanga designer, revived the bijin-ga tradition of Utamaro with modern psychological intimacy and richly burnished woodblock printing.

title: Ici
description: Alfred Stieglitz appears as a broken bellows camera, with an automobile gearshift in neutral and an engaged handbrake, reaching toward the word IDEAL. Picabia's mechanomorphic portrait was based on a Vest Pocket Kodak advertisement and ran on the cover of issue 5-6 of the New York review 291 in July 1915.

title: Kanae Yamamoto
description: A cow rendered in sōsaku-hanga style, its bulk built up from carved planes of color. Yamamoto launched Japan's creative-print movement, insisting that the artist personally design, carve, and print the block, and his rural subjects helped redirect woodblock practice from commercial ukiyo-e toward modernist self-expression.

title: Monet w1976
description: A late work in Monet's water-garden idiom, where pond, foliage and reflected sky merge into a single chromatic field. The surface is heavily worked, each pass of the brush adjusting temperature rather than drawing form.

title: Nature morte à la nappe à carreaux
description: A guitar, wine bottle, fruit dish and Bass ale with its red diamond logo sit on a checked tablecloth, the arrangement also legible as the head of a bull. Gris painted the 116-centimetre canvas in Paris in March 1915, shortly after returning from a wartime stay in the South of France; it entered the Metropolitan Museum of Art with the Leonard A. Lauder Cubist Collection in 2014.
credit: Christie's , LotFinder: entry 5766361 (sale 1505, lot 9) New version: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Leonard A. Lauder collection

title: Nu à la toilette
description: A nude at her dressing table dissolves into wheeling discs of pure colour, the mirror and figure interpenetrating. Delaunay painted the 140 by 142 centimetre canvas in 1915 during his Iberian exile from the war; it is held by the Musée d'Art Moderne de la Ville de Paris and belongs to his Orphist series exploring simultaneous contrasts.

title: Self Portrait in 4th Avenue Studio
description: Painted in his Fourth Avenue studio late in life, Chase shows himself in a dark suit among the bric-à-brac collection that doubled as his teaching tool. The bravura handling and theatrical self-presentation summarise the persona he cultivated at the Art Students League and Chase School.
credit: Upload Bot (Cobalty), possibly from a Art-CD-Rom; Richmond Art Museum, online collection

title: Self-portrait as a Soldier
description: Kirchner stands in his studio in army uniform with the bloodied stump of an amputated right hand, a nude model behind him in sickly yellow tones. The 1915 oil at the Allen Memorial Art Museum, Oberlin, references his service in the 75th Field Artillery Regiment and the breakdown that brought a provisional discharge; it was later included in the Nazi Entartete Kunst exhibition of 1937.

title: Still Life before an Open Window
description: A table holding a Médoc bottle, fruit dish, glass and a copy of Le Journal stands before a window looking onto a Montmartre balustrade and the trees of Place Ravignan. Gris painted the 115-centimetre canvas in 1915 from his studio in the Bateau-Lavoir; it is held by the Philadelphia Museum of Art and counts among his Synthetic Cubist breakthroughs.

title: Suprematism
description: Coloured rectangles and bars float on a white field, freed from any object reference. Malevich exhibited his first Suprematist canvases at the Last Futurist Exhibition 0,10 in Petrograd on 19 December 1915, declaring painting's right to non-objective form; he hung the Black Square in the corner traditionally reserved for the household icon.

title: The beauty
description: A stout nude reclines on a blue-painted bed amid floral wallpaper and stacked pillows, the colour scheme borrowed from peasant textiles and lubok prints. Painted in 1915 with the Moscow Art Theatre actress Faina Shevchenko as model, the 141 by 185 cm canvas is now in the Tretyakov Gallery.

title: Viktor Vasnetsov by S.Malyutin
description: The painter Viktor Vasnetsov sits in three-quarter length, his long beard and contemplative expression rendered in pastel on grey cardboard. Sergey Malyutin executed the 104 by 59 centimetre portrait in 1915 in Vyatka; it is now held by the Vyatka Art Museum named for the Vasnetsov brothers, inventory number Zh-180.

title: Water Lilies
description: A large-scale water-lily canvas of 1915, painted in the studio Monet built at Giverny to accommodate his ever-bigger formats. The pond has lost its banks entirely; tangled reflections of weeping willow descend through deep blues and violets while pads float as flat islands of green.

title: Water Lilies
description: One of the water-lily compositions Monet painted at his Giverny pond, dissolving the surface into floating pads, reflected sky, and submerged depths. The late series pushed Impressionism toward an immersive, near-abstract vision of light on water.

title: Water Lilies
englishTitle: Water Lilies (Agapanthus, Cleveland Museum of Art)
description: From Monet's late Giverny series, the painting abandons horizon and shoreline for a pure expanse of water surface. Lily pads and agapanthus stalks float among broken reflections of sky and trees, the brushwork loosened toward near-abstraction.

title: Charles W. Bartlett - Color woodblock print
description: Pilgrims and worshippers gather at the marble pool surrounding the Golden Temple in Amritsar, the gilded sanctuary mirrored in the still water. Bartlett based the design on sketches from his 1913 Indian travels; the 22 by 30 centimetre colour woodcut was published in Tokyo in 1916 by Watanabe Shōzaburō, one of twenty-one Bartlett prints Watanabe issued that year.

title: Google Art Project
description: Snow-covered Russian rooftops, golden church domes and bare birches frame troikas and crowds celebrating Maslenitsa beneath a pink and gold sky. Kustodiev painted the 1916 canvas at the State Russian Museum, Saint Petersburg, from his wheelchair following spinal surgery; it draws openly on the bright flat colour of the lubok print tradition.

title: Hawaiian Fisherman
description: A Native Hawaiian fisherman stands waist-deep in the surf casting his throw-net, the line of the horizon held high in the frame. Bartlett designed the print after settling in Honolulu in 1917, where the outbreak of the First World War turned an intended brief visit into a permanent residency; the woodblock was cut in Watanabe Shōzaburō's Tokyo workshop and is one of only three completed Hawaii subjects in his shin-hanga output.

title: Maslenitsa
description: Townspeople and sleigh teams cross a snowy public square ringed by onion-domed churches and merchant houses during the Eastern Orthodox Maslenitsa festival. Kustodiev returned to the Shrovetide subject several times in 1916, painting these celebrations of Russian provincial life from his wheelchair while bedridden Russia was fighting the Great War.

title: Parting Spring by Kawai Gyokudo
dateCreated: 大正5年 第10回文展出品
originalDateString: 大正5年 第10回文展出品
description: The left panel of a pair of folding screens by Kawai Gyokudō, designated an Important Cultural Property of Japan. Working in the nihonga tradition, the artist evokes the melancholy of late spring through misty mountains and falling cherry blossoms.

title: Parting Spring by Kawai Gyokudo
dateCreated: 大正5年 第10回文展出品
originalDateString: 大正5年 第10回文展出品
description: The right panel of Gyokudō's Parting Spring screens, completing a continuous landscape of waterfalls, drifting petals, and veiled peaks. The nihonga master fuses traditional ink technique with subtle modern atmospheric effect.

title: Portuguese Woman
description: A Portuguese woman pours from a pitcher, her costume and the surrounding still life dissolved into chromatic discs and arcs. Delaunay painted the canvas in oil and wax in 1916 during the family's stay in the Portuguese village of Vila do Conde near Oporto; the work, also known as the Tall Portuguese, is held by the Museo Thyssen-Bornemisza in Madrid.

title: Suprematist Composition
description: Geometric planes of red, blue, yellow, and black float against a white field in dynamic, weightless arrangement. Painted in 1916 and held at the Stedelijk Museum in Amsterdam, the canvas belongs to Malevich's Suprematist phase, his project to reduce painting to pure feeling expressed through non-objective form.

title: The Water-Lily Pond
description: A canvas from the Japanese-bridge and water-garden series of Monet's last years, painted as his cataracts deepened and his palette warmed toward reds and oranges. Form gives way almost entirely to colour and reflected light.

title: Udaipur
description: A view of Udaipur with its lakeside palaces silhouetted against an Indian sky, published as a woodblock print by Watanabe Shozaburo in Tokyo. Bartlett, a British painter who collaborated with Watanabe's Honolulu-based shin-hanga workshop, completed the design after travels through India in 1916.

title: Udaipur' by Charles W. Bartlett
description: Muslim worshippers gather for sunset prayers on the lake shore at Udaipur, the city walls and palaces rising on a hillside in the distance. Cut and printed by Watanabe Shozaburo's Tokyo workshop in 1916, the print belongs to the first set of six Indian landscapes Bartlett produced under the shin-hanga publisher.

title: Water-Lilies
description: One of the late Giverny pond pictures, painted as Monet was preparing the monumental Grandes Décorations now in the Orangerie. Lily pads drift across a mirrored surface in which sky, willow, and water trade places, the paint laid in long, lapping strokes of green, mauve, and rose.

title: Glass and Checkerboard
description: A drinking glass and a folded checkerboard arranged on a tabletop in tightly interlocking planes of grey, black, and ochre. Painted around 1917 and held at the National Gallery of Art in Washington, the panel belongs to Gris's late Synthetic Cubist phase, when he tightened the vocabulary toward crystalline geometry.

title: Monet w1897
description: From the long water-lily campaign begun once Monet diverted a branch of the Epte to feed his pond. The composition omits sky and bank entirely, training the eye on the drift of pads and the cool glaze of reflection.

title: Monet w1900
description: A turn-of-the-century pond view, made when Monet first showed the water lilies as a unified series at Durand-Ruel. The Japanese footbridge or its absence anchors a study of green-on-green reflection.

title: Philosophers
description: A double portrait of theologians Pavel Florensky and Sergei Bulgakov walking in conversation through a quiet wooded landscape. Nesterov's pared composition and contemplative palette frame the encounter as an icon of Russian religious philosophy on the eve of revolution.

title: Scheherazade
description: A stage design for the Ballets Russes production of Scheherazade, set to Rimsky-Korsakov's symphonic suite, with billowing curtains and oriental cushions in saturated greens and oranges. Bakst's 1910 décor for Diaghilev established the scenographic vocabulary of jewel-toned exoticism that defined the company's early Paris seasons.

title: yellow-irises-1917
description: A late Giverny study of yellow flag irises, painted as Monet's eyesight clouded with cataracts and his palette grew correspondingly hot and saturated. The flowers swim in loose, near-abstract bands of green and gold, anticipating the decorative scale of the Grandes Décorations.

title: A Merchant's Wife's Teatime
description: A young merchant's wife sits before a samovar laden with cakes, watermelon, and grapes, her cat resting on the table beside her. Painted in 1918 and held at the State Russian Museum in Saint Petersburg, the picture is one of Kustodiev's most reproduced canvases, an elegy for the pre-revolutionary provincial bourgeoisie composed from a bed where polio confined him.

title: Monet w1884
description: A late Giverny study in which the lily pond becomes a near-flat tapestry of floating discs and submerged shadow. Monet builds the surface in restless, overlapping touches that carry no firm contour.

title: Seated Nude
description: A reclining female nude with elongated neck and almond-shaped eyes, set against a deep red ground. Painted around 1918 and held at the Honolulu Museum of Art under accession 2895.1, the canvas belongs to the series of nudes that drew police censure when shown at Berthe Weill's Paris gallery in late 1917.

title: John Singer Sargent
description: A personification of the defeated Synagogue, blindfolded and clutching a broken staff, painted for Sargent's Triumph of Religion mural cycle in the Boston Public Library. The medieval iconographic pairing with a triumphant Church drew sustained protest from Boston's Jewish community. The cycle was left unfinished, partly in the wake of that controversy.

title: Kustodiev Winter-shrovetide-festivities 1919
description: Sledges glide through a snowbound Russian provincial town during the carnival week before Lent, with onion-domed churches and crowds of fairgoers under a pink winter sky. Painted in 1919 at the height of the Civil War, Kustodiev's nostalgic merrymaking belongs to a cycle of Maslenitsa scenes that imagined the lost merchant culture as folk pageantry.

title: Le bassin aux nymphéas
description: From the late Giverny series, the canvas crops the lily pond into a near-abstract field of floating pads and reflected sky. By 1919 Monet's failing eyesight pushed him toward broader, more saturated touches that would culminate in the wraparound Grandes Décorations of the Orangerie.
credit: Private collection institution QS:P195,somevalue,P3831,Q768717; Christie's , LotFinder: entry 5100003 (sale 7599, lot 16, london, 24 June 2008)

title: Prayers at Sunset
description: Worshippers gather at a ghat in Udaipur as evening light falls on the lake and palace beyond. Cut and printed in 1919 by Watanabe Shozaburo's Tokyo workshop and acquired by the Honolulu Academy of Arts, the print belongs to Bartlett's Indian series produced after his 1916 tour of the subcontinent.

title: Réveil Matin
description: Mechanical schematic of an alarm clock rendered in ink, its dial, springs, and bell drawn with engineer's precision and labelled in handwritten French. Made in 1919 and held by Tate in London, the drawing belongs to Picabia's machinist Dada period, when he used technical diagrams to satirise human function as mere mechanism.

title: Silk Merchants
description: Indian silk merchants display bolts of cloth in a bazaar, their turbaned figures backlit by daylight through the shopfront. Printed in 1919 by the Watanabe workshop in Tokyo and held at the Honolulu Museum of Art, the design belongs to Bartlett's Indian shin-hanga series adapting Asian travel subjects to the Japanese woodblock medium.

title: Still Life with Fruit Dish and Mandolin
description: A mandolin, fruit dish, and folded newspaper arranged on a patterned tablecloth in flat, interlocking planes of muted blue, ochre, and white. Painted in 1919, the canvas belongs to Gris's Synthetic Cubist maturity, when he composed by deduction from geometric scaffolds before adding the objects rather than fragmenting them in.
credit: The original uploader was Cactus.man at English Wikipedia . Transferred from en.wikipedia to Commons by Melesse using CommonsHelper .

title: Tabi Miyage Dai 1 - Shu
englishTitle: Souvenirs of Travel I: Mutsu Tsuta Onsen
description: From his first Souvenirs of Travel series, Hasui depicts the Tsuta hot spring deep in the mountains of Mutsu, framed by stands of beech and birch. The cool tonal harmonies typify the shin-hanga revival of landscape woodblock printing he led with publisher Watanabe Shozaburo.
credit: Online Collection of Brooklyn Museum ; Photo: Brooklyn Museum, 68.35.5_IMLS_PS3.jpg

title: Water Lilies p
description: Claude Monet (French, 1840–1926) Water Lilies, 1919 Oil on canvas; 39 3/4 x 78 3/4 in. (101 x 200 cm) The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York, The Walter H. and Leonore Annenberg Collection, Gift of Walter H.

title: Albert Gleizes
englishTitle: Femme au gant noir (Woman with Black Glove)
description: A standing woman wearing a black glove fragmented into curving and angular planes of muted earth tones. Painted in 1920 and measuring 126 by 100 centimetres, the canvas belongs to Gleizes's post-war reformulation of Cubism into a rhythmic, decorative system he later codified in his treatise La Peinture et ses lois.
credit: Michel Massenet, Albert Gleizes (1881-1953) , Somogy éditions d'art, Fondation Albert Gleizes, Adagp, Paris, 1998, ISBN 2-85056-241-2 Invalid ISBN

title: Albert Gleizes
description: A Cubist composition of a mother and child built from interlocking curving planes, surviving only through a black-and-white photographic reproduction. The painting was shown at the Exposition Internationale d'Art Moderne in Geneva in the winter of 1920-21 as catalogue number 185; its dimensions and present location remain unknown.
credit: Exposition Internationale d'Art Moderne, Geneva, 26 December 1920 - 25 January 1921

title: Charles W Bartlett's watercolor and ink 'Hana Maui Coast
description: Volcanic cliffs and palms along the windward coast of Maui rendered in transparent watercolour washes over ink. Painted in 1920 after Bartlett settled in Honolulu, the sheet belongs to the Hawaiian landscape work that occupied him after his Asian travels and that informed the prints he developed with Watanabe Shozaburo's Tokyo workshop.

title: Ernst-ludwig-kirchner-sertig-valley-in-autumn
description: The Sertig valley in the Swiss Alps, with steep slopes in autumn ochre and red flanking a narrow flat floor below jagged peaks. Painted on 20 April 1920 from his home above Davos, the canvas belongs to the alpine work Kirchner produced after his wartime nervous collapse, the angular Expressionist vocabulary of the Brücke years cooled by mountain geometry.

title: Evening Snow at Terajima Village
description: A lone figure trudges past snow-laden trees and a thatched cottage as dusk settles over the rural outskirts of Tokyo. Hasui's shin-hanga woodblock combines Western perspective and atmosphere with the layered ink and pigment registration of the traditional Japanese print.

title: Group portrait of the Mir Iskusstva artists
description: An assembly of the World of Art group, with Bakst, Benois, Roerich, Somov, Dobuzhinsky, and other members gathered around a table. Painted in 1920 as a study for an unrealised composition, the canvas portrays the Saint Petersburg circle that had shaped Russian fine printing and Diaghilev's early ballet productions before the Revolution dispersed it.

title: Kustodiev Trinity day
description: Villagers in bright Sunday clothes gather under birches for the Orthodox feast of the Trinity, with onion-domed churches behind them. Painted in 1920, the canvas belongs to Kustodiev's cycle of provincial holiday scenes composed from memory during his confinement to a wheelchair, an idealised reconstruction of pre-revolutionary peasant ritual.

title: Odalisque
description: A reclining model in striped pantaloons inhabits the patterned Nice studio Matisse converted into a North African stage set. The early Riviera odalisques mark his return to sensuous, decorative figuration after the austerity of the war years.

title: Reflections of Clouds on the Water-Lily Pond
description: A late, large-scale Giverny panel related to the Grandes Décorations Monet was preparing for the Orangerie. Clouds are present only as inverted reflections, the painting collapsing sky, water and lily into one immersive plane.
credit: Digital image, The Museum of Modern Art, New York

title: Remaining Snow at Inokashira
description: A shin-hanga woodblock print of the wooded park at Inokashira in Tokyo, with patches of late snow lingering beside dark water. Hasui treats the season with the muted palette and atmospheric stillness that defined his landscape practice.

title: The Bolshevik
description: A giant Bolshevik in winter coat and felt boots strides over the rooftops of Moscow carrying an enormous red banner, with crowds streaming through the streets below. Painted in 1920 and held at the Tretyakov Gallery, the canvas reads as both celebration and warning, its scale rhetoric drawn from icon and lubok traditions Kustodiev had absorbed in his pre-war work.

title: Water-Lily pond
description: Water lilies float on the green-blue surface of the Giverny pond, the bank dissolved in a tapestry of brushstrokes that releases the picture from any horizon. Painted during Monet's late, near-abstract Nymphéas campaign and now installed in Tadao Ando's Chichu Art Museum on Naoshima, the canvas is housed in pure natural light.

title: Waterlilies Pond
description: Waterlilies Pond, Green Reflection

title: WLA moma Monet Reflections of Clouds on the Water-Lily Pond
englishTitle: Reflections of Clouds on the Water-Lily Pond
description: Monet's mural-scale Water-Lily triptych at the Museum of Modern Art carries the open-air pond at Giverny across forty feet of canvas. Painted in his last decade and installed as a continuous horizon, it dissolves figure and reflection into a slow shift of greens, lilac, and white.
credit: Uploaded from the Wikipedia Loves Art photo pool on Flickr

title: Woman in Blue Combing Her Hair
description: A woman in a sheer blue summer kimono draws a comb through her loosened hair, her concentration absolute. Hashiguchi was a leading shin-hanga designer who oversaw every stage of his prints; the work uses mica grounds and subtle keyblock embossing to revive the bijin tradition for the Taishō era.
credit: Walters Art Museum : Home page Info about artwork

title: Albert Gleizes
description: A woman holding a child constructed from intersecting curving and angular planes in muted tones. Reproduced in 1921 in Gleizes's published portfolio, the composition belongs to his early-twenties efforts to integrate the figure into the rhythmic translation-rotation system he set out in his book La Peinture et ses lois.
credit: Michel Massenet, Albert Gleizes (1881-1953) , Somogy éditions d'art, Fondation Albert Gleizes, Adagp, Paris, 1998, ISBN 2-85056-241-2 Invalid ISBN

title: Asahi Bridge in Ojiya
description: A woodblock print from the Souvenirs of Travel II series depicts the Asahi Bridge spanning the river at Ojiya. Hasui's shin-hanga style fuses Western perspective with traditional Japanese block-printing, building atmosphere through layered bokashi gradations.

title: Kawase Ebisu-11
description: A quiet harbour scene from the Souvenirs of Travel II series, capturing a wooden boat at the small port of Ebisu on Sado Island. Kawase, a leading shin-hanga artist, renders the wet stone and overcast sky in muted, atmospheric washes that revive the woodblock tradition for the modern era.

title: KustodiyevSemenov Kapitsa
description: The young physicists Pyotr Kapitsa and Nikolai Semyonov sit shoulder to shoulder over a workbench, both still in their twenties. Painted by Kustodiev in 1921 after Kapitsa joked that they would one day win Nobel Prizes, the canvas was paid for with two pounds of flour and a cockerel, and remains with the Kapitsa family.

title: Old Woman and Young Woman
description: An old woman and a young woman in a Davos interior, their faces stretched into angular masks and the room flattened into bands of acid colour. Painted in 1921 and held at the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum, the canvas dates from Kirchner's Swiss alpine period when he returned figure compositions to the angular tension of his pre-war Brücke work.

title: Part of the Byōdō-in Temple at Uji
description: A partial view of the Phoenix Hall at Byodo-in in Uji, rendered as a shin-hanga woodblock print. Hasui isolates a fragment of the eleventh-century temple's tiled roofline, using flat colour fields and quiet tonal washes characteristic of the Souvenirs of Travel II series.

title: Sailboats
description: Sailboats lie at anchor in a sheltered bay, their masts and sails answered by wide reflections in glassy water. The composition belongs to Yoshida's celebrated set of six prints in which the same sailboat block was printed in different colorways to render morning, afternoon, evening, mist, and night.
credit: book scan: "Printed to perfection. Twentieth-century Japanese Prints from the Robert O. Muller Collection". Amsterdam: Hotei, 2004, p.46.

title: A Young Lady’s Adventure
description: A small female figure picks her way across a fantastical landscape of arrows, plant forms, and disembodied eyes in watercolour and pencil on paper. Made in 1922 during Klee's first years teaching at the Bauhaus in Weimar and held at Tate Modern, the sheet belongs to the inventive, fairy-tale graphic vocabulary he developed alongside his colour theory lectures.

title: At Volga
description: A young woman in a bright sarafan stands on a bluff above the Volga, with steamboats and white-walled churches visible along the bend of the river. Painted in 1922, the canvas belongs to Kustodiev's late series of provincial pastorals that rebuilt the lost world of the Russian merchant towns from memory.

title: Atlas and the Hesperides
description: A circular ceiling painting for the rotunda of the Boston Museum of Fine Arts, showing the Titan stooping under the celestial sphere while the nymphs of the western garden recline at his feet. Sargent took on the rotunda decoration as a late, demanding mural commission. The composition reads from any vantage on the floor below.

title: Francis Picabia
description: Concentric black rings around a frontal female figure, with letters and the title Optophone inscribed at the edges, executed in ink, watercolour, and pencil on board at roughly 72 by 60 centimetres. Made around 1922, the work nods to Raoul Hausmann's invented optophone device, a Dada-era machine for converting light into sound.

title: La Tour Eiffel et Jardin du Champ de Mars
description: A later, lyrical revisiting of the Eiffel Tower set against the green expanse of the Champ de Mars. By the 1920s Delaunay had softened his Cubist fragmentation into rhythmic curves and bright contrasting colour, integrating the tower into a holiday vision of Paris.
credit: Hirshhorn Museum and Sculpture Garden Collection

title: Leon Bakst - Peasant woman Costume design for the Vaudeville Old Moscow
description: A peasant woman in embroidered red sarafan and headscarf, designed as a costume study for the vaudeville Old Moscow staged in 1922. Bakst, by then in Paris and famous for his Ballets Russes work for Diaghilev, drew on the Russian folk vocabulary of his early career for this late commission.

title: Night Shadows - Oct 1922 Shadowland
description: An anonymous pedestrian crosses an empty street under a sharply raking street lamp, watched from a high, vertiginous viewpoint. The etching, published in Shadowland magazine, sets out the lonely urban geometry Hopper would later expand into his great oil paintings.
credit: Shadowland (Sep. 1922 - Feb. 1923) on the Internet Archive

title: Senecio
description: A stylised head built from concentric planes of yellow, orange and red, the eyes asymmetrical, one circular and one almond-shaped. Painted in oil on chalk-primed gauze in 1922, the panel was acquired by the Kunstmuseum Basel in 1931 and so escaped Nazi confiscation. Klee made it during his Bauhaus years in Weimar, where he was pushing colour theory toward geometric reduction.

title: Sleeping Beauty by L. Bakst 04
description: Costume study for a Countess in Act IV of Tchaikovsky's Sleeping Beauty, drawn in pencil and watercolour. Bakst designed roughly three hundred costumes and five scene changes for Diaghilev's 1921 London production at the Alhambra Theatre, his last collaboration with the Ballets Russes before his death in 1924.

title: Starry Night
description: Painted from the terrace of Munch's Ekely estate outside Oslo, this nocturne reduces landscape to broad zones of indigo, snow-white and shadow. A revisitation of his 1893 motif, it trades earlier symbolism for a quieter, late-career meditation on solitude under the winter sky.

title: Franz von Stuck
description: A late self-portrait on board, signed and dated 1923, presents the Munich Secession founder in dark dress against a neutral ground. The clipped scale and sober finish reflect von Stuck's habit of treating his own image as part of his public persona as artist-prince.

title: After the Battle of Grunwald
description: From the twenty-canvas Slav Epic that Mucha worked on for nearly two decades, this scene shows the aftermath of the 1410 Polish-Lithuanian victory over the Teutonic Knights. The Art Nouveau poster designer here deploys monumental tempera-and-oil composition to advance a pan-Slavic political mythology.

provenance.collection: museum collection of the Prague City Gallery

title: De Gion brug te Hondo in Amakusa Amakusa Hondo Gionbashi
englishTitle: Gion Bridge at Hondo in Amakusa (Amakusa Hondō Gionbashi), from Selected Views of Japan
description: Kawase Hasui's view of the Gion bridge crossing at Hondo on the Amakusa islands, from his series Selected Views of Japan. The print pairs the cool blues of an evening landscape with the softly graded skies that became his signature.

title: Kustodiev Voloshin
description: Portrait of the Symbolist poet and critic Maximilian Voloshin, painted in 1924. By that date Kustodiev had been confined to a wheelchair for eight years after spinal surgery, working almost entirely from photographs and sittings arranged at his Petrograd apartment.
credit: Taken from http://www.abcgallery.com/K/kustodiyev/kustodiyev74.html . High resolution version from http://www.kpnemo.ws/other/2008/09/07/russkie_zhivopistsyi__boris_kustodiev/

title: Matsue
description: A crescent moon hangs over the still moat and tile roofs of Matsue Castle, the lights of the lakeside town reflected in pale washes of water. The print is from Hasui's 'Souvenirs of Travel' series for publisher Watanabe Shōzaburō, a flagship of the early-twentieth-century shin-hanga revival.
credit: Flickr The Sandiego Museum of Art collection

title: Rachel Strong by L.Bakst
description: Portrait of Rachel Strong, the American heiress who would marry Comte Henri de Boisgelin. Painted by Bakst in 1924 during his final months in Paris, where he had moved between theatre work for Diaghilev and society portrait commissions from wealthy expatriates.

title: Shironeko by Takahashi Hiroaki
description: A white cat is shown in profile against a plain ground, executed in the shin-hanga revival of woodblock printing. Shōtei's subtle gradations of grey in the fur and quiet, almost domestic mood typify the movement's blend of tradition and Western naturalism.

title: Enbu by Hayami Gyoshu
description: Black-winged moths spiral upward through tongues of flame, set against a ground of deep ink. Hayami fused traditional nihonga pigments with the decorative geometry of Rinpa, producing an emblem of Taishō-era modernism now held in the Yamatane Museum.

title: Het Zojo heiligdom in Shiba Shiba Zojoji
englishTitle: The Zōjō-ji Temple at Shiba (Shiba Zōjōji), from Twenty Views of Tokyo
description: The Zōjō-ji temple at Shiba, captured by Kawase Hasui for Twenty Views of Tokyo. Hasui became the most prolific landscape designer of the Shin-hanga revival, working closely with the publisher Watanabe Shōzaburō from the early 1920s.

title: Irissen
description: Blossoming irises rise against a softly modulated field of red, white, and blue. Ohara Koson, working with the publisher Watanabe Shōzaburō, became the foremost Shin-hanga designer of flower-and-bird prints between the wars.

title: Kawase Zôjôji
description: View of the Tokugawa mortuary temple Zōjō-ji at Shiba, from the Twenty Views of Tokyo series. A solitary figure shelters under a paper umbrella as snow falls against the vermilion gate, a hallmark of Kawase's quiet, weather-soaked urban landscapes.

title: Russian Venus
description: A bare-breasted bather stands in a wooden bathhouse, gripping a birch besom, with steam and a samovar behind her. Painted in 1925 to 26, the canvas was Kustodiev's last major work, completed from his wheelchair on the reverse of an older student composition because canvas was scarce; it now hangs in the Nizhny Novgorod State Art Museum.

title: Siberische Blauwe Nachtegaal bij een pioenroos onder een besneeuwde schoof
englishTitle: Siberian Blue Robin with Peony Beneath a Snow-Laden Sheaf
description: A small green Siberian blue robin perches on a snow-dusted reed shelter above a single pink peony, the composition set against a deep black ground. Ohara Koson worked closely with the Watanabe house to produce a long sequence of bird-and-flower designs for export.

title: The Grand Canyon
description: The South Rim falls away into vast layered cliffs flushed with desert light, a Japanese sensibility brought to the American Southwest. The print belongs to Yoshida's United States series, made after his sketching tour abroad, and uses successive overprintings to suggest the canyon's atmospheric haze.

title: Twee kaketoes op tak met pruimenbloesem
englishTitle: Two Cockatoos on a Plum Branch
description: Two white cockatoos perch among the early flowers of a plum branch. Ohara Koson produced the design for Watanabe Shōzaburō's Shin-hanga programme, which translated the kachō-e tradition into a refined modern colour-print idiom.

title: Apotheosis of the Slavs
description: The closing canvas of the Slav Epic, in which Mucha gathers the history of the Slavic peoples into an allegorical apotheosis culminating in a youthful figure of independence. The cycle of twenty monumental paintings was his self-declared life's work, given to the city of Prague.

provenance.collection: museum collection of the Prague City Gallery

title: Clearing Sky after Snow
description: A plate from Hasui's Twenty Views of Tokyo, depicting the Sensō-ji temple complex at Asakusa under fresh snow. A leading figure of the shin-hanga revival, Hasui rebuilt the older ukiyo-e collaboration of designer, carver, and printer to record a modernising city in soft, atmospheric colour woodblock.

title: dahlias
description: A garden subject from Monet's Argenteuil period, when his suburban plot became a recurring laboratory for floral colour and dappled shade. Thick, comma-shaped strokes register each bloom as a discrete patch of pigment rather than a botanical specimen.

title: Eiffel Tower
description: The lattice of the tower rises among the rooftops of Paris in flat planes of orange, green and blue. Painted between 1926 and 1928, the canvas belongs to Delaunay's second Eiffel campaign, in which he reworked aerial photographs taken from a balloon by Schelchner and Omer-Decugis; the painting entered the Solomon R. Guggenheim collection in New York.

title: Hiroshi Yoshida, Hikaru umi, 1926
description: Two sailing junks lean before the wind on the dazzled water of the Inland Sea. From the Setonaikai series, the print is one of six in which Yoshida had identical blocks printed in different lighting keys, demonstrating his mastery of multi-impression woodblock colour.

title: Hodakayama
description: From Yoshida's Twelve Scenes in the Japan Alps, this view of Hotaka-dake records the artist's own mountaineering observations of the Northern Alps. Yoshida combined ukiyo-e block techniques with Western tonal modeling, often printing the same blocks in different palettes to capture changing light.

title: Kōjaku cavern at Oga Peninsula
description: A sea cave on the Oga Peninsula renders blue-green water against weathered rock, from Hasui's third Souvenirs of Travel series. The artist toured rural Japan compulsively, and these prints document a coastline that motorised tourism was just beginning to reach.
credit: National Diet Library Digital Collections: Persistent ID 2586549

title: Kumoi-Zakura (Kumoi Cherry Trees)
description: Pale clouds of Kumoi cherry blossom hang over a Japanese garden in the soft tonal gradations Yoshida coaxed from up to thirty separate woodblock impressions. Trained in Western oil painting before turning to shin-hanga, he supervised every stage of carving and printing personally.

title: Monet w1668
description: From the painter's final year, when cataracts and a programme of cataract surgery transformed his colour. The picture belongs to the freer, near-abstract late manner that prefigures mid-century painting and crowns the lifelong project of the Giverny garden.

title: Ochanomizu
description: From Hasui's Twenty Views of Tokyo, this woodblock print shows wet snow muffling the rooftops along the Kanda River at Ochanomizu. The artist was renowned for his subtle differentiation of snowfall, here rendered as soft cotton-like accumulation.

title: Sailing Boats
description: From the Inland Sea series of woodblock prints, this view shows fishing junks under afternoon light. Yoshida printed the same key block in successive variants from morning to night, a shin-hanga experiment in atmosphere achieved by altering only the inking and color blocks.

title: Sailing Boats
description: Junks ride a glassy sea under a low evening sun in this version of Yoshida's six-state Sailing Boats suite. The warm orange ground and silhouetted sails show how shin-hanga printers could transform a single composition through color alone.

title: Sailing Boats
description: Sailing junks drift in a pale, fog-bound sea, their masts dissolving into the haze. One of six time-of-day variants printed from a single key block, this state demonstrates Yoshida's command of bokashi gradations and his shin-hanga sensitivity to weather and air.

title: Sailing Boats
description: Boats glide on still water under the cool tones of dawn, the mountains of the Seto Inland Sea faint on the horizon. Yoshida printed the work in six time-of-day variations, a virtuoso shin-hanga study in the chromatic rendering of light.

title: Sailing Boats
description: The darkest of Yoshida's six Sailing Boats variants, the scene is steeped in deep indigo with the silhouettes of junks just visible against a moonlit sea. The print shows shin-hanga craftsmen working color and gradation to evoke night without losing the woodblock's clarity.

title: Self-Portrait with Palette
description: A late self-portrait in which Munch shows himself frontally before the easel, palette in hand, the face hollowed by age and frank scrutiny. Painting himself was a lifelong project for the artist, charting the shifts of his temperament as openly as any of his symbolic figures.

title: The Dinner
description: Camille and the infant Jean sit at the candlelit family table while a guest leans in from the doorway, the room warmed by lamp glow on porcelain and pewter. An early experiment with artificial light and intimate genre, painted at Étretat during a precarious winter for the young household.

title: Vase of Tulips
description: Vase of Tulips
credit: Claude Monet - Vase of Tulips , Irina , 2014-05-29 23:25

title: Hachirōgata Lagoon
description: A view of Akita's vast Hachirōgata Lagoon from the shin-hanga series Souvenirs of Travel III. Hasui's quiet woodblock composition relies on flat washes of muted color and a low horizon to evoke the stillness of the inland water at dusk.
credit: National Diet Library Digital Collections: Persistent ID 2586549

title: Kameidô
description: The arched drum bridge of Kameido Tenjin shrine reflects in the still pond below, surrounded by spring wisteria. Yoshida revisits a motif made famous by Hiroshige, but rebuilds it with the soft tonal gradations and calibrated overprinting of the shin-hanga revival.

title: Karasu Marsh
description: Karasu Marsh in Akita rendered as still water and reed beds under a quiet sky, from Hasui's third Souvenirs of Travel set. The reduced palette and emphasis on horizon embody the contemplative restraint that defines his shin-hanga landscapes.
credit: National Diet Library Digital Collections: Persistent ID 2586549

title: Kawase Tenno-ji-27
description: Plate from the Souvenirs of Travel III series, depicting the precincts of the ancient Shitennō-ji temple in Osaka. Kawase's shin-hanga method preserves Edo-period block-cutting techniques while indulging Western sensibilities for soft light and weather, here a damp, lantern-lit dusk.

title: Morning on the Daikon Wharf
description: Daybreak over the Daikon vegetable wharf on the Sumida, drawn from Hasui's series Twenty Views of Tōkyō. The print is characteristic shin-hanga: traditional ukiyo-e workshop methods adapted to atmospheric, Western-influenced views of a modernising city.
credit: National Diet Library Digital Collections: Persistent ID 2586549

title: Dawn at Beppu
description: Morning rises over the hot-spring town of Beppu in Kyushu, with steam and hills pressed into a tight horizon. Hasui's bokashi gradations carry the cool light of dawn, a signature effect of his shin-hanga landscapes.
credit: National Diet Library Digital Collections: Persistent ID 2586549

title: Espagnole et agneau de l'Apocalypse
description: A Spanish woman's face is overlaid with the lamb and other contour images in superimposed line. Made in 1928, the work belongs to Picabia's Transparencies series, begun the previous year, in which he alternated paint with resinous varnish so that motifs drawn from Renaissance frescoes, Catalan murals and popular sources could coexist without fully merging.

title: Hōrai Rock
description: A scene of the towering Hōrai Rock rising from the Kiso River, drawn from Hasui's Souvenirs of Travel III. The print balances the cliff's bulk against soft atmospheric washes, a hallmark of the shin-hanga revival of traditional landscape woodblock.
credit: National Diet Library Digital Collections: Persistent ID 2586549

title: Kamezaki in Owari Province
description: A coastal view of the fishing port of Kamezaki in former Owari Province. Hasui frames boats and shoreline buildings under wide skies, using restrained palette and bokashi shading to render the still atmosphere of an Aichi inlet.
credit: National Diet Library Digital Collections: Persistent ID 2586549

title: Kiyomizu-dō Temple in Ueno
description: The Kiyomizu Hall in Ueno Park seen across blossoming trees, from Hasui's Twenty Views of Tōkyō. The shin-hanga design preserves the planar colour fields of the woodblock tradition while introducing softened, plein-air light.
credit: National Diet Library Digital Collections: Persistent ID 2586549

title: Nishi Park
description: Fukuoka's Nishi Park rendered in the shin-hanga manner, with figures threading through trees and lanterns. Hasui's design uses overlapping woodblock impressions to suggest dappled light and the casual pace of urban leisure in early Shōwa Japan.
credit: National Diet Library Digital Collections: Persistent ID 2586549

title: Rapids at the Upper Reaches of Tone River
description: White water churns over boulders in a narrow gorge, with overhanging pines describing the steep banks. Yoshida, trained as a Western-style oil painter before turning to woodblock, achieves the river's translucent depth through dozens of hand-pulled impressions in a single block-printed image.

title: Red Cavalry Riding
description: Three lines of Red Army horsemen gallop across a horizon banded with twelve Suprematist stripes of earth colour. Painted between 1928 and 1932 and inscribed 'God 18' in the lower corner, the canvas was Malevich's one work accepted into the Soviet pantheon; it entered the State Russian Museum in Leningrad on the strength of its title and is the only abstract painting permitted into that lineage.

title: Starlit Night at Miyajima
description: From the shin-hanga series Souvenirs of Travel III, this nocturne shows the floating torii of Itsukushima beneath a star-pricked sky. Hasui pairs deep indigo bokashi gradations with sparse highlights to register the hush of Miyajima after dark.
credit: National Diet Library Digital Collections: Persistent ID 2586549

title: Yoshida Komagatake
description: Ridges of the Southern Japanese Alps recede in cool blues from the summit of Komagatake, a vantage informed by the artist's lifelong mountaineering. Yoshida's woodblock layering produces the thinning air and dry granite light that he sought in his alpine series.

title: Evening in Beppu
description: Evening settles over the Beppu coast in this Souvenirs of Travel III sheet. Hasui anchors the composition with darkened silhouettes against a dusky sky, exploiting the shin-hanga technique of bokashi to dissolve land into water.
credit: National Diet Library Digital Collections: Persistent ID 2586549

title: Hera
description: Three female faces float in superimposed contour against a ground of leaves and pale flowers, with the suggestion of a nude back behind them. Executed around 1929 in oil, gouache, charcoal and pencil on board at 103.4 by 74.9 cm, the picture belongs to Picabia's Transparencies series begun on the Riviera after his break with the Paris avant-garde.

title: Kamisuki
description: A bijin-ga showing a young woman drawing a comb through her loosened black hair, her undergarment slipping from one shoulder. Kotondo revives the intimate vanity scenes of Edo-period printmaking within the early Showa shin-hanga movement.
credit: Walters Art Museum : Home page Info about artwork

title: Shinobazu Pond in Rain
description: Rain falls across Shinobazu Pond in Ueno, the lotus leaves and far shore softened to muted greys and greens. Hasui's mastery of bokashi gradation and overprinted rain-lines made him the foremost printmaker of weather in twentieth-century Japan.
credit: National Diet Library Digital Collections: Persistent ID 2586549

title: Takinogawa River
description: From the series Twenty Views of Tōkyō, this print follows the Takinogawa River as it winds through suburban greenery. Hasui captures a quieter periphery of the modernizing capital, layering subtle woodblock washes for foliage and reflected water.
credit: National Diet Library Digital Collections: Persistent ID 2586549

title: The Pond at Benten Shrine in Shiba
description: A shin-hanga woodblock from Hasui's Tokyo Twenty Views, showing the red-railed bridge to the Benten shrine reflected in still water at twilight. Layered bokashi gradations and crisp keyblock lines exemplify the Watanabe workshop's revival of ukiyo-e technique.

title: American Gothic
description: A stern Iowa farmer and his daughter stand before a white frame house with a Carpenter Gothic window, the pitchfork echoing the seams of his overalls. Wood used his sister Nan and his dentist as models, fashioning a dry, hard-edged image that became shorthand for rural America.

title: Moon at Magome
description: Part of Twenty Views of Tōkyō, the print shows the moon hanging over the rural fringes of Magome. Hasui builds the night scene from layered indigo blocks and a single luminous disc, demonstrating shin-hanga's debt to classical Edo landscape traditions.
credit: National Diet Library Digital Collections: Persistent ID 2586549

title: Nikkō Kaidō
description: A shin-hanga woodblock print depicting a quiet stretch of the Nikkō Kaidō, the historic highway leading to the Tokugawa mausoleum. Hasui captures the avenue's towering cryptomeria with the soft atmospheric tonality and precise gradation that define his landscape work.

title: Ōmori Coast
description: A view of the Ōmori coast on Tokyo Bay, drawn from Twenty Views of Tōkyō. Hasui registers the meeting of urban edge and water in soft, overcast tones, the shin-hanga answer to Hokusai and Hiroshige's earlier capital views.
credit: National Diet Library Digital Collections: Persistent ID 2586550

title: Sumō-wrestling toads by Hōson
description: Two toads grapple in a sumō ring while companions wait their turn, a gentle parody of the Edo wrestling print. Koson, working in the shin-hanga revival, brings naturalist observation to a comic subject with long roots in Japanese caricature.

title: Woman Before a Mirror
description: A bijin-ga in which a woman in a patterned kimono adjusts her hair before a round mirror, the reflection partly visible at the print's edge. Kotondo balances flat decorative pattern against a quietly observed private moment.
credit: Walters Art Museum : Home page Info about artwork

title: Meguro Fudō Temple
description: Meguro Fudō Temple (Meguro Fudō-dō)
credit: National Diet Library Digital Collections: Persistent ID 2586549

title: Midnight Ride of Paul Revere
description: Grant Wood collapses the night of 18 April 1775 into a single moonlit vista, the white steeple of the Old North Church lit at upper centre as Revere gallops the country road through sleeping Lexington and Concord. Painted in 1931 on Masonite in the Iowa Regionalist's mature style, the canvas entered the collection of the Metropolitan Museum of Art in 1950.

title: Shinagawa
description: Hasui Kawase, Shinagawa

title: Snow in Mukojima
description: Woodblock print

title: De rand van de Shinobazu vijver tijdens een mistige avond. Kasumu yube Shinobazu chihan
englishTitle: Edge of Shinobazu Pond on a Misty Evening (Kasumu yūbe Shinobazu chihan)
description: Lanterns burn in the haze of a foggy evening at Ueno Park, with figures passing beside the still water of Shinobazu Pond and a pagoda rising behind. Kasamatsu Shirō was a leading designer of the second Shin-hanga generation; this print was issued by Watanabe Shōzaburō in 1932.

description: Morning Mist in Taj Mahal, no. 5, Hiroshi yoshida

title: Charles W. Bartlett - watercolor self-portrait
description: Bartlett pictures himself in watercolour, painted in Honolulu in 1933, the year he helped found the Honolulu Printmakers. The English-born artist had settled in Hawaii in 1917 after travels in Japan and India, where he had learned colour woodblock from Watanabe Shozaburo and become a central figure of the shin-hanga movement.
credit: Miles, Richard and Jennifer Saville, A Printmaker in Paradise, The Art and Life of Charles W. Bartlett, with a catalogue raisonné of etchings and color woodblock prints , Honolulu, Hawaii, Honolulu Academy of Arts, 2001

title: Ohara koson
description: Art of Japan in the Cincinnati Art Museum

description: Accession Number: 1998. 101 Display Artist: Yoshida Hiroshi Display Title: The Golden Pavilion Series Title: Kansai District Creation Date: 1933 Height: 14 13/16 in. Width: 9 5/8 in.

title: Akashi strand Akashi no hama
description: A solitary pine bends over the moonlit waters of Akashi Bay as sailboats drift in the distance. Tsuchiya Kōitsu designed the print for the Watanabe Shin-hanga workshop, which carried the lyric landscape tradition of Hiroshige into the twentieth century.

title: De grote lantaarn van de Kannon tempel in Asakusa Asakusa Kannondo ochochin
englishTitle: The Great Lantern of the Kannon Temple at Asakusa (Asakusa Kannondō ōchōchin)
description: Pilgrims climb the steps beneath the giant red lantern that marks the entrance to the Kannon temple at Asakusa. Kasamatsu Shirō issued the design through the Watanabe publishing house at the height of the Shin-hanga revival of traditional ukiyo-e subjects.

title: Het drijvende paviljoen te Katada in de sneeuw Yuki no Katada Ukimido
englishTitle: The Floating Pavilion at Katada in the Snow (Yuki no Katada Ukimidō)
description: A lantern-lit wooden temple stands on the snowy shore of Lake Biwa during a night snowfall. Tsuchiya Kōitsu's 1934 print exemplifies the Watanabe Shin-hanga workshop's mastery of weather and luminous nocturne.

title: Rhythms
description: Interlocking discs of saturated red, blue and green rotate against a black field. Painted in 1934, the canvas belongs to the late Rythmes cycle that Delaunay developed from his earlier Simultaneous Disc paintings, and the work was shown in the Centre Pompidou's 'Rythmes sans fin' exhibition in 2014.
credit: Exposition Robert Delaunay "Rythmes sans fin" - Centre national d'art et de culture Georges Pompidou - Paris [Note: This caption is incorrect. The painting by that name is actually this one also in the same gallery, same artist, same creation year. The painting depicted here is simply "Rythmes".]

title: Archers
description: Three figures draw bows in a darkened landscape, the foremost woman holding arrows in her hand. Painted in oil between 1935 and 1937 at the Wildboden farm near Davos, the canvas belongs to Kirchner's final phase; he wrote to Carl Hagemann that the large shadowed areas were a new discovery, intended to make the picture 'calm and monumental.'

title: Suzukawa River
description: Yoshida Hiroshi, Suzukawa, 1935

title: Walpurgis Night
description: Tangled scratched lines suggest figures and a vulpine head emerging from a brown ground. Executed in gouache on fabric mounted to plywood in 1935, the panel was acquired by Tate in 1964; Klee, by then exiled in Bern after losing his Düsseldorf post to the Nazis, drew on the German folk legend of witches gathering on the Brocken on the eve of May.

title: Three Sisters' by Yamakawa Shūhō
description: "Three Sisters", painted four-fold screen, Honolulu Museum of Art, accession 11822. 1

title: De warme bronnen van Shuzenji Shuzenji onsen
englishTitle: The Hot Springs of Shuzenji (Shuzenji onsen)
description: Lit hotels line the Katsura River at the hot-spring town of Shuzenji on the Izu peninsula, with cherry blossom in the foreground. Kasamatsu Shirō's 1937 design pairs the meticulous block-cutting of Shin-hanga with a romanticism inherited from late nineteenth-century landscape prints.

title: Toshogu Shrine
description: Accession Number: 1998. 102 Display Artist: Yoshida Hiroshi Display Title: Toshogu Shrine Creation Date: 1937 Height: 14 13/16 in. Width: 9 13/16 in.

description: Hiroshi Yoshida - Yomei Gate, 1937

title: Kanae Yamamoto
description: Oil painting by Japanese artist Kanae Yamamoto

title: Rythme n°1
description: Rotating discs and concentric arcs in saturated primaries fill a panel commissioned to decorate the sculpture hall of the 1938 Salon des Tuileries. Delaunay worked alongside Sonia Delaunay, Albert Gleizes, Jacques Villon and André Lhote on the cycle; the canvas was donated to the City of Paris in 1939 and remains in the collection of the Musée d'Art Moderne.

title: Sketches of Famous Places in Japan: Asakusa Kinryūzan Temple
Parson Weems’ Fable
